article_content: Genoa climbed back to third place in the Serie A table on Sunday after Luca Antonelli's goal handed AC Milan their third defeat of the season. Napoli's earlier failure to defeat Empoli left the final Champions League spot open, and Genoa reclaimed it with Antonelli's first-half header securing a 1-0 home win. While Milan suffered their first away loss of the season, they remain in contention for a European place. The Genoa squad celebrated at full-time following the result that puts them third in Serie A. Napoli managed to rescue a point with two goals in five minutes, drawing 2-2 at home against Empoli. Empoli appeared set for their third win in four games after Simone Verdi scored in the first half and Daniele Rugani doubled the lead eight minutes into the second half. However, Napoli staged a comeback as Duvan Zapata reduced the deficit in the 67th minute before substitute Jonathan de Guzman equalized not long after. Lazio added to Parma's troubles with a 2-1 win at Stadio Ennio Tardini, leaving Roberto Donadoni's side at the bottom of the league. Raffaele Palladino gave Parma the lead in the 45th minute, but Lazio responded immediately through Stefano Mauri before halftime. Felipe Anderson put Lazio in front before the hour, ending their three-game winless run and moving them up to fifth place. Atalanta ended a six-match winless stretch with a 3-2 comeback victory over Cesena. Gregoire Defrel scored twice for Cesena to put them 2-0 up after 43 minutes, but Yohan Benalouane cut the deficit on the brink of halftime. Early second-half goals from Guglielmo Stendardo and Maximiliano Moralez secured Atalanta's first league win since October 19, taking them four points clear of the relegation zone.

Napoli ndaikatúi gueteri Empoli rehe ojavy, upévare pe Champions League pegua apyta hovayguépe, ha Genoa ojoko jey upéa Antonelli iñakã-gol rire pe peteĩha mitãme ha ohupyty 1-0 oguahẽrõ guare. Milan ohasa peteîve hasyha hogapegua aho, ha katu oĩ gueteri ñembosarái europeo rehe. Genoa atyguasu ovy’a opa rire pe jey peteĩha Serie A-pe. Napoli ojuhu peteî puntu mokõi gol rehemi cinco aravo’i jave, ha upéicha empate 2-2 Empoli rehe hógape. Empoli oĩ porã ha ohecháva hína mbohapyha ipu’aka irundyha jave, Simone Verdi ojapo pe peteĩha gol ha Daniele Rugani ombojoapy ocho aravo’i ohasa rire pe mokõiha mitãme. Felipe Anderson ome’ẽ Lazio-pe frente, upéva ombopaha mbohapyha ára’ỹijára jey ha ojupi poha pevarã. Atalanta opaha irundyha’ỹha seis jeyha omopu’ãvo 3-2 Cesena rehe. Gregoire Defrel ojapo mokõi gol Cesena rehe 43 aravo’i jave, ha Yohan Benalouane omboguejy diferencia pe intervalo tarovy rehe. Mokõiha mitãme, Guglielmo Stendardo ha Maximiliano Moralez ome’ẽ Atalanta-pe pe primera victoria liga guive jasypa 19 guive, ha upéicha oho irundyha punto más iguambahague rehe.

article_content: Poland's opposition parties have signed a coalition agreement, paving the way for a new government after their majority win in last month's elections. Donald Tusk, the former prime minister and leader of the Civic Coalition (KO), announced the deal on Friday, stating the group is "ready to take responsibility for Poland in the coming years." The coalition, which includes the economically liberal Third Way and the left-leaning New Left alongside KO, is united in its aim to strengthen Poland’s ties with the European Union. Despite their majority, President Andrzej Duda has granted the nationalist Law and Justice (PiS) party—which received the most votes as an individual party—the first opportunity to form a government. However, success for PiS is widely considered unlikely. Communicating as the "democratic opposition," the coalition pledges to reinforce democracy following criticism of PiS for actions that undermined the independence of the judiciary during its eight years in power. The judicial reforms begun in 2019 stopped Polish courts from applying some EU laws and from sending legal questions to the European Court of Justice (ECJ). As a result, the EU froze billions of euros in funding earmarked for Poland, and, in June, the ECJ ruled that these reforms violated the EU’s rule-of-law standards. The opposition prioritizes rebuilding relations with Brussels to unfreeze these EU funds, alongside commitments to restore transparency in public finances and to depoliticize state-owned companies. The coalition has also agreed to overturn the 2020 Constitutional Tribunal ruling that brought about a near-total ban on abortion in Poland. With some of Europe’s strictest abortion laws, Poland has seen mass protests—including after a pregnant woman died from sepsis in June—with few exceptions to the abortion ban, even when the mother's life is at risk. Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, leader of the center-right Polish Peasants’ Party (PSL), said the coalition found consensus on several issues: supporting families, workers, rural areas, education, healthcare, and women's rights. The coalition has also pledged to bolster Poland's position in the EU and NATO amid security concerns following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

article_content: Emmanuil Sadikov has filed a $5 million lawsuit in Brooklyn, New York, alleging that his ex-girlfriend and three other individuals launched an online smear campaign against his fiancée, Evelina Elterman. According to Sadikov, the defendants created sexually explicit profiles by merging Elterman’s photos with nude images of other women and posted them on Russian dating websites. These profiles were then sent to the couple's friends and family, allegedly as retaliation for Sadikov ending an online relationship with one of the defendants. The lawsuit identifies Izabella Avshman, Khananiya Avshman, Florida Fishkin, and Seymond Fishkin as those responsible for creating and distributing the false profiles. Court documents claim that Izabella Avshman threatened to persist with the campaign until Elterman's reputation was destroyed. While some of the profiles have been taken down, others remain online. Sadikov asserts that these actions have led to alienation from friends and family and loss of business opportunities, as associates have declined to work with him. Both Sadikov and his attorney, Stephen Dickerman, have not commented further on the matter.

article_content: Bob Ney, a former chairman of the House Administration Committee and Republican Representative from Ohio, has published a new memoir, 'Sideswiped: Lessons Learned Courtesy of the Hit Men of Capitol Hill.' In the book, Ney criticizes former House Speaker John Boehner, also from Ohio, claiming Boehner was more interested in socializing, golfing, and fundraising than in his official duties. Ney describes Boehner as 'a bit lazy' and accuses him of prioritizing the high life—golf, women, alcohol, and cigarettes—over his responsibilities. According to Ney, much of Boehner’s political career focused on fundraising and leisure, with some of these activities allegedly paid for by lobbyists. Ney alleges that Boehner once promised to help him secure a job and legal defense support if Ney resigned amid the corruption scandal, but Ney claims this promise was not fulfilled. Boehner and his spokesperson, Michael Steel, have dismissed the memoir’s allegations as baseless and attempts to sell books, pointing out Ney’s status as a convicted felon. Ney, whose political career ended in 2006 due to his involvement in the Jack Abramoff lobbying scandal, served 17 months in prison after admitting to accepting bribes. Ney’s book also includes criticisms of other political figures, such as George W. Bush, Dick Cheney, Karl Rove, Andy Card, and Alberto Gonzales. Once close allies due to their shared Ohio background, Ney and Boehner are now publicly at odds.

Ko kuatiañe’ẽme, Ney oñe’ẽ upe rire moakãharakuéra John Boehner rehe, avei Ohio pegua, he’ívo hendápe Boehner hetave oikuaaha golf, je’u ha viru mono’õ, hembiapokuéra rangue. article_content: NASA has partnered with car manufacturer Nissan to develop new self-driving car technologies that could one day be used on Mars. The five-year collaboration will also help improve autonomous vehicles for use on Earth. Robotics experts from NASA will work with Nissan engineers to adapt the company's electric Leaf vehicles. Future Mars rovers might use technology inspired by Nissan's Leaf cars, as the automaker and NASA aim to create advanced autonomous vehicles suitable for both space and terrestrial environments. Nissan has promised to introduce self-driving cars by 2020, but major challenges remain to make them safe on public roads. NASA believes that sensors and systems being developed for autonomous vehicles—such as those handling pedestrians, cyclists, and parked cars—can also improve robotic rovers exploring other planets. NASA plans to send a new rover to Mars in 2020 to study its rocks and environment, searching for signs of life and evaluating the planet's potential for human settlement. The new mission will collect and store Martian rock and soil samples. With a future mission, these samples may be brought back to Earth. Dr. Charles Elachi, director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, has emphasized that returning rock samples from Mars is a top priority. Scientists want these samples to analyze hazards like Martian dust and to develop methods for generating oxygen—important steps for future human missions and possible colonization. The rover effort is part of fulfilling the U.S. goal of sending humans to Mars in the 2030s. Currently, Mars rovers like Curiosity travel slowly—at just 0.08 mph—to avoid obstacles. This limitation means they've explored only small parts of Mars. For example, the Opportunity rover has covered just 25 miles in more than a decade. The new autonomous technologies could help rovers move faster and cover more ground. This collaboration could help identify landing sites for future human missions. Dr. Pete Worden of NASA Ames Research Centre notes that robotics will need greater autonomy for future, more hazardous missions. NASA and Nissan previously worked together in 2005 to design more comfortable car seats, using NASA's research on astronauts' body position in low gravity. Nissan CEO Carlos Ghosn and NASA's Dr. Pete Worden have agreed to work together on autonomous vehicle technology. Early stages of the latest partnership include mapping roads around NASA Ames Research Centre for testing autonomous Nissan Leaf cars. Dr. Maarten Sierhuis, Nissan's Silicon Valley Research Centre director and a former NASA scientist, is leading the project. Engineers will begin with online simulations and hope to test a car on real roads by late 2015. NASA's experience in designing safe, reliable rovers is seen as valuable to Nissan's efforts. Concerns remain about the safety of autonomous vehicles sharing roads with humans. Dr. Worden highlights that Ames has contributed to Mars rover planning software, space station robots, and air traffic systems—all relevant to future collaborations. Carlos Ghosn says the partnership will speed up Nissan's development of safe and reliable autonomous driving technology, with a gradual rollout starting in 2016 and continuing through 2020. Experts note that human drivers may adapt their behavior when interacting with autonomous vehicles, as observed in recent studies. For instance, drivers tend to leave less space when following self-driving cars but may not react as quickly. Google’s driverless cars have been updated to behave more assertively to better navigate mixed traffic.

Ko misión pyahu ombyaty ha omo'ãta yvy ha ita Mars-gua. Peteĩ misión tenondeve ohupytyta ko'ã muestra omondo hag̃ua Yvy ári. Dr. Charles Elachi, NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory director rehegua, omombe'u pe muestra ita ogueru hag̃ua Yvy ári ha'eha prioridad tuichavéva. Encientíficokuéra oipota ko'ã muestra oanalisa hag̃ua mba'éichapa Martian polvokuéra ha umi modo ojejapo hag̃ua oxígeno—which mba'e iñimportantevéva umi misión yvypóra rehe ambue ára ha espero peteĩne colonización rehegua. Oĩ mbeguekatu mba'éichapa autónomo auto seguro ohupytyhumby humana ndive. Experto-kuéra omombe’u heta humano chofer oikosẽ comportamiento rehe ha autónomo auto rehe oñembohasa ha ojeporavóva investigación pyahúpe. Por ehemplo, choferekuéra oñemomichĩve umi autónomo auto renondépe ha katu ndoikatu epya’e ombohovái. Google driverless auto oñemoambueva asertiva rehe oguata hag̃ua tráfico rehe.

article_content: Southampton FC has reportedly decided to retain Nigerian striker Paul Onuachu, despite strong interest from Turkish club Trabzonspor in making his loan move permanent. Onuachu, currently thriving at Trabzonspor with six goals in eight matches, struggled during his time at Southampton, failing to score in 18 appearances after his transfer from Belgian team KRC Genk in the January window. Although Trabzonspor is eager to secure Onuachu, Southampton's management is not interested in selling him, potentially halting the Turkish side’s hopes. Southampton, sitting fourth in the EFL Championship and nine points behind leaders Leicester City, remain contenders for promotion to the Premier League if their positive form persists. Sources suggest Southampton plans to have Onuachu back for the 2024 season as they bolster their squad for a promotion push. After signing a three-year contract in January, Onuachu still has time to establish himself at the club, unless an attractive transfer offer emerges.

article_content: Chen Shaojie, CEO of the Tencent-backed streaming service DouYu, has been unreachable for several weeks, according to multiple news sources. State-owned Cover News initially reported, citing unconfirmed sources, that 39-year-old Chen is being investigated by Chinese authorities and has not been in contact for about three weeks. These reports have not been independently verified by Insider. Cover News mentioned that Chen’s last public appearance was during DouYu’s quarterly earnings call in August. The Financial Times, quoting a person close to Chen, reported he had been taken away by authorities to be investigated for issues related to pornographic and gambling content on DouYu. DouYu representatives did not provide an immediate comment to Insider. However, a spokesperson told CNN that company operations continue normally and any important news will be disclosed promptly. Disappearance of top business executives has grown more frequent in China. Notable examples include Alibaba’s Jack Ma’s period out of public view after government scrutiny, Bao Fan of China Renaissance, and Hui Ka Yan of China Evergrande, who have all faced investigations or detentions.

article_content: Daphne Oxenford, former BBC presenter known for Listen With Mother, has died at the age of 93. The actress and broadcaster became a familiar voice to children in the 1950s and 60s, beginning each episode with the memorable phrase: 'Are you sitting comfortably? Then I'll begin.' Oxenford balanced a no-nonsense approach with warmth, captivating around a million young listeners every weekday through stories and songs. Many adults later told her, 'I grew up with you!' Yesterday, the BBC announced that Oxenford had died peacefully, according to her family. For those outside the era, it's hard to convey how such a simple format enthralled children for 15 minutes each day, especially before television became widespread. The show aired from 1950 and ran for about two decades before changes in format and competition from TV led to its decline, ending in 1982 despite efforts by celebrity fans to keep it alive. Oxenford continued a vibrant career on both radio and television, with roles in Coronation Street, The Sweeney, Man About The House, and Heartbeat. She also appeared in 'To The Manor Born' and was a voice on 'What The Papers Say.' She worked frequently with comedian Les Dawson and, in 2008, played Dame Agatha Christie in a Doctor Who DVD episode. Her husband, David Marshall, whom she married in 1951, died nine years ago. She spent her final years in a retirement home in Northwood, Middlesex. Daphne Oxenford is survived by her two daughters, Kate and Sophie, and two grandsons.

Ko akãgua ha omyasãiva, iñe’ẽ ko'ãga gueteri sapy'a sapy'ánte ombyaty mitãnguéra rehe 1950 ha 1960 jave, upe ñe’ẽ porãitépe oñepyrũha programa: ‘Pejapópa porã peguapy? Upéicharõ, añepyrũta.’ Oxenford niko oikoe heko mbarete ha ipy’a porã, ombovy’a haguéicha heta mitãme ára ha ára umi mombe’upy ha purahéi rupive. Hetaiterei tapicha omombe’u chupe rire: ‘Nderehe ñande okakuaa!’ Kuehe, BBC omombe’u Oxenford omanohague py’aguapy rehe, he’i hogaygua. Umi ndaha’éiva upe árape, hasýpe ikatu oñemyesakã mba’éichapa programa hesakã porãitéva ha'e ombovy’a mitãnguéra 15 aravopýpe, tele oguerekóva mbovy aja. Pe programa oñepyrũ 1950-pe ha ohupytykuri 20 arykue, upe rire oñemoambue ojupi televisión ndive ha ipahápe oñepysyrõ’ỹre ojeheja 1982-pe, oĩramo jepe umi famoso oipytyvõse. Oxenford ohechauka sãso avei radio ha televisión-pe, Coronation Street, The Sweeney, Man About The House ha Heartbeat rehe. Oĩ avei ‘To The Manor Born’ ha iñe’ẽkuri ‘What The Papers Say’-pe. Omba’apo heta Les Dawson ndive ha 2008-pe ojapo Dame Agatha Christie rol Doctor Who DVD-pe. Iména David Marshall, omenda hague 1951, omano nueve ary ohasa rire. Ipahapegua oiko actor kuéra rendápe Northwood, Middlesex-pe. Daphne Oxenford heja mokõi rajy, Kate ha Sophie ha mokõi ta’ýra michî.

article_content: PC David Rathband, who lost his sight after being shot by Raoul Moat in 2010, died by suicide in early 2012, as detailed in an inquest. Rathband had sent worrying signals before his death, including telling his estranged wife Kath in a FaceTime call that he intended to hang himself and she would witness it. Despite these remarks, DC Alison Brown—assigned as the family's police liaison—did not believe he was truly at risk of taking his own life. Brown shared concerns about his mental health and unpredictable social media posts leading up to the tragedy. After his injury, Rathband was commended for his openness and resilience, establishing the Blue Lamp Foundation to aid other injured emergency workers. However, his personal situation deteriorated due to marital issues, including an affair that ended his 20-year marriage. On the day he died, Rathband's sister Debbie Essery expressed alarm after Kath discovered Rathband in poor condition. While these concerns were relayed to senior officers, police hesitated in their response, given prior occurrences and unclear information. The official welfare check was delayed, and officers entered Rathband's home hours later, ultimately finding him deceased despite resuscitation efforts. The case highlights the need for vigilant and timely action when approaching mental health emergencies, especially among those under public and professional pressure.

Oje’e hague peteĩ Facetime-pe, he’i iñemenda’ỹmava Kath-pe ojekutaitaha ha ha’e ohechataha upe mba’e, omombe’u hague. Oñemomba’eguasu chupe upéi, ha’e ojepy’apy ha oñeñe’ẽkatu oguerohory haguére upe mba’e oguerohory Blue Lamp Foundation rehe. Ko’ã mba’e oñemomandu’a umi policía ruvicha-kuérape, ha umi hesegua hesaráikuri pe ñemyrõ akutî rehe, ndoikuaáigui porã mba’éichapa ojehu hína. Finally oñeinvestiga rire oreko haguã lento, oike kuéra hógape are rire, ha ojejuhu omanóva, ojepuru rire umi intento de recuperación. Ko tembiapo ohechauka tekotevẽha ojekuaa porãve ha oñeñangareko pya’e umi mental rehegua ñembyasy rehe, umi ava guasu rehe ha umi protección rehe.

article_content: For those seeking adrenaline-fueled adventures, some of the most demanding road journeys on earth offer not only jaw-dropping scenery but real risks. From traversing the lonely stretches of the Australian Outback to climbing the world's loftiest highways or hugging cliff edges high above rainforest, these trips require serious preparation and resilience.  Canning Stock Route, Australia: This legendary 1,820 km track slices through Western Australia’s arid heartland, across traditional lands of the Tjurabalan, Ngurrara, Martu, and Birriliburu peoples. Travelers encounter both the harshness of the desert and the rich traditions of its custodians, with opportunities to view ancient rock art. The trail, open between Wiluna and Hall’s Creek from May to September, demands a robust 4WD, comprehensive planning, permits, survival gear, and advanced off-road skills. There are few resupply points, and the track is unmaintained but signposted. Guides and preparation guides are available via Four Wheel Drive Australia.  Karakoram Highway, Pakistan & China: Stretching 1,200 km from Abbottabad to Kashgar, this high-altitude wonder traverses the dramatic Karakoram Range, following old Silk Road trading paths. It's an iconic feat of engineering—and a memorial, with over 1,000 workers lost during construction. Spring and early autumn are the safest periods, while heavy winter snows and summer monsoon landslides can cut access. Travelers must arrange visas in advance, check current road conditions, and note that part of the route in Hunza Valley now involves a boat crossing due to a landslide-formed lake.  North Yungas Road, Bolivia: Also known as 'Death Road,' the 69 km route from La Paz to Coroico weaves through narrow turns flanked by vertical drops. Although safety has improved after the 2007 opening of a bypass, the original road remains a favorite for thrill-seeking cyclists. Rainy season travel is discouraged. The route is lined with crosses marking past victims and concludes in the subtropical town of Coroico, gateway to further Amazonian expeditions.  Manali-Leh Highway, India: Covering 490 km from Manali to Leh, this Himalayan road presents alternating panoramas of lofty mountains and high plains. Open from June to mid-October, the route crosses towering passes, requiring two days by bus (with an overnight in Keylong to combat altitude sickness). Bus reservations are advised. Rapid taxi journeys are tougher on travelers and offer minimal time for sightseeing.  Trans-Sahara Highway, Algeria, Niger, Nigeria: Spanning 4,500 km from Algiers to Lagos, this route is a marathon through desert extremes and bureaucratic obstacles. Attempting the journey requires self-sufficiency, a trustworthy 4WD, and desert driving expertise. Foreigners face legal requirements like hiring escorts in southern Algeria, and some borders may be temporarily closed due to security issues. Most sections are paved, except for a sandy 150 km near the Algeria-Niger border. Travel advisories should always be checked before departure.  Source: 'Strap yourself in: the world’s most extreme road trips' © 2012 Lonely Planet.

article_content: It has now been fifteen years since the devastating 26/11 Mumbai terrorist attacks, which shook India’s financial hub on November 26, 2008. Ten members of Lashkar-e-Taiba carried out coordinated assaults on prominent locations such as the Taj and Oberoi hotels, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Nariman House, and Leopold Cafe, frequented by locals and international visitors. The violence resulted in 166 deaths and more than 300 injuries over four days. Nine terrorists were killed during the operation, while the lone surviving attacker, Ajmal Amir Qasab, was captured alive. He was sentenced to death in 2010 and executed in Pune two years afterward. The attacks aggravated already strained Indo-Pakistani relations and heightened communal tensions in India. On this fifteenth anniversary, Israel has unilaterally declared Lashkar-e-Taiba a terrorist organization, emphasizing the importance of international cooperation against terrorism. This step was taken without any official request from India and was praised by Israel’s Ambassador to India. Commemorative events were held, including a poster exhibition at the United Nations in Geneva, organized by activist Priyajit Debsarkar, to honor the victims and spotlight global anti-terror efforts. Indians continue to remember and honor the victims and brave security forces lost in the attacks, underscoring the ongoing need for vigilance and unity in combating terrorism worldwide.

Pa tembiguái Lashkar-e-Taiba gua ojapo ñemomba’apo vai tuichaitereíva umi tenda tuichaveha, Taj ha Oberoi hotel-kuéra, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Nariman House ha Leopold Café rehe – tenda oĩhápe heta tapicha ha avei tetã ambuegua. Ko mba’e ojejapo porandurã’ỹre India-gui ha oñemomba’e Israel embajador India-pe. India retã pegua ojegueromandu’a ha oñemomba’e meme umi hasýva ha tembisa ojejukáva ko tembiapo vaípe, ohechauka joaju ha py’a guasu oikotevẽha peteĩ ára guive terrorismo rehe ojepytaso haguã.

article_content: Tony Blair, the former UK Prime Minister, has been using a £30 million private jet to travel globally in his current roles as a business consultant and public speaker. When he was in office, plans for an official government jet, called 'Blair Force One', were dismissed due to high cost. Currently, Blair personally covers the cost of chartering a bespoke Bombardier Global Express jet, reportedly at £7,000 per hour. This 19-seater aircraft includes a luxurious interior with a stateroom, lounge, kitchen, bed, leather seats, and walnut paneling. Blair, aged 60, has been seen using the jet for trips to Bangkok, Sardinia, New York State, Switzerland, Ukraine, and Israel. The jet, owned by Aravco Ltd and registered with the Civil Aviation Authority, flies up to 13 hours non-stop and has a range of approximately 7,000 miles. According to Bombardier, it is among the most luxurious and advanced business jets available. For example, Blair was photographed leaving the plane in Sardinia on August 25 and in the Adirondacks, New York, the following day—a flight estimated at £60,000. A journey from London to Bangkok with this jet would be around £90,000. Blair has previously faced criticism for flying in jets lent by leaders such as former Libyan dictator Colonel Muammar Gaddafi and Rwanda’s President Paul Kagame. Since leaving office in 2007, Blair has accumulated an estimated £50 million through consultancy, lecture tours, and advisory roles, though his work as a Middle East peace envoy is unpaid. A spokesperson for Blair stated that taxpayers do not pay any part of these travel expenses. The article also notes that the US Presidential aircraft, a Boeing 747, was purchased in 1990.

article_content: Dr. Yetunde Adeniji, the Senior Special Assistant to the President on School Feeding, has announced that the Federal Government is planning to provide meals to 100,000 displaced children in Nigeria's North. Adeniji made this known during a familiarisation tour when she and her team met with Nasarawa State Governor Abdullahi Sule and the Emir of Borgu Kingdom, HRH Dr. Mohammed Sani Dantoro, seeking their support for the initiative. According to Adeniji, the program will begin by targeting 5,000 displaced children in its first phase with the goal of increasing the number to 100,000 over time. This was revealed in a statement issued in Abuja on Saturday by Adeniji’s media team. During their courtesy visit, Emir Dantoro pledged ongoing support to the program started by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, but also raised concerns about existing challenges. He stressed that effective implementation, monitoring, and evaluation are vital for the program's long-term success. The Emir also underscored the importance of meeting the expectations for the initiative and addressing obstacles and bottlenecks. After the Emirate visit, the delegation was received by Governor Sule, who expressed the Nasarawa State Government’s readiness to help achieve the program’s objectives. He noted that incorporating the Almajiris as part of the reforms would help get more vulnerable children off the streets. The delegation also held discussions with Aliyu Tijani, the Federal Commissioner for the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons, to foster collaboration and address the needs of IDPs, Almajiris, and children living with disabilities within the school feeding program.

Adeniji he’i ko mba’e peteî jeho oñemoherakuãhápe, ha’e ha hembiokuéra oñe’êjey Nasarawa Tetã Sãmbyhyhára Abdullahi Sule ha Borgu Ruvicha HRH Dr. Mohammed Sani Dantoro ndive, ojerurekuéra iñepytyvõ ko apopyrã rehe. Ko mba’e ojekuaauka peteî marandu osêva Abuja-pe arapokõindy ohasapýva, Adeniji remianduha rupive. Oñemomba’eguasúvo oguata, Ruvicha Dantoro ombojopyru iñepytyvõ apopyrã ome’ẽva Presidente Bola Ahmed Tinubu, ha’e avei ohechauka umi apañuãi oîva. article_content: A confrontation occurred on Friday at the Kaduna Zonal Command of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) between EFCC officials and some Nigerian Air Force (NAF) personnel. The incident reportedly stemmed from the NAF personnel's attempt to secure the release of their colleagues, who had previously been arrested by EFCC operatives for allegedly attempting to forcefully free fraud suspects from custody. According to the EFCC, its officers had on Monday arrested five individuals—Favour Itung, Rachael Ande, Zuleiman Haruna, Abubakar Ismaila, and Solomon Olobatoke—at an eatery in Barnawa, Kaduna, following credible intelligence on alleged internet fraud. The EFCC stated that after the sting operation, six military personnel who witnessed the arrests at the eatery went to the Kaduna Command and attempted to forcibly release the detained suspects. The EFCC subdued and detained these intruding individuals over the security breach. The six detained individuals were identified as four Air Force personnel—Lawal Abdullahi, Chukwuma Christian, Alfa Suleiman, and Emmanuel Ekwozor—and two students of the Nigerian Air Force Institute of Technology, Chidera Anuba and Joseph Tokula. While in detention, the leadership of the EFCC and the NAF maintained communication in an effort to resolve the situation. However, according to the EFCC, negotiations broke down on Friday, November 17, 2023, when several NAF officers reportedly attempted a forceful entry into the Kaduna Command to release their detained colleagues. The EFCC said its operatives exercised restraint during the confrontation and continued engaging with the NAF leadership. The detained officers were later released to the NAF Provost after proper profiling. The EFCC assured the public that it remains committed to its mandate of combating economic and financial crimes.

Ko mba’e oiko NAF rembipykuaakuéra ohechaukase rire oñemokyre’ỹ hikuái omosãso hag̃ua iñirũnguéra, ojeherókuri EFCC rembiapokuairekuéra rehe he’i haguére oñembosako’irõ hikuái omosãso hag̃ua umi persona oje’inave hague fraude rehe. Peteĩ jeyrí, EFCC he’i oñemopẽhague finde semanape (Arapoteĩ 17, jasypateĩ, 2023), hetave NAF mba’apohára oñeha’ãhague oike kyre’ỹme Kaduna Command-pe omomyatyrõ hag̃ua iñirũnguéra. EFCC omombe’u tetãguárape ohechauka haguã ojapoha hembiaporã, oñorairõ hese opaichagua tembiapo economía ha virupyrusu rehe.

article_content: The Minister of Steel Development, Shuaibu Audu, has announced that the Federal Government, led by President Bola Tinubu, is committed to completing the Ajaokuta Steel Company in Kogi State to boost wealth creation and employment opportunities. At the 20th anniversary and annual conference of the Geoinformation Society of Nigeria (GEOSON) in Jos, Plateau State on Wednesday, the minister, represented by Prof. Linus Asuquo, Director General of the National Metallurgical Development Centre, emphasized the vital role of steel in national development. He stated, 'Steel is vital in our daily lives and works alongside other materials to promote growth and progress. The current administration, led by President Bola Tinubu, is determined to finalize the Ajaokuta Steel Company project to generate wealth and increase employment, aiming to transform Nigeria into a manufacturing nation.' Similarly, the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, called on GEOSON to support government efforts to address insecurity and oil theft in the country. Governor Caleb Mutfwang of Plateau State expressed eagerness to partner with GEOSON for personnel training and to fully utilize geoinformation tools. Represented by Peter Nyam, Commissioner for Lands, Survey, and Town Planning, the governor proposed establishing a framework for knowledge exchange and capacity building. Fitka Bilshakka, National President of GEOSON, reported that the association's membership now exceeds 1,200 across all 36 states. However, he noted that many state governments have not fully engaged with GEOSON's programs, limiting the achievement of its objectives and benefits.

article_content: Federal authorities in New York have announced the largest-ever seizure of counterfeit goods in U.S. history. The haul, valued at over $1 billion, included handbags, shoes, and other luxury merchandise. According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, two individuals have been charged with trafficking these knock-off items from a New York City storage unit and additional locations between January and October. Prosecutors released photographs depicting shelves filled with counterfeit wallets and bags, as well as handbags hanging from hooks covering an entire wall. 'The seizures announced today consist of merchandise with over a billion dollars in estimated retail value, the largest-ever seizure of counterfeit goods in U.S. history,' said U.S. Attorney Damian Williams. If convicted, the two men could face up to 10 years in prison.

article_content: Sir Michael Wilshaw, chief of Ofsted, is expected to raise alarm over the ongoing struggles state secondary schools face with basic educational standards. Recently released figures show that 170,000 students are enrolled in secondary schools labelled inadequate by Ofsted, marking a significant increase despite initiatives to raise standards. The number of schools placed under special measures has climbed to 147—a rise of 62%—while roughly 70% of schools still achieve 'good' or 'outstanding' status, indicating no improvement in top ratings. Sir Michael interprets these trends as signs that progress in secondary education has reached a standstill, or may even be regressing. Even with increased autonomy given to school leaders through policies like the academies programme, many secondary schools are still falling short on fundamental teaching quality and discipline. Ofsted's latest annual report shows that, over the past two years, the number of students attending inadequate secondary schools has grown by 70,000. In comparison, primary schools continue to demonstrate progress, whereas secondary school improvements have stalled. Sir Michael highlights weak school leadership, insufficient oversight, and tolerance of poor behaviour as critical failings. He emphasizes that many secondary schools lack effective support systems, despite government policies granting more autonomy or placing new management in charge. Sir Michael argues that a school's structure—whether academy, local authority maintained, or part of a trust—is less important than the strength of its leadership, governance, and approach to teaching and behaviour. He calls for improved monitoring of underperforming schools that often operate in isolation without adequate backing from local authorities or sponsors, noting that such schools frequently miss out on good leadership practices and beneficial partnerships. Conversely, he commends 'outstanding' schools for fostering strong learning cultures and excellent student outcomes. Improvements among primary schools, Sir Michael notes, are due to a steady focus on foundational teaching skills, such as the use of phonics in reading. Ofsted's national and regional reports further reveal that in 13 local authority areas, fewer than half of all secondary schools meet the 'good' or 'outstanding' standard.

article_content: Numerous parents of autistic children in the United Kingdom report being wrongly accused by educators and social workers of fabricating their children's autism. Jenny Lockley, a single mother from Solihull, experienced this when school staff monitored her after she sought additional help for her son, Sam, who had been professionally diagnosed with autism several times. Despite medical evidence, some educators suspected her of having Münchausen Syndrome by Proxy, a rare disorder where a caregiver invents health issues in those they care for. Lockley learned about the suspicions only after she requested access to council records using the Freedom of Information Act. She was deeply upset to discover that staff at Lady Katherine Leveson Church of England Primary School had held undisclosed meetings about her and watched her while she arrived at the school. She described the ordeal as a 'witch hunt' and shared that she spent considerable sums on private medical assessments and legal representation to secure support for her son. Lucy and Chris Mallows faced similar allegations regarding their daughter Josie's autism. Though Josie's diagnosis was confirmed by a consultant paediatrician, school staff raised doubts, leading to an investigation by social services prompted by rumors. These allegations proved unfounded, but the stress of the situation compelled the family to relocate. Medical professionals and autism advocates have voiced concerns about these occurrences. Carol Povey of the National Autistic Society noted that many families across the country struggle to have autism recognized and to obtain appropriate services, often finding that there is insufficient understanding among local officials. In the wake of ongoing reports, nearly 800 people signed a petition calling for stronger action to prevent baseless accusations from being used as a form of intimidation. Statistics underscore this issue: there are only about 64 suspected MSBP cases annually in Britain, while approximately one in 100 children is believed to be autistic. Solihull Borough Council and Lady Katherine Leveson School have both declined to comment on the cases.

article_content: Following Kevin McCarthy’s historic removal as Speaker of the House, discussions quickly began on who might take his place. Senator Lindsey Graham, a South Carolina Republican and former House member, described the situation as chaotic, noting that such an event has never occurred in over two centuries. He added that people would likely reflect and realize this was not a good decision, but 'it is what it is.' According to NBC News, Virginia Democrat Senator Tim Kaine jokingly reminded Graham that a Speaker does not have to be a House member. Graham declined the notion, saying, 'You’ve got to be sane. And I’m sane enough to say no.' McCarthy had faced longstanding resistance from hardline members in the Freedom Caucus before finally becoming Speaker after 15 voting rounds, having agreed to rules that made it easier for members to seek his removal. On Tuesday, Florida Representative Matt Gaetz, who has often clashed with McCarthy, initiated a motion that resulted in eight Republicans joining 208 Democrats to remove McCarthy. That evening, McCarthy announced he would not seek the speakership again. The next Speaker will face a deeply divided 221-member Republican majority and must address urgent issues such as immigration and government spending.

article_content: For his debut at the New York City Marathon, Stephan Shay ran to honor his older brother, Ryan. The 28-year-old from Huntington Beach, California, achieved an impressive finish: 16th place in 2:19:47. 'The time isn’t what matters most because of the tough conditions, but I’m thrilled with my place,' Stephan said. Almost seven years earlier, Ryan Shay died while racing in the Olympic trials in Central Park. An autopsy showed he suffered cardiac arrest due to an enlarged, scarred heart. As Stephan neared that spot in the race, emotions hit him hard—he had never felt that while running before. 'I got pretty emotional and teary-eyed during the race. For a moment, it was difficult, but I pulled myself together,' he said. His brother Nathan and other family members waited by that significant spot to give support. A bench nearby, dedicated to Ryan, is inscribed with his words: 'It is necessary to dig deep within oneself to discover the hidden grain of steel called will.' Inspired, Stephan surged ahead, passing two more runners to finish as the fourth American. 'Finishing fourth among Americans in such a strong field feels amazing. I would have been pleased just knowing that in advance,' he commented. Although Stephan previously ran a half marathon in New York in 2011, the full marathon proved more demanding. Entering the race back in July, he anticipated the challenge. Unable to be there in person, their father, Joe Shay, expressed how proud he was of Stephan’s performance. Joe recalled finding it emotional when Stephan told him of his plan to run New York. 'He knew it would be hard for me,' Joe shared while holding back tears over the phone. 'I’m proud and grateful for what he’s doing. Maybe next time, we’ll be there to watch. That would bring me a lot of joy.' On race day, Joe attended a service in Ryan’s memory and kept track of Stephan’s race on the marathon’s tracker app. He planned to visit Ryan’s grave later that day. Stephan is now aiming for the 2016 Olympic trials and hopes to compete in the Rio Games. He qualified at the Houston Half Marathon in 2010, finishing in 1:02:26, but subsequently suffered a foot injury that required surgery. After recovering, Stephan decided that if he was going to honor his brother in New York, he would make it count—and he certainly did.

'Pe aravo ndaikatuvéima ramo guarã, umi condición heta vy’apavẽ, pero cheavyiterei gueteri pe lugar rehe,' he’i Stephan. Avy’apáta peteĩpente ikatúrõ aikuaapa haguã aikatu,' he’i. Stephan orekóma experiencia ambue media maratón rehe New York-pe 2011-pe, pe maratón tuichavéva ha ijyvy’ave. article_content: The retrial has started for Kent Easter, a Southern California attorney accused of trying to frame PTA volunteer Kelli Peters by planting drugs in her car. Peters became visibly emotional while testifying, forcing the courtroom to adjourn early for the day. Easter, who faces charges of false imprisonment by fraud or deceit, is currently free on bail after a previous trial ended with a jury deadlocked 11 to 1 in favor of conviction. Prosecutors allege that Easter and his wife, Jill, held a grudge against Peters over an incident involving their son at school. If convicted, Easter could face up to three years in prison, according to ABC News. Authorities say that in February 2011, Easter called 911 and falsely claimed Peters appeared to be using drugs and had hidden them in her car. He is accused of planting prescription painkillers, marijuana, and a marijuana pipe in Peters' vehicle while in frequent contact with his wife by phone. Police responded to the tip and located the drugs. After a lengthy interview with Peters, officers began to suspect foul play when they learned Peters was in class at the reported time of the incident. Peters denied any knowledge of the drugs, and a subsequent search of her home turned up nothing. Kent and Jill Easter were arrested once police determined the drugs found in Peters' car had been planted. Prior to the incident, the Easters had attempted to sue Peters and Jill had tried unsuccessfully to obtain a restraining order against her, claiming Peters was unstable. Prosecutors assert that the Easters disliked Peters because they believed she had not properly supervised their son at school. Their previous lawsuit, stemming from an incident in March 2010 when Peters briefly locked their son out of the school, was dismissed. A surveillance video reportedly shows Kent Easter calling the police from a hotel business center near his office. During the first trial, Easter testified that his wife became obsessed with removing Peters from her school volunteer role. His defense has argued that he only acted to please his wife, whom they claim masterminded the scheme. Jill Easter pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 120 days in jail and 100 hours of community service for her role in the incident. She also writes under the pen name Ava Bjork and published a novel titled 'Holding House,' according to the Los Angeles Times.

article_content: Despite clear evidence confirming Barack Obama's birth in Hawaii on August 4, 1961, doubt about his citizenship persists among some Americans. The so-called 'birther' movement, which claims Obama was born abroad, lingers even after he provided both a standard and long-form birth certificate. Recent polls show that around 25% of Americans—and more than 40% of Republicans—continue to question whether Obama was born in the United States. Obama has addressed the controversy directly, calling the continued debate a distraction. Still, some groups and politicians reject the documents released, fixating on their wording and repeating unverified alternatives. Psychologists suggest that people are often unwilling to change their beliefs even in the face of contrary evidence, especially when those beliefs are tied to political identity. While some analysts think underlying racial biases may fuel persistent doubts about Obama, others say that conspiracy theories in general have long been present in American political life. Although presidential candidates have faced scrutiny over their backgrounds in the past, experts point out that social media and nonstop news coverage have intensified the birther controversy. Many suggest the debate will finally end only when key political leaders from all parties move on.

Pe ‘birther’ movimiento, he’íva Obama heñói hague ambue tetãme, ndojei gueteri, ha’e ome’ẽ rire mokõive certificado, pe común ha avei pe largo, omohechauka hag̃ua. Encuesta ipyahúpe ojehechauka 25%-pe rupi Amerikagua—ha hetave 40% Republicano—ndoikuaái porã Obama heñói hague Estados Unidos-pe. Obama oñe’ẽ mba’epu ári ko apañuãime, he’ívo ko debateha peteĩ distracción. Jepe upéicha, grupo ha político oheja reíva umi documento oñeme’ẽva, oñemohendáva ñe’ẽrã rehe ha ojapo version pyahu ndohechaukái porãva. article_content: Tesla disclosed this week that it is currently the subject of a U.S. Department of Justice investigation covering several matters: executive perks, ties to related parties, personnel decisions, and the accuracy of its vehicles’ driving ranges. This revelation follows a Reuters report that pointed out multiple drivers’ dissatisfaction with their Teslas, saying the vehicles often failed to deliver the range that’s been advertised. Notably, a Model 3 owner reported frequently receiving less than half of the claimed 353-mile range; Tesla later canceled his service appointment after a remote diagnostic suggested the battery was functioning properly. Reuters also reported that Tesla created a so-called 'Diversion Team' tasked with canceling service appointments related to driving range concerns, particularly as such complaints became more widespread. In response, three Tesla owners filed a class-action lawsuit in August, alleging that Tesla misled consumers about its electric cars’ range capabilities. Meanwhile, The Wall Street Journal detailed a separate federal investigation into the possibility of personal benefits improperly provided at Tesla, focusing on a confidential endeavor known as 'Project 42.' This project allegedly involved constructing a glass house for CEO Elon Musk, with both the Department of Justice and the Securities and Exchange Commission examining whether company funds were misdirected for this purpose. Furthermore, these matters have been reviewed internally by Tesla’s board. Tesla stated in a recent report that, to its knowledge, no government agency conducting these ongoing investigations has concluded that any misconduct occurred. The company declined to comment further to Insider.

article_content:
Tyree Landrum, a father of six, was on his way to one of his three jobs during San Diego’s rush hour when he encountered Ferguson protesters blocking the I-5 highway in La Jolla. Concerned that the delay might cause him to lose his job, Landrum exited his car and confronted the group of student protesters. Speaking to an ABC News 10 photographer, he said, 'If I don't get there, I'm going to get fired. I've got six kids to feed.'

Landrum’s reaction, captured on video, quickly went viral on social media and drew support from many viewers. The demonstration was part of nationwide protests following a grand jury’s decision not to indict Darren Wilson, the police officer who fatally shot unarmed teenager Michael Brown in Ferguson.

Hundreds of motorists were delayed, including other frustrated drivers such as nurses heading to work. At one point, Landrum wrestled a bullhorn from a protester who shouted, 'No justice, no peace.' Landrum responded, 'I feel you; we don't have justice either.' A bystander called for arrests, and police and California Highway Patrol officers arrived approximately 30 minutes after the protest began. Authorities determined the demonstration was peaceful, and no arrests were made.

Reflecting on the incident, Landrum said he did not consider himself a hero, but simply an ordinary person acting on impulse. He acknowledged regretting his loss of temper: 'I'm nobody special, just doing what I thought was right.' Landrum's employer reportedly understood the circumstances and did not take disciplinary action for his lateness.

Moved by Landrum's situation, Ryan Fusco, a stranger, launched a YouCaring campaign to support his family by raising funds for Christmas presents for his children. Landrum called the gesture a blessing, while Fusco said Landrum’s dedication to his family inspired him to help.

Oñemondýi ikatu haguére omokangy chupe hembiapo rehe, Landrum osẽ hapegui ha oñe’ẽ umi protestante ndive. He’i ABC News 10-pe: ‘Che ndaguahẽirõ, oheja chéne trabajo-gui. Che niko areko poteĩ mitã rreguakatu hag̃ua.’

Landrum rembiapo ojapo viral social media-pe ha heta tapicha oipytyvõ chupe. Pe protesta ojehu protestas nacional reheve upe grand jury ndaikatúi haguére omombyta Darren Wilson-pe, policía ojuka va’ekue mitãrusu Michael Brown-pe Ferguson-pe.

Cientos de conductores ojedesespera avei, oñembohovái umi ogueruataha hembiapo, ijapu nurse-kuéra umi hospital-guaiteva. Peteĩ jey, Landrum ojopy peteĩ protestantegui bullhorn, he'i: ‘No justice, no peace.’ Landrum ombohovái: ‘Che avei aiko péicha; ore avei ndoguerahéi justicia.’ Kuñakarai ojerure detención rehe, policía ha California Highway Patrol ou 30 aravo’i protesta ñepyrũrã. Autoridades he’i protesta oguata py’aguapyhápe ha noñemohenda avaveténte.

Landrum he’i ojapohague humanoite ha nda’ijavei héro rupi, ha oporandu hague ha ojechauka. ‘Che niko persona comum, ajapo añete che py’a omanda haguéicha.’ Iporã hag̃uáre, patrón ohecháma mba’érepa okúe hague ha ndojapói kárta rehegua.

Ryan Fusco, peteĩ ndoikuaáiva Landrum oipytyvõ hag̃ua, omoñepyrũ peteĩ campaña YouCaring ojupyty hag̃ua ayuda Navidádpe Landrum ha ijfamilia rehehápe. Landrum he’i pa’ũha pe ayuda, ha Fusco he’i Landrum rupi oinspiraha chupe oipytyvõ hag̃ua.

article_content: Hampton, Florida, a small city often labeled the most corrupt in the state, has managed to remain incorporated after lawmakers considered dissolving it. The effort to dissolve the city followed a harsh state audit that revealed city hall accrued hundreds of thousands of dollars in debt and committed 31 violations of the city charter as well as federal laws. This audit occurred only months after the city's mayor was accused of drug-related offenses. The city, with 477 residents, is located in Bradford County between Savannah and Orlando and covers just one square mile. Hampton was given a final opportunity to make changes, which included disbanding its 19-member police force, transferring law enforcement duties to the County Sheriff's office, and requiring all current elected officials to resign. The decision to allow the city to remain came after state officials agreed to implement recommendations from State Representative Charles Van Zant and Senator Rob Bradley, as reported by First Coast News. After a meeting at Victory Church in Hampton, state lawmakers withdrew the bill to dissolve the city. During the efforts to save Hampton, supporters created a Facebook group titled 'Save Our Town of Hampton, Fla.' One post declared, 'Hampton lives!' and another expressed relief at the city's turnaround. Hampton drew public attention for a notorious speed trap on Highway 301. To maximize traffic fines, the city's borders were extended by 1,260 feet along the highway. The city collected over $600,000 in fines between 2010 and 2012, using the funds to build up a police force of 19 officers, an unusually high number for a city with only 477 residents. A state investigation found unclear accounting for much of the revenue. For example, $132,000 was charged to a convenience store using a city account; some employees received $9,000 in excess payments, and $27,000 had been spent on the city credit card without clear justification. The city also faced scrutiny after Mayor Barry Layne Moore was arrested for allegedly selling oxycodone to an undercover officer. He remains in jail, unable to pay a $4,500 bond, and has since resigned. Former mayor Jim Mitzel, who left office two years ago, defended Hampton and questioned why the state could not offer support, comparing the situation to federal bailouts of large corporations. Senator Bradley, whose district includes Hampton, described the situation as resembling a Southern Gothic novel. The audit documented 31 significant violations of state and local laws, ranging from serious misconduct to unusual administrative lapses.

article_content: In 2023, China Hongqiao Group, one of the world’s largest aluminum producers, shut down 1.5 million tons of smelting capacity and relocated it across the country. This shift involved disconnecting from coal-powered electricity and switching to cleaner hydroelectric energy. On its own, this step is projected to reduce carbon emissions from these smelters by 30%.  Such bold business decisions were almost unimaginable only a few years ago. This marks a striking example of a growing trend: businesses taking direct action to combat climate change.  Addressing climate change demands innovative business leadership and mobilization of vast capital—recent estimates indicate $3 to $5 trillion annually is needed over the next decade to support practical solutions that lower emissions, restore ecosystems, and enhance quality of life.  While scientists can diagnose environmental challenges and activists can raise awareness, businesses are uniquely positioned to deliver solutions at scale. This shift is just beginning to take effect.  In the United States, the Inflation Reduction Act is viewed as a landmark in climate legislation, with $370 billion earmarked over ten years for investment in climate solutions. Consequently, a new generation of business leaders is leveraging these incentives to develop better products, services, and companies.  Despite positive movement, business progress on climate remains too slow and often goes unnoticed. Most people are unaware of ongoing transformations in commerce, law, policy, technology, leadership, and science. The phenomenon of 'greenhushing'—where companies stay quiet about climate action to avoid criticism—remains prevalent and more widespread than expected.  Nevertheless, a closer look reveals numerous encouraging examples of business leaders driving progress even in highly polluting sectors like shipping, manufacturing, agriculture, and energy.  To highlight true change-makers, TIME editors and climate experts at TIME CO2 spent months reviewing nominations from across the economy. They prioritized recent, measurable, and scalable achievements, focusing on five key areas: energy, nature, finance, culture, and health.  Ultimately, the first TIME100 Climate list found no single example of perfect climate action, but it did uncover many individuals making significant strides in tackling climate change by creating real business value. These leaders were invited to share their perspectives, with the hope that their stories will inspire others to take similar action.

article_content: Thousands of people with advanced kidney cancer in England and Wales are being denied access to a new treatment, Axitinib, that doctors say could prolong patients' lives. Studies show Axitinib adds about two months to the lifespan of people with advanced cases. However, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has decided not to recommend Axitinib for NHS funding, citing its high monthly cost of around £3,000. This decision follows NICE's rejection of other drugs, such as everolimus, for those whose cancer worsens after initial treatments. Professor Tom Powles of Barts Health NHS Trust criticized the move, arguing that restricting access to newer therapies limits survival benefits and could lead to less efficient use of NHS resources. Powles pointed out that improved drug treatment has more than doubled average survival for advanced kidney cancer patients over recent years. Axitinib, known by the brand name Inlyta, targets molecules that encourage blood vessel formation in tumors, cutting off their supply of oxygen and nutrients. About 9,000 UK residents are diagnosed with kidney cancer annually, and many only find out after it’s spread, since symptoms are often absent early on. Nearly two-thirds of eligible patients could benefit from Axitinib if other treatments fail. James Whale, a broadcaster, kidney cancer survivor, and chair of the James Whale Fund for Kidney Cancer, called NICE's draft decision unacceptable. Dr. David Montgomery, Medical Director for Pfizer Oncology UK (Axitinib’s manufacturer), also expressed disappointment, saying Pfizer has worked to prove Axitinib’s value and cost-effectiveness. He confirmed that Pfizer would continue to contest the decision for the sake of patients. NICE maintains that Axitinib offers only a limited improvement in survival compared to its cost and, for now, is not endorsing the drug for NHS funding.

article_content: Clive Turner, a 73-year-old from Rossett, North Wales, died at home following a fatal haemorrhage in his digestive tract, just hours after being released from hospital with a diagnosis of constipation. Mr. Turner waited five and a half hours for an ambulance and another two hours at Wrexham Maelor Hospital before being seen. He was evaluated by Dr. Tatiana Rooney, who diagnosed constipation after tests showed no bowel blockage, and discharged him the next morning. After returning home, Mr. Turner died. A post-mortem found a gastrointestinal haemorrhage due to ischaemic bowel from atherosclerosis, not constipation. Coroner John Gittins determined the diagnosis was incorrect and highlighted concerns over delays in emergency care. He referred to a 2013 case with similar issues, stating that any death caused by such delays is unacceptable. Gittins stated he will seek detailed reports from the Welsh Ambulance NHS Trust and Betsi Cadwaladr Health Board about how they are tackling these problems. He will also file a report on how pain relief and discharge safety are assessed. A spokesperson from Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board offered condolences to Mr. Turner’s family, accepted the coroner’s findings, and committed to working with ambulance services to minimize delays in emergency departments.

article_content: Since the 1990s, Ebola has devastated Africa’s great apes, with current estimates indicating that a third of the world’s gorillas and chimpanzees have died from the virus. While media coverage has mainly focused on human victims, the Ebola crisis also poses a critical threat to our closest relatives: gorillas and chimpanzees. For these apes, Ebola is currently the gravest threat to their survival. The fatality rate of Ebola among great apes is alarmingly high, killing about 95% of infected gorillas and 77% of chimpanzees. Many ape deaths occur in epidemics, similar to humans. In 1995, an outbreak reportedly killed over 90% of gorillas in Minkébé Park, northern Gabon. In 2002-2003, a single event of the Zaire strain of Ebola (ZEBOV) in the Democratic Republic of Congo killed an estimated 5,000 Western gorillas. The World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) estimates that up to 100,000 gorillas remain in the wild, so outbreaks can have devastating impacts on their populations. Other serious challenges facing Africa’s great apes include illegal wildlife trade, hunting for bushmeat, war, habitat loss due to deforestation, and other diseases. As their living spaces shrink, remaining wild apes are pushed into isolated forest patches, limiting their ability to find food, breed, or evade hunters. There is increasing evidence that deforestation and the resulting climate changes fuel the spread of Ebola and other diseases. A 2003 study led by primatologist Peter Walsh warned that, without significant investment in law enforcement, protected area management, and Ebola prevention, the next decade could push these species to the edge of extinction—a prediction that appears to have come true. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) has listed the Eastern Gorilla as 'endangered' and the Western Gorilla as 'critically endangered' since 2008. Without swift action, these may be the last decades that apes survive in their natural habitats. However, there seems to be a lack of political will to enact effective solutions. Both short-term interventions to stop Ebola's spread and long-term prevention strategies are needed. For immediate response, vaccination may be effective. A safe and effective Ebola vaccine has been developed for apes, unlike for humans; although, vaccinated chimps have not yet been exposed to live virus in trials. In much of Europe, medical research involving great apes is either limited or banned due to their high cognitive abilities, raising ethical debates about exceptions for such urgent cases. On a long-term scale, restoring larger stretches of forest could decrease virus transmission risks by reducing contact among infected animals. Alongside forest regeneration, increasing protection from hunters and enforcing strict laws against bushmeat trade would greatly benefit both apes and humans. Additionally, new studies by researchers from the University of St Andrews and Heriot-Watt University have shown that chimpanzees, like human children, can learn kindness and altruism by observing others—suggesting deep evolutionary roots for compassion.

article_content: Nick Clegg advanced his flagship policy to provide free school meals to all infant pupils, despite warnings that the cost could necessitate cuts to teaching and learning budgets, according to emails revealed yesterday. The Deputy Prime Minister implemented the pledge in the face of opposition from Education Secretary Michael Gove. While Clegg and the Liberal Democrats asserted that the scheme was fully funded, leaked emails suggested officials were aware that this was not the case. These revelations prompted a former aide to Mr. Gove to accuse Clegg of misleading the public about the true cost and impact of the policy. The correspondence, disclosed after being leaked to BBC Radio 4’s World at One, shows concern among officials that the funding shortfall might force schools to divert money from other priorities, such as maintaining buildings or providing enough school places. The leaked documents included a letter from Mr. Gove to Danny Alexander, Chief Secretary to the Treasury, stating the policy would cost more than £1.1 billion over two years. Gove requested assurance that his budget would be increased accordingly, as he could not cover the shortfall internally. Shortly thereafter, Clegg announced an additional £150 million in funding, partly sourced from unspent Department for Education maintenance funds. However, a senior civil servant at the DfE emailed Clegg, Laws, and Chancellor Osborne, noting that the amount was less than the £200 million believed necessary and warning that essential resources could be diverted away from school maintenance and capacity. Another email to Treasury civil servants warned that it would be misleading to claim the extra funds could be met without impacting other education capital budgets. Dominic Cummings, former special adviser to Gove, told the BBC that Clegg was misrepresenting the funding to advance his own interests, while Gove was trying to protect taxpayer money. In response, Lib Dem deputy leader Sir Malcolm Bruce accused Conservative opponents of leaking information for political reasons, stating Gove had already approved and supported the policy. Education minister David Laws emphasized that the funding package had government-wide agreement and included sufficient revenue and capital allocations to ensure schools would not have to subsidize free meals through teaching budgets or by reducing funds for maintenance.

Pe marandu oñemboguejyva'e oikuaauka pe ko'ã mba'e ha'eha Michael Gove omondova'ekue kuatia Dani Alexander-pe (Chief Secretary to the Treasury), he'ívo tembiapo osẽtaha £1.1 billón mokõi arýpe. Gove ojerureha oñemohendava ipresupuesto ohepyme'ẽ hag̃ua, ha'e ndaikatúi haguére oiporavo viru ipype. Peteĩ semana rire, Clegg he'i ojuhuha £150 millón oñemyanyhẽ hag̃ua ko tembiapo haguã, peteî parte ve oúva Departamento de Educación-gui. Peteĩ mburuvicha guasu oiméva DfE pe, omondo e-mail Clegg, Laws ha Ministro Osborne peve, he'ívo ko monto michĩve £200 millón tekotevẽvagui, haumpyhare ikatuha oiko tapykuehópe viru oñemomba'e'ỹramo mba'e rehegua. Avei, peteĩ e-mail Treasury mba'apohára pegua oavisa hague ikatuha oiko oje'éva viru avei oñembohasa reiha, ha añetehápe ndoikuaaséiha mba'e rehe. Dominic Cummings, Gove remianduha, he'i BBC-pe Nick Clegg ojapo hague oikotevẽ'ỹháicha viru rehe, ha Gove otryrã omomba'apo tavayguápe. Ambue hendápe, Lib Dem tendota Sir Malcolm Bruce omoañete ikatuha Conservative-kuéra oipe'a hague marandu tee hikuái politikarehe, he'i avei Gove omoañetehague oñemog̃uahẽvo tembiapo. Ministro David Laws he'i upejave marandu oñemohendáva gobierno reheve ha ohechauka opa mba'e viru oñemohendaha ndokotyeséiha tembiapo rehegui térã mba'e rehegua.

article_content: Jared Golden, a Democratic representative and Marine Corps veteran from Lewiston, Maine, declared Thursday that he now supports a federal ban on assault-style weapons. This marks a reversal of his earlier position following a mass shooting in his community. During a press conference with Maine officials, Golden acknowledged, 'I have resisted efforts to ban dangerous firearms like the assault rifle involved in this tragedy. It’s time I take responsibility for that stance.' He urged Congress to enact legislation prohibiting these weapons. Golden had previously voted against a federal ban proposal in 2022—though it passed the House, it was not signed into law. According to the Associated Press, he stated last year he did not support any version of the ban. A previous federal ban on assault weapons was implemented in the 1990s and expired after ten years. The current political landscape features strong disagreement, with Democrats advocating for stricter gun laws in response to mass shootings, while Republicans often emphasize mental health solutions and express skepticism about the effectiveness of bans. Senator Susan Collins, a moderate Republican from Maine, expressed support for restricting high-capacity ammunition magazines but maintained her opposition to banning assault rifles. The Lewiston shooting left at least 18 dead and 13 injured on Wednesday night. Robert Card, a 40-year-old former Army reservist, has been identified as the suspect and remains at large, according to Governor Janet Mills.

Ko cambio oikókuri ojapo rire peteĩ tiroteo tuicháva oñemohenda ipehẽnguepe. Aty guasu oiko jave ambue autoridad-kuérape, Golden ohechakuaa: ‘Che nambi peve añemoĩ hague armas peligrosas rehe, ojepuru va’ekue ko tragedia-pe. Ko’ág̃a akyhyje ha hape añemuña che rembiapo. Ojerure Congreso-pe ojapo léi oheja’ỹva ko’ã armas.’ Golden he’i ojehechauka hague oñemoĩhague veto rehe armas de asalto rehegua 2022-pe—Congreso-pe oñemoneĩmba jepi, ha katu nomba’apo léina. Senadora Susan Collins, peteĩ moderada republicana Maine-gua, ohechauka oipota ojejoko magazines grandes rehe, ha katu ndoipotáikatu veto armas de asalto rehe. Tiroteo Lewiston-pe omopu’ã 18 omanóva ha 13 hasýva, ára miércoles pyhare. Robert Card, peteĩ ex-reservista ejército, 40 ary, oñemohendáva sospechoso ramo, gueteri ndojuhúi, Janet Mills Gobernadora he’i.

article_content: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has postponed a hearing concerning Laurent Gbagbo, the former president of Ivory Coast who is facing charges of crimes against humanity. The critical hearing to confirm charges, originally planned for Monday, has now been rescheduled to August 13, according to the ICC. Gbagbo’s lawyers requested more time to prepare his defense, resulting in the delay. This hearing gives both sides an opportunity to present their arguments regarding whether enough evidence exists to proceed to trial. The charges relate to the 2010 post-election crisis. After losing to Alassane Ouattara, Gbagbo refused to give up power, leading to months of violent clashes between the two camps and thousands of deaths. Gbagbo is accused of responsibility for actions carried out by his supporters, though he denies wrongdoing. The ICC announced that Gbagbo allegedly shares responsibility, as an indirect co-perpetrator, for four types of crimes against humanity: murder, rape and other sexual violence, persecution, and other inhuman acts. These acts reportedly occurred from December 2010 through April 2011. Gbagbo was arrested in April last year, putting an end to the standoff, and was brought to The Hague in November, where the ICC is based. Human rights groups have reported that both sides’ followers committed serious crimes during the conflict.

Ko audiencia iñimportantevéva, oiko va’erã kuri lunes-pe, oñemomombyry jasypoapy 13-pe, ICC he’i. Gbagbo rembiporavopyre ojerureve aravo oñembosako’ivohaguã hembiapo rehe, upéva rupi oñemomombyry audiencia. article_content: A painting once purchased on eBay for £3,000 eight years ago has been authenticated as the work of famed French Impressionist Edouard Vuillard and may now be valued at £250,000. This unexpected discovery was made by experts on the BBC’s 'Fake or Fortune?' program, who are searching for the buyer to deliver the good news. Art dealer Robert Warren, who formerly owned both pieces in a pair, sold one at auction to writer Keith Tutt and the second on eBay, though he cannot recall the online purchaser. The eBay painting, notable for its large four-foot oval frame depicting a couple sharing oysters and champagne, is now believed to be a genuine Vuillard. Presenters Fiona Bruce and Philip Mould explained that the attribution was confirmed through a combination of forensic science, historical research, and material analysis. Vuillard’s works have attained high market values in the past, with 'Les Couturieres' selling for over £5 million at Christie’s in 2009. The recently rediscovered artworks could each command around £250,000. The show has previously identified other long-lost masterpieces, including a Van Gogh in Norway and a King Henry VIII portrait whose value rose dramatically after experts dated it using dendrochronology.

Ko mba'e oikuaa ndaha'éiva ojeha'arõ BBC 'Fake or Fortune?' apopyvusúpe, ha oñeha'ãhína ojuhu upe ojoguáva ta'anga rehegua oikuaa hag̃ua ko maravilla. Ko programa oikuaa avei ambue tesorokuéra, oikuaahápe Van Gogh rembiapo Noruega-pe ha Henry VIII retrato oñemyatyrõ rire ijvale umi mba'ekuaahára dendrocronología rupive.

article_content: Motilal Oswal Financial Services, a leading financial firm in India, has introduced a novel 'switch-off' policy to enhance employee wellness and productivity. Group Chief HR Officer Niren Srivastava stated the policy covers about 9,500 out of 11,000 employees, focusing on those at senior manager level and below. This initiative requires employees to disconnect from work and emails beyond their standard 8.0 to 8.5-hour shift. After a 45-minute grace period post-shift, email servers will be shut down, blocking internal and external communications. Employees staying beyond their shift and grace period will be asked to leave the office. Top executives and teams in private equity, asset & wealth management, and investment banking are exempt due to their specific responsibilities. The Admin and HR departments will enforce compliance across all offices. CEO Motilal Oswal emphasized that the policy prioritizes employee satisfaction, mental health, and productivity over mere hours spent at work. 'Our focus is well-being first,' he affirmed. Future plans include restricting access to business-specific applications during 'switch-off' hours, adjusted for job roles and operational needs. HR is informing managers about the policy, and mechanisms exist to receive feedback or concerns. In other corporate news: Tata Group has acquired Wistron's manufacturing facility for $750 million, making it the first Indian firm to assemble iPhones. India has surpassed China in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2024 for the most represented universities. Independent board members at Religare Enterprises have raised objections to a proposed acquisition by the Burman family, citing fraud allegations.

article_content: Gamal and Alaa Mubarak, sons of former Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, appeared in a Cairo criminal court on Monday facing charges of insider stock trading. Prosecutors allege the brothers illegally earned millions by using confidential information related to the 2007 sale of Al Watany Bank of Egypt. The Mubarak brothers are on trial with seven others, including deputy chief executives of the bank. Prosecutors claim all defendants conspired to acquire illicit funds and control 80% of the bank's shares. According to the prosecution, Gamal Mubarak gained nearly 500 million Egyptian pounds (about $82 million), while Alaa Mubarak reportedly earned 12 million pounds (about $1.9 million) through the use of insider information. Prosecutors stated the two 'intentionally withheld vital information on the bank sale from other shareholders to carry out their crime, thus violating transparency and fairness.' They are also accused of selling shares to strategic partners at EFG Hermes. EFG Hermes joint CEOs Yasser El-Malawny and Hassan Heikal are among the co-defendants. After Monday’s session, the trial was postponed to September 8. The court denied the Mubarak brothers' bail request, even though the other defendants were released on bail but remain subject to a travel ban. The court kept the travel ban for all nine defendants. All the accused, including Gamal and Alaa Mubarak, deny the charges. In court, Gamal stated, 'There is no basis whatsoever to these accusations,' while Alaa said, 'Unfortunately, these are all lies. None of this happened.' The Mubarak brothers have been in prison since spring 2011 and were acquitted of corruption charges in another case last month. EFG Hermes, a major investment company in the Middle East, has offices in nine Arab countries. In May, Hermes stated its two executives acted properly during the Al Watany bank acquisition. The National Bank of Kuwait obtained nearly 100% of Al Watany Bank in November 2007. Hermes also said its CEOs had no personal interest, gains, or involvement in trading Al Watany Bank shares and that the company has taken legal actions to defend them. The bank's deputy chief executives are accused of earning concealed percentages and conducting hidden deals without informing the stock exchange authority, allegedly breaching Egyptian Central Bank and securities laws. Last month, Gamal and Alaa Mubarak reportedly offered to pay a 2 billion-pound ($330 million) settlement, but prosecutors refused. Prosecution spokesman Adel Al-Saeed said, 'The prosecutors insisted they admit guilt first, and required all defendants to participate in the reconciliation.' Only one other defendant offered payment. Hosni Mubarak, president of Egypt for over 30 years, was removed from office by Arab Spring protests and later convicted for complicity in the deaths of anti-government demonstrators. The 84-year-old is reportedly in worsening health and was recently moved to a military hospital.

article_content: As North Korea began the trial for American journalists Laura Ling and Euna Lee, former Japanese reporter Takashi Sugishima, once held in a North Korean prison for two years, shared his harrowing story. Arrested during a trip to Pyongyang in 1999, Sugishima faced unsubstantiated spying charges; neither he nor the Japanese and South Korean governments acknowledged the accusations. Sugishima endured constant anxiety in prison, never knowing when the guards might turn hostile. According to Reporters Without Borders, Ling and Lee are the first foreign reporters since Sugishima to be detained for such a lengthy period in North Korea. The two Current TV journalists were arrested in March while covering the plight of North Korean defectors near the China border. They are accused of illegal entry, espionage, and 'hostile acts' and could receive long sentences in labor camps. Sugishima feels North Korea is once again using detainees as diplomatic leverage, a tactic analysts say was likely used in his own case. He credits his 2002 release to the advocacy of his family and Japanese officials, though others believe he was a pawn in political negotiations. Contact with Ling and Lee has been limited to visits from the Swedish ambassador, since diplomatic ties between the U.S. and North Korea do not exist. Their families report that both women are terrified and isolated. Lisa Ling, Laura's sister, made a public appeal to North Korean leaders for the journalists' freedom, insisting the pair never meant to break any laws.

Sugishima ojejagarra Pyongyang-pe 1999-pe, ha oñemohenda hese ijojaha'ỹva acusación de espionaje; ni ha'e ni Japón ha Corea Sur ndogueroviaséi upéva. Sugishima ohasa kuri heta kyhyje ka'irãme, ndokuaái araka'épa umi guardia ikatu oikoa hese. Reporters Without Borders he'i Ling ha Lee ha'eha tapicha ambuéva peteĩha oñeñongatuetevo hetápe Norcorea-pe Sugishima rire. Mokõi Current TV periodista ojejagarra kuri jasyapy-pe ha'e kuéra oike ha peteĩ informe ojapo hína China ha Norcorea rembe'ýre, oñemomba'e umi peteĩha pytyvõ rehe. Oje'acusa chupekuéra oike rei haguére, espía ha avei 'mba'e vai' rehe, ha ikatu hikuái ohasa heta áño tembiaporã ka'irãme. Sugishima he'i Norcorea oipuruporãha ko'ã tapicha oñeñe'ẽ hag̃ua avei tetã ambuéva ndive, analista-kuéra he'i upéva ojapo hague avei hese. Ohechakuaa hague osẽ hague oñemomba'e haguére ijogapegua ha gobierno japón-ygua, ha katu oĩ he'íva avei ojeporúva hague peteĩ mba'e ojejapo hag̃ua diplomátiko-pe. Ling ha Lee ndaikatuvéima oguerekóvo comunicación añetegua, embaxadór suéco rupi umi visita, oiko rupi Estados Unidos ha Norcorea ndorekói relación diplomática.
