article_content: According to a new study, commuters on the 10 most congested highways in the U.S. might travel faster by bicycle than by car. Researchers used GPS-equipped vehicles to analyze over 100 million records from taxis, shuttles, delivery vans, trucks, and passenger cars in 2011. A 13-mile segment of the San Diego Freeway (I-405) near Los Angeles ranked as the country’s most congested, but drivers in Honolulu spent the most time in traffic, averaging 58 hours per year. The study found that urban traffic congestion nationwide declined significantly for the first time since 2008. In 70 of the top 100 largest U.S. cities, congestion decreased last year. The study, commissioned by INRIX, a traffic-data company from Kirkland, WA, linked the decline to factors such as slow employment growth and higher fuel prices, causing fewer people to commute and overall less driving. Last year, only 890,000 of the 2.6 million new jobs were in urban areas. However, job growth in cities like Tampa, Houston, and Austin led to more traffic on their roads. Eight of the 10 worst highway segments for delays are located in New York or Los Angeles. On average, Americans spent around 40 hours annually stuck in bottleneck traffic. Fridays offer both the best (6–7am) and worst (5–6pm) commute times, while Tuesday mornings are considered the worst for travel. According to Jim Bak of INRIX, Mondays tend to be better because of late arrivals or three-day weekends. The 10 worst cities for commute times and their peak congestion intervals are: — Honolulu: 58 hours; 5:15–5:30pm Tuesday — Los Angeles: 56 hours; 5:45–6pm Thursday — San Francisco: 48 hours; 5:45–6pm Thursday — New York: 57 hours; 5:30–5:45pm Friday — Bridgeport, CT: 42 hours; 5:30–5:45pm Friday — Washington, D.C.: 45 hours; 5:45–6pm Thursday — Seattle: 33 hours; 5:30–5:45pm Thursday — Austin, TX: 30 hours; 5:30–5:45pm Thursday — Boston: 35 hours; 5:30–5:45pm Thursday — Chicago: 36 hours; 5:30–5:45pm Thursday The 10 worst U.S. highway segments for daily commuting in 2011 were: 1. Los Angeles: 13 miles of I-405 N, from I-105 to Getty Center Dr. (33 min avg., 20 min delay) 2. New York: 16 miles of I-495 E, from Maurice Ave to Minneola Ave/Willis Ave (39 min, 22 min delay) 3. Los Angeles: 15 miles of I-10 E, from CA-1 to Alameda St. (35 min, 20 min delay) 4. New York: 3 miles of I-678 N, from Belt Pkwy to Main St. (13 min, 10 min delay) 5. Pittsburgh: 3 miles of I-376 E, from Lydia St. to US-19/PA-51 Exit (13 min, 9 min delay in morning peak) 10. San Francisco: 11 miles of California Delta Hwy, from Bailey Rd. to Somersville Rd. article_content: At the 2023 Cricket World Cup final in Ahmedabad, a breathtaking drone light show dazzled viewers both in the stadium and watching remotely. This elaborate presentation featured 1,200 drones, all managed by Botlab Dynamics, an IIT Delhi-incubated startup. According to Sarita Ahlawat, Botlab’s cofounder and managing director, a 35-member team dedicated a full month to planning, with significant time spent on in-stadium rehearsals. Botlab's innovative swarm technology allows multiple drones to coordinate autonomously, enabling visually impressive aerial performances. While entertainment remains their primary revenue stream, Botlab is also leveraging its technology for defense applications, such as drone-based surveillance, disaster relief, and efficient payload delivery. The company has already executed major events, including large drone shows at the Indian Premier League and a record-setting 3,500-drone performance at Rashtrapati Bhavan. The company is now developing new drones for the Indian Armed Forces and will soon supply 10 units of autonomous survey drones through a government-backed initiative designed to promote defense self-reliance. Botlab also seeks to increase its drone fleet from 5,000 to 10,000 by March-April, introduce consumer drones for special occasions, and potentially stage a 6,000-drone event to set a global record. With international competition from firms in China and Russia, Botlab remains unique in India by designing and manufacturing all key drone components locally and having user-friendly controls via mobile devices, removing the need for trained pilots. Established in 2016, Botlab began with defense and disaster-management drones before shifting focus to entertainment, enabling them to self-fund research and adapt quickly to new opportunities. Their business has almost doubled in the last year, and after securing additional investment, total funding will reach ₹40 crore. Botlab’s short-term objective is to expand into African and West Asian markets, highlighting that Indian engineering has global potential in both hardware and software sectors.

article_content: Three crew members of a U.S. Navy helicopter died after their aircraft crashed in the waters off San Diego, California, according to Navy spokeswoman Karin Burzynski. Rescue teams are still searching for two other crew members who remain missing after the helicopter went down late Tuesday night. The helicopter was operating from the USS Nimitz, and the Navy received notification of the crash around 11:30 p.m. The incident occurred approximately 20 miles off the Mexican coast. Coast Guard spokesman Henry Dunphy stated that Coast Guard helicopters and boats, as well as vessels from other agencies, are participating in the ongoing search efforts.

article_content: A swimmer in his 40s lost his life after being attacked by a large great white shark roughly 200 meters off the coast of Muriwai Beach, just west of Auckland, New Zealand. The incident took place during a sunny afternoon as beachgoers enjoyed the weather. Nearby fisherman Pio Mose witnessed significant blood in the water and thought additional sharks might have joined after the initial attack. Emergency services, including police, lifeguards, and the Westpac Rescue Helicopter, responded quickly. Officers shot at the shark when it stayed near the victim, after which it disappeared. After the attack, authorities shut down Muriwai Beach and surrounding beaches, expecting closures to continue for several days. The New Zealand Department of Conservation highlighted that deaths from shark attacks are exceptionally rare in the country, with fewer than 20 recorded in over 175 years, compared to the approximately 25 shark-related deaths worldwide each year. The event led to a wave of sympathy and concern on social media, and users like Aaron Jeavons commented that they were now hesitant to swim at the affected beaches.

article_content: The controversy known as 'Deflate-gate' has dominated sports discussions leading up to the Super Bowl on Sunday, with New England Patriots quarterback Tom Brady saying that the football tampering allegations have affected him personally. The NFL discovered that 11 out of 12 footballs used by the Patriots offense during the AFC Championship game were under-inflated by about two PSI below league standards. Speaking with WEEI sports radio in Boston, Brady again denied any involvement with the footballs being under-inflated, stating that the speculation has hurt his feelings. Brady appeared on Monday at a send-off ceremony for the team, standing alongside owner Robert Kraft and head coach Bill Belichick as they prepared to head to Phoenix for the Super Bowl. He commented, 'I’ve tried to wrap my head around it. I personalized a lot of things and thought this was all about me, and my feelings got hurt. Then I moved past it, because it’s not serving me.' The Patriots continue to deal with accusations of cheating less than a week before facing the Seattle Seahawks in the Super Bowl. Head coach Bill Belichick, previously involved in another controversy, denies any wrongdoing. Critics allege that Patriots owner Robert Kraft’s close relationship with NFL commissioner Roger Goodell could influence the outcome. Seattle Seahawks cornerback Richard Sherman has expressed doubts that the Patriots will face penalties, suggesting Kraft’s connection with Goodell represents a conflict of interest. Brady told WEEI that he has moved past the speculation and is focusing on the upcoming Super Bowl, his sixth appearance with the Patriots. On Sunday, he told ESPN he has not been contacted by NFL investigators and does not expect to hear from them until after the game. The initial complaint came from the Indianapolis Colts after their loss in the AFC Championship game on January 18. Under-inflated footballs may provide advantages such as being easier to throw, catch, and hold in poor weather conditions. Statistical analyst Warren Sharp has observed that the Patriots have a remarkably low fumble rate, statistically significant given the number of plays run.

article_content: Singapore is enhancing digital payments for both shoppers and retailers with SGQR+, an improved payment system that enables merchants to accept 23 payment types through a single sign-up with their bank or payment provider. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) began a month-long trial of SGQR+ on November 1, involving over 1,000 merchants in neighborhoods such as Loyang, Bedok, Upper East Coast, and Changi—including Jewel Changi Airport. This system allows customers to pay by scanning a single QR code, streamlining checkout. Additionally, SGQR+ will be tested by merchants at the Singapore FinTech Festival, happening at the Singapore Expo from November 15 to 17. The new system is intended to make digital transactions easier and more convenient nationwide.

article_content: Searchlight Pictures and L.A. Times Studios have joined forces to present 'The Last Repair Shop,' an acclaimed documentary short that recently earned two nominations from the Critics Choice Association and a spot on DOC NYC’s Short List, following its premiere at Telluride. The film, directed by Oscar- and Grammy-nominated, Emmy-winning filmmaker and musician Kris Bowers alongside Oscar winner Ben Proudfoot, is being positioned for further awards consideration. It will be available to stream for free worldwide starting November 8 on the L.A. Times’ YouTube channel and at latimes.com. "We’ve found something truly special with 'The Last Repair Shop,'” said Searchlight Pictures Presidents David Greenbaum and Matthew Greenfield. “This is exactly the kind of story we need right now, and we're proud to highlight these remarkable personal journeys." Leslie Lindsey, director of development for L.A. Times Studios and supervising producer of L.A. Times Short Docs, added, "We're excited to release 'The Last Repair Shop' as part of our Short Docs series. Ben Proudfoot and Kris Bowers are masterful storytellers who have beautifully captured the dedication of those ensuring city students have access to musical instruments. We can’t wait for audiences to discover it." While providing and repairing musical instruments free of charge to public schoolchildren was once widespread across the United States, Los Angeles is now one of the last—and by far the largest—cities to continue this tradition, which has lasted since 1959. 'The Last Repair Shop,' by the team behind the Oscar-nominated short 'A Concerto Is a Conversation,' offers an inside look at a modest downtown warehouse where a devoted group of craftspeople keep over 80,000 student instruments in working order. The film introduces viewers to general manager Steve Bagmanyan and technicians from each department, including Dana Atkinson from the strings division, Paty Moreno who oversees brass and is the only woman in the shop, and Duane Michaels, who cares for woodwinds. Their personal stories—ranging from Atkinson’s journey toward self-acceptance, Moreno’s experience as a Mexican immigrant and single mother, to Michaels’ colorful life as a musician—highlight the human side of this invaluable service. Steve, originally from Azerbaijan, shares how he came to the US and learned his craft after escaping ethnic persecution in the late 1980s. Bowers, an LAUSD alumnus, shared: “Discovering that Steve, a central figure in the film, tuned the very pianos I learned on as a child was incredible. Making this film became a heartfelt tribute to the unsung heroes who provided me and countless others with the gift of music. I truly owe my career to people like the four repair specialists featured in our story.” Proudfoot added: “Every child deserves the opportunity to play music. Music isn’t just a valuable discipline or a potential career—it can also be a source of healing that brings out the best in us. 'The Last Repair Shop' is a celebration of that spirit and a tribute to a unique program that has helped nurture talents from John Williams to Kendrick Lamar.” A national impact campaign will accompany the film’s release to spotlight LAUSD’s one-of-a-kind music repair program as a model for other cities. Produced by Breakwater Studios, 'The Last Repair Shop' features executive producers Jane Solomon, Peter Rotter, Ben Proudfoot, Kris Bowers, and Briana Henry. Proudfoot and Bowers also produced with Jeremy Lambert and Josh Rosenberg, while Bowers collaborated with composer Katya Richardson on the original score. Executive production for L.A. Times Studios was provided by Sharon Matthews, Terry Tang, Jason Spingarn-Koff, and Leslie Lindsey, with Shani Hilton and Nani Walker as co-executive producers, Karen Foshay as senior publishing producer, and Jessica Q. Chen as associate producer. Negotiations for the deal were managed by Paul Hoffman and Chan Phung for Searchlight Pictures and Sam Widdoes for Breakwater Studios.

Pe película, omoakãva Kris Bowers (Oscar ha Grammy nomba'eguasúi, Emmy pu'akapyréva) ha Ben Proudfoot (Oscar ipuhegua), ojeruréháicha heta jehecharamo. Times YouTube ha latimes.com-pe. “Roikuaa peteî mba'e jakurusu'ỹva 'The Last Repair Shop' rehe,” he'i Searchlight Pictures presidente David Greenbaum ha Matthew Greenfield. “Ko'ãichagua mombe’u tekotevẽ ñande rehehápe, ha romomba'e umi tapei personal tenondeve.” Leslie Lindsey, L.A. Times Studios-pe desarrollo rerekua ha L.A. Times Short Docs omoakãva, he’i avei: “Roipotaite ojehecha 'The Last Repair Shop' peteĩ tapenumeguáicha. Ben Proudfoot ha Kris Bowers mbarete omombe'u ko tembiapo ichupekuéra oguerojera umi tapicha omba'apóva mitãrusu-kuérape instrumento rehe. Naiñambyhyiete roha'arõta maymáva ohechaha.” Oi peichaháicha, Estados Unidos-pe oikova’ekue instrumento musical ome'ẽ ha omyengovia rei mitãrehe escuela pública-pe, Los Angeles oguerekóva upe tapicha guasu ha ipyahúva omyengoviáva ko tembiapo 1959 guive. 'The Last Repair Shop', A Concerto Is a Conversation ndive avei, ome'ẽ peteî jehechaha peteĩ oguatáva galpón-pe, upe rupi tapicha mbarete oñangareko omohenda 80,000 instrumento mitãrehe. Pe película ombojopyru Steve Bagmanyan (gerente) rehe, ha técnico kuéra: Dana Atkinson (cuerdas rehe), Paty Moreno (brass rehe, peteĩnte kuña, inmigrante méxicano ha isymi), ha Duane Michaels (woodwind rehe oguerekóva). Ha'ekuéra rembiapo personal—Atkinson ijehegui he'i, Moreno (Mekihagua) rembiasa ha isymi, Michaels rehe mba'e musicista—oikuaauka mba’etépa tembiapo. Steve Azerbaijan-gui, he'i mba’etépa ou Estados Unidos-pe, hasy asy rire persecución étnica 1980 década-pe. Bowers (LAUSD rehegua), he’i: “Aikuaávo Steve (película-pe principal) ombotopáva piano escuela-gua che rehegua, ha'e hína maravilla. Película hína peteî aguyje umi karai katuete nomba’eguasúiva ome'ẽva chéve ha hetaiterei mitãme música rupi. Che rembiapo avei aikuaa umi irundy repair rehegua.” Proudfoot he’i: “Mitãnte ojejapyhýta oportunidad ombopu hag̃ua música. Música ha’e peteî mba'e tee ha ikatúva tembiapo iporãva, avei katu ha'e omboguapy ñande pohýi ha ohechauka ñandeko. 'The Last Repair Shop' omomba’e ko espíritu ha omomba’e peteî programa ojapo heta tapicha yvotyha guasu, John Williams guive Kendrick Lamar peve.” Omoirũta avei peteî campaña nacional omyesakã hag̃ua programa LAUSD, modelo ojehecha hag̃ua ambue távape. Breakwater Studios rehe oî productor ejecutivos: Jane Solomon, Peter Rotter, Ben Proudfoot, Kris Bowers, Briana Henry. Proudfoot ha Bowers avei ojepytaso producción-pe Jeremy Lambert ha Josh Rosenberg ndive, ha Bowers omba’apo Katya Richardson ndive pe música original rehe. L.A. Times Studios-pe Sharon Matthews, Terry Tang, Jason Spingarn-Koff ha Leslie Lindsey exec producen, ha Shani Hilton ha Nani Walker coproductor exec, Karen Foshay prod. senior ha Jessica Q. Chen prod. asociado. Paul Hoffman ha Chan Phung ojapo kuri negociación Searchlight Pictures-gui, ha Sam Widdoes Breakwater Studios-gui.

article_content: Police Scotland's chief constable, Jo Farrell, has apologized after a police officer drove her home to England when her train was cancelled. Farrell was driven about 120 miles from Edinburgh to Northumberland on 20 October, during Storm Babet. She had taken on the position of Scotland's top police officer just 11 days earlier, after previously serving as chief constable of Durham Constabulary. Ms. Farrell issued a statement expressing regret for her 'error of judgement,' explaining that she requested her office arrange a car to take her home after train services were cancelled and her own police vehicle was unavailable. She stated, 'I have apologized for this error of judgement.' A civilian worker from Durham Constabulary was also a passenger in the police car and was dropped off 15 miles further south, in Gateshead. A Durham Constabulary spokesperson noted that senior officers and staff regularly visit other forces for professional advice and collaboration. In this case, the staff member was present to discuss police finances and resources with Farrell. After completing the trip, the road policing officer returned to Edinburgh, making the round trip about 250 miles and lasting approximately six hours. At the time, much of Scotland faced severe weather warnings due to heavy rain and strong winds from Storm Babet. Train services such as LNER and Transpennine Express, which link Edinburgh to destinations south of the border, had been cancelled due to the extreme weather. Scottish Conservative shadow justice secretary Russell Findlay criticized Farrell's use of police resources, especially considering recent budget cuts. He raised concerns about the safety of the officer and the appropriateness of the decision. The Scottish Police Authority acknowledged the incident, with its chair discussing the matter with Farrell. After her apology, the authority stated it considers the matter closed. This incident is seen as embarrassing for the new chief constable, who has kept a low profile since her appointment to the UK's second-largest police force. The timing is particularly sensitive as Farrell is set to make her first public speech next week, where she will call for increased funding for Police Scotland.

Ha'e oñepyrûkuri Scotland policía ruvicha ramóvo 11 ára haguépe, oiko rire hague lika jefe Durham Constabulary-pe. Farrell ome'ê peteĩ ñe'ê he'ívo hasýha ojapo 'marandu vaíva', omyesakâvo ojerure hague oficina-pe ojapo hag̃ua peteî mba'eveve haguã chupe hógape, tren ojapóva cortes ha ha'e voi policía mba'evevégui ndoiporuvéi. He'i avei, 'Ajerurevy ko marandu vaíva'. Peteî civil Durham Constabulary-gui avei oguerekókuri hendive policía mba'evevépe ha ojeheja 15 milla gotyo, Gateshead-pe. Durham Constabulary-gui oñemombe'u rupi pe rembiapoha he'i ofisial yvyrakuéra ha tembiasa oguahêve hague ambue policía-pe oñondivepa ojapo hag̃ua consejo tembiapo rehe. Ko jejuhu-pe, tembiapoha oñemohendákuri ha omoirû Farrell-pe tembiapo viru ha recursos rehe. Opa rire pe tape, pe policía chofer oujey Edinburgo-pe, ojapóvo 250 milla rupi oñembojereháme, peteî 6 aravo rupi. Upe aja, Escocia tuichakue rupi oîkuri kalamidad rehe, oky hetaite ha okê viento vai Storm Babet reheve. Tren serviciónguéra, LNER ha Transpennine Express, ojapóva Edinburgo peve ha oñesêva Inglaterra gotyo, oñembotáva pe arapytu vai rehe. Scottish Conservative shadow justice secretary Russell Findlay omba'apo'asy Farrell rehe oporombohovakévo policía mba'eveve porupyre, taha'e avei presupuesto jekutáva rehe. Omoingove hesaho pe seguridad rehe policíape ha mba'éichapa añemomba'éne ko mba'e. Scottish Police Authority oguerohory upe mba'éva, ha ijapytépe ruvicha oñomongeta Farrell ndive. Pe ára avei iñimportánteva Farrell-pe, ha upépe ojapóta hembiapo voré rire, ojerure jeyve viruve Policía Scotland-pe g̃uarã.

article_content: A small passenger plane crashed Monday into a hillside near the capital of Honduras, killing all 14 people on board, according to officials. "The impact of the plane was extremely severe; survival would have been unlikely, looking at the state of the fuselage," said Oscar Triminio, spokesperson for the fire department. The twin-engine Let L-410 aircraft had departed from San Pedro Sula in northwest Honduras, carrying 12 passengers and two pilots, and was headed to Toncontin International Airport in Tegucigalpa, the Civil Aviation Department reported. The carrier, Central American Airways, is not connected to the US airline of the same name. At around 8 a.m., after being cleared to land, the plane began its descent but lost contact with air traffic control, the department said. Rescue teams were subsequently alerted. The crash occurred atop a hill about 2,000 feet (600 meters) above sea level, near Santa Ana in Francisco Morazan, according to Triminio. The weather was cold and foggy, as it had been since the weekend. One pilot initially survived the crash but died en route to the hospital, Triminio stated. Local villagers were the first to reach the wreckage, discovering one pilot still alive. "It's heartbreaking to hear someone in the debris pleading, 'Help! Help! Help!'" said Jorge Sandrez, mayor of Santa Ana. Emergency personnel searched for the aircraft's data recorders as part of the investigation. The remains of the 11 men and three women were transported to a morgue in Tegucigalpa, where families would identify them. Civil aviation officials identified three of the passengers as US citizens and provided CNN with the passenger list. Among the victims were Rodolfo Rovelo, identified as assistant secretary for public works; Jose Israel Salinas, a trade union leader; and Carlos Chain, a former finance minister.

article_content: The Beatles have made a remarkable return with their latest release, 'Now and Then,' which is described as their final single. The track has found widespread global success, notably achieving new milestones for the legendary band on several U.S. Billboard charts. 'Now and Then' climbed to a career-best No. 2 for The Beatles on the Hot Rock & Alternative Songs chart, just behind Zach Bryan and Kacey Musgraves' 'I Remember Everything.' This breaks their previous high of No. 3 with 'Here Comes the Sun.' On the closely-related Hot Rock Songs chart, the single mirrored this achievement, again securing the No. 2 spot and marking the band's highest placement so far. In terms of streaming, the song leaped to No. 5 on the Rock Streaming Songs chart—making it the first time The Beatles have cracked that list's top 10, surpassing 'Here Comes the Sun,' which previously reached No. 14. On the Adult Alternative Airplay chart, the single debuted at No. 9. This represents the group's first top 10 appearance on that chart, overtaking their 1990s track 'Free as a Bird,' which narrowly missed the top 10. The Beatles also recently reached No. 1 for the first time on the Digital Song Sales and Rock Digital Song Sales charts with 'Now and Then.' While the band maintains the top spot on the Rock Digital Song Sales chart for a second week, they dropped to No. 2 on the overall Digital Song Sales chart—replaced by Jung Kook's hit 'Standing Next to You.'

Adult Alternative Airplay chart-pe, oñepyrũvo purahéi oguerekóva No. 9-pe, mba’e rehegua ojapóva top 10 umi lista pire. ‘Free as a Bird’ ndaikatúi kuri upe top 10 pyaha 90 arýpe. Opyta gueteri yvate Rock Digital Song Sales-pe ára mokõiha, uperire katu oguejy No. 2 Digital Song Sales guasúpe, ha Jung Kook ‘Standing Next to You’ ohupi ijyvateve.

U.S. customs officials intercepted shipments valued at $10,000 en route to a Seattle distributor after testing by the Consumer Product Safety Commission revealed the costumes had more than 11 times the permitted amount of lead. Officials did not specify when the seizures took place but stated the contaminated products will be destroyed.

article_content: British novelist A.S. Byatt, celebrated for her ability to blend history, myth, and keen observations of human character, has died at 87. Known formally as Antonia Susan Byatt, she passed away peacefully at her London home, surrounded by loved ones, according to her publisher Chatto & Windus. Byatt's literary career spanned over twenty books, beginning with her first novel, 'The Shadow of the Sun,' in 1964. Her works, translated into 38 languages, include the acclaimed Booker Prize-winning novel 'Possession.' This novel intertwines the lives of two modern scholars with those of two imagined Victorian poets, earning widespread success and the Booker Prize in 1990. On receiving the Booker, Byatt remarked that 'Possession' was inspired by the pleasures of reading. The story was made into a 2002 film starring Gwyneth Paltrow and Aaron Eckhart. Other adaptations include 'Morpho Eugenia,' from her 1992 collection 'Angels and Insects,' which became a 1995 film featuring Mark Rylance and Kristin Scott Thomas, and 'The Djinn in the Nightingale’s Eye,' a story that won the Aga Khan Prize for Fiction and inspired the 2022 film 'Three Thousand Years of Longing,' directed by George Miller and starring Idris Elba and Tilda Swinton. Her other significant works encompass the Frederica Quartet—'The Virgin in the Garden,' 'Still Life,' 'Babel Tower,' and 'A Whistling Woman'— set in mid-20th-century Britain. Byatt was shortlisted for the Booker again in 2009 for 'The Children's Book,' a sweeping tale situated in Edwardian England about a writer of fairy tales. Her last published book was 'Medusa’s Ankles,' a short story collection released in 2021. Byatt’s agent, Zoe Waldie, extolled her as a writer whose multi-layered, intellectually engaging narratives captivated readers. Her publisher, Clara Farmer, praised her works as treasure troves of stories and ideas, confident that her legacy will endure through generations of readers. Born as Antonia Susan Drabble in Sheffield in 1936, she grew up in a Quaker household and studied at Cambridge University. Her sister, Margaret Drabble, is also a notable novelist. Byatt was first married to economist Ian Byatt, with whom she had a daughter and a son; the couple later divorced. A profound personal tragedy occurred when her son, Charles, died at age 11 after being struck by a car. Byatt became a full-time writer after leaving her university post in 1983. She later married Peter Duffy, with whom she had two daughters. Over her lifetime, Byatt received numerous accolades, including being made a Dame by Queen Elizabeth II in 1999 and a Chevalier of France’s Order of Arts and Letters in 2003. In 2014, an iridescent beetle—Euhylaeogena byattae Hespenheide—was named in her honor, inspired by her literary depiction of naturalists.
translated_content: Inglesia héra A.S. Byatt, karai oñemomba’eguasúva ombojoajúvo historia, mitología ha ava reko, omano 87 áño rehe. Antonia Susan Byatt héra tee, omano py’aguapýpe hogapýpe Londres-pe, ipehẽngue kuéra ndive, he’i iñe’ẽha Chatto & Windus. Byatt ohai heta arandukarã, 20 rupi, ha iñe’ẽ peteîha va’ekue ‘The Shadow of the Sun’ 1964-pe. Irembiapo oñe’ẽ 38 ñe’ẽme, ha iñaranduka herakuãvéva hína ‘Possession’, omombe’úva mokõi aranduhára ko’ãgagua oheka mokõi poeta Victoriano rembiasa. Ko tembiapo oguereko éxito tuicha ha ohupyty 1990-pe Booker Prize. Ohupytyrõ guare Booker Prize, Byatt he’i ‘Possession’ ha’eha ñe’ẽ lýriko rehe vy’apavẽ rehegua. Ko kuatiañe’ẽ ojapo hikuái película 2002-pe, Gwyneth Paltrow ha Aaron Eckhart ndive. Ambue aranduka ojesareko avei película-pe, umíva apytépe ‘Morpho Eugenia’ (1992 ‘Angels and Insects’-pe oĩ), ojapo película 1995-pe, Mark Rylance ha Kristin Scott Thomas ndive. Avei hembiapo michînva ‘The Djinn in the Nightingale’s Eye’, ohupyty kuri Aga Khan Prize, omoheñói película 2022-pe hérava ‘Three Thousand Years of Longing’, omoakãva George Miller ha Idris Elba ha Tilda Swinton. Ambue arandukarã tuichavéva Byatt-gui ha’e Frederica Quartet—‘The Virgin in the Garden’, ‘Still Life’, ‘Babel Tower’, ha ‘A Whistling Woman’—heñói 1950 ha 60 arýpe Inglaterra-pe. 2009-pe oĩ jey shortlist Booker Prize-pe ‘The Children’s Book’-re, peteĩ historia tuicháva Inglaterra Edwardiano rehegua ha omombe’úva toryrã. Ipahaite tembiapo ha’e ‘Medusa’s Ankles’, peteĩ arandukarã michĩ oñemohendáva 2021-pe. Iagente Zoe Waldie omombe’u Byatt-pe iñe’ẽpoty ha arandukakuéra multi-kapa rehegua, ombotavyvaitéva lénte. Clara Farmer, iñe’ẽha, ohechauka iñe’ẽpoty orypegua tesorokuéra rehegua ha ojerovia omyandy ha ombovevetaha arandukakuéra hetaiterei generación-pe. Antonia Susan Drabble héra tee, Sheffield-pe onaséva 1936-pe, oguerekova’ekue família Quaker rehegua ha oestudia Cambridge University-pe. Iñermána Margaret Drabble avei haihára. Omanova’ekue peteîha ména Ian Byatt rehe, economista, oguerekova’ekue peteĩ rajy ha peteĩ ta’ýra, ha upéi omenda jey Peter Duffy rehe, oguerekova’ekue mokõi rajy. Mba’e vaiete ohasa hague, ta’ýra Charles omanóvo 11 áñore, auto ojupi hese. 1983-pe heja mbo’ehaópe omba’apo haguãpa ha oñeme’ẽ añónte mburuvicharã. Upe rire omenda jey ha oguereko avei mokõi ra’y. Hembiapokuéra rehe oñemomba’e hese heta hendáicha, ha oñemoangekói Dame reino guasu Isabel II-gui 1999-pe ha Chevalier Francia Orden de las Artes y las Letras 2003-pe. 2014-pe peteĩ kumbaha porãva héra Euhylaeogena byattae Hespenheide oñehenói hese haguã, ohayhu haguére naturalista rehegua iñe’ẽpoty.

article_content: Talks between SAG-AFTRA and Hollywood’s top studios are ongoing, as the actors’ union replied on Monday to the studios’ self-described ‘final’ contract offer. Although companies such as Disney, Netflix, NBCUniversal, and Warner Bros. Discovery have put forward their terms, the union insists that important points—most notably the future use of artificial intelligence in creating entertainment—remain unsettled. SAG-AFTRA, which represents around 160,000 actors, stressed their aim to secure an agreement that ends the strike responsibly. The labor action began on July 14, overlapping with a writers’ walkout, prompted by concerns over AI affecting creative jobs. Although writers approved a new agreement in October that restricts AI use, actors’ negotiations continue. With the winter television season at stake, more than 5,000 SAG-AFTRA members have petitioned negotiators to maintain a firm stance for fair terms. Both sides are working to resolve the dispute soon.

Disney, Netflix, NBCUniversal ha Warner Bros. Discovery omohendáva ijatyre, SAG-AFTRA he’i oguerekoha gueteri heta mba’e iñimportánteva—ñe’ẽme’ẽ AI rehegua tembiapo apo rehe ndaha’éi oñemohu’ã gueteri. article_content: MARRAKECH, Morocco — Thirty years ago, Palestinian actor Hiam Abbass left her home to pursue her dreams in film, following a lineage of women in her family shaped by exile who 'learned to leave everything and start anew.' This journey is depicted in 'Bye Bye Tiberias,' a documentary directed by her daughter Lina Soualem, which tells the story of four generations of women in their family. At the Marrakech International Film Festival’s Arab world premiere, the film received a standing ovation and calls of 'Long Live Palestine.' 'Bye Bye Tiberias,' Palestine’s entry for next year's Academy Award for Best International Feature, follows Abbass and Soualem as they share laughter, tears, and their family’s moving story. The film first debuted at the Venice International Film Festival, more than a month before the war between Israel and Hamas broke out on October 7 after the group’s incursion into Israel. It is currently the only Palestinian film in Marrakech’s competition, where, differing from previous years, organizers did not hold screenings in the main square, often the center of protests regarding the war. During the introduction, Soualem and Abbass admitted it was a very emotional time to show the documentary, especially considering the situation of Palestinian refugees' children and grandchildren in Gaza. Soualem declined to discuss how the ongoing war impacted reactions to her film. Later, she expressed how festival audiences in Europe and the U.S. responded emotionally and stated the importance of telling new Palestinian stories that humanize Palestinian women and explore their complex decisions. ‘Our hearts are heavy seeing all the destruction and death in Gaza, which we mourn,’ she said to The Associated Press. ‘Each screening brings a sense of repair and warmth. Many people feel silenced or unable to speak.’ The film includes personal interviews with Soualem’s family—especially her mother, Abbass, widely recognized for her work in shows like 'Succession' and 'Ramy,' as well as films like 'The Lemon Tree' (2008), 'Blade Runner 2049' (2017), and 'Gaza Mon Amour' (2020). It builds on Soualem’s earlier documentary, 'Their Algeria,' about her grandparents' migration from North Africa to France during war and economic difficulty. Unlike stories focused on the Palestinian diaspora or territories like Gaza and the West Bank, 'Bye Bye Tiberias' recounts the story of a family displaced by the 1948 Arab-Israeli war, moving from one city to another inside present-day Israel. Although they kept Israeli citizenship, they lived in a Palestinian village that was mainly separated from Jewish Israeli communities. Viewers see Abbass pushing her mother Nemat in a wheelchair through Tiberias, passing Hebrew street signs and an aging mosque, as Soualem narrates how the 1948 war disrupted her grandmother’s education and 'propelled her at full speed into history.' Personal interviews are interwoven with old home movies filmed by Soualem’s father in Deir Hanna and archival footage dating back to 1948. That year, British authorities required the family to leave their home in Tiberias, which was later destroyed. Barred from returning, they relocated to Syria and to Deir Hanna in modern Israel. ‘These images are the treasures of my memory that I don't want to fade,’ Soualem says in narration. Living amid tension eventually became 'suffocating' for Abbass, prompting her emigration to France three decades ago to pursue acting. ‘Today, I wish I could ask my mother if she forgives me for making a choice opposed to her traditions and her life,’ Abbass says in the documentary. For much of Soualem’s life, Abbass seldom discussed her departure from the Middle East, not wanting to 'open the gate to past sorrows,' as Soualem explains. In the film, she finally does. Soualem shows Abbass mourning her mother, reflecting on performances at Jerusalem's Palestinian National Theatre, and looking across the Sea of Galilee as she comes to terms with both Palestinian history and her own decision to leave a cherished homeland.

Kóva ojehecha documental 'Bye Bye Tiberias'-pe, omotenondéva ijindy Lina Soualem. Pe película omombe'u mba'e irundy generación-kuña rehegua, ha oguerohoryeterei hikuái ita'anga réra Marrakech Festival Internacional de Cine-pe, oje'e avei 'Palestina toiko' peteĩ ovación ryepýpe. 'Bye Bye Tiberias', ha'e pe película Palestina opyta oñembohóva ára ambuépe Academia-pe Best International Feature rehe, ojuhu Abbass ha Soualem oñembohasa gueteri vy'a ha mba'e vai reheko rupi, oñe'ẽva ifamília rembimbo rehe. Pe película oñepyrũ raẽ Venice Festival Internacional de Cine-pe, areve oikove Guerra Israel ha Hamas octubre 7-pe. Umi mba'e ojapohague upe banda oike Israel-pe. Oñembohóva añoite película Palestina Marrakech rembiapo guasúpe, ñemoñare ary ohasáva, organisadorekuéra ndojapói proyección plaza principal-pe, peteĩ hendápe oiko hagua protesta guerra rehe. Película oñepresenta aja, Soualem ha Abbass ohechauka itaryrýi, omandu'a umi mitã ha nieto-kuera refugiado palestinogua oĩva Gaza-pe. Soualem noñe’ẽi mba’eichaitépa guerra oikuaa hague umi ohecha rehe. Upe rire, he'i ijapytepekuéra oñanduja hikuái heta emotiva festival Europa ha Estados Unidos-pe, ikatu haguã omyesakã peteĩ narrativa pyahu, ombojerovia kuña palestinagua rehe ha umi jehasa asy ojavy hague ojapo hague. 'Ore korasõ pohýi, rohecha destrucción ha omanóva Gaza-pe ha ñamindu’u hese', he’i Associated Press-pe. 'Opa proyección ha'e peteĩ reparacion rehegua ha mborayhu katu. Oĩ heta ohendu'y térã oremokirirĩva.' Pe documental omoinge entrevistas personal Soualem familia rehe, chespecial isy Abbass reheve ojeguerohory programa 'Succession' ha 'Ramy' ha película 'The Lemon Tree' (2008), 'Blade Runner 2049' (2017) ha 'Gaza Mon Amour' (2020)-pe. Oñemopu’ã Soualem rembiapokue tenonderã 'Their Algeria' rehe, omombe’u ituvakuéra oho hague África del Norte-gui Francia-pe guerra ha economia vai rire. Hetave narrativa Palestina omombe'u diaspora guasu, Gaza térã Cisjordania rehegua, ko película 'Bye Bye Tiberias' ohechauka peteĩ familia ojehechauka haguã 1948 árabe-israelita-guerra, táva guive ambue távape Israel pehẽme. Oguereko hikuái ciudadanía israelí, oiko Jefferson peteĩ komunidade separada judío-israeligua. Abbass ojehecha ogueraha imamá Nemat ape silla de ruedas-pe Tiberias rupi, ohasávo cartel hebreo ha peteĩ meskita itujáva, Soualem omombe'u mba'éicha 1948 guerra omanohague isy rembiapokue ha omboguata chupe historia-pe. Oñehenói entrevista kuatia hogar reheve Soualem ru ojapo Deir Hanna-pe ha archivo 1948 guive. Upe ary, autoridad británica omanda ipehẽnguekuérape oheja Tiberias hogakuéra, ojeity rire hógape. Ndojekuerái chupekuéra ou jey, resettahikuái Siria ha Deir Hanna-pe, Israel pehẽ ngagua. 'Ko’ã ta’anga che mandu’a aitende’ỹva ndachepotái ojehague', he'i Soualem ipurahéi rehe. Oiko rire upe tension, Abbass ojuhu ijehe 'sufri' ha ovavá Francia-pe mbohapy pa ary ohasa rire ihupyty hag̃ua actor rembiapo. 'Ko’ãga, aipota ajerure che mama pe oheja haĝua che rehe oajapohague peteî elección oñemoambuéva heko ha hekovia rehe', he'i Abbass documental-pe. Hetaiterei tiempo Abbass ndoñe’ẽi isy rehe oheja hague Medio Oriente, ndoipotái ojehapykueho porã 'omokañymby' ko'ã mba'asy, he'i Soualem; peliculape katu, oñemoañete. Soualem ohechauka Abbass ombyasy imamá renondépe, omandu'ávo ojapo hague presentación Teatro Nacional Palestino Jerusalén-pe ha oma’ẽ yvate Galilea rembe’ýpe ohecha hague mba’éichapa historia oiko hague familia palestíno rehe ha hembiapokue oheja haguã yvy omomba’éva chupe.

President Bola Tinubu has cancelled the proposed policy that would have deducted 40% of internally generated revenue (IGR) from federal universities across Nigeria. Represented by the Minister of Education, Tahir Mamman, Tinubu made this announcement on Friday at the University of Ibadan’s 75th Founder’s Day ceremony. He described the policy as 'ill-timed,' emphasizing that federal universities are already facing significant financial challenges and that such a deduction would not be appropriate at this time.

The President reaffirmed his dedication to reforming the education sector, describing it as the foundation of national development. Previously, the Federal Government had issued a letter on October 17, 2023, stating that the 40% IGR deduction would begin in November 2023, as outlined in a finance circular. 

The announcement sparked strong opposition from the Committee of Vice Chancellors of Nigerian Universities. Secretary-General Prof. Yakubu Ochefu argued that it was unfair to demand 40% of universities’ revenue when the institutions had not been granted full autonomy. Ochefu warned that, if enforced, the policy would have forced parents to bear additional financial burdens.

With the cancellation of the policy, universities and education stakeholders have expressed relief, seeing this move as a positive step towards supporting higher education in Nigeria.

article_content: Eric Nordstrom, who once oversaw security for U.S. posts in Libya, told Congress that higher-ups stood in the way when he sought stronger protection for the American mission in Benghazi. Nordstrom said the hardest part of his job wasn't threats on the ground, but dealing with officials who blocked his attempts to bring in more security staff, even describing the experience as feeling like 'the Taliban inside the building.' His comments came at the end of a tense House hearing, where State Department officials tried to defend their handling of the September 11, 2012, attack that killed Ambassador Chris Stevens and three other Americans in Benghazi. The fallout from the incident has been a big issue in the presidential campaign, as critics—including Republican Mitt Romney—claimed the tragedy underscored deeper problems in President Obama’s approach to foreign policy. Patrick Kennedy and Charlene Lamb of the State Department argued that their security decisions were based on risk assessments and available intelligence. Lamb insisted the number of security personnel in Benghazi was right at the time, which Committee Chairman Darrell Issa strongly disputed, given the deadly outcome. The hearing revealed sharp disagreements over staffing. Nordstrom said his request for 12 security agents was dismissed as too much. Lt. Col. Andrew Wood, who was in charge of on-site security for part of the year, confirmed that repeated efforts to add staff had gone nowhere and that security was always inadequate. On the night of the attack, Stevens had finished meeting with a Turkish diplomat and returned to his quarters. Not long after, armed attackers entered the compound, set fires, and forced Stevens and others to take shelter. Amid the chaos and smoke, Stevens was separated from his team and later found dead at a local hospital. Some lawmakers accused the State Department—and the Obama administration—of misleading the public by first describing the attack as a sudden protest rather than a planned assault. State Department officials said they shared the most accurate information available as events unfolded, and a review board led by former Joint Chiefs Chairman Michael Mullen was established to fully investigate. The Benghazi hearing highlighted deep political divisions, with Republicans charging negligence and Democrats condemning what they saw as partisan posturing.

Nordstrom he’i ijetu’uvéva ndaha’éi avei peligro, síno umi ojokóva ojapo hag̃ua hembiapo, ha oñandukuaa la Taliban oĩháicha óga ryepýpe. Oiko hague ojuhu mokõive elección presidencial-pe, ha umi ohechauka—republicano Mitt Romney avei—oje’éva umi problema tuichaha Obama rembiporã ha’eha mba’e guasu. Robyn Lawley, a 25-year-old Australian model, is receiving widespread praise online after sharing unretouched and makeup-free photos of herself on Facebook. She posted the photos to protest the heavy use of airbrushing and the unrealistic beauty standards common in professional photography. Lawley, who has also criticized the recent Sports Illustrated swimsuit issue, sends a clear message: beauty comes in many forms and sizes.

Interestingly, the modeling industry classifies Lawley as 'plus-size,' yet by everyday standards, she appears closer to average. This highlights the distorted body image expectations within the fashion world. When viewers see her unedited photos, many question why she is considered plus-size, noting that if she represents that category, industry definitions are clearly out of line with reality.

Lawley's case sheds light on broader issues such as vanity sizing, where clothing sizes have become smaller in label but not in actual size compared to previous decades. As a result, someone who is considered a size 14 or 16 in the 1950s might be labeled an 8 today. Lawley is a size 12, serving as both a plus-size role model and an example of the shifting definitions of average.

While unrealistic appearance expectations have traditionally been directed at women, men are not immune. Examples include magazine covers airbrushing male celebrities like Prince William and Andy Roddick, or highlighting changes in male beauty standards, such as increased grooming and use of performance-enhancing substances. This reflects growing pressure on men as well as women to conform to digital or edited ideals.

By sharing unedited images, Lawley encourages a conversation about authentic beauty and challenges the fashion industry's narrow standards. Her willingness to put herself in the spotlight is considered brave, especially in a culture where such labels and expectations persist. Ideally, her actions will inspire broader recognition of healthy, realistic perceptions of body image.

article_content: Unlike many in Hong Kong who rely on disposable cups, pet groomer Lucine Mo now drinks her coffee from a thermal mug with a QR code, part of a Greenpeace pilot. This initiative involves 35 coffee shops and seeks to reduce single-use cutlery and cups. Mo said, 'Since learning about the service, I stopped using plastic and paper cups. If a restaurant offers reusable cutlery for takeaway, I'm happy to use it.' While this behavior is still uncommon in Hong Kong, things are set to change when a ban on disposable plastic cutlery takes effect on Earth Day, April 22, 2024, across more than 28,000 eateries. Authorities say the plan is to nurture a 'plastic-free culture.' However, environmentalists warn that simply replacing plastic with other disposable materials may not truly address the problem. Hong Kong's waste issue is severe: 13 dumpsites are already filled, and the remaining three landfills are projected to reach capacity by 2030. Greenpeace campaigner Leanne Tam noted, 'The real problem is our throwaway culture. We need to focus on switching from disposable items to reusables.' Plastic is a major concern, making up the second-largest source of municipal solid waste: in 2021, Hong Kong discarded 2,331 tonnes of plastic each day, roughly the weight of 70 adult humpback whales. In October 2023, Hong Kong's legislature amended the 'Product Eco-Responsibility Bill,' introducing a two-step ban on certain plastic products. The first phase, starting on Earth Day, bans specific polystyrene and hard-to-recycle plastic tableware in eateries for dine-in customers and office workers seeking takeaway. Plastic containers like cups and bowls will still be allowed for takeaway for now but will be phased out later depending on whether reusable options are practical and affordable. Volunteer Yeungs Ting is among those cautious about the new rules’ impact. 'It's about the culture of throwing things away after one use, not just the material,' she explained, recounting how her team collected 140 kilograms of trash—including over 3,000 plastic bottles—during a beach cleanup. She wonders if wider adoption of a cutlery borrowing system will happen. Taiwan provides an interesting example. With four billion plastic cups used annually, the island has imposed bans, incentives, and requirements for fast food and convenience stores to use reusables. Lin Yu-Huei, Taipei’s recycling chief, told AFP that since the ban in December 2022, about 76 million cups are kept out of landfills each year. Lin added, 'It's very resource-intensive to process and recycle plastics. We want to cut waste at the source.' Hong Kong’s environment minister Tse Chin-wan also highlighted that swapping plastic for other single-use materials like paper or wood is not a real fix. During a recent campaign launch, he said, 'To reduce waste effectively, we should use reusable products.' Till the end of April, more than 750 eateries, including major fast food chains, will reward customers who refuse disposable cutlery. Tam from Greenpeace supports creating an accessible loan system for borrowers to use and return reusable utensils for takeaway meals, viewing it as a solution where 'being green and convenient go hand in hand.'

article_content: Ukrainian authorities and pro-Russia rebels in eastern Ukraine agreed to a comprehensive ceasefire and established a buffer zone during talks in Belarus, as reported by Russia's state-run RIA-Novosti news agency. Both parties also agreed to withdraw heavy weaponry from the front lines of the conflict, which has been ongoing since April, until a preliminary truce was reached two weeks prior. That ceasefire has been unstable, with intermittent and sometimes heavy fighting. The recent agreement, reached in Minsk with representatives from Russia, the Ukrainian government, rebel leaders, and the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), includes nine provisions aimed at establishing a more lasting ceasefire, according to RIA Novosti. The 'Minsk memorandum,' announced by former Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma, outlines key points: a bilateral ceasefire; no movement of military forces beyond the front line as of September 19; a prohibition on the use of weapons or offensive actions; and the relocation of heavy weaponry at least 15 kilometers (nine miles) from the front line to create a 30-kilometer buffer zone. Additional provisions call for a ban on the use of heavy weaponry in residential areas, a ban on flights over the buffer zone except by OSCE monitors, and the withdrawal of all foreign fighters and military equipment from Ukrainian territory, all to be monitored by the OSCE. Ukraine and Western nations continue to accuse Russia of providing heavy weaponry, training, and even troops to the rebels. Russian President Vladimir Putin denies these allegations. Meanwhile, Russia's state-run Itar-Tass news agency reported that a third Russian humanitarian aid convoy arrived in Donetsk on Saturday, having crossed the border earlier that day. The convoy of 200 trucks delivered food, power generators, medical supplies, clothing, and bottled water. Itar-Tass stated that Ukrainian authorities and the International Committee of the Red Cross were given an opportunity to inspect the convoy, but reportedly declined without explanation. According to Ukrainian National Security and Defense Council spokesman Col. Andriy Lysenko, Russia informed Ukraine of its intent to send a convoy but did not request formal permission. Lysenko could not confirm that the convoy had crossed the border, noting that the Izvarino checkpoint is controlled by separatists, preventing Ukrainian border guards from inspecting the trucks. Two previous convoys entered Ukraine from Russia without Ukrainian authorization or inspection, delivering supplies to Luhansk, another stronghold of pro-Russia rebels. On Thursday, Ukrainian President Petro Poroshenko addressed the U.S. Congress in Washington, requesting increased military support as Ukrainian forces continue to battle pro-Russia rebels in the east. While the U.S. has provided nonlethal aid such as blankets and night vision goggles, Poroshenko’s request for arms was declined once again. Poroshenko, who also met with U.S. President Barack Obama, told CNN's Wolf Blitzer that Ukraine was 'fully satisfied' with the current level of U.S. assistance, emphasizing that the crisis in eastern Ukraine cannot be solved by military means alone. Earlier in the week, a rocket attack by pro-Russia rebels killed 10 civilians and wounded 12 more in eastern Ukraine, according to Ukrainian military officials. During the same week, lawmakers in Ukraine passed legislation granting 'special status' to rebel-controlled areas in Luhansk and Donetsk. The law offers amnesty to separatists, contingent upon their disarmament, the release of hostages, and surrender of occupied buildings. The law also provides protections for Russian-language speakers in these regions. Russia’s involvement in Ukraine has led to several rounds of economic sanctions by the United States and Europe, yet these measures have not changed President Putin’s course of action. Following Poroshenko’s address to Congress, a Senate Foreign Relations panel advanced a bipartisan aid package for Ukraine, including $350 million in both military and non-military support. At the same time, the Ukrainian Parliament and the European Union ratified a political and economic agreement that includes provisions for free trade, set to take effect in early 2016. Former President Viktor Yanukovych's decision to abandon the EU association agreement in favor of closer ties with Russia triggered widespread unrest, leading to his ouster in February, Russia’s annexation of Crimea, and the ongoing conflict in eastern Ukraine. Moscow remains opposed to Ukraine’s move toward closer ties with the West, a direction championed by Poroshenko.

article_content: ShareChat co-founders Farid Ahsan and Bhanu Pratap Singh have raised $3 million in seed funding for their new industrial robotics startup. The round was led by India Quotient and Elevation Capital. Their company, General Autonomy, will build AI-driven machines to automate labor workflows in factories. According to Ahsan's post on X (formerly Twitter), the company aims to revolutionize factory operations, making mass manufacturing more agile and distributed, similar to software development. General Autonomy is headquartered in Bengaluru but operates globally. Angel investors participating in the funding round include Zetwerk co-founder Srinath Ramakkrushnan, Livspace co-founder Ramakant Sharma, and ShareChat founder Ankush Sachdeva. Earlier this year, Ahsan (former COO) and Singh (former CTO) stepped down from active roles at ShareChat, which has recently scaled down operations. ShareChat laid off about 20% of its employees, roughly 500 people. The industrial robotics sector has seen other deals, such as Ati Motors raising $10.85 million in July in a round led by True Ventures. Additionally, the Indian Income Tax Department is investigating Apple, Google, and Amazon’s Indian units regarding transfer pricing practices. Indians have become significant investors in Dubai’s real estate market, and Razorpay plans to relocate its parent company to India, which may result in a substantial US tax payment.

Ahsan he’i X-pe (Twitter yma guaré) oipotaha ombovavývo fábrica rembiapo, omyengovia hag̃ua producción industrial oñembojoaju software rehe guáicha. India-gua kuéra oñemba’éva Dubai rehe inmobiliaria-pe, ha Razorpay ojapose ome’ẽ parent company India-pe, ha ikatu hague tásapy guasu Estados Unidos-pe.

article_content: San Diego, California (CNN) -- At San Diego Comic-Con, the annual gathering of enthusiastic fans, early movie screenings can feel like rock concerts—and sometimes actually become one. On Thursday night, some attendees at the ‘Scott Pilgrim vs. the World’ panel, where star Michael Cera arrived dressed as Captain America, were surprised with an advance screening of the entire movie at a nearby theater. The audience cheered during the opening credits and celebrated whenever Scott Pilgrim bested one of his new girlfriend’s ‘evil exes.’ The film, based on a manga-inspired comic series, has strong appeal for both comic book fans and gamers. Gabriel Simon said after the screening, ‘It surpassed my expectations, and I’m a huge fan.’ The event ended with a performance by the band Metric, as cast members including Anna Kendrick danced from the balcony. Brittany Hernandez of La Jolla, California, called the film the highlight of the convention so far. ‘I thought the movie was amazing. I saw the panel after The Expendables. Sylvester Stallone is hard to beat, but that was pretty awesome.’ Hollywood studios are competing to win over these dedicated fans, offering early looks at upcoming projects, interactive experiences, and exclusive merchandise. ‘Scott Pilgrim’ also offered an off-site area for custom T-shirts. Not to be outdone, ‘The Green Hornet’ showcased the Black Beauty car and featured costumed Green Hornettes throughout the convention. Attendees could visit Britt Reid’s Garage to view the Black Beauty and other vehicles from the film. Seth Rogen, who stars as the Hornet, commented, ‘We tried to take risks and make something interesting, and also make something that is worth this amount of money.’ He explained the car’s design process, noting it’s similar to the TV version but with bigger guns. Rogen, a Comic-Con regular and Marvel Comics fan, wished for more comic-focused content at the event. For fans interested in technology, ‘Tron: Legacy’ offered an updated ‘Tanks’ game for iPhone and brought back Flynn’s Arcade, featuring a Twitter-based scavenger hunt that unlocked special events and movie secrets. ‘Salt’ took a classic approach, surprising fans with an appearance by Angelina Jolie, just 24 hours before the film’s release. Bruce Willis attended to promote the adaptation ‘Red,’ while Helen Mirren discussed her first action role. Sylvester Stallone also made an appearance to promote ‘The Expendables,’ joined by a lineup of action stars. Food promotions were featured too, with Robert Rodriguez’s upcoming ‘Machete’ serving tacos and showing exclusive footage. Several more major movies, including ‘Green Lantern’ with Ryan Reynolds, and upcoming Marvel adaptations like ‘Thor’ and ‘Captain America: The First Avenger,’ were scheduled for Hall H presentations. Fans also saw early props, such as Abin Sur, Thor’s hammer, and Captain America’s shield. Director Jon Favreau hoped to find success at Comic-Con with ‘Cowboys & Aliens,’ still in production. ‘Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows’ made its first Comic-Con appearance, with horcrux replicas on display before the panel. With such spectacle, even ‘Harry Potter’ has to pull out all the stops to stand out amid the event’s flashy atmosphere.

article_content: Oscar Pistorius, the South African Paralympic athlete, has been staying at his uncle's home in Pretoria since the fatal shooting of his girlfriend, Reeva Steenkamp. Over recent months, Pistorius has remained out of the public eye, choosing to grow a beard to avoid being recognized and keeping photos of Steenkamp close by. His uncle Arnold reports that Pistorius is deeply affected by grief and struggles with the reality of his actions. Reeva Steenkamp, a 29-year-old model and law graduate, died on February 14. Pistorius faces murder charges. He states her death was a terrible accident, explaining he mistook her for an intruder; authorities contend it was deliberate. Pistorius's close circle—including uncle Arnold, agent Peet van Zyl, and coach Ampie Louw—describe him as overwhelmed by emotion, rarely leaving the house, and tending to his own sorrow. Van Zyl remembers a frantic call from the estate manager's daughter, followed by a rush to Pistorius's home. Louw describes hearing Pistorius’s cries upon arrival, underscoring the distressing scene. A court hearing is scheduled in Pretoria, where prosecutors may request more time for investigation. The trial date is uncertain and could occur next year. Media attention remains intense as debates continue over the facts of the case.

article_content: Tencent Music Entertainment posted third-quarter revenue that outperformed Wall Street predictions, driven by continued growth in its paid music streaming subscriptions. The Tencent Holdings affiliate runs multiple popular music platforms in China—including QQ Music, Kugou, Kuwo, and WeSing—with a broad offering of services from karaoke to live concert streaming. Despite surpassing analyst projections by reporting 6.57 billion yuan in revenue, the total marked a year-over-year decline. Market analysts had forecasted the company would bring in about 6.31 billion yuan, based on LSEG figures. Tencent Music’s social entertainment revenue fell sharply—down almost 50%—as a result of China’s crackdown on online gambling. This led the company to suspend features like virtual lucky draws, which had been popular on their platform. However, there were positive trends: The company’s net profit rose to 1.71 billion yuan, up from last year’s 1.06 billion yuan, and paying subscribers surged to 103 million from 85.3 million in the previous year. Tencent Music also slightly beat profit expectations, reporting earnings per American depository share at 89 yuan, just above the predicted 88 yuan.

Tencent Holdings oguereko heta plataforma popular Paraguáipe—QQ Music, Kugou, Kuwo ha WeSing—ojapóva hetaichagua tembiapo, karaoke ha concierto en vivo avei. Tencent Music avei ojapo pe oraketa analista-kuéra remiandu rehe, oguerekóvo 89 yuan peteĩ American depository share rehe, oñembosako’i 88 yuan reheguágui.

article_content:
An asteroid the size of an aircraft carrier, designated 2005 YU55, passed within the moon’s orbit on Tuesday, making it the closest approach by such a large object in over 30 years. At 6:28 p.m., NASA reported the asteroid came within 202,000 miles of Earth—approximately four-fifths of the moon’s distance from our planet.

Marina Brozovic, a researcher at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California, explained that the agency observed 2005 YU55 using powerful instruments, including the massive radio telescope at Puerto Rico’s Arecibo Observatory. “This is a rare event, and we learned a lot,” Brozovic said.

Despite being classified as a “potentially hazardous object,” NASA’s Near Earth Object Program confirmed there was no collision threat. In the event of an impact, Purdue University scientists estimate the asteroid could have generated a 4,000-megaton blast and a magnitude 7.0 earthquake. If it struck the ocean, a 70-foot-high tsunami could have developed within 60 miles of the site.

NASA noted that the last asteroid of this size passed so close in 1976, with the next similar event expected in 2028.

As the asteroid approached, NASA observed it with the Goldstone radar antennas in California’s Mojave Desert. These sensitive radio telescopes enabled scientists to reconstruct the asteroid’s shape with a resolution as fine as 13 feet (4 meters).

The event also gave amateur astronomers a rare chance to view the asteroid with optical telescopes 6 inches (15 cm) or larger, though it appeared faint and moved quickly at 11th or 12th magnitude.

CNN’s Sean Morris contributed to this report.

article_content: Father Jose Funes, director of the Vatican Observatory, has dismissed widespread doomsday predictions based on the Mayan calendar, assuring the public that the world will not end on December 21, 2012. Speaking in the Vatican newspaper L’Osservatore Romano, Father Funes stated that 'it's not even worth discussing' such apocalyptic scenarios, which have proliferated online ahead of the supposed 'apocalypse'. He explained that while the universe is slowly expanding, any destruction of Earth would not occur for billions of years. Father Funes added that Christians believe 'death can never have the last word'. Apocalyptic speculation has been fueled by the Mayan Long Count calendar, which began in 3,114 B.C. and tracks time in approximately 394-year cycles known as Baktuns. The 13th Baktun ends on December 21, 2012, leading some to predict an impending catastrophe. Father Funes, a 45-year-old Jesuit priest and scientific adviser to Pope Benedict, has also argued that astrobiology—the study of the possibility of life beyond Earth—is a legitimate field for the Catholic Church. In past interviews, including a 2008 article titled 'Aliens are my brother', he suggested that the existence of intelligent beings created by God elsewhere in the universe would not conflict with Catholic faith. Funes even proposed that such beings might not require salvation to enter Heaven, particularly if they were more advanced than humans.

Vaticano pegua kuatiahaipyre L’Osservatore Romano-pe he'i Pa'i Funes: 'ndaha'éi jepe ikatúva oñemoñe'ẽ' umi apocalipsis oiko kuri internet-pe ko tiémpope.' article_content: Edward Snowden, the former NSA contractor who exposed classified U.S. surveillance programs, is seeking to extend his residency in Russia before his visa expires at the end of July. His lawyer, Anatoly Kucherena, has said Snowden submitted an application to Russian migration officials, but declined to specify the type of immigration status requested. Kucherena emphasized that the application was filed well in advance and the decision is up to the migration service. In 2013, Snowden was stranded in a Moscow airport after leaking sensitive NSA documents and trying to travel from Hong Kong to Cuba. Russia’s choice to grant him asylum aggravated the United States, which has urged his return for prosecution. Since arriving, Snowden has maintained a low profile, is rarely seen in public, and avoids interactions with journalists. In April, Snowden appeared via a pre-recorded video to question President Vladimir Putin during a televised call-in show. According to his lawyer, keeping Snowden’s location confidential is essential for his protection, though critics suggest the secrecy may also indicate surveillance by Russian authorities.

article_content: A seventh-minute goal from Brazilian teenager Alexander Pato secured a 1-0 home victory for AC Milan over Fiorentina. The match took place during a week of intense speculation over Manchester City’s $150 million bid for Milan playmaker Kaka. Pato and David Beckham celebrated the winning goal at the San Siro on Saturday evening. The goal originated when Beckham beat two defenders to a loose ball, passed it to Marek Jankulovski, who then played Pato into the penalty area. Although the danger seemed minimal, Pato delivered a powerful strike from the left that bounced in off the far post. Fiorentina nearly equalized in the 66th minute when Juan Vargas crossed to Mario Santana, but the Argentine's shot went directly to Milan goalkeeper Christian Abbiati, who saved comfortably. With this win, Milan remain third in Serie A with 37 points, six points behind league leaders and city rivals Inter, who still have a game in hand. Inter, managed by Jose Mourinho, will travel to Atalanta on Sunday. Jankulovski received a late red card for timewasting, but Milan held on for all three points. Meanwhile, Milan supporters made their opposition to the Kaka transfer bid clear throughout the match, displaying banners and singing in support of the Brazilian staying at the San Siro. Elsewhere, Reggina remain in relegation trouble after a 1-0 loss to Siena. Mario Frick’s goal 15 minutes from time gave Siena the win, helping them move up to 14th place ahead of Sampdoria. Siena, however, stay second from bottom and could drop to last place in Serie A if Chievo beat Napoli on Sunday.

article_content: Jahi McMath's family is continuing their efforts to keep her body functioning after she was declared brain dead following a surgery to remove her tonsils. Their attorney, Chris Dolan, states that they are still trying to save the 13-year-old’s life, even after doctors at Children’s Hospital Oakland confirmed she is brain dead. The family blocked the hospital’s plans to remove Jahi from her ventilator through legal action and managed to transfer her to another care facility. Still, medical experts say that after an extended lack of nutrition and severe brain damage, Jahi’s body is deteriorating and meaningful recovery is almost impossible. Documents shared in court reveal worsening conditions, with doctors describing Jahi's current state as only an 'illusion of life.' Despite this, her uncle Omari Sealey maintains that Jahi is alive because her heart continues to beat. The family reports increased movement and responses to sound and touch, and long to see her smile again. Omari describes Jahi as a kind, shy girl loved by those around her, and the family holds onto hope of hearing her voice again. Medical professionals, however, emphasize that recovery is not possible. Further court papers outline the steep challenges the family now faces. Dr. Heidi Flori, pediatrician at the hospital, explained that due to damage to Jahi’s brain stem, her body cannot regulate core functions such as temperature, heart rate, and breathing. Additional signs of decline include tightening muscles, loss of skin tissue elasticity, changes in blood pressure, and reliance on external temperature control. Dr. Flori commented that these developments were inevitable after brain death, and that medical measures can merely maintain the appearance of life without restoring true function. She warned that ongoing interventions might ultimately cause her heart to stop sooner.

Chris Dolan, hogaygua abogado, oñe’ẽ ko araite gueteri ha he’i ojapo hikuái opa ikatúva ojehekypy’áva mitãkuña 13 arýgui, umi pohanohára Oakland Mitã Pohanohápe ohechakuaávo omano hague iñakãgui. article_content: This fall, airlines are making significant efforts to enhance the passenger experience. In response to major changes in loyalty programs—such as those announced by Delta Air Lines, which caused many top-tier SkyMiles members to look for other airlines—carriers are working harder than ever to win over travelers. This is especially important as the holiday travel season approaches and booking activity rises. Below are the latest updates and changes in the airline industry to help you plan your next trip. United Airlines has debuted new and upgraded United Club lounges in Newark and Denver. The 18,000-square-foot Newark lounge features a premium bar, buffet, and a Manhattan-inspired design by local architect and artist Ron Norsworthy, drawing inspiration from Grand Central Station. It also offers New Jersey’s state sandwich: Taylor ham, egg, and cheese. In Denver, United now operates the world’s largest United Club, with a 35,000 sq ft lounge in Concourse B and a 24,000 sq ft lounge in Concourse A, with an additional club opening in 2025. Guests can enjoy regional artwork and specialty menu items like Colorado Club Sandwiches and an egg frittata inspired by the Denver Omelet. United has also upgraded its Polaris business class, collaborating with Saks Fifth Avenue and Therabody. New amenities include enhanced bedding products—such as a redesigned blanket by Cameroonian designer Claude Kameni—and a commitment to eliminating plastic wrapping for environmental reasons. Updated amenity kits now feature items like eye serum with niacinamide, caffeine, hyaluronic acid, and Vitamin B5. Therabody products, including Theragun and RecoveryAir JetBoots, will be available in lounge shower suites and 'reset lounges.' According to United, this marks their largest update to business class products since 2016. JetBlue Airways has improved its Mosaic status program, following recent changes to Delta’s SkyMiles program. Eligible Delta Diamond Medallion members can match to Mosaic status, which now includes benefits such as IHG One Rewards Platinum Elite status, a 20-Tile bonus for status qualification, and eligibility for Avis car rental status match. Starting in 2024, Mosaic 3 and 4 members can gift Mosaic 1 status and use upgrade certificates for confirmed Mint seat upgrades, with the number of certificates required varying based on a dynamic pricing model. The ability to confirm Mint seats in advance represents a significant improvement. Marriott Bonvoy and United MileagePlus expanded their loyalty partnership. A new promotion, available until December 9, allows eligible members—Marriott Bonvoy Titanium and Ambassador members, or United Gold elites and higher—to earn 500 United miles per eligible Marriott stay or 750 Marriott points per eligible United trip by linking their accounts. This initiative mirrors similar partnerships, like that of American Airlines and World of Hyatt. KLM introduced its 104th Delft House collectible for business class passengers on international flights, honoring its 104th anniversary. This year’s Delft House is modeled after Valkenburg aan de Geul’s historic train station in the Netherlands. KLM also unveiled a redesigned lounge at Houston Bush Intercontinental Airport, featuring Dutch house visuals, eco-leather, and recycled materials. The lounge is accessible to Priority Pass members and echoes the style of KLM’s Amsterdam home lounge. A new generation of digital innovators is transforming the UK government, making significant savings and improving public services. One standout is Jordan Hatch, who left school at 17 to join the Government Digital Service (GDS). Based in Holborn, Hatch and a team of 250 are working to centralize government websites into one easy-to-use platform, gov.uk, a move projected to save taxpayers £1.2 billion by 2015.

Now 19 and living in North London, Hatch has created features like a real-time calendar for bank holidays and an online tool for paying council tax. Though the gov.uk website’s simple design has had its critics, it was honored with the Design of the Year award, beating rivals like The Shard and the Olympic cauldron.

For Hatch, public service is fulfilling: "It's satisfying to make government more accessible," he says, choosing to serve citizens over joining large tech companies. Cabinet Office Minister Francis Maude, supportive of the initiative, believes high-quality digital solutions can revolutionize government, delivering smarter and more affordable services. As GDS grows, it aims to be the cornerstone of digital government in the UK, ensuring convenient access to information for everyone.

Ko'ág̃a 19 arýpe, Hatch oiko gueteri hogayguakuéra ndive North London-pe ha omopyenda heta mba'e porã: kalendario oikóva meme feriado rehegua ha peteĩ herramienta peg̃uahẽhápe ikatu ojejapo pago council tax línea rehe. Gov.uk diseño simple orekóva algunos kritika, péro ohupyty Design of the Year jehepyme'ẽ, pu'ãvo The Shard ha Olympic cauldron rehegua.

Hatch he'i chupeguarã servísio público hína ombovy'ave: "Oporombojerovia che rehe ojapo haguére gobierno ikatu porãvévape oĩ tavayguápe." article_content: Mumbai’s L T Marg police have arrested two men accused of robbing a jewellery manufacturing unit at gunpoint in the Kalbadevi area on November 9. They fled with gold jewellery valued at over Rs 7 lakh. The suspects, Rajesh Bodhu Rai and Vasant Pelli (also known as Chittu), were presented in court on Sunday and remanded to police custody. Recently, police in Kalyan, Thane district, apprehended two individuals—Nihal Shaikh and Chand Shaikh—on charges of assaulting people, stealing valuables, cash, and three motorcycles. Thanks to CCTV footage, officers recovered the stolen items, including a gold chain and cash. Both suspects, described as drug addicts, allegedly stole to support their addiction. In another incident, authorities arrested a juvenile from Jaipur at Guwahati Railway Station for attempting to smuggle approximately 500 grams of gold, worth Rs 30 lakh, which was hidden under his belt. The Government Railway Police are investigating the origin of the gold and the wider smuggling operation. On a different note, the comedy-drama 'Entangled' starring Rob Lowe and his son John Owen Lowe, has been renewed for a second season. The new season, set to feature eight episodes, will follow the father-son duo as they continue to navigate their complicated relationship, with production commencing later this month.

article_content: Swansea City's hopes of signing Franck Tabanou have been stalled, as St Etienne president Bernard Caiazzo has firmly stated that the French defender will not be leaving this winter. Tabanou, known for his ability to play on both the left side of defense and attack, has attracted Swansea’s interest in their search to add strength to the squad. Tabanou’s agent, Philippe Lamboley, confirmed that discussions between the clubs are happening, but noted that no official offer from Swansea has been made. Despite this, Caiazzo has reiterated that regardless of any potential offers, Tabanou will stay with St Etienne, as the club currently sits fourth in Ligue 1 and is aiming for a place in the Champions League. After selling striker Wilfried Bony to Manchester City for up to £28 million, Swansea is still working to boost their defense, even after signing full-back Kyle Naughton from Tottenham. Manager Garry Monk wants to create competition for Neil Taylor, the only established left back at the club, and is also reportedly considering Norwich’s Swedish international, Martin Olsson.

Tabanou, oikatuva ohecha mokõi hendápe, defensa ha ataque la izquierda gotyo, oime Swansea apytépe omyasãiva hatãve hembiapo. Tabanou rehegua representante, Philippe Lamboley, omanomba'ekue oĩha conversación mokõi club apytépe, péro ndoikuaái ndaipóriha oferta oficial Swansea-gui. Caiazzo imandu'a avei jeýnte, oferta porã oike jepe, Tabanou opytáta St Etienne-pe, ha ág̃a hína irundyha Ligue 1-pe, ojapose Champions League-pe oike. article_content: On the Pacific Coast Highway in Malibu, California, a four-car collision involving Bruce Jenner occurred. Jenner’s Cadillac Escalade rear-ended a white Lexus around midday, sending it into oncoming traffic where a Hummer struck it. The crash resulted in the death of an elderly woman and injuries to five children and two adults. Several hours later, around 6:30pm, officers reported that a suspected drunk driver bypassed police barricades and crashed into the debris left from the earlier accident. The individual was arrested at the scene on suspicion of driving under the influence. After the first accident, Bruce Jenner took and passed a field sobriety test before being taken by police, reportedly for a blood test. Cleanup from the initial crash was ongoing when the second crash occurred.

Pya’e rire, aproximadamente 6:30 pm, policía omombe’u peteĩ chofer oikuaaháicha hague okaru alkohol rehe, ohasa barricada policial ha oike accidenteko hyepýpe oĩma haguã fragmentos accidente peteĩhápe.
