article_content: Two years after their daughter disappeared, the parents of Lisa Irwin remain hopeful she will return home. Lisa was just 10 months old when she went missing from her family's home in Kansas City, Missouri, during the night of October 4, 2011. Her parents, Deborah Bradley and Jeremy Irwin, are marking the anniversary with a candle-lit vigil this Saturday. They have worked with the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children to release an age-progressed image showing what Lisa might look like today, hoping it will revive interest in the case. Authorities say the number of tips has decreased over time, with about one tip per week now being received compared to more than 1,600 in the first year. The family and a private investigator remain dedicated to finding Lisa, and a $100,000 reward is being offered for information leading to her return. Bradley continues to relay any tips she receives to the police and maintains her and her husband’s innocence, expressing faith that this will be proven if Lisa is found. Their attorney, John Picerno, stated the family is pleased with the new age-progressed image and remains hopeful as the investigation continues.

article_content: According to a white paper by credit bureau Experian, borrowers from Delhi, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh top the list for fraudulent loan applications. The report highlights that millennials and postgraduates show a particularly high incidence of application fraud for loans below Rs 50,000. Bankers have expressed concerns about the credit appraisal processes of certain fintech companies, which have driven credit growth in these segments. The highest growth in personal loan originations has taken place in small cities such as Alwar and Barpeta. A senior banker from Punjab National Bank stated, “This clearly shows that many new-age fintech companies are prioritizing customer acquisition over proper due diligence in credit appraisal.” Earlier this month, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) increased risk weights on unsecured personal loans, credit cards, and lending to non-bank finance companies (NBFCs) by 25 percentage points following concerns about higher unsecured retail lending. Transunion Cibil reports that small-ticket personal loans under Rs 50,000 are especially risky, with a delinquency rate (90+ days overdue) of 5.4% as of June 2023. Experian’s white paper, ‘Building a Sustainable Fintech Portfolio’, notes that post-pandemic, fintechs rapidly expanded small-ticket unsecured personal loans. The report says fintech companies fostered a new class of borrowers through products like Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) by offering simplified customer experiences. The Indian Bankers' Association previously highlighted that banks may not have visibility into such fintech-facilitated transactions, especially since some firms do not report to credit bureaus. This omission raises risks for lenders relying on bureau data. Experian Hunter analysis indicates that fintechs and modern NBFCs source more loans from millennials, highly educated individuals, and the small-ticket segment. It also notes that areas with higher fintech presence have a higher incidence of reported fraud. A banker from Bank of Baroda emphasized the need to strengthen the central KYC (CKYC) system to prevent multiple bank accounts with varied KYC information, noting, “This loophole has led to cases where borrower data was not recorded accurately.” In 2022, the RBI instructed issuers of non-bank prepaid payment instruments (PPIs) not to fund wallets and cards via credit lines or preset borrowing limits. Although net delinquency rates have improved for fintechs since the pandemic, Experian suggests this may be due to more accounts being written off, rather than genuine improvement in asset quality.

Opaichagua viru oikevéva che rehegua oĩ távaguasu michĩvagui, Alwar ha Barpeta rehe. article_content: Natalie Thomas, 25, has been officially charged with theft involving a memorial charity fund created for Laura Rees, who died in a car accident in October 2012. Thomas, along with Laura’s family, established the fund to support the creation of a children’s medical center at Glangwili. Laura, aged 23, tragically lost her life just before she was supposed to be a bridesmaid at her close friend’s wedding. During the inquest in Carmarthenshire, Laura’s mother Angela described her daughter’s last day, mentioning Laura had picked up her bridesmaid dress and was looking forward to the wedding. Laura worked at Glangwili Day Nursery and had been employed at the Black Lion Hotel in St Clears. According to Dyfed-Powys Police, Thomas is set to appear in court later this month in connection with the theft allegation.

Thomas ha Laura familia ojapo peteĩ viru aty ojepytyvõ haguã omopu’ã peteĩ mitãnguéra renda pyahu Glangwili-pe. Laura, 23 ary, omanóma peve oikóta raka’e bridesmaid iñamiga kasamientopépe. Carmarthenshire-pe oiko va’ekue inquest-pe, isý Angela omombe’u mba’éichapa Laura ohasa ára ipahague: ohupyty hague ijao bridesmaid ha oñembosako’i hague pe boda rehe. Laura omba’apo kuri Glangwili Day Nursery-pe, ha avei Black Lion Hotel St Clears-pe. Dyfed-Powys Police ohechauka Thomas ohoha corte-pe ko arapokõindy pahápe pe viru ogueraha rei hague rehe.

article_content: Quoc-Viet Phan Hoang, a student at the University of Minnesota, has shared the harrowing story of losing two friends after the trio fell into the Chicago River late Monday. Recovering in the hospital, Hoang said he held his cousin Ken Hoang as they waited for help, but Ken did not survive. He also described the anguish of seeing his friend Lauren Li swept away by the cold river. After an extensive search, authorities discovered Li's body on Wednesday afternoon. The incident unfolded just after midnight, when Ken dropped his phone while taking photos of the icy river. Quoc-Viet and Lauren jumped in after him to help. A passerby heard their calls for help and contacted emergency services. Rescue teams were able to pull Quoc-Viet and Ken from the river, but Lauren was not found right away. The Cook County Medical Examiner reported that Ken died from drowning, with alcohol as a contributing factor. Lauren's body was recovered two days later. In a heartfelt Facebook post, Quoc-Viet expressed his grief and sorrow, mourning the loss of both his cousin and his friend. Friends and family have posted tributes to Lauren Li and Ken Hoang, and Ken's family has set up a memorial fund online. The three friends, who were on a road trip from Minnesota to New Jersey and had stopped in Chicago, have left a grieving community behind. Lauren's father waited anxiously at a hotel for word about his daughter. The tragedy has brought friends and loved ones together in remembrance.

Ho'a rire hasyhápe, Hoang he'i oipyhy hague iñirũngue Ken Hoang rehe, oha'arõrõ ojepytyvõ, ha upéicharõ Ken omano. Avei oñe'ẽ pe py'amirĩ oguahẽ haguã ohechávo iñirũ Lauren Li oñemohenda ysyry ro'ysãme. Mba'apoharakuéra oheka rire puku, ojuhu hikuái Lauren rete miércoles pyhare. Upe mba'e vai oiko pyhare asajefué, Ken oheja upevove ipópe iteléfono ho'a ojapo jave imaguara chupe ombotývo hielo rehe. Quoc-Viet ha Lauren oñemohenda ysyrype oipytyvõ haguã chupe. article_content: Debra, a mother of four from Australia, has spoken openly about her life with HIV, aiming to challenge the stigma that surrounds the illness. She learned she was HIV-positive two decades ago after her husband, Gary, became severely ill with pneumonia in 1995. At the time, Debra was unaware of Gary's diagnosis until hospital tests confirmed that both he and Debra were living with HIV. The couple had enjoyed ten years of marriage and family life before Debra was blindsided by the news that Gary had contracted HIV through relationships with men and intravenous drug use. Though she felt betrayed, she cared for him during his decline, tending to him for 11 months until he died from AIDS-related complications. Their three children all tested HIV-negative. Throughout this period, Debra focused on her family's wellbeing, balancing her grief and resentment with appreciation for the family she had. Not long after Gary’s death, Debra met Paul, who is HIV-negative. Within a year, they formed a strong partnership and, after following professional medical advice, welcomed a healthy son, who is now 15. Thanks to advances in treatment, Debra leads a healthy and fulfilling life. Supported by Paul, who is unafraid of her diagnosis, she is determined to combat the misconceptions and shame surrounding HIV. Debra insists that she is just a regular mother and woman—and that HIV is only a small part of her life.

Ohechakuaa HIV reheguaha mokõi ary dekada mbohasávo, iména Gary hasyete rire pneumonia rehe 1995-pe. Ha’e omombe'u so oikoha peteĩ sy ha kuña como pesy jeýnte—HIV michĩnte ha’e rekohápe.

article_content: Every day, thousands of children live and work on the streets of cities across Vietnam. Michael Brosowski is working to give many of these children a better future. Through Brosowski’s Blue Dragon Children’s Foundation, over 350 Vietnamese children have received safe shelter and been enrolled in school. The organization operates a network of programs in cities throughout Vietnam and has recently expanded its efforts to combat child trafficking. So far, it has rescued over 100 trafficked children. Brosowski recently spoke with CNN about the challenges that Vietnam’s street children face. CNN: Who are Vietnam’s street kids? Michael Brosowski: When we started out in 2002, the children were mostly boys from rural areas who came to the city to earn money to support their families. Many families could not afford to send all their children to school or provide enough food, so they sent some children to Hanoi to work. These days, most of the children we see are runaways dealing with family problems. Poverty is still a factor, but it’s not the only issue. Often, there are problems like alcoholism or drug use at home, or sometimes a parent has died, and the new step-parent does not want children from the previous marriage. Now, street children in Hanoi are more likely to be there because they feel unwanted at home rather than needing to earn money. CNN: What dangers do street kids face in Vietnam? Brosowski: The dangers are greater now than when we started. There is more gang activity and more cases of trafficking. Families sometimes think boys are safer on the streets, but in reality, they are not. Boys face gangs and risk arrest, and the longer they are on the streets, the more harmful habits they may pick up. Heroin is cheap and easy to get, and there are people trying to get young people addicted. Meanwhile, girls are at risk of exploitation or abuse. We also need to focus on protecting girls. CNN: What are some of the challenges in working with street kids? Brosowski: As rewarding as this work is, it is not easy. I always tell my staff: ‘It’s never the end of the story.’ A child who is struggling today might make positive changes tomorrow, while a child doing well today could backslide. There are times when kids we have helped for a year return and steal from us. That is very hurtful because we invest so much in them. But sometimes those same children come back, apologize, and try to make amends, which shows the impact of our work. See the full story on CNN Hero Michael Brosowski: Giving Vietnam’s street kids a chance. CNN’s Danielle Berger and Alex Zolbert contributed to this report.

Brosowski rembiapo Blue Dragon Children’s Foundation rupive, 350 Vietnamgua mitã rasaiterei oguereko tetã rendágua ha oñemohenda mboʼehao-pe. Ko organización orekóta heta programa opa rupi Vietnam-pe ha koʼág̃a ombaʼapo avei oñorairõ hag̃ua mitã jeporerahaʼi rehe. Upeicha rupi, oguenohẽma 100 rasa mitã jeporerahaʼi vaʼekuégui. Brosowski oñemongeta CNN ndive umi mbaʼe ijetuʼueterei ha omanombáva Vietnam-pe umi mitã okarusu rehe. CNN: Mávapa Vietnam peguá umi mitã okarusu? Michael Brosowski: Róga guive ñepyrũrã, 2002-pe, umi mitã oiko vaʼekue okarusu heta oĩ kuri kuimbaʼýntema, rural guive ouvaʼekue oñemombaʼapo haguã ohupyty hag̃ua plata ojoko hag̃ua iñaranduka ha hoʼu hag̃ua. La familia ndaikatúi omeʼẽ mitãme mboʼehao térã comida, upévare omondo mitã kuimbaʼérape oho hag̃ua Hanoi-pe ombaʼapo. Koʼág̃a, amoña avei vajerekaha. Upe pobreza ndoipurukái peteĩnte; oĩ avei alkoholismo, droga térã peteĩ tavýi, térã peteĩ familiar omanóva ha upéi peteĩ tuja térã sy pyahu ndohayhuvéima umi mitã ouva epyahu guive. Koʼág̃a umi mitã oĩ okarusu reheve ohupytývo ndorrespetái hógape, ndahaʼéi katuete oipota plata joguerekóvo. CNN: Mbaʼépa umi peligro umi mitã ojuhúmava okarusu rehe Vietnam-pe? Brosowski: Koʼág̃a kutueteve umi peligro ñepyrũrãgua ndive. Oĩve karai okarusu ha jeporerahaʼi. Umi familia orovia peteĩteĩ mitã kuimbaʼe ndahasýi che rehe, ha avei okarusu katuete ojeheja rire. Peteĩ mbaʼe opavavete ohasa hína: umi mitã kuimbaʼe okaruse pehónte oñemeʼẽ karai aty guasupe, oñembosakoʼi policía rehe ha okarusu reicorre rehe iñeʼẽ vai. Heróina oĩ barato ha oñeg̃uahẽ porã, oĩ umíva omokyreʼỹséva umi mitã oipuru hag̃ua. Ipotĩ avei ñamboguejy, pórke umi mitã kuñakarai oĩ riesgo de explotación térã abuso rehe. Avei tekotevẽ jahecha mbaʼéichapa ikatu ñangareko mitãkuñare. CNN: Mbaʼéichapa umi oipytyvõva oñemotenonde umi mitã okarusu rehe? Brosowski: Haʼe avei heʼi, ojekuaa ha oreko ijoyvy. Che avañeʼẽ kuña tembiapo rembiapo: ‘Ndaipóri mbaʼeve ipahaʼúva.’ Heta mitã ojapo ivaíva ko árape, ha upéicha omyengovia porã koʼẽrõ, ha avei oĩ mitã oguereko porã hína ha upéi oguata vai. Ára rupi oĩ mitã oñembohasa porã rire peteî ary rire ou jey ha omonda orégui. Ideprovecho ndaje, pórke ore roñehaʼã heta hesekuéra. Ha heta jey umi mitã oúva jey, oñeperdonase ha ohechauka haʼe rei ko tembiapo ore, pe mbaʼe hasy vaʼekue rire ou jey ha ome’ẽ porã. Ehecha pe mombeʼu tuichaiteve CNN Hero Michael Brosowski rehe: Omeʼẽ Vietnam mitã okarusu rehe guarakateʼỹ. CNN-pe Danielle Berger ha Alex Zolbert oipytyvõ ko marandu oñembosakoʼihápe.

article_content: Swansea City clinched their third consecutive Premier League victory with a commanding 3-0 win over West Bromwich Albion at Liberty Stadium. English players Nathan Dyer and Wayne Routledge led the way: Dyer opened the scoring just two minutes in and netted again in the 71st minute, while Routledge added a brilliant volleyed goal in the 24th minute. Midfielder Jonjo Shelvey stood out with dynamic forward runs and accurate passing, displaying improved decision-making from previous games. Swansea controlled the match, rarely troubled by West Brom’s offense. West Brom’s defensive lapses—highlighted by Jonas Olsson’s early slip and errors by Chris Brunt and Craig Dawson—directly led to Swansea’s goals. The visitors created few threats, with Saido Berahino’s shot easily saved by Lukasz Fabianski as one of their best chances. Gylfi Sigurdsson effectively directed Swansea’s attacks, and Dyer was deservedly named Man of the Match. The win again brought attention to England manager Roy Hodgson’s absence, especially given the exceptional performances by English players. Swansea were never in danger as they continued their winning streak, with 20,318 spectators in attendance. Leon Britton remains sidelined with injury for several weeks. Managed by Alan Irvine, West Brom are still searching for their first win this season, with two draws and a loss so far. Swansea’s comprehensive performance underlines their strong start to the Premier League campaign.

Alan Irvine oguereko West Brom rehe, oikotevẽ gueteri iprimer victoria, mokõi empate ha peteĩ perda upe arakõi. Swansea ohechauka ijapu’aka ha oñemotenonde Premier League-pe.

article_content: A 26-year-old Chinese entrepreneur, known in reports as 'Danny,' recounted his frightening encounter with the Boston Marathon bombers when they hijacked his Mercedes SUV late one night. Danny had just parked on Brighton Avenue in Boston when a man in dark clothing, later identified as Tamerlan Tsarnaev, approached, quickly entered his car, and threatened him with a handgun. Tamerlan confessed to Danny that he was responsible for the recent marathon bombing and for killing a police officer in Cambridge. During the carjacking ordeal, Tamerlan and his younger brother, Dzhokhar, forced Danny to drive while discussing both their crimes and everyday topics like music and technology. At one stage, Tamerlan warned Danny not to look at his face and made comments about race. The brothers expressed disappointment over the music options in Danny's car and debated radio stations before settling on playing a CD. After driving for over an hour with the suspects—who eventually transferred their belongings to Danny's vehicle—Danny saw a chance to escape when they stopped at a gas station to refuel. As Dzhokhar went inside to pay and Tamerlan became distracted, Danny managed to slip out and run to a nearby Mobil station, where he asked the clerk to call 911. Authorities credited Danny’s swift escape with helping them locate the stolen Mercedes quickly, which was instrumental in stopping the suspects’ possible plan to go to New York and in triggering the subsequent police shootout in Watertown. Tamerlan was killed in the exchange, and Dzhokhar was found hiding nearby with serious injuries. After the incident, Danny worked with police and federal agents, helping to piece together the timeline between the killing of MIT police officer Sean Collier and the Watertown events. Although he feared for his safety in the aftermath, Danny’s actions are widely acknowledged as playing a key role in ending the Tsarnaev brothers’ rampage.

Danny opyta haimete ijyvy ári Brighton Avenue-pe, Boston-pe, upe jave peteĩ kuimba’e ao hũva—ha’e Tamerlan Tsarnaev—ojupi chupe ha ohechauka peteĩ pistola. article_content: Former Apollo 14 astronaut Edgar Mitchell recently reiterated his belief that extraterrestrial life exists and accused governments, including the United States, of hiding this reality. He made these remarks at the National Press Club following the X-Conference, an event for UFO researchers and activists. Mitchell, who was raised in Roswell—the location of the disputed 1947 UFO crash—shared that locals he knew felt pressured by military authorities to keep silent about their alleged experiences, some even threatening consequences. Over the years, several residents confided their stories to Mitchell, considering him trustworthy because of his background. According to Mitchell, about 10 years ago he was granted a meeting with an unnamed Pentagon official who initially confirmed details related to Roswell but was then denied additional information and later dismissed the story. Mitchell encouraged the public to research UFO encounters, suggesting humans should prepare to become part of a larger interplanetary community. NASA spokesperson Michael Cabbage refuted claims of a cover-up, stating that NASA does not monitor UFOs nor conceal evidence of alien life. Prior Air Force statements linked materials recovered at Roswell to a classified balloon program, not to extraterrestrial activity. Stephen Bassett, who leads the Paradigm Research Group and organized the X-Conference, contended that the government keeps information about UFOs secret due to its highly sensitive and potentially disruptive impact.

article_content: As the chilly November weather sets in, it's the perfect time to stay in and check out the latest streaming releases. The grand finale of Loki Season 2 delivered plenty of surprises, while Gen V—a recent spinoff from Amazon’s The Boys—wrapped up impressively, almost matching the original series. Meanwhile, Invincible returns for its second season, with the newest episode available on Amazon Prime Video starting Friday, November 17th. For something new, keep an eye on a comedy project by Please Don’t Destroy. Narrated by John Goodman and with Conan O’Brien as one of the dads, the special promises plenty of slapstick adventures and laughs and could be a fun pick. Apple TV+ introduces Monarch: Legacy of Monsters, a series starring Kurt Russell and Wyatt Russell as Lee Shaw, following him across decades as the mysteries of Godzilla and Monarch unfold. While previous Godzilla films have had varied success, this series is generating excitement, and new episodes drop weekly. Fans of Scott Pilgrim Vs. The World will be happy to see the original cast return for an animated series based on the graphic novels. With Michael Cera, Mary Elizabeth Winstead, Brie Larson, and others reprising their roles, the show closely follows the books and echoes much of what made the movie a cult favorite. Netflix brings out the final season of The Crown, with Elizabeth Debicki taking on the role of Princess Diana. The first set of episodes is streaming now, and the story will continue in December. Unsure if you should start? This season has drawn quite a bit of interest. On FX/Hulu, Fargo Season 5 is set to premiere, starring Jon Hamm as a sheriff, alongside Juno Temple, Joe Keery, and Jennifer Jason Leigh. Even if the previous season left you undecided, the new cast and story look promising, with the first two episodes arriving this Tuesday. Elsewhere, a long-running TV series is concluding after a much-criticized eighth season. For those still watching, now's the time to see how it all ends. If you're in the mood for a theatrical outing, consider checking out the Hunger Games prequel or The Holdovers—a character-driven drama that looks particularly engaging. With the holidays approaching, a trip to the movies or a great seasonal film might be just what you need. Share your must-watch picks or let us know what we missed on social media this weekend!

article_content: Finland and Estonia announced on Sunday that the Balticconnector undersea gas pipeline between the two countries has been temporarily shut down due to a suspected leak. Gasgrid Finland and Elering, the respective gas system operators, detected an unusual drop in pressure in the pipeline just before 2 a.m. on Sunday, prompting the shutdown of gas flow. Gasgrid Finland stated that based on these observations, there was suspicion of a leak in the offshore section of the pipeline between Finland and Estonia, and that all valves have been closed to stop the leak. The Finnish operator has not specified the cause of the suspected leak and is investigating the situation together with Elering. If the pressure drop is confirmed to be the result of a leak that has damaged the pipeline, repairs could take at least several months depending on the extent of the damage, according to Gasgrid Finland. The article references the September 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions between Germany and Russia, which led to four gas leaks in Nord Stream 1 and 2 and remain unsolved. Gasgrid Finland emphasized that the Finnish gas system remains stable, with supply secured through the Inkoo floating LNG terminal, operated from the support vessel Exemplar at the southern Finnish port of Inkoo. Elering confirmed that gas supply to Estonian consumers is unaffected, as Estonia is now receiving gas from Latvia following Balticconnector’s shutdown. The Balticconnector is a bi-directional pipeline, allowing natural gas to be transferred between Finland and Estonia based on demand. Prior to the shutdown, gas was flowing from Finland to Estonia and then forwarded to Latvia. The offshore portion of the Balticconnector runs 77 kilometers (48 miles) from Inkoo to the Estonian port of Paldiski. The pipeline began commercial operations in early 2020. Finland’s Minister of Climate and the Environment, Kai Mykkänen, assured that the gas system’s stability is not immediately compromised by the disruption, and investigations into the cause are ongoing. Finland and Estonia, both EU and NATO members, have not imported Russian oil or gas since 2022 as part of sanctions following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

Kai Mykkänen, ministro Finlandgua clima ha ambiente rehegua, ombojerovia gas sistema gueteri orekopa estabilidad, ohechakuaa ojejapohína investigación rehe. article_content: Three members of the Russian punk band Pussy Riot—Nadezhda Tolokonnikova (23), Maria Alyokhina (24), and Yekaterina Samutsevich (29)—were sentenced to two years in prison by a Moscow court after performing a protest song criticizing President Vladimir Putin inside Moscow's Christ Savior Cathedral in February. Wearing neon masks, the group sang 'Mother Mary please drive Putin away,' a phrase now associated with their movement. The verdict attracted international attention and widespread support on social media. High-profile figures such as Paul McCartney, Bianca Jagger, Robert Smith of The Cure, and actress Mischa Barton publicly expressed their support for Pussy Riot, calling for greater freedom of expression in Russia. Paul McCartney posted his support on Twitter, pledging solidarity to the group and artistic freedom, while Mischa Barton also tweeted her shock at the sentencing, referencing her time in Moscow. Supporters organized protests outside Russian embassies in Europe and the United States, often wearing balaclavas and sharing updates and photos on social media. Amnesty UK described the prison sentence as a setback for freedom of expression and called for demonstrations. Some citizens in Moscow opposed Pussy Riot, with anti-Pussy Riot demonstrators reportedly chanting insults. Civil activist Oleg Kozlovsky noted the divided response. In Kiev, the feminist activist group Femen protested by cutting down an Orthodox cross dedicated to victims of political repression. They threatened further actions if the sentencing of Russian activists continued. Russian opposition leader and former world chess champion Garry Kasparov was reportedly detained and assaulted by authorities during demonstrations at the courthouse, according to his assistants. Throughout these events, messages of support for Pussy Riot continued to circulate online, with activists and journalists like Jessica Haworth emphasizing the importance of freedom of speech and sharing rally information.

article_content: The United Nations Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC) reported Thursday that Latin America's growing specialization in exports to China—particularly in oil and mining—shows a 'worrying' pattern. ECLAC cautioned that as China advances toward energy decarbonization, core Latin American exports like oil may become vulnerable. Trade between Latin America and China has surged, reaching nearly $500 billion last year from about $14 billion in 2000. However, this boom is largely limited to a narrow range of commodities. The report indicates a 'mixed picture' for Latin America's trade with China. While there are risks, exports such as copper and lithium, especially important for electric vehicle batteries, could experience increased demand. Chile and Peru remain the world's leading copper producers, while South America hosts the 'Lithium Triangle'—Chile, Argentina, and Bolivia. Agriculture and livestock, mainly soybeans and beef, account for about 20% of Latin American exports to China. ECLAC notes this industry could further boost trade in the short term. With its significant natural and water resources, Latin America is well-placed to supply China with high-quality, safe food, ECLAC observed. The region’s role could become more vital as U.S.–China tensions and the war in Ukraine continue to affect global supply chains. China has been a net food importer since 2004 and already depends heavily on Latin America—particularly Brazil—for goods such as cane sugar, soybean oil, cherries, shrimp, and frozen beef. ECLAC also noted China's expanding role in Latin America's manufacturing sector has brought 'conflicting effects.' While households now enjoy greater access to manufactured goods, domestic production has suffered, negatively impacting local industries and jobs.

article_content: Marian Wright Edelman, president of the Children's Defense Fund, has dedicated her career to championing children's rights, particularly those suffering due to poverty and structural injustice. As the first black woman to join the Mississippi bar and a respected civil rights advocate, Edelman points out that many black children in America are born into difficult circumstances. She contends that the rising rates of incarceration represent a new form of segregation, particularly hurting poor children of color. Many are born without needed prenatal care, may have low birth weights, and are raised by single mothers with scarce resources. These factors combine, elevating their risk of later involvement in the criminal justice system. Edelman describes this as America's 'pipeline to prison.' According to national statistics, one in three black boys and one in seventeen black girls born in 2001 may be incarcerated during their lives. She urges immediate efforts to stop the criminalization of children and to address racial inequities in youth and adult justice systems. To address these challenges, Edelman supports stronger preventive care, mental health resources, early learning initiatives like Early Head Start, and comprehensive education. She insists that preparing every child for the modern economy is essential for progressing beyond past injustices and ensuring opportunity. Edelman highlights notable leaders such as Geoffrey Canada of the Harlem Children’s Zone, who employs an integrated educational and social program across Central Harlem. Covering 97 blocks, the HCZ provides services from early childhood to college preparation, prioritizing early support and a strong community network. Evidence indicates that this comprehensive approach helps reduce achievement gaps for black students. She also acknowledges Connie Rice, co-founder of the Advancement Project, who focuses on educational reform and violence prevention in Los Angeles. Rice has led creative legal actions, attaining significant funding for schools in need, and persistently advocates for systemic change to help poor children of color. Edelman calls on communities to support leaders like Canada and Rice, emphasizing that issues like systemic inequality, child poverty, and the school-to-prison pipeline are products of policy choices that can be changed through collective leadership and action. These reflections present Edelman's own perspective and challenge society to take responsibility for protecting all children’s futures.

Edelman, peteĩha kuña hũva ojeguerekóva Mississippi bar-pe, oikundaha avei hetã civil rights rehehápe, omohesakã heta mitã hũ oikeha haipyre ivaípe ojeguerekóva ypy guive. Ha’e he’i mba’e vai pyahuha pe oike hag̃ua kárselpe, ojehejaséva apartheid reko pyahu, ombohasa asy hetave mitã imboriahu ha color-gua. Heta mitã oikovy peteĩ madre sy mitã-ramo, rehegua sa’ive ayuda rehe, ndohupytyri cuidado prenatal, ha ikatu oguereko sobrepeso térã karẽ. Ko’ã mba’e ombohasave ivaíva ojupekuéra rehe ha oike hag̃ua heko vaihápe justicia penal-pe. Edelman ohenói ko proceso-pe pipeline to prison Estados Unidos-pe. Estadística ohechauka peteĩ mokõi paapyha mbohapy mitã kuimba’e ha peteĩ paapyha pokõi mitã kuña, oñemoñava’ekue 2001-pe, oĩhague peligro oike hag̃ua cárceles-pegua hekovia pukukuévo. Ha’e ojerure tapiaite máva guive oipytyvõ hag̃ua oñembojo’áva criminalización rehe mitãnguéra renda rehe ha oñembohape hag̃ua igualdad racial sistema justicia juvenil ha adulto-pe. Oĩrõ hag̃ua solución, Edelman ombojeroviave prevención rehe, ayuda salud mental rehegua, programa mitãguéra pequeña-pegua hi’ãva ichupekuéra oike estudio ha educación completa rehe. Omoĩ mba’e porãve omomba’eguasu rehekombo’e katupyry rehe siglo XXI-pe, ojeguereko hag̃ua futura ore mitãguéra rehe. Omomba’e avei Geoffrey Canada, Harlem Children’s Zone motenondehára, omohu’ã peteĩ sistema educación ha apoyo social Central Harlem 97-block-pe. Oguereko servicio mitãnguéra ypy guive colegio ha formación profesional peve. Oî evidencia omyesakã método comprehensive rehe, omomichĩha achievement gap mitã hũ ha sa’yju apytépe. Kóva avei Connie Rice, Advancement Project motenondehára, oipytyvõ reforma educativa ha violencia prevención rehe Los Ángeles-pe. Rice oisãmbyhýkuri acción legal pyahu, orekóva heta apoyo monetario escuela iky’aveva rehe, omba’apo tapiaite oike hag̃ua cambio real umi mitã imboriahu color-guápe. Edelman ohenói opavave-pe oipytyvõ hag̃ua koichagua líder rembiapo, ohechauka pe mboriahu, injusticia sistema ha pipeline-to-prison, ha’eha mba’e política ojapo, ojehecha porã ikatuha ojejavy liderazgo fuerte rehe. Ko ñe’ẽ ha’e Edelman mba’e, ha ombohape sociedad-pe ombohape hag̃ua futuro iporãva opavave mitãme.

article_content: A Tennessee judge is set to decide today whether Beau, a golden retriever-German Shepherd mix, will be euthanized. City officials say Beau killed a duck and reportedly acted aggressively toward a young boy in Dyersburg two months ago. Beau’s owner, Danny Higgins, who was not at home during the incident, was granted a 30-day delay on the euthanasia order on October 21, which expires today. The judge's ruling will determine Beau's fate. Beau, a two-year-old golden retriever and white German Shepherd mix with no prior history of aggression, was ordered to be put down after the duck incident. More than 570,000 people have signed a petition to prevent Beau’s euthanasia. Danny Higgins has cared for Beau since he was a puppy. Since September, Beau has been held at the Dyersburg Humane Society. Mr. Higgins said, 'My attorneys tell me that we will go to the Supreme Court if we have to. He is not vicious. I don’t want that label on him.' Earlier hearings permitted Higgins to keep Beau if he complied with the city’s vicious dog ordinance, but Higgins says he cannot afford to meet those requirements. Another option is to have Beau adopted in another state, but Higgins does not want to give up his dog. Police responded to Higgins’ trailer park home on September 19, 2014, after the reported incident around 6:20 p.m. An eight-year-old boy claimed Beau killed his duck and tried to attack him. Police officers also described Beau as aggressive when they arrived. Since then, Beau has been kept at the Humane Society. Beau’s case has gained national attention, with a website ‘Please Help Beau’ and a change.org petition attracting significant support. The associated Facebook page has nearly 60,000 likes. Golden retrievers are generally known for their gentle temperament.

article_content: The Metropolitan Police Department and U.S. Secret Service are investigating an agent-involved shooting after up to three people allegedly tried to break into a government vehicle outside the Georgetown residence of President Joe Biden’s granddaughter, Naomi Biden, according to sources familiar with the matter. A Secret Service spokesperson did not confirm the identity of the protectee but stated that, late Sunday night in Washington, D.C.’s Georgetown neighborhood, agents encountered up to three individuals breaking a window on a parked, unoccupied government vehicle. "During this encounter, a federal agent discharged a service weapon, and it is believed that no one was struck," the spokesperson said. "The offenders immediately fled in a red vehicle and a regional lookout was issued to supporting units. No protectees were ever in danger, and the incident is being investigated by the D.C. Metropolitan Police Department and the Secret Service." It is unclear if Naomi Biden heard what happened at the time, but sources say she was informed about the incident later. In a statement, the Metropolitan Police Department said, "Second District officers and MPD Internal Affairs were on scene assisting the U.S. Secret Service. We have no further information at this time." On Monday evening, the department provided an update: "The officer-involved shooting incident remains under investigation by the Metropolitan Police Department Internal Affairs Division’s Force Investigation Team, which examines all law enforcement shootings in the District. article_content: Google and Match Group, the owner of Tinder, have reached a settlement regarding the Play Store's billing policies, according to TechCrunch. Under this agreement, Match is required to provide both its own payment system and the Google Play billing option, giving users the freedom to choose. This 'user choice billing' feature must be implemented on the Play Store by March 31, 2024. In addition, Match Group announced it will pay lower commission rates to Google, with the percentages dropping from 15% and 30% to 11% and 20%, depending on the transaction. This settlement resolves the legal dispute between Match Group and Google, which stemmed from Google's 30% developer fee and mandatory use of its payment platform. Match and other companies had sought alternatives to avoid these charges. However, Google’s legal challenges persist. Epic Games, the company behind Fortnite, continues its lawsuit against Google. Epic CEO Tim Sweeney has publicly rejected Google's updated 'user choice billing' system, describing it as still too restrictive and asserting that Google continues to monitor and charge for transactions made between users and developers. Epic’s conflict began when it offered its in-game currency, V-Bucks, for purchase outside Google’s system, resulting in Fortnite being removed from the Play Store. Epic argues that Google’s policies force developers to choose between expensive fees and difficult technical workarounds to avoid using the Play Store. As the Epic Games versus Google trial is set for November 6, the result could affect developers and app store practices across the industry.

article_content: MEXICO CITY—Mexican officials have imposed severe, months-long cuts to Mexico City's water supply, starting at midnight Friday, just a month after initial restrictions began as drought conditions dry the city's reservoirs. The Mexican National Water Commission and the city's mayor announced these measures at a news conference, but updates were shared on social media only four hours before implementation. Exceptionally low rainfall has reduced the Cutzamala system—Mexico City's main water source, a network of three reservoirs serving over 20 million residents—to historic lows. The system now holds 44% less water than is typical for this time of year. Officials first cut water from the Cutzamala system by about 8% on October 17. The latest cuts are more drastic, reducing system flow by an additional 25%. Twelve boroughs, primarily in the western part of the city, will experience lower water pressure until the restrictions are lifted. Authorities have not provided an end date, stating only that the measures will last 'the next few months.' The rainy season, which usually refills reservoirs, is not expected until around May. Mexico has never before implemented restrictions this strict or prolonged due to drought. Previous, worse cuts were linked to repairs or labor actions, and typically resolved within days. Officials attribute the crisis to El Niño and recent heatwaves, but note that droughts have intensified over the past four years, gradually lowering reservoir levels. Studies indicate climate change may intensify El Niño, resulting in periods of reduced rainfall. 'The country has been subjected to extreme weather phenomena, and the Cutzamala System is no exception,' said Germán Arturo Martínez Santoyo, head of the water commission. Mexico received 25% less rainfall this year than the 30-year average. More than three-quarters of the country, and about 93% of the Valley of Mexico, are in drought conditions. Officials announced plans for three new water wells, upgrades to 58 existing wells, and ongoing work on a new treatment plant at the Madin reservoir, northwest of the city. However, experts caution that groundwater levels are already severely depleted. Rafael Carmona Paredes, Mexico City's chief water official, called on residents to adopt water conservation habits, emphasizing shared responsibility in facing the crisis.

article_content: Miles Scott, a five-year-old cancer patient, dreamed of becoming a real-life superhero. On a remarkable day in San Francisco, with the help of thousands—including President Barack Obama—his dream came true as he became 'Batkid.' Around 10,000 people lined the streets as San Francisco transformed into Gotham City, allowing Miles to take on Batman’s iconic foes, The Penguin and The Riddler. Accompanied by a Batmobile, police motorcycle escort, and news helicopters, Batkid 'saved the city' to the delight of spectators. A special edition of The San Francisco Chronicle proclaimed, 'Batkid Saves City,' while President Obama sent a congratulatory video message: 'Way to go, Miles. Way to save Gotham!' At City Hall, Mayor Ed Lee presented Miles with a giant chocolate key to the city as crowds cheered. The event was organized by the Make-A-Wish Foundation after Miles’s mother, Natalie, wrote to them about her son's wish to fight crime like Batman. Miles originally believed he was visiting San Francisco to receive a Batman costume, but was surprised with the city-wide adventure. Police Chief Greg Suhr helped launch Batkid’s missions by recording calls for help, praising the community spirit: 'Everyone joined together to make this young boy’s dream come true.' The US Attorney’s Office even issued a playful ‘indictment’ against the villains. Miles’s mother, Natalie, described the day as unforgettable, moved to tears by the generosity and kindness shown to her son. Having battled leukemia since he was 18 months old, Miles recently completed his final surgery and is now in remission. 'This day marks the end of more than three years of difficult treatment,' said Mrs. Scott. 'He is our superhero.' Eric Johnson, who played Batman alongside Miles, called him a mild-mannered kid who transforms with the mask. Together, they made a city believe in heroes.

article_content: The battle against high inflation is nearly over, which could soon prompt the Federal Reserve to start lowering interest rates, according to Wharton professor Jeremy Siegel. He noted the recent decline in inflation, with consumer prices rising just 3.2% year over year in October—a drop from September's 3.7%. Although inflation remains above the Fed's 2% target, Siegel told CNBC that 'it's all clear on the inflation front.' Siegel believes the next move by the Fed is likely a rate cut, even without a recession, due to the ongoing economic slowdown. 'It could happen as early as March of next year,' he said, adding that he wants Fed Chair Powell to 'un-invert this curve,' referencing the 2-10 Treasury yield curve, a key recession indicator that signals risk when short-term rates exceed long-term rates. The Federal Reserve has raised short-term interest rates by 525 basis points over the past year, a move Siegel previously warned could spark a recession. However, the US economy has proven resilient, with GDP surging 4.9% last quarter despite tighter financial conditions. Some experts caution against lowering rates too early, warning that it could lead to a surge in prices later and potentially create a crisis similar to the stagflation of the 1970s. Siegel argues that the current situation is different because the Fed is no longer injecting liquidity and is reducing its balance sheet. He also suggests that waiting too long to lower rates could be riskier now, as the economy is already slowing down. Recent data shows signs of softening: job growth slowed in October, and retail spending declined for the first time since March, indicating possible weakness among US consumers. Meanwhile, Wall Street's confidence in a soft landing has increased as inflation continues to decrease. Goldman Sachs has cut its estimated recession odds for next year to just 15%. Bank of America, which previously anticipated a mild recession, has improved its outlook and now sees the US economy heading for a soft landing.

Ha'e ohechauka avei inflación oguejy hague, og̃uahẽvo 3.2% octubre-pe, oguerekova'ekue septiembre-pe 3.7%. article_content: A Michigan man has defied the odds by winning large lottery prizes twice within two years. Officials report that Joseph Palmarchuk, 66, of Mecosta County, won a $1.35 million jackpot in Michigan's Classic Lotto 47 game on Wednesday. Just two years earlier, Palmarchuk also won $1 million in a lottery game in Tennessee. Joe Palmarchuk and his wife Phillis celebrated their latest windfall together. The retired couple moved from Tennessee to Mecosta County, north of Grand Rapids, in 2011 to be closer to family. Six months after relocating, Palmarchuk learned he had won $1 million in a second-chance Tennessee lottery draw. "I moved to be close to family so they could help take care of me," Palmarchuk said in 2011. "Now I can help take care of them!" Palmarchuk is the father of seven, grandfather to 23, and great-grandfather to four. He says he enjoys buying lottery tickets that were originally set aside as errors by retailers and believes his good fortune is a result of karma. Palmarchuk predicts he will win again within the next year, though likely not another million-dollar jackpot. "I play the lottery several times every day," Palmarchuk told local news. "I've learned that it works—you can't win if you don't have a ticket." He expects any next win to be smaller but hopes to win Powerball or Mega Millions in the coming years. The Palmarchuks plan to use their winnings to help family, travel in their RV, and buy a home in a warmer state to avoid Michigan winters. Joe Palmarchuk says he will keep playing the lottery every day.

article_content: Emily Hartridge has earned a dedicated fan base for her witty '10 reasons why' videos, in which she unpacks various aspects of young adult life with humor and candor. Over 35,000 fans tune in to her YouTube channel, where she tackles everything from sibling dynamics to awkward holidays. Her newest video spotlights the perks of dating older women—affectionately called 'cougars.' With her friend George acting as her boyfriend, Emily humorously outlines why dating a cougar might appeal to men. Reflecting on her own brief experience dating someone a couple of years younger, she references pop culture like American Pie’s Stifler’s mom to keep things light. Emily lists reasons such as greater confidence, emotional independence, and life experience as why cougars make attractive partners. She also jokes that older women are less likely to track your online activity, adding that their lower dependence on others can actually make them more caring in relationships. She highlights that wisdom and self-assuredness tend to equal less relationship drama, more assertiveness, and, often, a better grasp of what they want from life. Plus, Emily adds, they might even be more skilled in the bedroom. Other playful points include not having to watch teen movies together and the bonus of possibly making your friends jealous. Through her skits and the use of a digital aging app, Emily combines honesty with self-deprecating humor, encouraging viewers to enjoy the quirks and realities of dating across age gaps. By blending playful mockery with real talk, Emily’s video invites her audience to laugh and reflect on modern dating dynamics.

article_content: NBA legend Shaquille O’Neal has voiced his support for New Jersey Governor Chris Christie’s re-election, appearing in a new TV commercial. In the 30-second spot, aired just before the NBA season and the first anniversary of Hurricane Sandy, O'Neal calls Christie a 'great man,' saying he doesn’t usually support politicians, but Christie is an exception. O’Neal highlights Christie’s work on job creation in cities, education improvements like increased funding, school choice, and merit pay for outstanding teachers. He encourages viewers to join him in backing Christie for another term as governor. Although Christie is strongly favored to win the upcoming November 5 election, many believe Shaq’s endorsement could further boost his appeal, especially with minority and Democratic-leaning voters. Shaq, a Newark native who now lives in Florida, has previously collaborated with Christie on community efforts, including gun buyback programs and youth initiatives, and acts as a youth ambassador in New Jersey. Christie’s campaign has emphasized reaching out to African American and other minority voters, resulting in much higher approval ratings compared to when he first ran in 2009. Recent polls show a majority of non-white voters approve of Christie’s performance. The governor has also gathered support from prominent African American leaders and some Democrats, particularly due to his backing for school choice and the Opportunity Scholarship Act—a proposed scholarship pilot for low-income students—that was ultimately blocked by state Democrats. Still, the article notes that not all celebrity endorsements work out, referencing Clint Eastwood’s controversial speech at the 2012 Republican National Convention as a recent example. Overall, Shaq’s endorsement highlights Christie's efforts to build bridges across party and community lines.

article_content: Reverend George Gebauer described homosexuality as a ‘medical issue’, attributing it to a hormone imbalance. A Church of England vicar initially refused to baptize a baby boy because both of his lesbian parents wished to be recognized as his mother. Aimi Leggett, 25, and her civil partner Victoria, 22, wanted to christen their one-year-old son Alfie. However, Reverend Gebauer told them it was ‘impossible’ for Alfie to have two mothers listed, prompting intervention by his archdeacon to allow the ceremony. Reverend Gebauer, 87, from St Mary’s Church in Warsash, Hampshire, claimed he felt sorry for gay people, considering them to be ‘medically imbalanced’. He refused to conduct the baptism, saying it might be illegal to list two mothers. The couple left the meeting after he suggested one of them be listed as godmother, since the certificate only provisioned space for one mother and one father. Aimi, Alfie’s birth mother, stated: ‘There was no way one of us was going to be listed as the godparent. We are both Alfie's mum. Rev Gebauer told us that no child could have parents of the same sex or two mothers. He questioned us for around ten to fifteen minutes about why we wanted Alfie baptized.’ Aimi continued: ‘I’m baptized Church of England and Victoria is Catholic. We want Alfie to have a Christian upbringing like we did. We even said to the Reverend: “Do you want Alfie to be ashamed of his family? He’s not gay; we are, and what we do is our choice.”’ Aimi and Victoria, who reside in Fareham, had arranged the baptism with Rev Andy Norris, who has since left. Retired vicars, including Rev Gebauer, are currently officiating at St Mary’s Church until a new vicar is appointed. The couple chose St Mary’s Church because Aimi was baptized there and her parents were married there. Rev Gebauer, a vicar for forty years, insisted sexuality was not an issue and would baptize Alfie if only one mother was listed. He said, ‘They insisted on being registered as both mums and refused to compromise. The register makes no provision for two mothers. We’ve tried to accommodate this family, but I believe it’s illegal to list them both as mother. The soul of the boy is the most important thing, but we are at an impasse.’ Victoria said, ‘It’s hard not to be discouraged by our experience. We were given approval, then it was revoked. We didn’t expect this.’ In a last-minute decision, the Ven Gavin Collins, Archdeacon of the Meon, intervened. He confirmed the christening could proceed with both women named as mother. ‘We have resolved the legal issue. Victoria has full legal co-parental responsibility for Alfie, so both their details can be entered as mother and mother in the baptism register.’ He expressed his pleasure at the outcome and welcomed the family and their friends to the church. Aimi’s mother, Donna Leggett, 44, reported that the church apologized and confirmed the baptism would go ahead, expressing relief but also concern that it should not have reached this point.

article_content: The United States and China are the world's two largest economies, together accounting for more than 40% of global goods and services. When these two nations clash economically, as they have for the past five years, the rest of the world also feels the impact. Conversely, when U.S. and Chinese leaders meet—such as the planned summit this week between Presidents Joe Biden and Xi Jinping—the outcome can affect the global economy. The global economy could benefit from reduced tensions between the U.S. and China. Since 2020, ongoing crises—including the COVID-19 pandemic, high inflation, rising interest rates, and conflicts in Ukraine and Gaza—have strained worldwide growth. The International Monetary Fund expects the global economy to grow by just 3% this year and 2.9% in 2024. Eswar Prasad, a trade policy professor at Cornell University, notes that: 'Having the world’s two largest economies at odds at such a turbulent time worsens the effects of the various geopolitical shocks to the global economy.' There is hope that the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, beginning Sunday in San Francisco, can cool some of these tensions. The event brings together 21 Pacific Rim nations representing 40% of the global population and nearly half of global trade. The highlight will be a meeting between Biden and Xi on Wednesday, marking their first direct conversation in a year marked by increased friction. The White House has managed expectations, downplaying chances for breakthroughs. Still, Prasad suggests that simply preventing further deterioration in the U.S.-China relationship would count as a success. Years of strained U.S.-China trade relations culminated in 2018 with a trade war initiated by President Donald Trump. The Trump administration argued that China violated commitments from its 2001 World Trade Organization accession, particularly regarding market access for foreign companies. In response to China’s trade practices and efforts to overtake U.S. tech supremacy, the U.S. imposed tariffs on Chinese imports. Many experts supported the administration’s concerns about alleged cyberespionage and forced technology transfers. China retaliated with its own tariffs, making U.S. goods more expensive for Chinese buyers. Senator Mark Warner, chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, emphasized the need for continued pressure on China regarding intellectual property theft and for collaborating with regional allies. He highlighted that national security now also depends on technological dominance, including AI and advanced telecommunications. When President Biden took office in 2021, he retained much of Trump’s trade policy, including tariffs. U.S. tariffs on Chinese imports have climbed to over 19%, up from 3% before the trade war, while China’s tariffs on U.S. goods rose to 21%, from 8%. Biden’s economic strategy includes reducing U.S. reliance on Chinese manufacturing—particularly after COVID-19 exposed vulnerabilities—and strengthening partnerships with other Asian countries, including a 2022 economic framework with 14 Indo-Pacific nations. Trade tensions have continued and, in some respects, intensified. The U.S. has expanded export controls to restrict China's access to advanced computer chips and associated equipment. In response, China now requires government licenses to export gallium and germanium, key metals for chips and solar cells. Chinese authorities have also increased scrutiny of foreign businesses, raiding offices of U.S. consulting firms and investigating semiconductor firms. Some analysts now talk of 'decoupling' between the two economies. Through September, U.S. imports of Chinese goods dropped 24% compared to the same period in 2022. Many countries find themselves caught in the middle, wishing to trade with both the U.S. and China. The IMF warns that global economic ‘fragmentation’ poses serious risks. It estimates that higher trade barriers could reduce global economic output by $7.4 trillion after adjustment. Trade restrictions are rising: in 2022, countries put in place nearly 3,000 new trade barriers, up from fewer than 1,000 in 2019. The IMF forecasts global trade will grow just 0.9% this year and 3.5% in 2024, down from a 4.9% annual average between 2000 and 2019. The Biden administration states it does not aim to undermine China's economy. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen, meeting with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in San Francisco, said both nations seek 'a level playing field and ongoing, meaningful, and mutually beneficial economic relations.' China faces internal economic challenges: a collapsing real estate sector, high youth unemployment, and declining consumer confidence. Government moves against foreign companies have worried international investors. Wendy Cutler of the Asia Society Institute notes that with China’s serious headwinds and some U.S. firms leaving, Xi Jinping must reassure investors that China remains a viable business destination—an increasingly difficult task. Tensions between China and the U.S. extend beyond trade. Under President Xi, China’s government has been criticized for its approach in Hong Kong and Xinjiang, assertive territorial claims in Asia, border clashes with India, and pressure on Taiwan and neighbors in the South China Sea. U.S.-China tensions may escalate further with upcoming elections in Taiwan and the United States—a time when China skepticism is one of the few bipartisan issues in American politics. China's global reputation has suffered: a Pew Research Center survey of 24 countries found the U.S. is viewed more favorably than China in all but Kenya and Nigeria. Still, some remain optimistic about possible changes. U.S. Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi said at a Washington think tank that Xi has shown flexibility before, such as reversing the zero-COVID policy. He urged openness to positive developments while remaining vigilant.

article_content: The Cartier Love bracelet, once nicknamed the ‘slave bracelet,’ is rumored to have been inspired by the medieval chastity belt, though this origin is unconfirmed. Still, the bangle has become a sought-after accessory among celebrities. Hollywood figures such as Lindsay Lohan and Katie Holmes have worn the Cartier Love bracelet, and last week Pippa Middleton was seen at Cartier’s Bond Street store replacing her 18-carat gold bangle. Launched in 1969 by designer Aldo Cipullo, the Cartier Love bracelet was intended as a gift for one’s loved one, fastened with screws to symbolize lasting commitment. Chloe Green, daughter of Topshop owner Sir Philip Green, owns six Love bracelets, sometimes wearing several at once. Cartier, a favorite among many prominent individuals including the Duchess of Cambridge, designed the bracelet to be secured by two screws. It is reported that Pippa Middleton, who is in a relationship with financier Nico Jackson, lost her original bangle when the screws came loose. A replacement screw can cost up to £245, while the bracelets themselves range from £4,450 to £39,900 for diamond-studded bespoke designs. Reportedly, Pippa received a replacement as a gift from Cartier. Celebrities such as Lindsay Lohan and Katie Holmes are fans of the bracelet, which ranges in price from £4,000 to £40,000. Cilla Black was fortunate when burglars left her Love bracelet untouched during a break-in. Tom Cruise reportedly purchased an 18-carat gold Love bracelet for Katie Holmes after the birth of their daughter Suri in 2006. Estee Lauder executive Leonard Lauder also gave a Love bracelet to actress Elizabeth Hurley as a token of his regard. Now marking its 45th anniversary, the Love bracelet was created by Italian designer Aldo Cipullo in 1969. Cipullo drew inspiration from historical legends, including the story of men securing fidelity with iron chastity belts while away at war. His design captures the idea of a cherished, committed relationship. Cipullo once said, 'Love has become too commercial, yet life without love is nothing – a fat zero. What modern people want are love symbols that look semi-permanent – or, at least, require a trick to remove. After all, love symbols should suggest an everlasting quality.' Initially, Cartier enforced a rule that customers could only buy a Love bracelet as a gift for another person, a policy that has since ended. The company presented bracelets to 25 notable couples, including Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton, at a ceremony in its New York boutique. Each couple fastened the bracelet on each other’s wrist before exchanging screwdrivers. To ensure authenticity, Cartier lent a pink-gold diamond Love bracelet to the BBC for its 2013 film Burton and Taylor. As the bracelet’s popularity grew, it appeared on the wrists of many celebrities including Nancy and Frank Sinatra, Joan Collins, Princess Diana, Jane Seymour, Elton John, Jennifer Aniston, Angelina Jolie, and Rosie Huntington-Whiteley. The Love collection expanded to include diamond bracelets, rings, cufflinks, and earrings. For some, the bracelet became a measure of commitment, sometimes as meaningful as an engagement. Cartier currently lists 16 lockable bracelets available in yellow, pink, or white gold, with some designs featuring sapphires, garnets, and amethysts. The bracelets have also been sold at prestigious auctions such as Christie’s and Bonhams. In 1998, Sotheby’s auctioned two gold Cartier bracelets formerly owned by the Duke of Windsor and Wallis Simpson, achieving more than three times the estimated value. Although intended to represent eternal love, the bracelet can be removed with a mini screwdriver sold with each purchase. Tamara Ecclestone famously returned two diamond Love bracelets to her former boyfriend Omar Khyami after their breakup. Ultimately, anyone reconsidering can simply unlock the bracelet using the screwdriver.

article_content: Macquarie Group's half-year profit dropped to its lowest level in three years as costs rose and the company reported fewer asset sales, especially in green energy. However, Macquarie says it expects better performance in the second half and has announced a A$2 billion ($1.29 billion) share buyback. The first-half 2024 financial results, announced on Friday, marked an unusual miss for the Australian firm, which operates globally across retail banking, offshore wind, and commodity trading. This is the steepest first-half profit drop in over a decade for Macquarie. In the previous year, Macquarie benefited from 'exceptional conditions' in commodity trading and asset management due to energy market volatility and favorable circumstances for asset sales, according to Chief Financial Officer Alex Harvey. 'We knew those circumstances were exceptional and did not expect them to continue into 2024,' he told Reuters. Macquarie had already reduced its earnings forecasts twice since announcing record results in May 2023. The 39% decline in net profit to A$1.42 billion for the half ended September 30 fell short of the A$1.77 billion consensus estimate compiled by Citi. Shares fell as much as 3% in early trading but recovered to close 1.8% higher, outperforming the Australian benchmark's 1.1% gain. The A$892 billion asset management division saw profits fall 71% to A$407 million, as costs increased and there were fewer sales amid weaker market conditions following several large deals last year. The company retained much of its green asset portfolio, with some earmarked for a new fund and others for future sales. Chief Executive Shemara Wikramanayake told investors that Macquarie expects to sell these assets without significant discounts and to avoid the write-downs faced by operators caught between fixed-price contracts from 2020-2021 and later inflation. 'We are comfortable our portfolio is different from those with recent large write-offs,' she said on the earnings call. 'These are operating assets with major power purchase agreements generating revenue, and there is ongoing interest.' Macquarie expects asset management division income to rebound in the second half to around A$940 million, matching last year's figure. Profits also fell in the commodities and global markets segment, down 31% to A$1.4 billion, as energy markets normalized after volatility from Russia's attack on Ukraine and extreme North American weather. Wikramanayake told Reuters that energy markets have yet to react to the Israel-Hamas conflict, but the company is watching for wider effects in the Middle East and oil sectors. Despite the weaker result, Macquarie's board approved a share buyback of up to A$2 billion and declared an interim dividend of A$2.55 per share, citing its ability to return excess capital to investors. Investment bank Barrenjoey called the result 'disappointing' and expects rising costs in staffing, technology, and regulation could lead to earnings downgrades of 5% to 10%. Fees and commissions at Macquarie Capital matched the previous comparable period, but profit fell 28% to A$430 million. The division now expects full-year transaction activity in line with last year, rather than its earlier forecast for higher activity. The banking and financial services division, which includes Australia's fifth-largest retail mortgage business, was a bright spot, with earnings up 10% to A$638 million due to loan growth and improved margins. (Exchange rate: $1 USD = 1.5550 AUD)

article_content: Former Formula One world champion Kimi Raikkonen is looking forward to his return to F1 next season after signing a two-year contract with the newly renamed Lotus team in November. Raikkonen won the drivers' title in 2007 with Ferrari before leaving the sport in 2009 to compete in the World Rally Championship and NASCAR. "There has been quite a bit of talk in the media about my comeback and plenty of rumors," the 32-year-old told the UK-based team's website. "For me, returning to Formula One is a positive move, and I hope it will be good for the team and the fans as well." Raikkonen brings extensive F1 experience, having started 156 grands prix over eight seasons with Sauber, McLaren, and Ferrari. He continues to enjoy preparing the car for the challenging season ahead. "I love this time of year at the factory," he said. "There's a real buzz around the new car. Every department is working flat out to make sure everything is ready on time. You can really feel everyone's dedication, and it's great to be part of that. You spend so much time in the car, so getting the seating position exactly right is crucial. I'd rather focus on perfecting it now because there are so many races in the season. Getting it right the first time is essential." Raikkonen and French driver Romain Grosjean will form a new driver pairing for Lotus, replacing Bruno Senna of Brazil and Vitaly Petrov of Russia. This will be Lotus' first year under the legendary name after previously racing as Renault and then as Lotus Renault when the French manufacturer reduced its F1 involvement. This season will feature six world champions, including Raikkonen, Red Bull's Sebastian Vettel, Mercedes' Michael Schumacher, Ferrari's Fernando Alonso, and McLaren's Lewis Hamilton and Jenson Button. The season-opening Australian Grand Prix takes place at Melbourne's Albert Park on March 18. In other motorsport news, the sixth stage of the Dakar Rally was halted on Friday due to summer snow in the Andes. Competitors were supposed to complete a 394km route from Fiambala in Argentina to Copiapo in Chile, including 247km of special timed sections, but the stage was called off after the border was closed. "Due to severe weather continuing over the Andes, Chilean authorities were forced to close the Paso de San Francisco, which sits at 4,700 meters, for the night," according to a statement on the official Dakar Rally website. The event will resume Saturday in Copiapo with the seventh stage, featuring 573km (419km of timed special sections). France's Stephane Peterhansel and Cyril Despres lead the car and bike categories respectively in the 14-day endurance rally.

article_content: Owen Paterson, the UK's Environment Secretary, believes that public resistance to genetically modified (GM) foods has eased and supports growing and producing GM crops domestically. He argues that adopting GM technology would lower food prices, making life easier for consumers struggling with costs. Paterson also points out that the majority of animal feed in the UK already contains GM material and that consumers have generally not objected—since products from animals fed GM feed are indistinguishable from others. Paterson highlights widespread global use of GM crops, citing 17 million farmers cultivating 170 million hectares without reports of health issues. He sees agritechnology, encompassing GM and traditional crop advancements, as a promising business sector where Britain could take a lead. On the other hand, critics like Dr. Helen Wallace from GeneWatch argue that growing GM crops might hurt the UK's reputation for high farming standards. She points to research showing that some GM crops have led to heavier herbicide usage, harming wildlife, and advocates for clearer labeling of products from animals fed GM feed. Public surveys, she notes, indicate strong support for such labels, allowing informed consumer choices. Currently, commercial GM crops are not grown in Britain, but imported GM feed is common in livestock farming. Nevertheless, various government figures and much of the scientific community support the potential expansion of GM technology in Britain, favoring product-by-product assessments. Critics warn, however, that introducing GM crops could still trigger significant public opposition.

Paterson he’i avei ojeporúvo ko tecnología oñemomichĩvetaha tembi’urã repykue ha upéicha oipytyvõta umi oñandúva apañuãi viru’íre. He’i avei, hetaite mymbaitýra oñemongaru GM rehegua rembi’urãre, ha hetave gente nontendéi ha upéva, ndikatúi ojekuaa so’o ambuévagui. article_content: As what may be the final battle unfolds in Libya, another crucial struggle is emerging: the challenge of building a functioning democracy. While Libyan rebels consolidate their military gains in Tripoli, the National Transitional Council (NTC) in Benghazi is working to implement plans for political transition. The role of the United States in Libya's future remains uncertain, but many believe it will be a significant partner in international efforts. The U.S. State Department emphasizes the urgency of establishing an interim government to begin drafting a constitution and paving the way for elections—the key steps in developing a democracy. International assistance is considered essential to achieve lasting stability. Ensuring security is a top priority, said State Department spokeswoman Victoria Nuland, who emphasized the need to prevent further civilian casualties. U.S. officials noted the rebels’ efforts in setting up checkpoints around public buildings to enhance safety. Assistant Secretary Jeffrey Feltman remarked that the situation in Tripoli contrasts with post-Saddam Baghdad, where looting was widespread. Questions about the opposition's management arose after conflicting reports about the capture of Moammar Gadhafi’s son, Saif al-Islam. The confusion, resulting from unclear communication within the NTC, highlighted challenges in gaining public and international trust. Despite these challenges, U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Susan Rice stated that the American government considers the rebels to be credible and reliable partners. Professor Daniel Serwer of Johns Hopkins University observed that the NTC appears aware of the need to establish the rule of law, aiming for a multiparty, democratic, and liberal Islamic state. NATO-backed rebels, lacking professional military training, require support to secure Gadhafi’s large weapons stockpiles, including chemical arms like mustard gas. Reports indicate that some Gadhafi loyalists have blended into the general population, representing ongoing security risks. Retired U.S. Army Brigadier General James 'Spider' Marks suggested that some level of foreign ground presence may be necessary during this transition to prevent Gadhafi’s forces from regrouping. However, President Obama has reiterated that the U.S. will not deploy ground troops, and administration officials confirmed that the rebels have not requested such assistance. The NTC is considering requesting a limited force from Arab nations, such as Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and Jordan, to help secure critical sites in Tripoli. Stockpiles of chemical weapons and missiles pose dangers that could extend beyond Libya’s borders, worrying both regional and international observers. Robert Kagan of the Brookings Institution expressed confidence in the rebels’ intentions but questioned their capacity to secure dangerous weaponry, suggesting that international involvement may be necessary if the NTC is unable to do so. There are also concerns about the expertise retained from Libya’s former nuclear weapons program. The NTC has outlined a timetable to form a new, more inclusive government by expanding membership and establishing an 'interim authority.' Plans include drafting a constitution within 45 days, followed by a national referendum and legislative elections four months later, then a presidential election two months after that. Officials project the process will take 10–15 months. Victoria Nuland noted that the interim government aims to represent a broad cross-section of Libyans. However, potential divisions over tribal loyalties, control of oil revenues, and disputes about government assets, including $30 billion in U.S.-frozen funds, pose risks of instability. Nicholas Burns, former U.S. undersecretary of state, warned there may be a slow, chaotic, or even violent transition due to long-standing divisions. The U.S. and U.N. are working to release $1–$1.5 billion in frozen assets to the NTC for humanitarian aid and government stabilization. Burns and other experts believe the European and Arab nations should now take the lead in supporting Libya’s reconstruction, given their historical ties and regional interests. Former Defense Secretary William Cohen emphasized that other nations need to share the burden of assisting Libya’s future. The U.S. can contribute intelligence and support, but regional and European powers must assume greater responsibility. CNN reporters Jill Dougherty, John Helton, Chris Lawrence, Tim Lister, Dan Lothian, and Laura Smith-Spark contributed to this report.

article_content: Jacqueline Hayes, a former finance chief from Cullercoats, North Tyneside, has been sentenced to two and a half years in prison for stealing nearly £100,000 from Jeremy Middleton, a leading Tyneside entrepreneur and prominent Conservative Party figure. Hayes abused her position of trust to conduct over 20 unauthorized electronic transfers from one of Middleton's bank accounts, deliberately selecting an account not subject to external auditing. To conceal her actions, Hayes created false accounting entries. She initially denied responsibility and gave false testimony, but just before a new trial was due to begin, she pleaded guilty to five counts of theft, totaling £97,347 committed between August 2008 and July 2009. Judge Roger Thorn QC, sentencing Hayes at Newcastle Crown Court, described her actions as greedy and devious, noting she may have believed her crime would be overlooked given Middleton’s public profile. Despite being defrauded, Middleton reportedly bears no personal malice toward Hayes. The court recognized Hayes' previous good character, but noted her conviction has gravely damaged her reputation and employment prospects. Defense lawyer James Walker said she is extremely remorseful and fearful of imprisonment. Authorities are now seeking to recover any assets Hayes may possess through a Proceeds of Crime application.

article_content: Nigerian striker Victor Osimhen has been named among the final ten-man shortlist for the 2023 CAF Player of the Year award. The 24-year-old is a leading contender, following his impressive eighth-place finish at the 2023 Ballon d’Or ceremony in Paris, France. Osimhen competes with former winners Sadio Mane, Mohamed Salah, and Riyad Mahrez for the prestigious title. The shortlist also includes four Moroccan players—Achraf Hakimi, Sofyan Amrabat, Yassine Bounou, and Youssef En-Nesyri—who played key roles in Morocco’s historic run to the 2022 FIFA World Cup semi-finals, marking the first time an African nation has reached that stage. Osimhen aspires to follow in the footsteps of Nwankwo Kanu, the last Nigerian to win the CAF Player of the Year award in 1999. The Napoli striker was instrumental in helping his club clinch their first Serie A title in 33 years and became the first African player to win Serie A’s Golden Boot by scoring 26 goals. The Interclub Player of the Year category features 10 contenders, while the Goalkeeper of the Year, Young Player of the Year, Coach of the Year, National Team of the Year, and Club of the Year categories each have five nominees. Winners in each category will be determined by votes from the CAF Technical Committee, media professionals, head coaches, and captains of member associations and clubs participating in the group stages of the Interclub competitions. According to CAF, 'The ultimate winner of each category will be decided after votes from a voting panel consisting of the CAF Technical Committee, media professionals, head coaches, and captains of Member Associations and clubs involved in the group stages of the Interclub competitions.' The award ceremony is scheduled for December 11 at the Palais des Congres in Marrakech, Morocco.

Osimhen oipotaiterei oñembojoaju Nwankwo Kanu rehe, upe tapicha Nigeria pegua ipahaite guive oganáva ko arandukuaa 1999-pe.
