article_content: The iconic, retro-styled TV-shaped YouTube app was one of the first apps on the iPhone when it was released in 2007. Now, for the first time, new iPhones will not come with the YouTube app pre-installed. However, YouTube has launched its own app for the iPhone. This new standalone app was released on Tuesday, just a month after Apple confirmed it would not include the YouTube app in the upcoming iOS 6. Having a built-in app on iPhones and iPads allowed YouTube to reach a growing mobile audience—YouTube now receives 1 billion mobile views each day, and mobile accounts for 25% of total YouTube views. Yet, the partnership with Apple had limitations. Apple’s version of the YouTube app was built into iOS, so YouTube had limited control over features and was unable to show video ads due to Apple’s restrictions. With its new standalone app, YouTube regains control but must encourage iPhone owners to download it from the App Store or access YouTube via the mobile website, particularly after upgrading to iOS 6 or buying new devices. Apple’s decision to drop the YouTube app follows its earlier move to remove Google Maps as the default navigation app on iPhones and iPads. These decisions reflect ongoing competition and legal disputes between Apple and Google, which owns YouTube. The removal of YouTube is seen as part of Apple’s effort to reduce reliance on Google products and services. YouTube officials downplay any conflict, highlighting continued cooperation with Apple. Andrey Doronichev, YouTube’s lead mobile product manager, told CNN: 'Apple and us have been working closely on this. It’s the right thing to do for both companies—the user experience is much better.' Doronichev explained that YouTube’s team spent several months developing the new app before the change was public. Available for free from the App Store for iPhones running iOS 4.3 or later, the new YouTube app features a redesigned interface similar to the Android version, a hidden side navigation panel, and new options for discovering and sharing content. The app can now display videos with ads, giving users access to many more videos, including official music videos that were previously unavailable. It also features search tools like auto-suggestions, voice search, and closed-caption overlays. A key new feature is in-page video playback, enabling users to continue watching videos while reading descriptions, posting comments, or browsing suggested videos. The video keeps playing even while navigating within the app. YouTube hopes these features will motivate iPhone users to download the new app. Although the removal of the default app may lead to fewer iPhone users for a while, it allows YouTube to push out faster updates and new features. The release of the new app comes a day before Apple’s anticipated press event, where the next iPhone is expected to be introduced.

article_content: E-commerce platforms like Amazon and CRED often host spin-the-wheel games and similar contests, offering prizes such as mobile phones, vouchers, or cashback rewards. Participation is typically free, and sometimes players earn points they can later redeem for gifts. Winnings from these games are taxable in India. From the financial year 2023-24, earnings from online games are taxed at a fixed rate of 30% plus any applicable surcharge and cess under Section 115BBJ of the Income Tax Act. Before this, both online and offline game winnings were handled similarly, but now online and offline contests are taxed separately: Section 115BBJ applies to online, while Section 115BB covers offline games. All rewards—whether they're cash or physical items like gadgets—must be listed as 'Income from Other Sources' in your income tax return. If the prize is not cash, its fair market value is considered for tax purposes. Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) depends on the game type. For online games, TDS under Section 194BA is deducted from every prize, regardless of the amount. With offline games, TDS under Section 194B applies only if winnings exceed Rs 10,000 in a year. The TDS rate for both types remains 30%. If your prize is fully or partly non-cash, and the cash isn’t enough to cover the tax, you must pay the required TDS to claim your reward. The contest organizer is responsible for collecting this amount and ensuring it is deposited; however, it is the winner's responsibility to pay the tax. You must report such winnings when filing your tax return under the correct section. Failing to disclose this income can trigger scrutiny, since tax authorities monitor these transactions. Organizers have to file TDS returns, issue Form 16A, and keep records. Regarding GST, starting October 2023, a 28% tax applies to both skill-based and chance-based games if a registration, entry, or platform fee is charged. However, if a spin-the-wheel contest is free—which is typical on many e-commerce sites—GST does not apply. If any site charges you to play, then GST is relevant.

Jeporavóvape ndoguererekói viru paga, ha heta jey oñeme’ẽ puntos ikatúva ova jopói rehe. Upe mboyve, online ha offline jeikohague tembiapo ojejapova’ekue peteĩchante, ko’ágã ojeguerekóva iñambuéva: online rehe 115BBJ ha offline rehe 115BB. Opaichagua jopói—viru térã mba’e jeporu—omiña va’erã ‘Otros Ingresos’ ramo declaración de impuestos-pe. Jopói chembojoajuvirũ ndaha’éiramo viru, ijyvy ára hepy’etéva oñemohenda. Organizador orekova’erã ko viru ha oñangareko depósito rehe; péro ha’e avei nde rembiaporã. Reikuaauka va’erã ko’ãichagua rembiapo ne declaración de impuestos-pe ikatu hag̃ua. Ani nde’emo’ã, autoridadkuéra oguahẽta; organizadorkuéra rembiapópe omoakã TDS form, ome’ẽta Formulario 16A ha omotenondeva’erã documento. article_content: Manchester United legend Paul Scholes believes Ravel Morrison still has a chance to revive his football career, even as Morrison appears set to exit West Ham United. Once regarded as Scholes' potential successor in United's midfield, Morrison's off-the-field challenges led to an early departure from Old Trafford, and his West Ham stint seems to be ending similarly. Scholes, writing in The Independent, recounted witnessing Morrison's difficulties firsthand but also highlighted his strong footballing talent. Morrison, according to Scholes, regularly stood out among United’s young players, especially when motivated. Warren Joyce, then United’s reserve and under-21 coach, made considerable efforts to mentor Morrison. Despite being tipped to follow in Scholes’ footsteps, Morrison has struggled to fulfill that promise. At 21, about to turn 22, Scholes stresses that Morrison still has time to reshape his career. After a loan spell at Cardiff City ended early—Cardiff manager Russell Slade said Morrison was not in the club’s plans—speculation now links Morrison with a summer transfer to Italy's Lazio. Throughout his two years at West Ham, Morrison has mostly been loaned to Championship clubs. Despite high hopes when he joined United, his professional progress has repeatedly been interrupted by personal challenges. Scholes remains cautiously optimistic, noting Morrison’s youth and unique abilities, and believes with the right support, Morrison can still turn things around.

Morrison oñemomba’e peichaháicha ikatuha omoañete Scholes rembiapo Manchester United-pe, ha umi mba’e ivaíva omo’ã upe tape. Hina West Ham-pe avei upéichante oikohína. article_content: On Friday night, two separate teams of meteorologists chasing storms narrowly escaped disaster when tornadoes struck the Oklahoma City area. Mike Bettes, from The Weather Channel’s Tornado Hunt Team, was traveling with two photographers near El Reno when a massive tornado picked up their SUV and tossed it roughly 200 yards. Bettes sustained minor injuries, including a hand that required stitches, but all occupants wore seat belts and walked away—making this the first on-field injury of a Weather Channel reporter. In another event, storm chasers Brandon Sullivan and Brett Wright filmed their close call with a tornado near Union City, southwest of Oklahoma City. Their SUV was hit by flying debris that shattered the windshield, and the video captures Sullivan urgently telling Wright to turn away from the storm. Despite serious vehicle damage, the two escaped unharmed. The outbreak of tornadoes across Oklahoma caused widespread damage—overturning vehicles, causing flash floods, and leaving major roads impassable. Five fatalities were reported, including a mother and her baby near Union City and another death in El Reno. Around 50 people were hurt, five critically. Although meteorologists had predicted severe weather, this event was less devastating than the previous week’s tornado in Moore. Strong storms also battered the St. Louis region, removing part of a casino roof, and torrential rain flooded Oklahoma City streets up to four feet, complicating the evening rush hour.

article_content: Ena Bernard joined the household of Robert and Ethel Kennedy in 1951, initially assisting with their newborn, Kathleen. Over the subsequent 44 years, she would play a central role in raising all 11 Kennedy children, and her presence continued to enrich the family even after her formal nanny duties ended. She passed away recently at the age of 105 in Sunrise, Florida. Ethel Kennedy and nearly all of the surviving Kennedy children—Joe, Bobby, Kathleen, Kerry, Christopher, Maxwell, Douglas, and Rory—attended her funeral, a testament to their enduring affection for Ena. During the ceremony, Ena’s daughter, Josefina 'Fina' Harvin, along with several Kennedy siblings, spoke about Ena’s deep bond with the family. Josefina reflected on how, after moving from Costa Rica and joining her mother in the U.S. as a teenager, she too became part of the Kennedy home and was embraced as one of their own. Josefina recounted moments of both guidance and care from Robert and Ethel Kennedy, highlighting Bobby Kennedy’s protective nature and Ethel’s encouragement as Josefina adjusted to life in America. The Kennedy children expressed immense gratitude for Ena’s warmth and mentorship. Maxwell Kennedy recalled praying she would always be safe, and Kerry Kennedy emphasized Ena’s joyful and gentle approach to discipline. Ena’s connection with the Kennedys began after she emigrated from Costa Rica, having previously worked for another prominent family. Once she joined, she traveled with them to family homes and vacation spots, such as Cape Cod and Palm Beach, and had her own room at Hickory Hill. Even after all the Kennedy children had grown and moved out, Ena remained involved with the family for years. She was present for significant occasions, such as Robert Kennedy’s swearing-in as attorney general, and supported the family through both celebrations and tragedies, especially after Robert Kennedy's assassination. Throughout her life with the Kennedys, Ena met various high-profile individuals and was steadfastly honored by the family. On her 100th birthday, she was celebrated warmly. Ena is survived by her grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and the Kennedy children she helped raise.

article_content: Human rights groups allege that Zimbabwean authorities are misusing the legal system to target opposition figures such as Job Sikhala. Sikhala, a 51-year-old lawyer and prominent member of Zimbabwe's opposition, has spent the past 17 months in Chikurubi maximum-security prison—the longest pre-trial detention of an opposition politician in Zimbabwe in nearly 40 years. Since entering politics as a founding member of the Movement for Democratic Change (MDC) in 1999, Sikhala has been arrested 65 times. His latest arrest, in June 2022, was based on accusations of obstructing justice and inciting public violence after he allegedly blamed the ruling party for the killing of opposition activist Moreblessing Ali. According to his son, Job Sikhala Jr.—a law student and the eldest of Sikhala's 16 children—these charges are mostly fabricated, and Sikhala has never been convicted despite numerous arrests. Sikhala's experience with political persecution began decades ago. As a child, his son remembers seeing their home raided and his father arrested, a pattern that continued over the years. Other critics of President Emmerson Mnangagwa's regime have also experienced extensive detentions. In 2020, journalist Hopewell Chin’ono spent 45 days in jail for allegedly inciting antigovernment protests. Opposition leader Jacob Ngarivhume was detained for over a month, and Parere Kunyenzura was held for more than 100 days for organizing a church gathering deemed illegal. Sikhala was born in 1972 in rural Masvingo and moved to Harare to study history and law at the University of Zimbabwe in 1995. He became involved in student politics, earning a reputation for fearless leadership and drawing inspiration from Nigerian activist Ken Saro-Wiwa. Sikhala joined the MDC at age 27 and was elected to parliament by 2002. His bold activism led to multiple confrontations with authorities, including accusations of arson and assault under Robert Mugabe's regime—charges for which he was acquitted. In the late 2000s, Sikhala took part in the Save Zimbabwe campaign, challenging one-party rule and economic decline. In 2014, he faced treason charges and was hospitalized after alleged torture, but again was acquitted. Since 2019, he has served as deputy national chairman of the Citizens Coalition for Change (CCC), Zimbabwe’s main opposition party, and has continued to challenge both Mugabe’s and Mnangagwa's governments—facing additional arrests and charges, all leading to eventual exonerations until a suspended sentence in May 2023. Human rights organizations, such as Amnesty International, argue that Sikhala’s ongoing detention symbolizes broader abuse of Zimbabwe’s legal system to silence critics. Stephen Chuma, a CCC spokesperson, says Sikhala’s imprisonment illustrates the plight of many citizens jailed without trial. Khanyo Farise, Amnesty International's deputy director for East and Southern Africa, called Sikhala’s prolonged pre-trial detention a miscarriage of justice and an indictment of Zimbabwe’s judiciary. Despite the hardships, Sikhala remains steadfast in prison, penning letters expressing his defiance and commitment to his cause. However, his family fears he may not be released soon. 'We are terrified, stressed, and have lost hope that our father will be released anytime soon,' Sikhala Jr. told Al Jazeera. 'We are just waiting for God’s time; it’s now in God’s hands.'

Sikhala onasẽ 1972-pe Masvingo okaháre ha oho Harare-pe oestudia historia ha derecho Universidad de Zimbabue-pe 1995-pe. Estudiante política-pe oñe’engatu, heta oñemomba’e Ken Saro-Wiwa rehe. Sikhala oike MDC-pe 27 ary-pe ha 2002-pe ojeporavo parlamentario-ramo. Activismo rehehápe oiko heta confrontación autoridad rehe, años arson ha violencia rehe Mugabe gobierno-pe — upévare ojeheja. 2000 década pahápe, Sikhala oike Save Zimbabwe campaña-pe oikuaauka Estado omba’apo haguã partido peteĩme ha economía vai rehe. 2014-pe, oñemoĩ chupe traición rehe ha hospital-pe omoingove torture rehe, péro ojeheja avei. 2019 guive, vice-presidente-pe Citizens Coalition for Change (CCC) — oposición guasuete akue— ha oike jey vaekue cárcel rehe peteĩ condena suspendida mayo 2023-pe. Derechorekuéra aty guasu, Amnesty International he’i detención Sikhala rehegua ohechauka mba’éichapa Zimbabwe autoridad oipuru justicia ojokua hag̃ua umi opositor-kuéra. article_content: Russian space officials report that the crew of the Soyuz spacecraft is recovering after a challenging return to Earth. Among the three crew members was South Korean bioengineer Yi So-yeon, marking her country's first astronaut in space. The capsule landed in northern Kazakhstan on Saturday, about 418 kilometers (260 miles) from its intended location. Mission Control spokesman Valery Lyndin stated that all three crew members—Yi So-yeon, American astronaut Peggy Whitson, and Russian flight engineer Yuri Malenchenko—are in satisfactory condition despite enduring intense gravitational forces during re-entry. Search helicopters found the capsule and confirmed the crew’s safety within 25 minutes. Officials explained that the Soyuz followed a very steep descent path, causing the crew to experience gravitational forces up to 10 times that of Earth’s gravity. Interfax news agency described the landing as rough. Such incidents are not without precedent. In October, a Soyuz capsule carrying two Russian cosmonauts and Malaysia’s first astronaut landed 70 kilometers from its planned site due to a damaged control cable.

article_content: Leicester City is aiming to sign Argentine midfielder Esteban Cambiasso, who recently left Inter Milan and is currently a free agent, ahead of their return to the Premier League against Everton. The 33-year-old, with more than 300 matches for Inter, is in talks with the club. Although manager Nigel Pearson wanted negotiations to stay confidential, the information was leaked, causing him frustration. Negotiations with Cambiasso continue, with Pearson confirming interest while avoiding public speculation to respect the process. He noted that finalizing the signing will depend on multiple factors, and Leicester remains committed to trying to secure the deal. After a decade away, Leicester is back in the Premier League and will start the season against Everton at the King Power Stadium. Last season, Leicester captured the Championship title, setting club records for points and victories. Pearson expressed belief in his squad’s ability to compete at the highest level, citing a healthy mix of youth and experienced players and emphasizing the value of teamwork. While surviving in the Premier League would meet business goals, he suggested the club’s potential goes further. Heading into the first match, Leicester may be without Jamie Vardy (thigh) and new signing Marc Albrighton (groin), but Anthony Knockaert is expected to be fit after recovering from injury. Pearson acknowledged the challenge of injuries but stressed that the team is ready and new opportunities will arise for other players.

article_content: ACT, an Indian venture philanthropy organization, and Global Health Labs (GH Labs), an international non-profit funded by Gates Ventures, have announced a collaboration to jointly identify Indian digital and medical technology innovators and support the development and scaling of their technologies within India's public healthcare system. The partnership aims to improve the quality and accessibility of primary healthcare services in regions with inadequate health infrastructure and a shortage of healthcare professionals. “Our collaboration with GH Labs will focus on bringing innovative health-tech solutions to the last mile, where they can have the most impact on underserved populations. The goal is to make a meaningful impact on the public healthcare system by bridging the gap between accessibility and affordability in quality healthcare for Bharat,” said Krisha Mathur, Director of ACT For Health. ACT For Health and GH Labs will provide technology assistance, conduct evaluations in public health settings, and explore pathways for scaling Indian health-tech innovations. “Global Health Labs is thrilled to collaborate with ACT For Health, bringing together our unique expertise and shared commitment to supporting innovation that can lead to improved primary healthcare and reduced health disparities,” said Sharon Bergquist, Vice President - Special Projects at GH Labs.

article_content: The U.S. Supreme Court on Tuesday expressed significant concerns about free speech while reviewing a federal law intended to prohibit the sale and marketing of videos depicting dog fights and other acts of animal cruelty. Under a 1999 statute, selling depictions of animal cruelty—including amateur dogfighting videos—may be illegal. The justices engaged in a lively hour-long debate about the law's scope and intent. Supporters argue the law helps curb profiting from animal torture and abuse, while opponents, including media groups and the National Rifle Association, say it is overly broad. Justice Antonin Scalia argued it is not the government’s role to determine the boundaries of acceptable content, suggesting that such logic could restrict dramatized depictions in various forms of media. Justice Samuel Alito, using sarcasm, questioned whether the logic could extend to blocking depictions of extreme acts like human sacrifice if they were legal elsewhere, challenging lawmakers’ discretion. The specific case concerns Robert Stevens of Pittsville, Virginia, who sold videos depicting pit bulls attacking animals and each other. Federal agents discovered Stevens advertising his tapes through an underground dogfighting magazine. Stevens was convicted in 2004 for violating interstate commerce laws by selling such depictions and sentenced to 37 months, a longer term than the one received by Michael Vick for a similar crime. It was the first case to go to trial under the 1999 law. A federal appeals court later overturned Stevens’ conviction, stating that available research did not prove banning depictions of animal cruelty was necessary or effective in prosecuting the underlying acts. Nearly all states and local jurisdictions have their own laws banning animal mistreatment. Media organizations have raised concerns that the federal law could affect content such as coverage of hunting or bullfighting. Justices raised numerous hypotheticals, hinting at uncertainty over whether the law is written too broadly. Justice Stephen Breyer suggested Congress rewrite the law to more clearly target its intended issues. Chief Justice John Roberts and Justice Sonia Sotomayor questioned how the law distinguishes between illegal depictions and documentaries or advocacy videos that use similar footage. Neal Katyal, representing the Justice Department, argued the law is narrowly targeted with specific exceptions for religious, political, scientific, educational, journalistic, historical, or artistic purposes. Justice Alito highlighted concerns about so-called 'crush' videos—which depict animals being killed for sexual gratification—and questioned whether the law might be too broad or whether Congress specifically targeted this content. The Humane Society states that the market for ‘crush’ videos dropped dramatically after the law's enactment. Patricia Millett, Stevens' lawyer, argued that the law could set a dangerous precedent for restricting speech protected by the First Amendment. Ultimately, the Supreme Court's ruling in U.S. vs. Stevens (08-769), expected in the coming months, will determine the future balance between combatting animal cruelty and protecting free expression.

Juez kuéra oñe’ẽ heta hipotético rehe, he’i ikatuha léi nopenái porã. Juez Stephen Breyer he’i Congreso omoĩ porãve haguã peteĩ léi oporohupytyséva. Justice Alito osẽ he'i ohupytyha 'crush' video rehe—ojekuaa gato ha kuri jejuka jehecha ha peteĩ mbaʼe—and oporandu léi ikatuveha térã Congreso omba’apo hague peteĩ mbaʼe rehe. article_content: Jason Timss, 54, was working as a driver for Amazon Flex in Seattle, earning between $25 and $35 per hour, when a neighbor told him about a bus driving job she had recently taken. Frustrated by the unpredictability of his earnings and schedule delivering packages, Timss applied to become a bus driver with King County Metro, Seattle's public transit authority, five years ago. For the first few years, he balanced part-time roles with both Amazon Flex and King County Metro as he gained experience. Recently, Timss left his Amazon Flex job and began working full-time as a Metro bus driver. With guaranteed pay increases, he expects to earn around $45 per hour next year, along with retirement and union benefits, overtime, and typically works nine to ten-hour days. 'It’s a great job for people looking for a fresh start and stability,' Timss said. Before this, he worked in video and photography. He now describes his life as comfortable. A growing number of Americans are turning to gig jobs like grocery delivery and digital freelancing for flexible income. The number of US gig workers more than doubled during the pandemic, with many Gen Xers and baby boomers leaving traditional corporate jobs for gig work. However, as gig work becomes more competitive, some have seen declining wages and increased difficulty finding jobs. As a result, some gig workers are pursuing more stable work like bus driving, which offers a median annual salary of $54,000 according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Many transit agencies provide benefits such as paid sick leave, 401(k) contributions, and health and dental insurance—perks not typically available to gig drivers for companies like Uber or DoorDash. Timss said he earned at least $1,000 per week at Amazon Flex, but work could be inconsistent, and expenses such as gas and maintenance—especially in winter—often ate into his earnings. He appreciated the flexibility, but rarely received bonuses or recognition for reliable service. When he started at King County Metro, Timss worked part-time four-and-a-half hour shifts at about $24 per hour, and needed training and licensing. Juggling both jobs was challenging, with long and unpredictable hours. 'I’d have to do an early bus route, then deliver Amazon packages, then return for another bus route later,' he explained. Switching to full-time at Metro meant better pay and the freedom to choose routes. Timss now earns about $40 per hour, is aiming for $80,000 in annual pay (including time off for medical leave), and anticipates reaching $10,000 a month before taxes next year. He also receives regular raises and comprehensive benefits. 'It's a demanding job, but ideal for older gig workers seeking stable careers,' he said. The agency offers training for commercial licenses and further career development within public transit or city services. Timss concluded, 'Gig work can be a useful step, but it shouldn't be the end goal.'

article_content: Zack Snyder's vision for Superman in 'Man of Steel' differs from earlier cinematic versions by taking a more spiritual and grounded approach. While Christopher Reeve brought an iconic portrayal in Richard Donner's 1978 'Superman' and its sequels, and Brandon Routh played the role in Bryan Singer's 2006 'Superman Returns,' Snyder set out to explore the deeper motivations behind the character. Composer Hans Zimmer highlighted that this Kal-El would have a spiritual element. Snyder told CNN his focus was on the mythic, Christ-like themes embedded in Superman’s story. He emphasized that these aspects already existed in the mythology, and chose to incorporate them rather than ignore them. The film opens with Kal-El’s miraculous birth on Krypton, distinguishing him from other Kryptonian children, who are genetically engineered. Jor-El, Superman’s father (played by Russell Crowe), takes an active part in his son's birth. With Krypton facing destruction, Jor-El sends Kal-El to Earth in hope he might save its people. 'He will be like a god to them,' Jor-El says. On Earth, Kal-El is adopted by Martha and Jonathan Kent and given the name Clark. Unlike traditional portrayals of Clark as a reporter at The Daily Planet, this version initially works manual jobs, reflecting his humble beginnings and nodding to biblical parallels. Snyder explained that he wanted Superman to balance the modern world with ancient archetypes, making the character seem more authentic. In this adaptation, Superman remains hidden from the world for most of his life and only reveals himself at the age of 33, when he is called to sacrifice himself for humanity. Played by Henry Cavill, this Superman is more humble, conflicted, and troubled. For a portion of the film, Clark sports a beard and does not immediately don the iconic suit. As a child, he experiences bullying but refrains from fighting back, knowing his strength could cause harm. This contributes to his emotional development. Snyder describes this Superman as both grounded and larger-than-life. The film encourages viewers to see events through Superman’s eyes, providing additional depth to the character. Krypton receives expanded treatment in the film, with an immersive opening sequence that explores its society and fate. General Zod (Michael Shannon) and his followers are given stronger motivations for pursuing Kal-El to Earth. Being a science fiction enthusiast, Snyder wanted the Krypton storyline to stand out. Although faithful to Superman’s comic roots, Snyder took creative freedom with certain characters, like changing Jimmy Olsen to Jenny Olsen. He believed in experimenting with established roles to add unpredictability for viewers. The movie includes nods to a larger universe: LexCorp logos are visible during city destruction, and a Wayne Enterprises logo appears on a satellite, implying Gotham and Metropolis coexist. Snyder confirmed these moments were intentional Easter eggs, foreshadowing future connections. Though Lex Luthor does not appear on screen, the film sets up his possible involvement in future installments, joking about how he might respond to the city's destruction. Plans for sequels and a potential 'Justice League' film are already being discussed. Snyder intentionally crafted 'Man of Steel' with the larger DC cinematic universe in mind, weaving in elements for future stories.

article_content: While visiting Cushing, Oklahoma, President Obama defended his energy policies, arguing that accusations about restricting U.S. oil production are inaccurate. He noted that domestic drilling and output have increased, but emphasized that more U.S. oil alone can't quickly reduce gas prices, since these are mainly affected by international markets and global issues like tensions with Iran. During his tour, which included a stop at The Ohio State University, Obama promoted a comprehensive energy plan. He advocated balancing increased output of traditional fuels such as oil and natural gas with investment in renewables like solar, wind, and hydrogen. Obama argued that ensuring U.S. energy security will require both boosting domestic supply and staying competitive globally. He countered Republican claims that exploiting all domestic oil reserves would solve high gas prices, explaining that U.S. production still depends on imports, and that world oil prices set the cost of fuel. Prominent Republicans, including Rick Santorum, Newt Gingrich, and Speaker John Boehner, critiqued Obama’s approach, referencing delays to the Keystone XL pipeline and claiming his administration hinders energy development. Obama responded by highlighting complexities in the decision process, which involve both state authorities and various federal agencies. Addressing infrastructure, Obama announced executive action to fast-track federal approval of large-scale projects, prioritizing the Keystone XL segment from Cushing to the Gulf Coast. Critics, however, contend that actual oversight over U.S. pipeline routes mostly lies with individual states. Obama questioned continued government subsidies for the oil and gas sector, suggesting these companies already profit from high fuel prices and no longer require such incentives. Instead, he supported channeling resources toward renewables, despite ongoing debate over the effectiveness and scale of green job creation. At a large solar facility in Boulder City, Nevada, Obama cited advances in clean energy and defended green jobs, pushing back against criticism from some lawmakers who have minimized the impact of renewable energy employment. He stated that innovation and investment in technology are key to maintaining U.S. economic leadership. This debate reflects broader political divisions over whether the focus should be on traditional energy production or on expanding clean energy infrastructure, encapsulating the nation’s long-term energy policy choices.

article_content: John Henry, principal owner of the Boston Red Sox, has agreed to purchase The Boston Globe for $70 million, a significant decrease from its peak price of $1.1 billion twenty years ago. The pending acquisition from The New York Times Company marks Henry’s first move into the news media industry, according to the Globe. The agreement includes the 141-year-old newspaper, its websites, and affiliated businesses. Henry emphasized the Globe’s essential role in Boston and New England, highlighting its award-winning journalism and tradition of excellence. Henry, who also owns Liverpool F.C., stated he would announce his plans for the Globe in the coming days. The New York Times Company announced in February its intention to sell the Globe and related assets to focus more on its flagship brand. Spokeswoman Eileen Murphy confirmed the sale. The all-cash deal, expected to close within 30 to 60 days, includes BostonGlobe.com, Boston.com, The Worcester Telegram & Gazette, Telegram.com, Globe Direct, and a 49 percent share in Metro Boston, a free daily for commuters. Globe editor Brian McGrory reassured readers that neither coverage of the Red Sox nor other editorial decisions would be affected by the sale. The Times acquired the Globe from the family of former executive Stephen Taylor in 1993 for $1.1 billion, then the highest price paid for an American newspaper. Henry’s offer is less than 7 percent of that amount. Like many newspapers, the Globe has recently faced financial pressures due to the transition of audiences and advertisers to digital platforms. Still, the Globe is regarded as a journalistic institution in New England and received praise for its reporting on the Boston Marathon bombings in April. A round of cost-cutting and pay cuts in 2009 helped stabilize the Globe’s finances, leading the Times to retract a previous attempt to sell. In late 2011, the Globe started charging for online content, which increased digital subscription revenue. Although the Times does not separately disclose the Globe’s earnings, the paper averaged a weekday circulation of 230,351 in the six months to September, according to the Alliance for Audited Media. Increases in digital subscriptions have partially offset declines in print, but total circulation remains well below the nearly 413,000 recorded in September 2002. Similar declines in newspaper purchase prices have occurred at other publications, such as Philadelphia’s two largest papers, which sold for $55 million in April 2012, compared to $515 million paid in 2006.

article_content: Rebekah Brooks received £10.8 million after resigning as chief executive of News International, a sum much larger than initially reported. At the height of the phone-hacking scandal, Brooks stepped down and her compensation package was revealed to be significantly larger than first believed, according to accounts released by Rupert Murdoch’s News Corporation. The package included ongoing benefits such as funding for a London office, staff for two years, and payment of all legal and professional costs related to ongoing investigations. News Corporation anticipates further costs may arise. Brooks, a close ally of Rupert Murdoch and friend of former Prime Minister David Cameron, faces multiple legal charges, including conspiring to pervert the course of justice and intercepting voicemails. Earlier this month, Brooks appeared at the Old Bailey alongside Andy Coulson—another former News of the World editor—regarding alleged illegal payments to public officials. James Harding, editor of The Times, also resigned, stating that News Corporation wished to appoint a new editor. Brooks edited the News of the World and The Sun before becoming chief executive of News International in 2009. She was considered instrumental in securing The Sun's endorsement of the Conservative Party during the 2010 general election. David Cameron received criticism for his close relationship with the Murdoch media empire, including his friendship with Brooks and her husband, Charlie, whom he attended Eton with. Lord Justice Leveson's report into media standards noted that Cameron’s closeness to senior media executives raised concerns about public perception. The report emphasized that while Cameron pursued face-to-face meetings with Murdoch and News International, there was no evidence of a deal trading support for policy favors. During the Leveson Inquiry—set up after the phone-hacking scandal—Brooks revealed friendly text exchanges with Cameron, including messages wishing him luck and expressing support. She was a key figure in persuading Murdoch to support the Conservative Party in 2010. The relationship between Cameron and Brooks reportedly cooled following the revelations of phone hacking in 2011, when Cameron called for her resignation. In her resignation email, Brooks expressed responsibility for those affected and stated her intent to correct misconceptions regarding her journalistic record. Due to legal reasons, comments on the article were not accepted.

Experts have warned that the Conservative Party may need to cut £21 billion from the welfare budget after the upcoming election due to increasing state pension costs. The Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) states that current Conservative spending plans would require deeper cuts to Britain's welfare spending than those made since 2010. In a recent study, the respected think tank reported that a £7 billion reduction in working-age benefits since 2010 has been offset by a matching £7 billion increase in pension costs, leaving total welfare spending at £220 billion—virtually unchanged.

Chancellor George Osborne would need to cut £21 billion from the benefits budget to adhere to his proposed spending plans. The IFS noted the welfare bill would actually be £16.7 billion higher without reforms introduced by the Coalition government. Prime Minister David Cameron has announced plans for £12 billion in welfare cuts post-election, such as reducing the benefits cap from £26,000 to £23,000, but the IFS estimates that nearly twice that amount—£21 billion—will be needed by 2020 if the Conservatives wish to maintain the current pace of government spending reductions. The think tank stressed that the largest cuts to the benefits system may still be to come.

According to the report, protecting state pensions while making further cuts could mean a 23% reduction in benefits for working-age adults and children. Paul Johnson, IFS director, outlined the scale of the cuts that would be needed to balance the budget after the election. The report also warned that maintaining the 'triple lock' on state pensions—ensuring they rise each year by inflation, earnings, or 2.5%, whichever is highest—will cause pension costs to outpace earnings and prices in the long term, costing the government billions every year. The state pension is already set to cost £1.1 billion more by 2015/16 than if it rose with inflation, and £4.6 billion more if linked only to earnings.

The increase in the number of pensioners and higher entitlements among new pensioners has raised pension spending by £12 billion between 2010/11 and 2015/16. This has been partially offset by a decrease in spending on other pensioner benefits, but overall benefits for pensioners have risen by £7 billion, while spending on working-age adults and children's benefits has dropped by about £7 billion.

Work and Pensions Secretary Iain Duncan Smith highlighted the sharp decline in Jobseekers’ Allowance costs, from £8.5 billion in 2010 to £5.2 billion this year—a £3.3 billion reduction, which he said could fund the employment of over 120,000 nurses. He stated: “Our welfare reforms, as part of our long-term economic plan, are moving people off benefits and into work, bringing greater financial security and helping reduce the deficit.”

The IFS also found evidence that stricter benefit sanctions have encouraged some claimants, especially single parents, to return to work. However, Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary Rachel Reeves criticized the government for failing to reduce welfare spending despite what she described as 'cruel and unfair' cuts.

Instituto de Estudios Fiscales (IFS) he'i Conservador-kuéra rembiaporã ojerure hetave jekytĩ welfare rehe 2010 guive ojapova'ekue rehe. Ko grupo he'i avei, hetave jekytĩ welfare rehe oguahẽtaha gueteri.

Informe-pe oñemombe'u, pension rehe ojejoko aja jekytĩ ambue parte rehe, ojapova'erã 23% jekytĩ ambue beneficio rehe working-age ha mitãnguéra rehe. IFS director Paul Johnson omyesakã mba'éichapa ojapo va'erã jekytĩ ikatu hag̃uáicha presupuesto oike. Avei, ko informe omyesakã triple lock política—ohechauka pension estatal oikehápe ojupi añosi, inflación térã 2,5% mba'eichaitépa—ombotuicha pension rehegua costo mbytérã, gobierno oñepyrũ ojepaga heta viru. IFS avei ohechauka sanciones más severas katu ombopyta tapicha juevy tembiapópe, hetave sy añoite rehe. Shadow Work ha Pensiones ministro Rachel Reeves katu okritika gobierno rehe ndohupytýi welfare gasto oguejy, omombe'u jekytĩha ha'etaha 'ivarã ha ndojokuái porã' tapichakuérape.

article_content: A 1954 Mercedes-Benz W196R, once driven by famed Formula One racer Juan Manuel Fangio, has become the most expensive car ever sold at auction. According to auction house Bonhams, the vehicle fetched $29.65 million on Friday at a sale in southern England. The new record surpasses the previous mark—set by the sale of a 1957 Ferrari in 2011—by roughly $13 million. Robert Brooks, chairman of Bonhams, described the event as the highlight of his decades-long career, saying, 'It was a privilege to preside over the sale of such a significant grand prix car, one of the most important motor vehicles of the 20th century.' Juan Manuel Fangio, from Argentina, drove the car to win his second of five Formula One world championships. The car was soon placed in a museum following his victory. Fangio won 45% of the grand prix races he entered and started from pole position nearly 60% of the time—achievements unmatched by current drivers such as Sebastian Vettel. Fangio remains the only driver to win world championships with four different teams and claimed his final title in 1957 at age 46, making him the oldest Formula One champion. Racing historian Doug Nye told Bonhams' website that Fangio, a humble man who started as a mechanic in Argentina, was a driving genius who never forgot his roots.

Bonhams, peteĩ auktion rógape Inglaterra ñembýpe, he’i ojeju hepy $29,65 millón ára viernes-pe. Ko cifra pyahu osyrýkuri pe taha’e orekóva tenonderã, peteĩ 1957 Ferrari oñemurã kuri 2011-pe, pe rupi $13 millón. Robert Brooks, Bonhams sãmbyhyhára, he’i ko tembiapo ha’eha pe iporãvéva hembiapokue pukukue aja, he’ívo: ‘Chemomba’e guasu ahechauka haguã ko jeroky guasuite peteĩ grand prix auto rehe, oĩva ijyvatevéva siglo XX motoka apytépe.’ Juan Manuel Fangio, oñemohu’ã va’ekue Argentina-pe, omba’apo ko autóre ogana haguã mokõiha Formula One arandupy guasu rehegua. Pe auto oñemoĩ kuri museo-pe upei ogana rire. Fangio ogana 45% umi grand prix ohóva ha ohupi oikehaguete punta-pe 60% jey – mba’apoite ndaikatúi oguerekóva ko’ág̃a Sebastian Vettel. Fangio ha’e peteĩnte ojapo haguã mundial irundy equipo reheve ha ogana ijapytepe’a 1957-pe 46 ary guive, oiko chugui arandu Formula One rehegua tujavéva. Carrera rehegua historiador Doug Nye he’i Bonhams’ kuatiápe Fangio ha’eha peteĩ avañe’ẽ jeike’ỹva oñepyrũva mecánico ramo Argentina-pe ha ndahesara’irĩmava heko rehe. Ha’e peteĩ mba’eapohára aranduete.

article_content: Over the last 18 months, central banks have mostly raised interest rates to counter inflation, but this pattern is now shifting. Several central banks have started to lower rates. According to Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid, more central banks lowered rates than increased them recently—something that hasn't happened since January 2021. Reviewing 81 global central banks, Reid notes that 10 cut rates last month, and this month five others, including Brazil and Peru, have followed. Major banks like the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank are holding rates steady for now, but there's debate about whether they’ll start cutting if the economy slows. Swiss bank UBS predicts a possible rate cut from the Fed in the middle of next year if the US enters recession, which would help reduce borrowing costs for consumers. However, Reid points out a broad drop in rates worldwide is unlikely unless the US does move into recession, since inflation is close to desired levels in key economies. Although the Fed has already raised rates 11 times since March 2022, the latest inflation figure was 3.2% in October, which remains above its 2% target. Many expect rate cuts because the economy may slow gently, but if conditions worsen, deeper cuts might be needed.

Jim Reid, Deutsche Bank-pegua, omombe’u ko arapokõime hetave banco central omboguejyha tasa de interés umi omopu’ãva guive – upéva ndokoguasúi 2021 jasypateĩ guive. In Westmont, South Los Angeles, daily life is overshadowed by frequent gun violence, particularly on 'Death Alley,' a two-mile portion of South Vermont Avenue near Imperial Highway. Since 2007, over 60 people have died there, mostly due to shootings. Local resident Christopher Calver Jr., who survived a 2012 drive-by where he was hit seven times, remembers almost losing a friend to a recent shooting. 

The area between Los Angeles and Inglewood—a stretch just 1.8 miles long—saw 100 homicides over seven years, as reported by the Los Angeles Times. Despite resources like a youth center and school programs, Westmont has no large-scale violence prevention initiative. Vermont Vista, which is adjacent to 'Death Alley,' recorded 57 homicides during the same timeframe.

Residents such as Angela Hawkins, who is saving to move her children to a safer place, struggle with constant concern. The toll of violence is personal for many, like Jackie Pineda, whose partner Isaiah Gray was killed outside their home in 2012. 

Statistics show that Black residents of Westmont are killed at four times the rate of Latinos. Around 40% of Westmont’s people live below the poverty line. Gang activity remains a significant threat, with groups like the Underground Crips, South Los, The Hoovers, 8 Trey Gangsters, Raymond Crips, and Rollin’ 100s present. Police report regular patrols and the need for residents to visibly show they aren’t armed.

The atmosphere is thick with frustration and fear, as communities yearn for normalcy where playing outside and simple strolls do not endanger lives.

Christopher Calver Jr., oikove peteĩ jeporojoka guasu rire 2012-pe (siete balínte), omandu'a mba'eichaitépa ha'e iñangirũ omano rangue hendive kuri peteĩ jeporojoka pyahu.

Pe territorio Los Angeles ha Inglewood pa'ũme—1.8 milla pukukuévo—Los Angeles Times he'i 100 jejuka oiko hague siete arýpe. Oĩ mitã renda ha mbo'ehao programa Westmont-pe, ha katu ndarekói programa tuicháva oñorãirõ ha jejuka joko hag̃ua. Vermont Vista, oĩva avei 'Death Alley' jerére, oguereko 57 jejuka upe árape.

Tapicha oikóva haguã py'aguapýpe, Angela Hawkins oñongatu pirapire ohoma hag̃ua iñemoñarépe ko'águi. Heta tapicha ohasa asy jehechauka rehe, peteĩcha Jackie Pineda reheve, iñirũ Isaiah Gray ojejukapyre hogaygua okápe 2012-pe.

Jejuka reheve, afroma oikóva Westmont-pe ojejuka irundy véseve Latino-kuéra rehe. 40% tapicha oikóva oĩ imboriahueterei. Gang-kuéra tuicháva umi rupi: Underground Crips, South Los, The Hoovers, 8 Trey Gangsters, Raymond Crips, ha Rollin’ 100s. Policía-kuéra oñangareko meme ha ojerure tapicha ohechauka ndorekói arma.

Oñandúva hína ñemondýi, tyejy ha py'ỹinte oipota tekoporã, ohecha haguã hendaitépe mitãnguéra oho okápe oiko ha oñembosarái oñembojopyre'ỹ rehe.

A Colorado man could be facing animal cruelty charges after allegedly abandoning his dog at Denver Animal Control last Monday. Officials report that the dog's owner, Daniel Sohn, was seen throwing his German Shepherd, named Bronson, into the shelter's lobby before quickly leaving. Despite this, Bronson managed to escape and ran after his owner. According to eyewitnesses, Sohn got into his vehicle, reversed, and nearly hit Bronson, who eventually jumped back into the car. Later the same day, Sohn attempted to leave Bronson at the shelter again, according to Lieutenant Aaron McSpadden of Denver Animal Control, who spoke with 9NEWS.

Sohn was located the following day by TheDenverChannel and confirmed that both the car and dog were his. He explained that Bronson followed him 'because we have a bit of a bond.' Sohn denies hitting Bronson and claims he was not intentionally trying to abandon his pet. 'He jumped in front of my car but I think he was triggered to do so by people around him,' said Sohn. Sohn also stated, 'I didn't ditch him. I actually dropped my dog off at the shelter where I first picked him up. I gave my dog a choice if he wanted to stay with me or find a new owner.' After two failed attempts to leave Bronson at the Denver Animal Shelter, Sohn said he drove with the dog to Los Angeles, where he claims Bronson jumped out of the car. 'Is he still alive? I'm sure he is,' Sohn told TheDenverChannel. Lieutenant McSpadden confirmed an investigation has begun into why Sohn attempted to leave Bronson without going through the proper surrender process.

Autoridad-kuéra omombe’u Daniel Sohn, ha’e orekóva peteĩ Ovecha Alemán hérava Bronson, opo’o ha omoinge Bronson refugio lobby-pe ha upéi pya’e osẽ. Bronson katu osẽ jeýnte oho ijararã reheve. Testigokuéra ohecha Sohn oike iñautópe, ojere omýi ha haimete oho ombohapy Bronson rehe, py’ỹi jagua oike jey iñautópe. Peteĩchagua árape, Sohn oheja jey Bronson refugio-pe, he’i Teniente Aaron McSpadden Denver Animal Control-gua, 9NEWS-pe.

Pe ára oúvape, Sohn oñe’ẽ TheDenverChannel-pe ha omyesakã pe auto ha jagua ha'eha iñe. Omombe’u avei Bronson oho hendive ‘ore mokõi ore rehegua vínculo rehehápe.’ Sohn oñemomba’e ijehegui he’ívo ndohupytyhague avei Bronson ha ndaha’éi ojapova’ekue oheja rei jagua. ‘Ha’e oike che renondépe, péro aimo’ã hague oiko umi gente jerére rupi,’ he’i Sohn. Avei he’i: ‘Che ndaha’éi oheja rei chupe. Añetehápe amongaru che jagua refugio-pe upepe amongaru hague avei hína chugui. Amoneĩ chupe oiporavo oho che ndive térã oikuaa ambue ijararã.’ Mokõi tentativa reínte rire Bronson ojeheja haguã refugio-pe, Sohn he’i ohohague hendive Los Angeles-pe, upépe he’i Bronson osẽhague iñautógui. ‘Ha’e gueteri oikovépa? Chemandu’a ha’eha, he’i Sohn TheDenverChannel-pe. Teniente McSpadden omombe’u oñepyrũ hague investigación mba’ére Sohn oheja Bronson rehe proceso correcta rehe’ỹ.

article_content: Scuba expert Derek Youd has an unusual dive companion: Yoyo, a macaroni penguin who loves helping divers improve their underwater skills. Yoyo, one of 70 penguins at the Living Coasts Zoo and Aquarium in Torquay, Devon, is central to the zoo’s 'diving with penguins' experience for qualified scuba divers. For Derek, 18-month-old Yoyo always makes the dive memorable. Hand-reared by keepers, Yoyo is very confident around people, eagerly helping divers as they prepare by inspecting their gear and fussing around them. Once in the water, Yoyo shows off his swimming skills, circling the divers and playfully tugging at any loose items. Yoyo’s playful personality means he’s often found close to Derek, both in and out of the water. Even though Yoyo has many penguin friends, sometimes keepers need to remind him that he’s a penguin too!

Derek-pe guarã, ko 18 mes orekóva Yoyo, katuete ome’ẽ experiencia memorable. Ýpe, Yoyo ohechauka mba’eichaite peve ikatupyryha, ojere buceador-kuéra rehe ha opoko hendive taha’e ikua rehe térã ipelo rehe. Yoyo rembiecharã ojapo chupe ovy’a meme Derec ndive, ýpe ha yvate avei. article_content: Shoppers at a Sainsbury’s Local in Nottingham have been left scratching their heads at a bank machine installed unusually close to the ground—just a couple feet high. To use this ATM, people have to crouch or kneel, making it an uncomfortable venture. Musician Steve Drury, 27, was among those who noticed and shared photos of the ATM online, pointing out how awkward it looked for users. Many others commented online, with people like Molly Kate Hancock questioning why the machine was set so low. Sainsbury’s explained that the ATM’s spot on a hillside caused the odd placement, but they wouldn’t elaborate further. The nearby World of Mobility shop highlighted that the ATM isn’t accessible for wheelchair users, as its height isn’t suitable. Sainsbury’s says it hasn’t received formal complaints about the ATM but is now looking into possible solutions.

Steve Drury, purahéiapoha 27 arýgua, ohecha upéva ha omyasãi jehapúva internet-pe, he’ívo mba’éichapa ojehecha vai oreréva tapicha oipuru hag̃uáicha. Oĩ heta ambueve omyasãiva peteĩcha, hend amonguéra Molly Kate Hancock oñembotuicháva mba’érepa pe cajero ojeguereko pype. Sainsbury’s he’i oĩha peteĩ yvy’y upépe ha upévare oñeme’ẽ peichaite, ha nohupytyi omombe’uve mba’eve. article_content: PARIS — A French commission examining sexual violence against children has called for removing all time limits on prosecuting people suspected of raping or sexually assaulting minors. The Independent Commission on Incest and Sexual Violence against Children (CIIVISE) also recommended making sexual abuse of children within families a distinct legal offense. Currently, French law allows prosecution of child sexual crimes up to 30 years after the victim legally becomes an adult at 18. In a report released Friday, the commission stated that eliminating the time limit is necessary because victims often take decades to come forward. CIIVISE was established two years ago after allegations of child abuse involving a prominent French political expert prompted a large social media movement, with hundreds sharing their stories of childhood abuse. According to the commission, about 160,000 children in France are victims of sexual violence each year. The conclusions are based on the analysis of 27,000 victim testimonies collected over two years. On average, victims were eight years old when the abuse began, and 80% were abused by a family member. The present statute of limitations prevents three-quarters of survivors from seeking justice, according to the report. In French, the word “inceste” is used broadly to refer to any sexual act between family members, including abuse of children, stepchildren, and younger siblings. The 2021 accusations against political expert Olivier Duhamel spurred debate on France’s response to child abuse. A book by Duhamel’s stepdaughter, Camille Kouchner, accused him of abusing her twin brother in the late 1980s when the siblings were 13. Until 2021, French law allowed for the possibility that a minor could consent to sex, resulting in some adults convicted of sexual assault receiving lighter sentences than for rape. Sexual assault carries a maximum 10-year prison sentence and a €150,000 ($163,000) fine, while rape is punishable by up to 20 years in prison. The French government later enacted a law stating that a child under 15 cannot consent to sex with an adult, closing this legal loophole. Some child protection groups still advocate for making statutory rape a specific crime. Many activists also continue to push for eliminating the statute of limitations for child sexual assault or rape. The World Health Organization says international studies show that one in five women and one in thirteen men report being sexually abused before turning 18. Experts note that these numbers are likely underestimated due to the secrecy surrounding the issue.

Comisión Independiente de Incesto ha Violencia Sexual rehe mitãre (CIIVISE) he’i avei ojejapo hag̃ua peteĩ ley ohechauka ha’eháicha peteĩ crimen especial abuso sexual oikóva ogapýpe. Ko’ágã, Francia-pe, ley omoneĩ oikeha umi proceso ohechauka abuso sexual rehe mitãre 30 ary haguépe omokunu’ũ guive 18 ára mitã oikóvo legalmente kakuaa. CIIVISE oñemohu’ã mokõi arýpe haguã umi denuncia ndive peteĩ político bekannte rehe, oiniciáva peteĩ gran movimiento redes sociales-pe, opavave omombe’u hag̃ua ijehegui ohasava’ekue mitãme. Comisión he’i, año-ryrýi, Francia-pe, 160.000 mitã ha’e víctima violencia sexual rehe. Informe oguereko 27.000 testimonio víctima rehe ojeanalisa mokõi ary jave. Promedio-pe, umi mitã abusado oguereko 8 ary oñepyrũvo abuso, ha 80% umi abusado ha’e hógape. Ko límite de tiempo omoinge’ỹ ¾ umi sobreviviente ojerure justicia, comisión he’i. Francia ñe'ẽme, “inceste” he'ise umi acto sexual oikóva familia apytépe, peteĩ mitã, hijastro térã joyke’y rehe voi. Oñemoĩ 2021-pe denuncia político Olivier Duhamel rehe ha ojapo heta debate Francia-pe ojehecha hag̃ua mba’éichapa oñeñangareko mitã rehe. Duhamel hijastrokuña, Camille Kouchner, ohai peteĩ aranduka omongaruha ijermano gemelo rehe abuse 1980-pe, ha’ekuéra 13 ary rehe. 2021 mboyve, ley francesa omoneĩ posibilidad peteĩ mitã ikatuha oime oñotỹguáicha sexo rehe, upéva rupi heta adulto condenado sexualmente omohonandi výro sentencias oñembojoajúvo rape rehe. Abuso sexual oguereko máxima 10 ary kársel-pe ha multa €150.000 ($163.000), rape katu ohupyty 20 ary. Gobierno francés oi omoîhague ley 15 arýgua ykére mitã ndaikatúi ohechauka consentimiento, upéicha ojoko pe vacío legal. Umi grupo oñangarekóva mitãre gueteri ojerure ojehapytĩ rape estatutario crimen mante térã. Activista hetave ojerure avei oñehundi umi límite tiempo crímenes sexuales contra mitã. OMS he’i, estudios internacionales ohechauka peteĩ pa mujer rehe guasu ha peteĩ 13 kuimba’e rehe omombe’u hague ohasa abuso sexual 18 guive mboyve. Expertokuéra he’i número ikatu iñambué ndojeikuaái haguére.

article_content: Dozens of Israeli security personnel entered the al-Aqsa mosque compound in Jerusalem on Friday after Palestinians threw rocks at police stationed nearby, according to Israeli police spokesman Micky Rosenfeld. Following Friday prayers, more than 100 Palestinians reportedly began throwing stones at a police post, prompting a response from Israeli forces. Witnesses said the police used tear gas and rubber bullets to disperse the crowd. Ziad Hammouri, director of the Palestinian Jerusalem Center for Socio-Economic Rights, reported that several Palestinians were arrested, with some sustaining injuries. This confrontation is the latest in a series of clashes and incidents involving stone-throwing at the site over the past week. There have been reports that Israeli authorities allowed right-wing Jewish activists access to the compound, which has contributed to rising tensions with Palestinians.

Arete rire, mas de 100 palestinoa oity itá policíape, upévare policía oike. Testigokuéra he'i policía oipuru gas lacrimógeno ha balín de goma omondopa hag̃ua. Ziad Hammouri, omoakãva Jerusalénguá Centro Palestino de Derechos Socioeconómicos, he'i oĩ hague oñemokañýva ha hasýva palestinoguakuéra. Ko mba'e oiko rire avei heta jey oñondive siniestru ha itá japi oike tupão rendápe última arapokõindy jave. article_content: A serious accident left the centuries-old Fox and Hounds pub in Barley, Hertfordshire, heavily damaged after a car crashed through the front. The Peugeot 306 careened off the road, went airborne, and tore through a children's play area and stock room before halting at the kitchen wall. The crash occurred at around 12:40pm on Tuesday, August 20, 2013. Emergency services responded swiftly; firefighters extracted the 64-year-old driver, who remains in critical condition at Addenbrooke’s Hospital in Cambridge. Thankfully, no customers or staff were harmed. The pub’s front has a significant hole, now covered temporarily, and workers are busy cleaning up and repairing. Owner Adrian Parkes plans to reopen for drinks by Friday or Saturday, with meals expected Sunday. However, a full menu will take longer to resume, as much of the homemade food was lost. Paramedics, firefighters, and the Herts Air Ambulance all took part in the emergency response. Despite the upheaval, Parkes is determined to reopen quickly.

Bombero-kuéra ou sapy’aite, osalva chófer 64-ary guaré, oĩ ojavyetereíma Addenbrooke’s Hospital, Cambridge-pe. Vyrorei cliente térã umi omba’apóva rehe. Taberna oguereko peteĩ agujero tuicháva tenondépe, oñembohypýi tempora-rã ha oĩ umi oñemopotî ha oñemoporâjey haguã. Jára Adrian Parkes oipota ojoavri viernes térã sábado haguã, ha domingo ho’u tembi’u. Menú completo katu ojeguerekóta tardeve, heta tembi’u oñehundi haguére. Oĩ bombero, paramédico ha Herts Air Ambulance oipytyvõva. Adrian Parkes he’i ipyapýva rehe omotenondejeýta taberna.

article_content: An 11-year-old autistic boy, Charlie Birely, tragically died on Sunday when his family's sailboat caught fire near Stuart, Florida. His parents, Brian Birely, 59, and Karen Laake, 53, are recovering in the hospital after suffering from smoke inhalation. On the morning of the incident, Brian Birely had gone ashore when he heard an explosion and saw the sailboat in flames. He quickly returned to the burning vessel in a small boat and managed to rescue his wife, Karen, but was unable to save their son, Charlie. The couple's 13-year-old daughter, Abigail, was not on the boat at the time. Brian attempted to pull Charlie from the fire and then searched for a fire extinguisher, but when he returned, he was unable to locate him. The explosion was so powerful that it was heard onshore, and the fire quickly engulfed the entire boat, intensified by a propane tank that exploded. Police responded but could not board the vessel due to the extreme heat. Despite their efforts and those of nearby boaters, only Brian and Karen made it to safety with the help of a small dinghy. Both were then transported to a Miami hospital for treatment. Local resident Frank Pagnini, who knew the family, described seeing the fully engulfed boat, remarking on the extent of the damage. The community has rallied around the Birely family, raising more than $10,000 through a GoFundMe campaign organized by Jennell Eve, a family friend, who spoke warmly about their character and kindness. The remains of the boat have been moved to a storage facility. Investigations into the cause of the fire are ongoing, with local police and several agencies involved. The state medical examiner is also reviewing the wreckage.

article_content: Since transferring from Atletico Madrid, Diego Costa has quickly established himself at Chelsea, netting seven goals in his first four Premier League games. Yet, against Manchester City, he faced a real challenge against renowned defender Vincent Kompany. In this high-profile match, Costa struggled to assert himself for much of the first half. He found himself defending more frequently than attacking and barely saw the ball, with Kompany effectively shutting him down and limiting his chances, particularly as Cesc Fabregas was unable to provide his usual support due to City's disciplined defending. This situation was largely a result of Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho’s tactical setup, which prioritized defensive solidity and restricted Chelsea’s own attacking play. On the rare occasions Costa got into City’s box, he was either caught offside or couldn’t get a shot on target. Tensions rose on the pitch, especially in a confrontation with Pablo Zabaleta, which led to the City defender receiving a red card. Until then, Costa had lost every duel with City players. But after Zabaleta’s dismissal, Chelsea had more room to attack, and Costa became more involved, notably helping to set up Andre Schurrle’s goal after linking with Eden Hazard. Late in the match, Costa managed a shot on goal and struck the post, showing flashes of his quality, but Kompany’s strong defending kept him from scoring. By the time Costa was substituted, it was clear that Kompany remained the dominant force, preventing Costa from making his usual game-winning impact.

Oimeve oñangarekóvo imba’erehe ojapóva ataque rangue, ha Kompany imbaretépe ojoko chupe, avei Cesc Fabregas ndokatúi oipytyvõ chupe City defensa hatã rupi. Ko situasión oiko José Mourinho rembiaporã reheve, omoĩ hague tenda ñangarekohápe Chelsea ha upéicha avei ome’ẽ’ỹve ataque. Umi pokãve jave Costa og̃uahẽ City área-pe, ha’e oĩ offside térã ndojapói sapy’aitépe mba’eve. Tensaión oñembohape Campo-pe, Pablo Zabaleta ndive oñorãirõ rire ha upéi ojepe’a ha’éva City-gui. Upéva mboyve, Costa ohasa rei va’ekue umi 10 pegua ñeñorãirõrã City rehe. Zabaleta ojepe’a rire, Chelsea oikotevẽve ohupi ataque ha Costa oipytyvõ mbykymi ataque-pe, ome’ẽvo pelota Hazard-pe ha’éva ome’ẽ Schurrle-pe gol. Ipahápe, Costa ojapose peteĩ tiro portería rehe ha ojapo avei pe poste rehe. Ohechauka ikatupyry, péro Kompany oñangareko hatã hese ani chupe ojapo gol. article_content: Telehealth Success: How to Thrive in the New Age of Remote Care by Drs. Aditi U. Joshi and Brandon M. Welch has been released by Forbes Books. The book is now available on Amazon in hardcover, Kindle, and Audible formats. During the disruption of healthcare caused by COVID-19, Drs. Joshi and Welch already had extensive experience in telehealth. Dr. Joshi served as a director in an emergency department that prioritized telehealth, while Dr. Welch is the co-founder and CEO of doxy.me, a telehealth software company that saw rapid growth following the initial lockdowns. After the pandemic, Dr. Welch observed that clinicians who effectively used telemedicine continued its adoption, while others disbanded its use. This insight led Drs. Joshi and Welch to collaborate and offer guidance for the future of healthcare, addressing both technological and clinical viewpoints. Their book argues that telehealth can make healthcare more accessible, convenient, affordable, and equitable. Telehealth Success offers a comprehensive roadmap for clinicians, focusing on five success domains: patients, clinical practice, technology, finance, and compliance. By applying these strategies, healthcare organizations can maximize the benefits of telemedicine. Drs. Joshi and Welch state, 'We wrote this book to assist healthcare stakeholders, clinicians, startups, and organizations working in healthcare to understand how to succeed with telemedicine. The five domains outlined provide insight into telehealth’s past, present, and future.' About the Authors: Dr. Aditi U. Joshi, MD, MSc, is a telehealth expert and emergency medicine physician who consults with health systems and digital health startups to improve healthcare delivery through technology. Dr. Brandon M. Welch, MS, Ph.D., is an innovator and telehealth leader, and the founder and CEO of doxy.me. He leverages his experience to advise on optimizing telehealth practices and healthcare innovation. article_content: The Isle of Wight Festival will return to Seaclose Park in Newport from June 20 to 23, 2024, with headline performances by The Prodigy, Pet Shop Boys, and Green Day. Other confirmed acts include Keane, Simple Minds, Zara Larsson, McFly, Beverley Knight, Scouting For Girls, Britpop band Suede, and DJ Jo Whiley with her popular 90s anthems, who will lead the entertainment in the big top arena. The Prodigy will take the main stage on Friday, followed by the Pet Shop Boys on Saturday. On Sunday, Green Day will make their only UK festival appearance of the year, a booking that promoter John Giddings had pursued for five years. Giddings expressed his happiness about confirming Green Day, stating, “I’m over the moon. It’s just a relief to be able to announce it. I had them confirmed six weeks ago but couldn’t tell anyone, so I’m pleased it’s out there.” He praised the headliners, saying, “The Prodigy deliver an incredible show. The Pet Shop Boys have had more hits than I’ve had hot dinners. It’s going to be a great weekend.” John Giddings has managed the revived Isle of Wight Festival since 2002, after attending one of the original events in 1970. Previous headliners have included legends like the Rolling Stones, Queen and Adam Lambert, and Robbie Williams. Giddings said, “It’s something I take great pride in. To see 50,000 people in a field enjoying themselves is the greatest pleasure I have—I enjoy it so much.”

article_content: Sierra Space is finalizing preparations for its Dream Chaser spaceplane, which is set to head to NASA's Neil Armstrong Test Facility in Ohio for intensive testing designed to ensure it can safely withstand the intense heat and stress experienced during reentry through Earth's atmosphere—an essential milestone prior to operational flights. Currently located at Sierra Space’s Louisville, Colorado facility, Dream Chaser will soon embark on a 60-mile trip to Sandusky, Ohio. At the NASA facility, it will spend one to three months undergoing testing in a large thermal vacuum chamber, simulating the physical demands and extreme environments of rocket launches and spaceflight. These evaluations are critical steps as Sierra Space targets 2024 for Dream Chaser’s first mission. Under a NASA Commercial Resupply Services 2 contract secured in 2016, the company is contracted for at least seven uncrewed deliveries to the International Space Station. The first operational spaceplane, named Tenacity, is being readied for launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan Centaur rocket, contingent on successful completion of testing and the Vulcan’s own first launch. The last stages of assembly for Tenacity are nearly complete, with final checks on landing gear and systems wrapping up before shipment. The vehicle features folding wings that deploy in orbit, solar panels to generate power, and a durable heat shield to survive atmospheric reentry. This configuration allows for safe rocket launches, runway landings, and sustained operations in low Earth orbit. Unlike suborbital spaceplanes from other companies, Dream Chaser is designed for orbital missions lasting up to six months. The U.S. Space Force’s own spaceplane recently completed a lengthy orbital mission as well. Although reusable rockets are a major focus in today’s commercial space industry, spaceplanes like Dream Chaser offer certain advantages: smoother landings, operational safety, flexibility, and the potential to open new commercial opportunities. Looking forward, Sierra Space plans to launch crewed missions and establish its own space station, though its partnership with Blue Origin on the Orbital Reef station is currently uncertain. As Tenacity’s anticipated launch approaches, Dream Chaser may soon become a key player in commercial space operations.

article_content: In Brazil, Phamela de Souza was surprised during her ten-week ultrasound when she and her husband, Marcelo, noticed what seemed to be the face of Marcelo’s late mother. The scan was performed in a hospital in Brasilia, just four months after his mother had passed away. When they looked at the scan at home, both felt the image in the top corner closely resembled the grandmother. They showed the picture to friends and family, many of whom agreed and found the resemblance unsettling. Although previous scans had not shown anything out of the ordinary, the de Souza family interprets the apparition as a comforting sign that the late grandmother is watching over them. Their daughter is now three, and Marcelo believes his mother continues to look after her. The experience has left a meaningful impression on their family and friends.

Agnikul Cosmos, a Chennai-based aerospace startup co-founded by Moin SPM (COO) and Srinath Ravichandran (CEO), has secured $26.7 million in a Series B funding round, bringing its total funding to $40 million. The investment included new backers Celesta Capital, Rocketship.vc, Artha Select Fund, and Artha Venture Fund, alongside existing supporters Mayfield India, Pi Ventures, and Speciale Invest. Agnikul has not disclosed its latest valuation.

Established in 2017, Agnikul designs and builds rockets for satellites weighing less than 100 kilograms. Its main launch vehicle, the Agnibaan SubOrbital Technological Demonstrator (SOrTeD), offers five configurations tailored to client requirements. A highlight of Agnikul's technology is Agnilet, its patented 3D-printed rocket engine, which the company claims is the world’s first single-piece 3D-printed engine.

The new funding will support Agnikul’s first commercial launches, construction of key launch infrastructure, and expansion of production, operations, and technology teams. The initial launch is planned for the end of 2023 from Agnikul’s private launch pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre.

CEO Srinath Ravichandran attributes increased optimism in the sector to India’s Chandrayaan-3 lunar mission, which landed on the moon’s south polar region in August, making India the first to reach this area and the fourth country to achieve a lunar landing. In April, the Indian government announced its first national space policy to encourage private participation.

India’s spacetech startup sector is experiencing rapid growth, with 190 registered companies as noted by Deloitte, the Indian Space Association, and NASSCOM in October. Key startups include Pixxel ($36M raised in June), Skyroot Aerospace ($51M in September), and Bellatrix, recently featured in Forbes Asia’s 100 to Watch and reportedly seeking further investment.

article_content: Over the last two years, the Nigerian Shippers Council (NSC) has launched significant efforts to combat long-standing extortion along port access roads, which had contributed to high freight costs. Since Emmanuel Jime became Executive Secretary in 2021, the NSC has made headway through reform and improved order at major ports, especially in Lagos. Truck and trailer drivers once faced illegal levies from non-state actors when entering port complexes. Despite rising fuel costs and operators’ complaints, the problem persisted until the NSC, under Jime, partnered with industry stakeholders and created the Ports Standing Task Team (PSTT), aiming to eliminate these unlawful payments. Industry figures like ENL Consortium’s Mark Walsh and former customs leaders Olayiwola Shittu and Eugene Nweke have credited the NSC's collaborative approach and deployment of the Nigerian Ports Process Manual (NPPM) for driving industry efficiency and better compliance. Still, there are concerns about the Council’s compromised enforcement powers given the constraints in the legislation establishing it. While some were initially uncertain about Jime’s suitability for the role due to his background outside the port sector, he quickly built credibility by fostering agency cooperation and bringing more transparency into port regulation. The NSC also asserted its authority over issues like cargo clearance and cost setting, reminding police and other port authorities of the Council's regulatory mandate. The adoption of the NPPM and new procedures resulted in joint boarding and inspection of vessels, minimizing port delays and enhancing operational efficiency. Clearing agents report that the implementation of these reforms has improved cargo turnaround times and reduced congestion. The Council’s efforts in arbitration and dispute resolution in import and export trade have been recognized as strengthening its role as an industry ombudsman. Despite resistance from some stakeholders and the need for legislative strengthening, the consensus is that the NSC, under Jime’s leadership, has had a positive impact on Nigeria’s maritime sector. The NSC continues working to establish itself as the central economic regulator, improve industry awareness, deepen stakeholder engagement, and enhance its regulatory and enforcement capacity.

Emmanuel Jime oñemoĩvo Secretario Ejecutivo ramo 2021-pe, NSC ohechauka oñemyatyrõha ha omoĩha orden puertokuéra tuichavévape, upéi Lagos-pe. article_content: Linda Yaccarino, the CEO of X (formerly Twitter), has hired her son, Matt Madrazo, to lead the company's political advertising sales despite his limited experience in this specific area. X is targeting approximately $100 million in revenue from political ads during the 2024 Presidential election period. There have been reports that some colleagues advised Yaccarino to step down from her position at X due to criticisms regarding leadership, brand safety, and controversial content moderation decisions. Rather than resign, Yaccarino moved forward with hiring her son. Matt Madrazo previously worked in ad sales for Studio71, a creator-focused media company, but had not specifically sold political ads before. He is now working closely with company leadership to rebuild X's political advertising segment, with a focus on attracting campaign spending for the 2024 elections. X had banned political ads in 2019 due to concerns over disinformation, but current management has chosen to resume political advertising as a revenue strategy. Advertising remains crucial for the company's revenue despite efforts by owner Elon Musk to promote a subscription-based model. The decision has drawn criticism from some observers, given the current challenges faced by X, including negative publicity, advertiser concerns, financial pressures, and allegations related to controversial content on the platform.

X oipota ohupyty $100 millón política publicidá suaite 2024-pe, Presidencial ñemuhã guasu jave. Oĩ kuri he'i haguã ambué kuñakarai Yaccarino-pe ohejántema tembiapo X-pe, oje'e peteĩhápe crítica rehe, seguridad de marca, ha contenido moderación rehegua, ha'e katu odesidi omba'apo Itaño'y ndive.
