article_content: Sean Geddes, a forward for Worcester City, balances a remarkable double life: He crafts components for Lewis Hamilton's Formula One car by day and scores spectacular football goals by night. Recently, Geddes made headlines after netting two goals that eliminated former winners Coventry City from the FA Cup's first round. He followed up with a stunning 'rabona' goal against Barrow in the FA Trophy, earning comparisons to Erik Lamela and Lionel Messi. This impressive piece of skill went viral, racking up nearly two million social media views worldwide. At 22, Geddes is a former Manchester United trainee now working as a machinist at A&M EDM Ltd. in the West Midlands, close to West Brom's Hawthorns stadium. A signed Mercedes poster from Hamilton and Rosberg hangs in the company reception, recognizing their contributions to this year’s Formula One championship. Still, Geddes’s fame stems not only from engineering excellence but also from his eye-catching performances for Worcester City, who travel to Scunthorpe for their FA Cup second-round clash. Videos of his Barrow wonder-goal have circulated globally, bringing him unexpected recognition. Geddes, who cycles to work and returns to the factory each morning after big matches, admits the attention is new. 'I’m getting messages from friends across Norway and America—they’ve seen the goal online,' he shares. 'The rabona is something I’ve tried since childhood, just part of my game. I didn’t even think about it; it was instinct.' Despite the attention, Geddes prefers a low-key life, splitting his time between the factory—where his mother Jo also works—and the football pitch. He values hard work, saving toward a house deposit rather than living off football wages, and helps operate complex molding machinery. On occasion, he works Saturday mornings before matches. 'After the Coventry game, I went for a pint but didn’t celebrate much—I had an early shift. That’s fine by me; I like working, and I know football careers can be short,' he says. Although football is a major topic at work, Geddes admits he prefers playing the game to watching it or supporting a club. Now with Worcester City in Conference North after stints at Manchester United, Walsall, and Stourbridge, Geddes has an impressive nine goals in 17 games. Worcester sits eighth in their league, brimming with renewed energy despite ground-sharing disruptions. Geddes’s performances have caught the interest of league clubs, but he remains focused. As he prepares for the FA Cup fixture against Scunthorpe, he reflects on his time alongside Danny Welbeck and Ravel Morrison at Manchester United. 'Danny was quiet but clearly talented. Ravel was the joker, but immensely gifted.' He remembers disagreements with a Walsall manager, leading to a loan spell, but is now settled and enjoying his football. The excitement of recent matches and passionate support from Worcester fans motivates him. 'At Coventry, the fans were incredible—singing all match. It’s my best football memory and makes us believe we can achieve even more.'

Ko’ágãramo, Geddes oiko herakuã mokõi gol ojapo haguére Coventry City rehe, ojapohávo heta mba’e porã FA Cup primera ronda-pe. Geddes oreko 22 ary, ha’e oikóva kuri Manchester United remimbo’e ramo, ha ko’ág̃a omba’apo machinista ramo A&M EDM Ltd.-pe, West Midlands-pe, hi’aguĩ West Brom Hawthorns estadio-gui. Video ohechaukáva ij ‘rabona’ gol Barrow rehe ojere hína oparupi internet rupi, ohechauka chupe herakuãhápe. Geddes oñani hína hekópe omba’apohápe ha ára pyahu oho jey fábrica-pe partido guasu rire. 'Ikatu che rehegua ndaha’éi aikotevẽ herakuã, ha katu oreko che rembiapo guasu. Che angirũ Noruega ha Estados Unidos-pegua ohenói hína chéve—ojuhúma upe gol online-rupi,' he’i. Ojapo tembiapo pohãno, oñongatu plata ohepyme’ẽ haguãrã óga peve, ndaha’éi oikose fútbol rehe año. Sapy’ánte avei omba’apo sábado pyhareve partido mboyve. 'Coventry partido rire, aha che tavarandúpe peteĩ cerveza haguã, péro ndachepochýi heta—ikatútama chepyhare sapy’aitépe che trabajo rehegua. Che ndachepochýi, chegustaiterei trabajo, ha aikuaa futbolista rapykuere ikatuha ipaha pya’e,' he’i. Fábrica-pe heta oñeñe’ẽ fútbol rehe, péro Geddes he’i ogustaveha ojapo fútbol oguerekóva, ndaha’éi ohecharamo equipo térã ohecháva partido. 'Danny hína peteĩ ojaporãva, Ravel katu peteĩ jokára, talentoiterei.' Ogueromandu’a ohecha hague jepy’apy Walsall manager rehe, upéicha rupi ova préstamo-rupi, péro ko’ág̃a oĩ porã ha ovy’a fútbol rehe. article_content: China has continued to expand its arsenal of missiles, nearly doubling the number of DF-21 medium-range ballistic missiles it possesses, according to the US Department of Defense’s latest China Military Power Report. By the end of 2022, the Pentagon estimates China had approximately 1,000 DF-21 missiles, up sharply from a little over 500 in 2021. This increase highlights the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force’s ongoing efforts to improve its missile capabilities, a key element of China’s strategy to deter foreign intervention in regional conflicts, such as potential disputes over Taiwan. The DF-21, which NATO designates as CSS-5, can strike targets 1,000 to 3,000 kilometers away—sufficient for reaching US bases anywhere in Japan. However, its range is limited compared to the intermediate-range DF-26, which can reach as far as Guam. The short-range DF-11, DF-15, and DF-16 are more suited for strikes on Taiwan itself. Analysts such as Tom Shugart, a former US Navy officer and senior fellow at the Center for a New American Security, note that the DF-21’s reach places all of Japan within China’s missile range, potentially posing a significant threat to US bases and undermining deterrence in the region. The missile is road-mobile, solid-fueled, and has been deployed by China since the early 1990s, with various versions developed for nuclear and conventional land-attack or anti-ship missions. The anti-ship variant, sometimes called a ‘carrier killer,’ is believed to be capable of threatening US Navy aircraft carriers, though some doubt exists about its effectiveness against moving targets. China’s current stockpile of about 1,000 medium-range ballistic missiles includes both land-attack and anti-ship variants, as well as limited numbers of the hypersonic DF-17. This buildup continues a longstanding priority for China: in 2017, a RAND report observed that US military bases in Japan were already within range of thousands of accurate Chinese missiles. The same report detailed how, by 2015, China’s missile forces had grown from a handful of inaccurate short-range rockets to over 1,200 conventionally armed ballistic missiles, including the DF-21C aimed at targets across Japan. China’s emphasis is not just on quantity but also on increasing accuracy. As Tom Shugart wrote in 2017, China’s improvements in both accuracy and numbers have given it an unprecedented ability to strike US and allied facilities—such as bases, logistics hubs, and command centers—quickly and without using nuclear weapons or establishing air superiority. This expansion comes as US–China relations remain tense, with limited channels of military communication and growing concerns over the risk of incidents or miscalculations escalating into a crisis. The Pentagon reported that in 2022, the Chinese military largely refused or ignored requests for official communication, a trend that continued into 2023 alongside increasingly assertive Chinese military maneuvers.

Ko oñemomba’eguasu China mbarete rapereka Rocket Force ojapo hína, parte iñimportanteva China rembiapokue ombohovái haguã ambue tetã oikeva regional conflicto-pe, por ehémplo ohóramo jeiko vai Taiwán rehe. article_content: Fiji’s Rugby World Cup campaign began and ended with narrow defeats against top-tier nations. Despite the pain of elimination, coach Simon Raiwalui believes the Pacific Islanders have more to offer in the future. On Sunday, Fiji lost 30-24 to England in the quarter-finals in Marseille, marking their third defeat in five games at the tournament in France. However, there is a strong belief that the team will continue progressing ahead of the 2027 World Cup in Australia. "For 15 weeks, these boys have worked hard and we will celebrate that," said Raiwalui. "We’re hurting now, but I couldn’t be prouder of this group and what they’ve achieved. They’ve built a foundation for the next generation of Fijian rugby players." Fiji's opening 32-26 defeat to Wales demonstrated both their potential and the unpredictable, free-spirited style reminiscent of the country’s famous rugby Sevens. They then recorded a superb 22-15 win over Australia and a determined 17-12 victory against Georgia, setting them on course for the knockout stages. Although they suffered a surprising 24-23 loss to Portugal, they secured enough points to advance. Against England, Fiji fought back from a 14-point deficit to draw level with 10 minutes remaining, but ultimately lacked the experience to secure the win. England coach Steve Borthwick praised the Fijian team, stating, "They have had a brilliant World Cup, and their squad is filled with world-class players. The speed and skill they showed in scoring consecutive tries is rare in world rugby." Fiji's progress has been amplified by the involvement of the Fijian Drua in Super Rugby, with 17 players from their 33-man squad in France hailing from that team. While Fiji remains dangerous with ball in hand, they recognize the need to improve their set-piece and breakdown play against top-level opponents. "We’re hurting at the moment and it will take time to recover because we believed we could go further. Still, the belief and pride in this team have always been strong," Raiwalui said. "The pride is everlasting—these boys are family, and that will never change."

article_content: Dominique Strauss-Kahn had a sexual relationship with Anne Mansouret, the mother of Tristane Banon, who has accused the former International Monetary Fund chief of attempted rape. Mansouret stated the encounter took place in 2000, describing it as consensual but 'brutal'. At the time, both were working at the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development, where Strauss-Kahn was a special adviser. Anne Mansouret, 65, revealed her past relationship with Strauss-Kahn during a police interview as a witness in the ongoing investigation into her daughter's allegations. Banon alleges Strauss-Kahn assaulted her in 2003 during an interview for a book she was writing. Mansouret, a regional official in the Socialist Party, said she kept her encounter with Strauss-Kahn secret until her daughter confided in her in 2003. Mansouret also met with Brigitte Guillemette, Strauss-Kahn’s former wife, who then confronted him about the alleged incident. According to Mansouret, Strauss-Kahn expressed regret about his actions involving both women. Banon has publicly described the alleged assault, comparing Strauss-Kahn's behavior to that of a 'rutting chimpanzee'. She also claimed her mother advised her not to file charges at the time. L'Express magazine reported that the previous relationship between Strauss-Kahn and Mansouret may explain why Banon waited eight years before approaching the police. Strauss-Kahn's daughter, Camille, a friend of Banon's, has also been questioned by police in connection with the case. Separately, Strauss-Kahn is awaiting trial in New York on separate charges related to the alleged assault of a hotel maid. His lawyer in France, Henri Leclerc, has denied Banon's allegations, calling them imaginary and has initiated legal action against Banon for libel. The case has caused divisions within the French Socialist Party, though some senior figures still argue Strauss-Kahn should run for president against Nicolas Sarkozy. Meanwhile, Francois Hollande, the leading Socialist candidate, has been questioned about whether he knew about Banon's allegations in 2003. Hollande maintains he acted properly and will not allow the case to be used for political purposes.

article_content: Last week, nine out of India's top ten most valuable publicly traded companies saw their collective market capitalization jump by about Rs 97,463 crore, with Reliance Industries making the largest gains. The BSE benchmark index also rose by 580.98 points, amounting to a 0.91% increase. With Bajaj Finance as the sole exception, all the other leading firms—including Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and State Bank of India—saw increases in their market value. Reliance Industries' market cap jumped by Rs 36,399 crore to reach Rs 15,68,995 crore, while State Bank of India added Rs 15,305 crore, bringing its total to Rs 5,15,976 crore. ICICI Bank’s value increased by Rs 14,749 crore to Rs 6,54,042 crore, and HDFC Bank gained Rs 11,657 crore to total Rs 11,25,842 crore. Bharti Airtel’s market valuation grew by Rs 9,352 crore (now at Rs 5,23,087 crore), while Hindustan Unilever added Rs 6,320 crore to reach Rs 5,89,418 crore. Infosys was up by Rs 3,507 crore (now Rs 5,76,529 crore). TCS’s valuation increased by Rs 109 crore to Rs 12,26,093 crore, and ITC added Rs 62 crore for a total of Rs 5,40,699 crore. Meanwhile, the market value of Bajaj Finance fell by Rs 5,211 crore, placing it at Rs 4,49,604 crore. Reliance Industries stayed on top as India's most valuable firm, followed in order by TCS, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Hindustan Unilever, Infosys, ITC, Bharti Airtel, State Bank of India, and Bajaj Finance. Significantly, Sweden’s Saab is the first foreign company to receive full approval for 100% foreign direct investment in India’s defense sector, enabling them to create a rocket manufacturing facility. The State Bank of India reported an 8% increase in second-quarter net profit, citing strong credit demand and a decrease in provision costs as key factors. Additionally, Byju’s disclosed a standalone revenue of ₹3,569 crore for the financial year ending March 2022—a 2.3-fold increase—with its core EBITDA losses narrowing to ₹2,253 crore, down from ₹2,406 crore the previous year.

article_content: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has warned about a listeria outbreak tied to certain peaches, nectarines, and plums, after 10 people were hospitalized and one person died across seven states. The outbreak involves non-organic fruits sold nationwide under the 'HMC Farms' and 'Signature Farms' names. HMC Group Marketing voluntarily recalled these fruits, which were available from May 1 to November 15 in both 2022 and 2023. Recalled fruits can be recognized by a 'USA-E-U' sticker and these PLU numbers: 4044 or 4038 (yellow peach), 4401 (white peach), 4036 or 4378 (yellow nectarine), 3035 (white nectarine), 4042 (red plum), and 4040 (black plum), including those sold in two-pound bags. The CDC’s investigation continues to determine if more fruits or products could be contaminated. Listeria is especially dangerous for pregnant people, seniors, or those with weakened immune systems as it may spread beyond the intestines. People who consumed the fruit could develop symptoms like fever, muscle pain, or fatigue any time from the same day up to 10 weeks after eating it. The CDC urges consumers to check freezers and discard or return recalled fruit, and to clean surfaces and containers touched by these fruits. HMC Group Marketing, through spokesperson Amy Philpott, expressed their commitment to food safety and sympathy for those affected, noting they're cooperating with the FDA in the investigation.

Umi oñemboja oúva hese ikatu oñandu tĩsyry, akãngusu ha kane'õ oúvo cualquiera aravo guive uso rire guive pe frutare, ko’ã síntoma ikatu ojevýkuaa upe árape térã 10 semana rire. article_content: Publicis Groupe India has appointed Kedar Teny as its first Chief Product Officer. In this role, Teny will focus on strengthening connectivity with clients and expanding the company’s expertise and services. This strategic appointment underscores Publicis Groupe’s commitment to investing in the Indian market as it continues to grow. Teny will be responsible for overseeing and expanding the company’s product offerings, utilizing capabilities in creative, media, commerce, public relations, production, digital technology, and analytics. He will work closely with leadership and strategy teams to craft business strategies that deliver value and long-term growth for clients. Teny will report directly to Anupriya Acharya, South Asia CEO of Publicis Groupe. With around 25 years of industry experience, Teny brings strong expertise in advertising and marketing. Anupriya Acharya welcomed Teny’s appointment, highlighting his marketing credentials and deep understanding of the agency ecosystem, as well as his approachable demeanor, which makes him well-suited for the role. She also emphasized that innovation and client-centricity remain central to the company’s strategy, with the Chief Product Officer role being a significant step in this direction. In response, Kedar Teny noted that the role represents both a significant opportunity and responsibility, expressing his excitement to join a company with strong clients, leading agencies, and robust growth momentum. He looks forward to working with the leadership team to generate noteworthy business impact. article_content:
Apple CEO Tim Cook has revealed that the upcoming Apple Watch could potentially replace your car keys, offering a convenient alternative to traditional key fobs. In an interview with The Telegraph, Cook confirmed the watch’s battery is expected to last all day and will charge faster than an iPhone.

Apple has scheduled a special media event in San Francisco on March 9 to showcase the Apple Watch ahead of its April launch. The invitation, titled 'Spring Forward,' plays on resetting clocks for daylight saving time, though it does not specify the event’s exact content.

The Apple Watch brings several innovative features, including a taptic engine for subtle notifications and a new user interface with a digital crown—a dial for zooming, scrolling, and returning to the home screen. Users can customize the watch face through taps, swipes, and force touches.

To promote physical activity, the device rewards users with credits for meeting exercise goals. Consistent activity can increase these goals, supporting healthier habits. Cook mentioned the watch can remind users to move if they are sedentary, addressing concerns from doctors about prolonged sitting.

Messaging on the watch works through voice dictation, emoji, or preset responses as there is no keyboard. Siri is integrated for voice commands. Users can also control iPhone music, view information via 'Glances,' and respond to messages by voice.

Apple experimented with advanced sensors for measuring stress and heart rate, but results varied for some individuals. Nonetheless, the watch provides reliable health and fitness tracking features.

The Apple Watch is priced starting at $349 and is expected to begin shipping in April, marking Apple’s entry into the wearable device market. This comes as Apple becomes the first company to reach a $700 billion market value, achieving record-breaking iPhone sales and a quarterly revenue of $74.6 billion. Apple’s cash reserves now exceed $178 billion, surpassing funding amounts for major national services.

Apple is expanding globally, with new stores and broader distribution, particularly in China. Analyst Brian White of Cantor Fitzgerald predicts continued growth due to strong iPhone sales, ongoing 4G expansion, and excitement for the Apple Watch. Apple’s stock remains attractively valued relative to its significant profits.

Additionally, Apple has pledged $848 million for solar energy projects with First Solar, Inc. Cook calls this Apple’s 'biggest, boldest, and most ambitious project ever,' demonstrating the company’s commitment to clean energy and corporate responsibility.

article_content: NEW DELHI: Australian Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles and Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with India's National Security Advisor Ajit Doval on Tuesday in New Delhi. The two sides discussed a range of issues, including global and regional developments, as well as bilateral security and defence cooperation. Discussions also covered various challenges and opportunities in maritime and space domains, which are recognized as part of the Global Commons. The leaders highlighted common values, shared heritage, and mutual respect as a strong foundation for advancing strategic interests. Both parties emphasized the importance of supporting countries in the Indo-Pacific, ASEAN, Africa, Global South, and Pacific Islands in pursuing their development priorities in a sustainable manner. They also identified specific long-term opportunities for bilateral strategic cooperation. Deputy Prime Minister Marles expressed his appreciation for the positive sentiments shared by cricketers from both countries, past and present. NSA Doval congratulated the Australian leaders on their victory in the Cricket World Cup finals and praised the tenacity, sportsmanship, and talent of Indian and Australian cricketers. Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Wong is conducting the Foreign Ministers Framework Dialogue with India's External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi. Earlier, on Monday, the India-Australia 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue took place, with EAM Jaishankar and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh meeting their Australian counterparts, Foreign Minister Penny Wong and Defence Minister Richard Marles. In her opening remarks, Wong stated that Canberra deeply values its bilateral relationship with New Delhi, emphasizing its crucial role in the region where sovereignty is respected. She noted that both countries have achieved much together and hope to do more in the future. During the meeting, Jaishankar remarked that the partnership between India and Australia has developed rapidly and carries significant implications for the region. He described the cooperation between the two countries within the Quad format as highly beneficial for both bilateral relations and the broader Indo-Pacific region.

article_content: Akwa Ibom State Governor Umo Eno has approved N450 million as the state’s counterpart funding for the Nigeria for Women Project, a World Bank-backed program designed to empower women in the region. The announcement was made during a meeting at the Government House in Uyo with a delegation from the World Bank led by Shudham Chaudhury, Nigeria's Country Director. Governor Eno assured that his administration is dedicated to partnering with development agencies, especially in agriculture and rural development, in line with the goals of his ARISE Agenda. He stated the state will work to bridge existing project gaps and seek new partnership opportunities with the World Bank to benefit Akwa Ibom’s people. World Bank Country Director Shudham Chaudhury said the Bank's visit aimed to strengthen collaboration and highlight its ongoing support for Nigeria’s development. He reaffirmed the World Bank's multi-billion dollar commitment to the country and praised the ARISE Agenda as a focused, effective initiative that could help reduce poverty in the state.

article_content: The Pentagon is closely observing a bitcoin mining operation in Cheyenne, Wyoming, situated near a Microsoft data center and the Francis E. Warren Air Force Base, known for housing intercontinental ballistic missiles. Concerns have arisen among US officials over possible connections between the mine’s ownership and China, with fears about risks to national security, as reported by The New York Times. Microsoft has raised warnings that the location might allow Chinese actors to conduct intelligence-gathering efforts targeting its data center and neighboring military facilities. The company reported its suspicions to the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States in August 2022, noting that the mine’s proximity and the presence of Chinese nationals could provide an opportunity for surveillance. Although Microsoft clarified that there is currently no definitive proof of malicious activities linked to the mine, the company underlined that the combination of significant computing power, Chinese personnel nearby, and closeness to key military installations could represent a meaningful security risk. After China’s 2021 bitcoin mining ban, several cryptocurrency operations with Chinese ties moved to countries like the US. Some are known to be linked to the Chinese government, while others are harder to trace. The Wyoming mine is associated with several firms, including Bit Origin Ltd., which was initially registered as a pork-processing company in the Cayman Islands. Li Jiaming, president of Bit Origin Ltd., emphasized their decision to open the facility in Cheyenne was due to an arrangement with the local power provider, rather than any connection to the Microsoft data center or Air Force base. He told The Times, "Without electricity, there is no business," highlighting that the necessity of reliable power was the deciding factor. US officials have also expressed apprehension about the immense power consumption of such crypto mines, warning these sites could either stress the electrical grid or be misused for cyberattacks, potentially resulting in power outages. The heightened vigilance comes amid reports of alleged Chinese malware designed to disrupt essential resources—like electricity and communications—at US military bases.

article_content: The Indian High Commission in Maldives has expressed deep sorrow after two Indian nationals died in a gas cylinder explosion on Haa Dhaal Makunudhoo island. The incident occurred near the local fish market, where both men were working for a company involved in land reclamation for the Makunudhoo Airport. Following the tragedy, the High Commission is in close contact with Maldivian authorities and the victims' families, offering support. According to local news outlet The Edition, police confirmed the men were foreign nationals employed at the site, though their identities have not been released publicly. Photos circulating on social media show part of the ceiling in a nearby building collapsed from the explosion. The Maldives National Defense Force and police have begun an investigation into the cause of the blast.

article_content: Keshav Maharaj’s determined celebrations—marked by flared nostrils, blazing eyes, and a chest-thump—have become an iconic image of South Africa’s fighting spirit at the 2023 Cricket World Cup. In their recent match in Pune, South Africa defeated New Zealand by 190 runs. Maharaj’s performance was outstanding, taking 4 wickets for 46 runs and playing a crucial role in restricting New Zealand’s chase. South Africa’s batsmen continued to dominate, scoring several centuries and amassing the most sixes by any team in a single World Cup. Marco Jansen and Gerald Coetzee also contributed key wickets, ensuring New Zealand never came close to the daunting target of 357 runs. Historically, New Zealand have been successful in World Cup chases against South Africa, and had not lost to them in a World Cup in the 21st century. However, Maharaj—who has gained respect for his composure and leadership—along with Jansen, changed the narrative with their skillful bowling. Maharaj’s calm demeanor is widely respected within the team. He raced back from a knee injury to participate in the tournament, with captain Temba Bavuma advocating strongly for his inclusion. During the match, Maharaj was introduced into the attack when Daryl Mitchell was threatening a comeback for New Zealand. Maharaj quickly dismissed Mitchell, then went on to remove Mitchell Santner, Jimmy Neesham, and Trent Boult, all with clever variations in his bowling. David Miller supported the team with excellent fielding, and South Africa’s leadership group continues to rely on Maharaj’s advice and cricketing insight. His religious background and respect for tradition—highlighted by the presence of a Lord Hanuman image on his bat—are valued by teammates. In addition to Maharaj’s exploits, Rassie van der Dussen and Quinton de Kock’s partnership in batting was notable, with van der Dussen describing de Kock as encouraging and a source of humor on the field. The crowd in Pune featured enthusiastic Proteas fans wearing historic jerseys, while many locals also cheered for Rachin Ravindra, reflecting the diverse support at the venue. Ultimately, it was Maharaj who received the loudest applause at the end, thanks to his match-winning performance.

Pune-pe jehechaitépe, Sudáfrica ojapo kuri victoria guasu, ogana 190 rupi New Zealand rehe. Maharaj ojapo kuri 4 wicket 46 run reheve, ha omba’apo guasu New Zealand rekutúva ojoko hag̃ua. Sudáfrica bateador-kuéra ohupyty heta siglo ha ojapo heta seis peteĩ World Cup-pe. Marco Jansen ha Gerald Coetzee avei omba’apo porã wicket rehe, ha ojoko New Zealand ndoikéi haguã 357 run-pe. Ymaguare, New Zealand ikatu kuri ogana Sudáfrica rehe World Cup-pe, ha ko siglo pyahu nde’íriva oguenohẽ chupe. article_content: World number one Caroline Wozniacki suffered another disappointing loss at the French Open, falling to 28th seed Daniela Hantuchova. Wozniacki, still searching for her first Grand Slam title, was defeated 6-1, 6-3 in only 73 minutes, extending her frustrating run at Roland Garros, where her best result was a quarterfinal finish in 2009. Hantuchova, from Slovakia, dominated the match, winning nine consecutive games to take the first set and build a strong lead in the second. Wozniacki broke serve to close the gap to 4-2, but Hantuchova held on, securing one of the biggest wins of her career. She will meet 2009 French Open champion Svetlana Kuznetsova, who advanced after defeating Rebecca Marino of Canada 6-0, 6-4. At the press conference, Wozniacki acknowledged Hantuchova played better and remarked, 'She knew what she wanted to do and I need to get back on the court, practice, and come back stronger. As the number one and two players, Kim and I must be doing something right.' She also reflected on learning more from losses than wins. The surprises continued as Australian 8th seed Samantha Stosur was upset by unseeded Gisela Dulko. Dulko started strong, taking the first four games, and though Stosur won the second set, her 35 unforced errors contributed to Dulko's victory. After her win, Dulko emotionally dedicated her performance to her brother’s newborn twins, Myla and Teo. Other matches saw defending champion and 5th seed Francesca Schiavone progress after her opponent Shuai Peng retired due to injury, with the score at 6-3, 1-2. Third seed Vera Zvonareva beat Austria’s Anastasia Rodionova 6-2, 6-3. Fourteenth seed Anastasia Pavlyuchenkova overcame Spain’s Nuria Llagostera Vives 3-6, 6-3, 6-3. Tenth seed Jelena Jankovic defeated American Bethanie Mattek-Sands 6-2, 6-2, while France’s Marion Bartoli, the 11th seed, battled past Germany’s Julia Goerges 3-6, 6-2, 6-4.

article_content: Julie Redfern, a 47-year-old from Padiham, Lancashire, spent seven years living with a rare medical condition that made her acutely sensitive to sounds coming from inside her own body. Diagnosed with superior canal dehiscence syndrome (SCDS), Julie could hear internal noises like her heartbeat, eye movements, and the flow of body fluids more loudly than normal due to a thinning or hole in her temporal bone that exposed her inner ear to extra vibrations. This unusual inner ear disorder, recognized officially only in 1998, causes symptoms such as vertigo, hypersensitivity to external noises, and an odd feeling that things are moving when they’re not. For Julie, ordinary activities like dining out or chatting with friends were difficult, as the sound of her own chewing or voice drowned out everything else. She had to avoid crisp foods and found even her receptionist work challenging because the vibration of the desk phone made her eye movements audible. Julie's first experience with the condition came soon after turning 40, when she realized she could hear her eyes moving while playing a video game. Initial doctors dismissed her complaints as age-related, but Julie eventually read about a similar case, which pushed her to seek a conclusive diagnosis. After consulting Dr. Gerald Brookes, a neuro-otologist, and undergoing scans at Manchester Royal Infirmary, Julie was confirmed to have SCDS. She suspects the origins of her condition might be related to a bicycle accident she had at age 24. SCDS can sometimes be congenital or result from trauma or gradual bone thinning. Julie had a complex five-hour surgery to fill the gap in her affected temporal bone, understanding that the procedure carried risks like possible hearing loss or facial changes. The surgeon, who had rarely performed the surgery because the condition is so rare, was able to relieve much of Julie’s unusual symptoms. However, she will need another operation on her other ear for a full resolution. Julie’s journey reflects the struggles faced by those with rare health conditions and the potential relief offered by advances in surgical treatment, even when a diagnosis is elusive and the disorder hard to recognize.

article_content: Archivists at the Naval History and Heritage Command (NHHC) in Washington, D.C., recently made a remarkable discovery while processing a backlog of artifacts: a wooden box containing 150 original glass plate photographs from the Spanish-American War. The plates, carefully wrapped in tissue paper with full captions and dates, were likely prepared by their creator, Douglas White—a war correspondent and photographer for the San Francisco Examiner, then owned by William Randolph Hearst. According to Lisa Crunk, head of the NHHC's photo archives branch, the box's etched cover explained that it held photographic slides of U.S. naval activities near Manila, Philippines, during the 1898 conflict. The collection included notable images such as American troops disembarking from a ship near Cavite, the burning of San Roque, and damage to Fort San Antonio Abad in Manila caused by the cruiser Olympia’s eight-inch shells. These pictures, hidden from public view for over a century, are significant because the Navy played a crucial role during the ten-week war with Spain, with decisive naval battles at Manila Bay and Santiago de Cuba. Joint Army-Navy operations in Santiago, Puerto Rico, and Manila were also key to the U.S. success. The Spanish-American War was sparked after the sinking of the Battleship Maine in Havana harbor on February 15, 1898, with the U.S. formally declaring war on April 25. Sensationalist journalism from Joseph Pulitzer and Hearst—pioneers of 'yellow journalism'—helped sway public opinion in favor of war. The war ended with the signing of the Treaty of Paris on December 10, 1898, granting Cuban independence, and ceding Puerto Rico and Guam to the U.S. The Philippines were purchased from Spain for $20 million. According to the Library of Congress, the war cost the U.S. $250 million and 3,000 lives, mostly from disease. NHHC staff discovered the box while preparing for a major update to their collection; the photographs will be digitized and made available to the public online as part of their ongoing preservation efforts. The Naval History and Heritage Command preserves, analyzes, and shares U.S. naval history through its library, archives, artifact collections, museums, and special facilities.

article_content: Nokia has introduced its new flagship smartphone, the Lumia 925, featuring a sleek aluminum design and the firm's most advanced camera to date. The phone is both lighter and thinner than prior models, with a display that remains easily readable in direct sunlight. Unveiled at a well-publicized event in London, the Lumia 925 is described by Nokia as its best device yet. The switch from plastic to a metal case sets it apart from earlier phones. Running Microsoft’s Windows Phone 8, the Lumia 925 will be offered at around 469 euros (£400) pre-tax, available as soon as next month. eMarketer projects Android to maintain its number one position in the UK’s smartphone market in 2013, with 15 million users (48.6%). Apple's iOS follows with 8.7 million users (28%). BlackBerry's share drops to 14% (4.3 million users) from 15.5% last year, while Windows Mobile is anticipated at 1.2 million users (3.8%, down from 4%). It is estimated that 30.9 million UK residents will use smartphones in 2013, representing 48.4% of the population. By 2014, smartphone ownership is expected to reach 53.4%. Jo Harlow, executive vice president of smart devices at Nokia, emphasized the company's commitment to continued innovation, citing new benefits for both existing and prospective Lumia owners. A standout feature of the Lumia 925 is its 'smart camera,' designed to take ten photos in quick succession for users to choose the best picture. This functionality will be extended to all Lumia smartphones with Windows Phone 8. Despite Nokia's claims of this being its most sophisticated device, some tech experts were less enthusiastic. Jason Jenkins, CNET UK's editor, commented that the launch didn't deliver as much innovation as anticipated given the intense promotion. Jenkins added that the phone may appeal to users looking for something simpler than many Android devices, or preferring a larger screen than what iPhones offer. However, he does not expect the Lumia 925 to greatly disrupt Apple’s or Samsung’s strong positions in the market.

article_content: OpenTable has published its 2023 list of America’s Top 100 Restaurants, recognizing the country’s favorite dining destinations based on real diner experiences instead of just industry critics. With input from over 12 million reviews and reservation patterns, this year’s list features restaurants from 64 cities, expanding significantly compared to last year’s 47 cities. The curated list includes acclaimed Michelin-starred spots such as Jeune et Jolie, neighborhood highlights like Bad Roman in Manhattan, and many lesser-known eateries. There’s also an increase in solo dining, and more restaurants are offering cuisines like West African, Lebanese, and other international flavors. OpenTable CEO Debby Soo noted that the diversity of the list spans everything from local gems to culinary hotspots, including Mediterranean, French, and Japanese cuisine. Importantly, every restaurant on this ranking accepts digital reservations through OpenTable, making it easy for diners to secure a table. Notable spots, like Mariposa Latin Grill in Sedona, Arizona, are featured, alongside restaurants across Alaska, Arizona, California, Connecticut, D.C., and additional locations, offering something for diners nationwide.

article_content: On January 14, 2014, billionaire Ty Warner, creator of Beanie Babies, was sentenced to two years' probation for hiding at least $25 million from U.S. tax authorities. Instead of prison, the judge cited Warner's significant charitable contributions as a reason for leniency. Warner, 69, appeared in Chicago federal court, apologized for his actions, and expressed 'shame and embarrassment.' He pleaded guilty to one count of tax evasion, after hiding his income through Swiss bank accounts for over a decade. Federal prosecutors, including Michelle Petersen, asked U.S. District Judge Charles Kocoras to sentence Warner to at least a year in prison. They pointed out that another businessman, Peter Troost, received a year in prison for hiding a smaller amount, $3 million. Judge Kocoras, however, emphasized Warner's philanthropic work, stating that 'society will be better served by allowing him to continue his good works.' He also mentioned Warner's hardships growing up and noted that Warner had paid a significant personal price through public humiliation. Warner's company, TY Inc., generated hundreds of millions of dollars from Beanie Babies in the 1990s and Forbes listed his net worth at $2.6 billion. He maintained secret offshore accounts since 1996 and reportedly took steps to hide this from authorities. The judge specifically referenced Warner's donations, including paying a woman's $20,000 medical bill and contributing $20 million to charity from proceeds of a Princess Diana commemorative toy. As part of his sentence, Warner must complete 500 hours of community service at Chicago high schools. Warner also agreed to pay $27 million in back taxes and interest, as well as a civil penalty over $53 million. U.S. attorney Zachary Fardon said the penalties, community service, and public humiliation sent the message that tax evasion does not pay. At the hearing's end, Judge Kocoras formally advised Warner of his right to appeal, joking that he could try for a 'better deal' if he wished.

Oguahẽ rangue cárcel-pe, juez ohechauka Warner rembiapo porãitasã ha upévare ome’ẽ hese mbovymi peneha. Fiscal-kuéra, Michelle Petersen reheve, ojerure U.S. District Judge Charles Kocoras-pe ome’ẽ hag̃ua Warner-pe año jepe cárcel-pe. Ohechauka avei ótro empresario, Peter Troost, ohupyty hague año cárcel-pe oñemomba’eguasu’ỹva $3 millón rehe. Juez Kocoras, upeichavérõ, oñe’ẽ Warner rembiapo porã rehe, he’i sociedad-pe oikota porãve ha’e ohasáramo, ikatu haguã osegi hembiapo porã. Ohechauka avei Warner rekotevẽ ohupyty haguãmboyve mba'e vai, ha onhechauka ohasa hague ñemotĩ eta hendaitépe. Warner empresa TY Inc. oguereko heta viru Beanie Babies rehe 1990-pe, ha Forbes he’i ijareha $2.6 mil millón. Ha’e oguereko cuenta viru okyje, 1996 guive, ha omokañy mba’e renda autoridád-gui. Juez ohechauka Warner remime’ẽ rehe, ome’ẽ hague $20.000 peteĩ kuñáme ho’a vai médiko rehe, ha avei $20 millón charity-pe, Princess Diana rembiporã juguete rupive. Sentencia-pe Warner oikotevẽ ojapo 500 aravo servicio comunitario Chicago mbo’ehao guasúpe. Warner avei oheja oñeme’ẽ $27 millón viru ha intereses, avei civil penalty ikatuha $53 millón rupi. Fiscal guasu Zachary Fardon he’i ko’ã pena, servicio comunitario ha ñemotĩ ohechauka tax evasion ndaikatúi opaga. Juicio paha aja, juez Kocoras omombe’u Warner-pe orekohague derecho apela hag̃ua, ha oñembohory he’ívo ‘ikatuha ojuhu trato iporãvéva’ corte de apelación-pe.

article_content: The Nigerian Thoracic Society (NTS) and respiratory experts have called on all levels of government to demonstrate strong political commitment in tackling the causes of soot pollution in Nigeria, especially in Rivers State, where residents are experiencing significant health impacts. In interviews with PUNCH Healthwise, experts explained that soot seriously harms respiratory health. They urged the government to address the main sources of soot in the region, mainly the operations of illegal oil refineries. According to the NTS, soot is a black, carbon-rich substance produced by incomplete combustion of fuels such as coal, wood, and oil. The fine particles adhere to surfaces, cause blackening, and can trigger lung diseases and respiratory infections. Professor Udegbunam Ele, NTS President and consultant pulmonologist at Nnamdi Azikiwe University Teaching Hospital, described the soot issue in the Niger Delta as a major public health crisis. He emphasized that governments must develop the political resolve to address it, beginning by eliminating the sources. Ele said that illegal oil refineries are the predominant cause of soot in the region. While former Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike tried to control the situation, Ele believes strong, ongoing government intervention is still necessary. Dr. Obiona Adeyemi, consultant pulmonologist at Osun State University Teaching Hospital and NTS Secretary General, agreed and highlighted the need for government determination to solve the soot crisis. He urged the new government to continue efforts to protect residents from daily exposure to soot-related illnesses. Dr. Adeyemi stressed the need for job creation among youths to discourage participation in illegal refining, explaining that poverty and unemployment drive many into such activities. He acknowledged that while some may still engage in illegal activities, providing employment would greatly reduce the number involved in illegal refining. Many people only participate in such practices due to lack of better options. Both Ele and Adeyemi pointed out that soot particles are harmful to lung health, increase the risk of cancers and infections, and when airborne, reduce visibility and contribute to road accidents, posing broader public safety risks. The NTS recommends halting all gas flaring in Port Harcourt and elsewhere, and urges government agencies to find and shut down all illegal refineries. They further suggest reducing traffic congestion, promoting cleaner cooking fuels, and boosting youth employment to address poverty and reduce illegal refining. Experts stress that a comprehensive approach, political will, and stakeholder cooperation are essential to protect public health and the environment in affected areas.

PUNCH Healthwise-pe oñe’ẽvo, umi especialista he’i so’o vaieterei pulmon rehe. Ojerure gobierno-pe ojapo hag̃ua tembiapo ojejuhuha peichagua so’o, chie rupi illegal refinería rehe. NTS he’i, so’o hína peteĩ mba’e hũ, carbón rehegua osẽva mba’e'apo’a'ỹ, tata, yvyrá ha petroleo rehe. Umi michĩ'i ojehupytýva ojupe ha ojehechaukáva hũ, oporombyahýi pulmóna ha ombohasy peny. Profesor Udegbunam Ele, NTS motenondeha ha especialista pulmon rehegua Nnamdi Azikiwe University Teaching Hospital, he’i Niger Delta-pe so’o ha’eha peteĩ apañuãi guasu tenguáva. Ohechauka gobierno tekotevẽha política añetete oñepyrũ hag̃ua motivos so’o rehe. Ele he’i illegal refinería ha'eha moõgui osẽve hína so’o. Dr. Obiona Adeyemi, especialista pulmon ha NTS Secretario General Osun State University Teaching Hospital-pe, oñe'ẽ avei ohechauka gapeha gobierno ha'eha pe oñorairõva ojoko hag̃ua so’o rehegua, ojerure gobierno pyahu oñepyrũ hag̃ua tembiapo ohechauka haipyahu rejupíva tapicha rehe. Dr. Adeyemi avei oñe’ẽ mba’érepa tekojoja mitãrusúpe g̃uarã iporã ojoko hag̃ua illegal refinación, ohechauka ndaha’eiha enterovape ojapoháicha umi mba’e, péro ñeme’ẽ tembiapo omoĩ guasu opa problemápe. Ele ha Adeyemi he’i avei so’o oikóva pulmon rehegua hína vaieterei, ombopy’a tarova cáncer rehe ha aire-pe, omboguejy mba’erecha ha ombosyry tape rehe, omoĩ tapicha apurosópe. NTS omba’apo oñembojúvo oje’e ojoko gas flaring Port Harcourt-pe ha ambue hendápe paíspe, avei ojerure gobierno rembiapo ojuhu hag̃ua ha omboty ilegal refinery. Umi especialista he’i tekotevẽha tembiaporã ko’ãva, política añetete ha oñondive tembiapo oipytyvõ hag̃ua tapicha rehe ha oiko porãve hag̃ua ko yvoty.

article_content: Former England midfielder Gareth Barry has publicly defended Wayne Rooney against criticism following England's World Cup opener. Barry, who played with Rooney during the 2010 World Cup in South Africa, insisted that every England player wants manager Roy Hodgson to start Rooney against Uruguay. Barry highlighted Rooney's importance, stating that England needs the 28-year-old if they are to make an impact in the tournament. Despite assisting Daniel Sturridge's goal in the match against Italy, Rooney faced scrutiny for a performance many considered below his usual standard, particularly as he played out of his favored position. "How many forwards playing on the left wing could deliver that kind of cross with their weaker foot?" Barry commented on the social media app Fanzai, referencing Rooney's assist. "There's no debate—Wayne Rooney should be one of the first names in the starting lineup. Every player in that dressing room would want him on the team. If England are to achieve anything at this World Cup, Rooney is essential." Although Rooney has not scored in nine World Cup appearances, Barry noted that being played out of position limited the striker's impact. Meanwhile, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain returned to training after a knee injury and is being considered as a possible alternative to Rooney. Barry, who was part of Fabio Capello's 2010 World Cup squad, emphasized Rooney's popularity and leadership within the team. Rooney himself acknowledged that his place is not guaranteed, telling the media, "I work hard to get into the team and never take my place for granted. We have a lot of good, young players, and whoever the manager chooses, we will all respect that." Rooney is still aiming to score his first World Cup goal to silence his critics.

article_content: An American healthcare worker with high-risk exposure to the Ebola virus in Sierra Leone arrived at Nebraska Medicine on Sunday for observation and possible treatment, according to the center. Dr. Phil Smith, medical director of the biocontainment unit at Omaha's Nebraska Medical Center, stated, 'This patient has been exposed to the virus but is not ill and is not contagious. However, we will be taking all appropriate precautions.' Nebraska Medical Center is one of only four hospitals in the United States with biocontainment units and has extensive experience treating highly infectious diseases like Ebola. The other three hospitals are Emory University Hospital in Atlanta, Rocky Mountain Laboratories in Montana, and the National Institutes of Health in Maryland. Previously, Nebraska Medical Center treated three patients with Ebola. Dr. Rick Sacra, infected in Liberia, was treated and released in September. NBC freelance cameraman Ashoka Mukpo, also infected in Liberia, was treated and released in October. Dr. Martin Salia, who was gravely ill when he arrived from Sierra Leone, died after less than two days of treatment in November. The patient who arrived Sunday was transported by private air ambulance and will be observed in the same specially equipped room used to treat the previous three patients. Medical staff will closely monitor the patient to see if Ebola disease develops. While the United States reported 10 Ebola patients last year, the situation in West Africa was much more severe. According to the World Health Organization, over 7,500 people died from Ebola in 2014, with most deaths occurring in Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Guinea.

Dr. Phil Smith, Omaha-peguá Nebraska Medical Center biocontainment unidad rehegua director médico, heʼi: 'Ko paciente oĩ vaʼekue kontaktorã virús rehe, ha katu ndaikatúi ojeʼe hasýpa térã ojeporukuaa mbaʼeve. Ambue mbohapy hospital haꞌe Emory University Hospital (Atlanta), Rocky Mountain Laboratories (Montana), ha National Institutes of Health (Maryland). Nebraska Medical Center orembohasa kuri mbohapy paciente Ebolá rehegua. Dr. Rick Sacra, ohasavaʼekue Liberiape, oñetrapa ha osẽ septiembre-pe. NBC rembiapokue-cameraman Ashoka Mukpo, avei oiméva Liberiape, oñetrapa ha osẽ octubre-pe. Upe paciente og̃uahẽva arapokõime ojegueru avión privado rupive ha ojepytaso upe koty especialitépe ojeipuruva’ekue umi mbohapy paciente rehe. Oñemaña mbarete hese ikatu’ỹre ojavy, ikatu hag̃uáicha ojekuaa oje’e’ỹre Ebolá rehe ikatu haguã oñembyai. Estados Unidos-pe oĩkuri 10 paciente Ebola rehe 2014-pe, ha katu West Africa-pe pe situasión ivaive. Organización Mundial de la Salud heʼi, hetave 7.500 tapicha omano Ebola rehe 2014-pe, ha mayoría omano Liberia, Sierra Leone ha Guinea-pe.

article_content: Stuart Kerner, vice principal and religious studies teacher at Bexleyheath Academy in south-east London, is on trial accused of having a sexual relationship with a 15-year-old pupil. Friends of the student said they warned police about the alleged affair, but officers told them they could not act unless the student herself made a complaint. Kerner, 44 and married, is alleged to have had a secret relationship with the girl at school, engaging in sexual activity in broom cupboards, locked offices, and at his home. The pupil, whose identity is protected by law, told friends about the relationship. Concerned for her safety and worried Kerner might pose a risk to others, her friends reported the situation to police. However, they said police were unable to intervene without a direct complaint from the pupil. Vanessa Morrison, Kerner’s personal assistant at the school, testified that the student seemed obsessed with Kerner. She said the pupil frequently sought out Kerner and spent time in his office under various pretenses. Jurors heard that the alleged relationship was uncovered after the girl’s mother found sexual content on her phone and confronted her, leading to a disclosure about the teacher. Kerner, who is from Aylesford, Kent, denies all charges, including sexual activity with a child and abusing his position of trust.

article_content: Gerrard Scanlon, a 53-year-old delivery driver from Enfield, North London, has been charged with a racially aggravated public order offense. He is alleged to have directed racist language at Leeds United striker El-Hadji Diouf during a Millwall match, as captured in a Sky Sports News broadcast. The incident took place at The Den in November. Scanlon has been released on bail and will appear at Bromley Magistrates' Court on February 27. In response, Millwall Football Club expressed deep concern and said it would reopen its investigation into the allegations. According to Chief Executive Andy Ambler, an earlier probe was concluded when Diouf reported no racist abuse, but newly released footage led to renewed action. Ambler stressed the club's commitment to combating racism in football. Club captain Danny Shittu issued a statement expressing disappointment and asserting that racism is unacceptable. He said he is working with the club to implement further measures against discriminatory behavior at games, emphasizing that all players deserve respect and protection from abuse. Millwall has committed to lifetime bans for those found guilty. There have been previous similar accusations, notably from Bolton's Marvin Sordell, after which a 13-year-old fan was banned following a related incident involving a derogatory banner.

Millwall ome’ẽ promesa omotĩtaha tapicha ojehechauka hembiapo vai rehe. The worldwide trade in counterfeit goods is estimated at $1.7 trillion to $4.5 trillion annually. The secondary market for fashion and accessories is also sizable, valued at about $120 billion. This underscores the critical importance of authentication to protect both brands and consumers.

Earlier this month, Entrupy, an artificial intelligence-powered authentication provider, announced it will authenticate pre-owned luxury handbags for TikTok Shop in the United States. Entrupy’s system uses AI and microscopy to verify item authenticity. When an item is scanned using Entrupy’s proprietary device and app, detailed microscopic images are collected. Machine learning algorithms then compare these images to a database containing millions of examples of both authentic and counterfeit products. Based on this analysis, the AI determines whether an item is verified as authentic or returns an “unverified” result. Each scan also helps expand and refine Entrupy’s database, improving the system’s accuracy over time.

Most items take three to five minutes to scan and authenticate through the Entrupy app. Some cases may require up to an hour, and verifying Hermès Premium items can take up to 24 hours. Since AI algorithms are only as reliable as their data, Entrupy’s team of data scientists and engineers continuously update the system in real-time. Since launching in 2012, the company has been building and improving its data resources. Entrupy states that its authentication achieves a 99.1% accuracy rate.

TikTok Shop seller Kimmiebbags welcomed Entrupy’s integration, saying, “Now anyone shopping through my page will trust that their purchases are authentic.” Entrupy’s founder and CEO, Vidyuth Srinivasan, added, “We want to make sure that when buying luxury items, it is a smooth experience. This integration allows us to continue our mission of protecting both businesses and consumers from purchasing counterfeit items.”

In the realm of luxury watches, Swiss foundation Origyn was among the first to authenticate items using technology. Last year, Origyn partnered with WatchBox, a leader in certified pre-owned luxury timepieces. Origyn combines human experts with a proprietary device that incorporates AI and ultra-high-resolution cameras to capture 360-degree images of each watch. Each watch also receives a digital certificate, which includes a unique biometric fingerprint stored securely on the blockchain.

While applying authentication technology to the secondary market offers immediate benefits, luxury brands are also focusing on long-term anti-counterfeiting measures by integrating authentication at the point of production. The Aura Consortium—which counts LVMH, Prada Group, OTB, Mercedes-Benz, and Richemont’s Cartier as founding members—pre-verifies items and issues unique digital IDs for garments, accessories, and jewelry. These digital IDs provide proof of authenticity and offer information about the item’s origins and manufacturing, enhancing transparency and traceability. The digital IDs are immutably encoded on the blockchain and are physically linked to each item via near field communication (NFC) chips or quick response (QR) codes, such as those used by brands like Margiela and Loro Piana. These digital certificates can transfer ownership when items are resold, offering further reassurance in the secondary market.

article_content: Political tensions over a possible change in leadership are high in Canberra, leading to confusion within the Liberal party. At a press event in Melbourne, Defence Minister Kevin Andrews voiced his support for Prime Minister Tony Abbott. Unexpectedly, Andrews mistakenly claimed he backed a leadership team of Abbott and former Labor Prime Minister Julia Gillard, rather than deputy Liberal leader Julie Bishop. The error quickly became a topic of humor and discussion on social media. Without acknowledging the error, Andrews continued with his statement, insisting that 'the team of Tony Abbott and Julia Gillard is the best leadership team for the Liberal party and for Australia as a whole.' The slip occurred while the nation was recalling Gillard's own experiences with party leadership challenges: she replaced Kevin Rudd in 2010, defended her position in 2012, and lost it to Rudd in 2013. Abbott's leadership has come under scrutiny before, with Education Minister Christopher Pyne saying recently on the Today Show that he 'hoped' Abbott had enough internal support. Pyne later described his remark as a result of tiredness. Labor's Anthony Albanese commented that when top leaders hesitate to affirm the prime minister's position, it's a sign of deeper trouble.

Melbourne-pe peteî maranduha guasu, Tetã Rekosãha Motenondehára Kevin Andrews he’i oguerekoha imba’eporiahuverekoha Ruvicha Tony Abbott rehe. Ha katu, Andrews ojavy ha he’i oikeha Tony Abbott ha Julia Gillard aty rehe, oîva’ekue Labor aty Motenondehára ramo, Julie Bishop rangue (oîva Deputy Liberal Leader ha Chanciller ramo). article_content: West Ham United have come under fire from their supporters for releasing mugs and t-shirts commemorating their three victories over rivals Tottenham Hotspur during the 2013-14 season. The club's official store is selling merchandise emblazoned with the slogan, 'The Treble: It's Happened Again.' The three wins include a 3-0 Premier League victory at White Hart Lane in October, a Capital One Cup triumph at the same ground in December, and a 2-0 league win at Upton Park in May. Despite these successes over Spurs, West Ham endured a lackluster season overall, finishing 13th with 40 points—six places and 29 points behind Tottenham's sixth-place finish with 69 points. Some fans expressed embarrassment over the merchandise, suggesting it makes the club appear small. One supporters’ Twitter account, @whustuff, shared a photo of the shirt, calling it 'embarrassing.' Another fan, Mick Lewsey, commented that producing these products for beating another Premier League team was not a good look for the club. Notable moments from the season include Ravel Morrison’s goal against Hugo Lloris in the 3-0 win, Modibo Maiga’s decisive performance in the Capital One Cup, and Younes Kaboul’s sending off as West Ham completed their hat-trick of wins in May. The club has made the merchandise available for purchase, with t-shirts priced at £20 and mugs at £7.99. Last month, West Ham announced that manager Sam Allardyce would remain in charge despite ongoing criticism from some supporters. The former Bolton manager has been tasked with introducing a more attractive style of play, with ex-England and Hammers forward Teddy Sheringham brought in as an attacking coach to help achieve this.

Umi mbohapy victoria: 3-0 Premier League pe White Hart Lane ári octubre-pe, Capital One Cup ári upeha’e avei diciembre-pe ha 2-0 liga-pe Upton Park-pe mayo-pe. Oĩ heta seguidor oñembyasy ha omoirûhague he’ise ndaha’eveichaiha club tuicháva. Peteî Twitter cuenta, @whustuff, omyasãi peteĩ camiseta ra’anga ha he’i: 'Cheveréma gua’u, péro ko’ãga chembyasy.’ Ambue fan, Mick Lewsey, he’i ojapo haguére ko’ã mba’e ndoikóiha porã club-pe otropa equipo rehe vitóriare. article_content: Ed Miliband, leader of Labour, has strongly criticized Prime Minister David Cameron over his stance on the UK's membership in the European Union, warning that Cameron's hints about leaving the EU could jeopardize the nation's economic prospects. Miliband contends that even considering an exit sends the wrong message to investors and endangers UK jobs. While the Conservative Party, led by Cameron, has committed to holding a referendum on EU membership after attempting renegotiation, Labour has declined to make such a promise. Addressing business leaders, Miliband is set to argue that risking Britain's stability for political purposes is irresponsible, and that the UK should work towards reform from within the EU alongside its European partners. Miliband has expressed that both advocating for immediate departure from the EU and suggesting it as an option are equally harmful. He believes this uncertainty discourages investment and weakens the UK's influence within Europe. The EU recently issued Britain a demand for £1.7 billion, later reduced to £850 million by Chancellor George Osborne—a cut that critics say was achieved by shifting forward a rebate payment, not through genuine negotiation. Home Secretary Theresa May has added that staying in the EU should depend on achieving major reforms. She writes that while access to the single market benefits the UK, some EU regulations hold back all member economies. May calls for a more adaptable EU that enables cooperation and safeguards national sovereignty. Miliband has pledged that under Labour, no further powers will be transferred to the EU without first seeking the explicit approval of British voters in a referendum. He maintains that the UK's future lies in forming effective alliances and pushing for constructive reform in the EU, rather than making threats or choosing isolation. He emphasizes that as Prime Minister he would prioritize genuine reforms and resist using EU membership as a tool for political gain, aiming to protect British jobs and prosperity through a responsible approach to the EU.

Al Jazeera has obtained exclusive access to Khankendi, the largest city in the Nagorno-Karabakh region, which now stands almost deserted after tens of thousands of residents fled. The city’s central square is eerily silent, scattered with abandoned items like baby strollers, chairs, and empty boxes—reminders of over 100,000 ethnic Armenians who left Khankendi in haste. Their departure follows last month's military defeat of separatist forces in the region by Azerbaijan, leading to an agreement that the self-proclaimed Republic of Artsakh would dissolve.

Ethnic Armenians, fearing persecution, fled to neighboring Armenia, leaving behind their homes and businesses, despite Azerbaijan's assurances of safety and equal treatment. The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is offering aid and evacuating those still stranded in Khankendi, which is also known as Stepanakert to Armenians. With the city’s morgue staff gone, even the deceased are being repatriated to Armenia by the Red Cross.

Marco Succi of the ICRC told Al Jazeera that urgent needs in the city include electricity, water, and gas as winter approaches. The ICRC is coordinating with Azerbaijani authorities to address these needs. Meanwhile, stray puppies and horses roam aimlessly through the empty streets, and ambulances continue to search for those in need of medical help. Some Russian peacekeeping checkpoints have also been abandoned since the conflict.

For many Armenians, leaving isn’t an easy choice—the city has been their home for generations. At evacuation points, some bid farewell to loved ones while a handful choose to remain, hoping to coexist with Azerbaijani friends. One resident told Al Jazeera he would stay because of his Azerbaijani friendships. The new Azerbaijani administration has set up a registration center, improved mobile networks, connected the city to the national electric grid, and provided ambulances, expressing hope that displaced Armenians will return and the city will be rebuilt after three decades of conflict.

Aykhan Hajizada, spokesperson for Azerbaijan’s foreign ministry, said around one million Azerbaijanis were displaced by the region’s previous occupation. Hajizada called for the Armenian population to return, stating Azerbaijan is ready to welcome them. However, trust is still lacking among those who have remained—the reality on the ground shows that rebuilding will require more than official assurances.

Pe plaza principal opyta hendy’ỹ ha ipyryrýi, oîhápe mitãngyra renda, guapyha ha kaja nandi—natekotevêvéima umi Armenia-gua hetave 100,000 osê rire pya’evy. Armenia-gua, oñemondýi haguére, osê hikuái oheja iñemurahéi ha tembiapo, ojejapómavaichnte Azerbaiján ome’ẽ seguridad ha jekupyty he’íva rehe. Pe Comité Internacional de la Cruz Roja (ICRC) pytyvõ oipytyvõ umi oîva gueteri táva-pe, ha avei omondo umi omanóva Armenia-pe. Upe aja, jagua michînguéra ha kavaju kuéra oiko oiko tapére, ha ambulancia oikóvo oheka tapicha oikotevêva pytyvõ pohãnohára rehe. Oî avei umi soldado Rusia-gua, ohejáma jepe hetaiterei tenda.

Hetaiterei Armenia-gua ohechakuaa hasyha oheja iñemoñare róga, oguata jeyvo ára pyahu rehe. Umi tapicha oîva upépe ohechauka huguaitépe oheja hikuái iñangirũ ha familia, ha oî avei mbovymi oipotáva opisopa oñondivehápe Azerbaiján-gua reheve. Peteî tapicha he’i Al Jazeera-pe opytataha upépe orekógui angirũ Azerbaiján-gua. Umi autoridad pyahu Azerbaiján-gua omopu’ã peteî centro de registro, omyatyrõ red de teléfono, omoî corriente eléctrica nacional táva-pe ha ome’ẽ ambulancia, oipota umi Armenia-gua ou jey ha ojehecha peteĩ táva pyahu rire 30 ary jepoko ha ñorairõ rire.

Aykhan Hajizada, portavoz de la cancillería Azerbaiján-gua, omombe’u hetave millón Azerbaiján-gua oñemosẽhague ndaitépe jey jave hikuái. Hajizada oinvita Armenia-gua ou jey, he’ívo país ipreparado ohupytyjey hag̃ua chupekuéra. Jepe upéicha, je confianza ndoîi gueteri umi opytáva apytépe—ñañe’ẽhápe jeikopyre, oñeikotevêve ijatyha iñemoañete hag̃ua.

article_content: Virat Kohli of India was congratulated by New Zealand’s captain, Kane Williamson, for reaching a record-breaking 50th century. New Zealand batsman Daryl Mitchell has addressed criticism faced by the Black Caps for assisting Kohli during Wednesday’s World Cup semi-final defeat, emphasizing that the team takes great pride in how they conduct themselves on the field. During the match at Wankhede Stadium, where India secured a 70-run win to reach Sunday’s final, several New Zealand players checked on Kohli and helped him stretch his hamstrings as he suffered from cramps while scoring his century. Former Australia all-rounder Simon O'Donnell criticized New Zealand for what he saw as a lack of competitive instinct, but Mitchell—who scored a 134 off 119 balls in New Zealand’s reply—insisted that their approach wouldn’t change. “That’s something we really pride ourselves on as Black Caps and as New Zealanders. We aim to play cricket in a way that reflects our country and how we want to be role models for kids,” Mitchell said to reporters before departing Mumbai on Thursday. “We’ll continue to play the way we do as Kiwis, and we hope others respect the way we go about things both on and off the field. It’s something we’re very proud of, so we’ll keep representing the Black Caps in our way.” New Zealand’s next assignment is a two-test series in Bangladesh starting November 28. Mitchell said disappointment from the semi-final wouldn’t affect their preparation. “That’s just part of international sport nowadays,” Mitchell said. “After the T20 World Cup final a couple of years ago, we played another T20 in India just 48 hours later, so we’re used to quick turnarounds. “We’ll be ready for the first test, and wearing the black cap always means a lot to this group.” Meanwhile, hotel tariffs and airfares in Ahmedabad have risen sharply ahead of Sunday’s World Cup final between India and Australia, causing some fans to reconsider their travel plans. In tech news, OpenAI has dismissed its cofounder and CEO Sam Altman, along with another senior leader, following internal disagreements over balancing AI safety and profitability. Additionally, the Indian government has approved IT hardware manufacturing proposals from 27 companies, both international and domestic, which are expected to generate ₹3,000 crore in investments over the next six years.

article_content: A night-time Superloop bus service should be launched to better connect London’s suburbs, according to a City Hall politician. Currently, six new routes are being created and four more are being incorporated into the express network, which was announced in March. Caroline Pidgeon, a Liberal Democrat assembly member, stated that operating the Superloop network at night would support the capital’s nightlife and assist shift workers. The office of Mayor Sadiq Khan has confirmed that there are currently no plans to introduce a night Superloop service. In response, the mayor’s office explained that the benefits are not obvious compared to the existing night bus routes. The Superloop service will consist of routes forming a large ring through outer London, with the main part of the network expected to be completed by spring. In a written question to the mayor, Ms Pidgeon recommended that the Superloop buses run at night. She explained to the Local Democracy Reporting Service that good late-night transport is essential for supporting nightlife, the night-time economy, shift workers, and women’s safety. Ms Pidgeon added that it is challenging to persuade shift workers to use public transport instead of cars when nighttime options are limited in their areas. The mayor’s office responded that about 73% of Superloop stops are already served by night bus services, and 95% are within 800 meters of a night bus stop. Additionally, 24 night bus routes, used by five million people annually, run parallel to Superloop routes for portions of their journey. The mayor's office stated that Transport for London will monitor the new network to fully understand how passengers are using it. Ms Pidgeon said she would continue to press the mayor to improve night-time public transport options. article_content: Banana Xanthomonas Wilt (BXW), a bacterial disease, is threatening banana crops in eastern and central Africa. Recent modeling by researchers at the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT indicates that, without intervention, BXW could reduce banana production by 55% in newly affected regions within ten years. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) reports that Sub-Saharan Africa produces around 50 million tons of bananas annually—about a third of global output, spanning over seven million hectares (60% of the world’s banana-growing area). BXW, caused by Xanthomonas vasicola pv. musacearum, is Africa’s most widespread banana bacterial disease and ranks among the top four emerging crop diseases in developing countries. A recent paper in Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems modeled three possible scenarios for BXW spread, based on the level of government and farmer response: two with partial or slow intervention, and one with no intervention. The results show that if unchecked, BXW could result in $25 billion in economic losses within a decade, with nearly 40% of these losses affecting consumers. Athanasios Petsakos, agricultural economist and lead author, emphasized that even limited policy action can help control infections and mitigate related production, financial, and food security problems. He warned that an uncontrolled outbreak could be catastrophic for farmers. The research also modeled the broader impact if BXW were to spread to every country in Sub-Saharan Africa—not just current affected areas. Petsakos notes that rapid and effective government and farmer responses could almost eliminate damage, but such swift action is not always realistic. The study underscores that integrated economic and disease models offer more accurate pictures of impacts, affecting producers via yield losses and consumers through price increases. Petsakos stressed that considering all these elements, including food security, is crucial for policymakers to avoid underestimating BXW’s impact. Co-authors Guy Blomme and Walter Ocimati contributed expertise on BXW control strategies and disease distribution. They highlight that BXW can be managed with strict application of proven interventions—such as sterilizing garden tools, removing male buds early, and uprooting diseased plants. The Single Diseased Stem Removal (SDSR) technique, developed specifically for BXW, is both effective and low-cost. The researchers conclude that their modeling provides essential information for decision-makers to guide effective containment. Uganda and Rwanda serve as examples of proactive and successful management strategies.

Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) he’i África Sub-Sahariana omoheñói 50 millón toneladas banana arýpe—ha’éva peteî vore peteĩha producción mundial rehe, ojapyhy hetave siete millón hectárea rehe (60% producción mundial rehegua). BXW, Xanthomonas vasicola pv. musacearum rehegua, ha’e hína mba’asy bakteria ojeporavovéva Africape banana rehe, ha peteîva irundy mba’asy pyahuitéva yvyramáta rehegua tetã mboriahueta rupi. Osẽháicha, ndaha’éiramo ojeguerekóva control rehe, BXW ikatu oporojavy 25 mil millón dólar rehe 10 arýpe, ha hi’ári 40% peve umi consumidor kuéra ombohasa. Athanasios Petsakos, economista agrícola ha kuatiañe’ẽ hlavautora, he’i jepe política ombokatupyrýramo mba’asy rehe control, ikatu oguenohẽ mba’asy ha oipe’apa heta problema oñehúva producción, economía ha seguridad alimentaria rehe. Osê mbaretépe he’i, mba’asy noñemombaretéiramo ikatu ombyaipaite hembiapópe avakuéra. Investigación avei ohechauka mba’éichapa ikatu ojavyvéta BXW oñemyasãi jave entero país Sub-Sahariana Africape, ndoikuaáiva hague gueteri. Petsakos ohechauka, gobierno ha chacarerokuéra okaru porã ha oikóramo rápido, ndojehúi mba’eve, pero peichaite peve rápidas reacción ndaha’éi normálmente. Estudio pyahu omombarete mba’e iporãitéva modelo económico ha mba’asy rehegua ombojoaju hag̃ua efectokuéra oguerekóva productor rehe (perdida producción), ha consumidor rehe (hepyve comida). Petsakos omombe’u jejuvéta mba’e iporãha umi elemento, seguridad alimentaria rehegua avei, ojehechaporã hag̃ua mba’éichapa BXW ipeligroso. Co-autores Guy Blomme ha Walter Ocimati oipytyvõ conocimiento rehe BXW control rehe, mba’asy ñemyasãi rehe ha mba’eichaitépa ojehecharamo. Ha’ekuéra ohechauka BXW ikatu ojehecha porã control rígido reheve: hetarecháva sterilización herramientas agrícolas, avei ojepe’a okára mba’e maleva ha oñemu plante iñembyaiha rehe. Ojedesarrolla avei Single Diseased Stem Removal (SDSR) BXW rehegua, tecnología barata ha ojeaplikáva porã. Investigadores ohechauka modelo kuéra ome’ẽha información iñimportantetereíva decidor reheguakuéra oipytyvõ hag̃ua control rehe. Uganda ha Rwanda momarandu ohechauka política control rehegua eficiente ha exitoso.
