article_content: R Raj Rao, acclaimed poet, novelist, and former head of the English department at Savitribai Phule Pune University, has long employed drama as a means to shed light on the challenges and hostility faced by the LGBTQIA community, both from society and their own families. Awaiting the release of his latest book, Rao emphasizes that 'a lot more needs to be done.' Rao notes that, despite the Supreme Court's decriminalization of Section 377 in 2018, genuine change has been limited for LGBTQIA individuals. 'Much more work remains for writers, academics, activists, lawyers, and others,' he says. 'My more than 20 books are just a small step in this direction.' His new book, 'The Wisest Fool on Earth: Ten Street Plays and Three Monologues,' will be launched on December 3. At the event, Shyam Konnur—Managing Director of Mist LGBTQ Foundation and Maharashtra state coordinator for the All India Professionals’ Congress for Diversity and Inclusion—will join Rao for a discussion and public reading from the book. Both are prominent members of the LGBTQIA+ community. Konnur, who has read Rao’s works since his early days coming out, shares that the book resonates with experiences of struggle shared by LGBTQIA individuals. The 135-page collection features street plays and monologues covering over thirty years of Rao’s writing. Rao explains, 'I wrote these plays because being gay makes us natural dissenters; one monologue even connects gay dissent to other political dissent. I've used novels and other forms to create similar awareness.' He adds that he wrote the title play, 'The Wisest Fool on Earth,' in the UK in 1990, while the street plays and the third monologue, 'Stand Up and Be Counted,' are more recent works. The monologues follow Jay, an educated yet unemployed man in his thirties who turns to male prostitution and speaks from a locked high-rise apartment. In the second monologue, 'Vanaprastha Ashram,' Jay appears twenty years later on a rooftop. In 'Stand Up and Be Counted,' Jay, now in his sixties, is imprisoned for attending the Koregaon-Bhima rally in 2018, speaking from his cell. 'The Wisest Fool on Earth' has been performed in English in Mumbai and Pune and in Hindi in Hyderabad. The street plays take place in varied locations—a courtroom, railway station, middle-class home, Mumbai street, marriage bureau, gay bar, hospital ward, sexologist’s clinic, and Irani restaurant—illustrating India's diversity. Published by QueerInk (India and Australia), the book will be launched at Pagdandi Bookstore in Baner on December 3. Rao is also preparing to release his fifth novel, 'Mahmud and Ayaz,' which uses the legendary relationship of Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni and his Turkish slave Ayaz as a lens to explore a modern gay love story set in Bombay.
translated_content: R Raj Rao, karai aranduka rehegua, poetaha ha novelista katupyry, avei Savitribai Phule Pune Universidad-pe Inglés atyguasúpe omba'apova'ekue, ojapo heta drama ohechauka hag̃ua mba’éichapa LGBTQIA aty ohasa jejopy omba’apo haguã ha’ekuéra rehe, ogayguakuéra apytépe voi. Ohupytyrõ mokõiveha, neve’ẽ ‘heta mba’e tekotevẽ gueteri ojapo’ he’i. Rao he’i, jepe Corte Suprema oipe’a va’ekue Section 377 2018-pe, ndohasái heta mba’e añetépe LGBTQIA rehegua. 'Heta mba’e tekotevẽ gueteri omba’eapo umi escritor-kuéra, académico, activista, abogado, ha ambuéva,' he’i. 'Che aranduka 20 rupi michĩnte ko tapépe.' Ipyahu aranduka, 'The Wisest Fool on Earth: Ten Street Plays and Three Monologues,' oñemboguata va’erã jasypakõi 3-pe. Upe atyhápe, Shyam Konnur – Mist LGBTQ Foundation ruvicha guasu ha Maharashtra pegua All India Professionals’ Congress Diversidad ha Inclusión rehe – ohói Rao ndive oñe’ẽ ha oikuaauka aranduka pegua. Mokõivéva LGBTQIA+ aty rehegua kuimba’e guasu hína. Konnur, osẽramo guare oipurukuaa ojoajúvo Rao rembiapo, he’i ko aranduka ombojoaju hesekuéra mba’e ohasa asy ha ojehasa’asy LGBTQIA rehegua. Pe aranduka ipahague 135 hoja, oñe’ẽ heta tema ohasa 30 ary rupi Rao rembiapokue rehe. Rao omyesakã, ‘Ahai ko’ã drama aikotevẽ rupi chejehe gay, ha upévare oiko peteĩ monólogo oikuaauka gay disidente ha ambue política rehegua disidente jejupe. Che avei aipuru novela ambue aranduka ojapo hag̃ua ko pu’aka.' He’i avei, omoñe’ẽramo ‘The Wisest Fool on Earth’ Inglaterra-pe 1990-pe, ha umi drama ha monólogo ‘Stand Up and Be Counted’ ojapo pyahu. Umi monólogo omoakã Jay rehe, kuimba’e arandu ha ndoguerohorýiva mba’evéichapa, opyta ndorekóiramo tembiapo, hembiapo kuimba’e rehe. Oñe’ẽ público-pe peteĩ edificio yvate piso-pe he’íva, oñembotyhápe. Mokõiha monólogo-pe, ‘Vanaprastha Ashram’, Jay ojehecha oguereko 20 ary heta rire, ha oñe’ẽ avei público-pe techo guýpe. ‘Stand Up and Be Counted’-pe Jay orekótama 60 ary rupi, oĩ cárcel-pe ohóre Koregaon-Bhima rally-pe 2018-pe, oñe’ẽ cárcelde. 'The Wisest Fool on Earth' oñembohasa Inglés-pe Mumbai ha Pune-pe, ha Hindi-pe Hyderabad-pe. Umi drama oikohápe: juzgado, estación de tren, óga mbyte, tape Mumbai-pe, korasõ mboja’o, bar gay, hospital, consultorio sexólogo, ha restaurante Irani – ohechauka India reko ambué. QueerInk (India ha Australia) he’íva, aranduka oñemoheñói va’erã jasypakõi 3 Pagdandi Bookstore-pe, Baner-pe. Oime avei Rao omba’apo hína imokõiha novela, ‘Mahmud and Ayaz’ rehe, oipuru mba’e Mombyryguasu Mahmud ha iservicio Ayaz rehegua ohechauka hag̃ua mombyry rehegaygua ohupytyrã ko’ágã Bombay-pe.

article_content: World number two Novak Djokovic overcame John Isner in a demanding four hour, 16-minute match to send Serbia into the quarterfinals of the Davis Cup on Sunday. Serbia, ahead 2-1 overnight in Belgrade, relied on Djokovic to clinch the tie against the towering American, and while he faced a tough battle, he ultimately prevailed 7-5, 3-6, 6-3, 6-7, 6-4. With this win, Serbia achieves its first-ever World Group victory and will play Croatia at home in the quarterfinals from July 9 to 11. Djokovic, backed by an enthusiastic home crowd, appeared set for an easy win after taking the first set, but Isner responded strongly, breaking Djokovic twice in the second set to draw level. Djokovic regained control in the third set but could not capitalize fully, losing a close tiebreak in the fourth set as Isner forced a deciding fifth. A crucial service break in the opening game of the final set gave Djokovic the edge, but Isner saved six match points before sending a forehand into the net. Djokovic fell to his knees in celebration after the exhausting contest. This defeat means that Patrick McEnroe's U.S. team will have to compete in a relegation playoff later this year to keep their spot in the World Group. Elsewhere, defending champions Spain advanced by defeating Switzerland 4-1 despite the absence of injured Rafael Nadal, setting up a quarterfinal against France. Russia narrowly beat India 3-2 and will face Argentina, who overcame Sweden 3-2 in Stockholm. Returning from injury, David Nalbandian secured Argentina's decisive win by defeating Andreas Vinciguerra after Sweden's Robin Soderling brought the teams level with a straight-sets victory over Leonardo Mayer. Past champions Croatia, last year's runners-up Czech Republic, and France all sealed their quarterfinal spots on Saturday by defeating Ecuador, Belgium, and Germany, respectively. The upcoming France vs. Spain clash is already generating excitement among tennis fans. 'It'll be like a final; it's the kind of thing you dream about,' said France captain Guy Forget to the official Davis Cup website.

article_content: Peter Boyd, an attorney and Founder of PaperStreet, has helped over 1,500 law firms with their websites and marketing strategies.  In the legal profession, reputation is everything. Building that reputation takes years of hard study and demanding work — so encountering a negative online review can feel devastating. However, one bad review doesn't determine your firm’s fate. There are practical steps attorneys can take to maintain a strong online reputation and minimize the impact of negative feedback.  Respond Quickly to Negative Reviews  When a negative review or comment appears online, respond promptly. Addressing concerns transparently and courteously shows accountability, professionalism, and a commitment to client satisfaction. Offer clear explanations or apologies as appropriate and engage with reviewers in an effort to resolve any issues. If the negative review is unfounded, politely clarify the facts in your response and report the review to the site. You can also ask colleagues to flag the review as spam.  Websites like Google and Facebook may not remove disputed reviews immediately, but quick, polite action is always productive. If the criticism holds some merit, consider a conciliatory reply and offer to communicate further with the client.  Encourage Feedback, Don’t Let Fear Hold You Back  Even if negative feedback is possible, actively seek client reviews—they are vital for managing your reputation. Regularly collecting positive reviews strengthens your reputation and can diminish the impact of occasional negative ones.  Strategies to gather reviews include: • Asking during client meetings or phone calls, alongside expressing appreciation. • Sending follow-up emails to clients after a case concludes, inviting feedback. • Providing printed materials, such as exit pamphlets, reminding clients to leave a review.  Focus initially on Google Business Profile, as it’s often the first place potential clients see your firm. After collecting at least five Google reviews, expand to other sites like Facebook, Yelp, or Avvo. Broadening your online testimonials enhances your credibility across platforms.  More reviews typically improve your firm’s visibility in search engine results and determine your ranking in Google’s Local Service Ads (LSAs). Having positive reviews and a higher star rating boosts your ad placement, making your firm more visible to searchers.  Showcase Your Results and Testimonials  Once you have handled several cases, create a results page on your website that highlights your achievements and expertise. Share descriptions of cases, results, and include reviews or testimonials—written or video—from satisfied clients.  Where specific case results aren’t possible, consider a page featuring representative transactions or general descriptions of successful resolutions. Even if client names can't be shared, detailing outcomes can demonstrate your effectiveness. Including authentic client testimonials humanizes your data and lends credibility.  Conclusion  Your online reputation plays a critical role in shaping how clients perceive your law firm. Fear of negative reviews shouldn’t keep you from soliciting client feedback or establishing your firm’s presence online. A consistently positive reputation across social media, review platforms, and your website can outweigh one or two negative comments. If a negative review does appear, it should be a small blemish, not the defining impression of your firm—provided you have built a foundation of positive feedback.  The Forbes Agency Council is an invitation-only network for leaders in PR, media strategy, and advertising agencies.

article_content: Four French journalists who were kidnapped in Syria last June by the radical militant group Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) have been found blindfolded and bound on the Turkish border. According to the Turkish news agency Dogan, an unidentified group brought the journalists to the Turkish border last night. Initially, Turkish soldiers mistook the group for smugglers, but upon hearing them speak French, took the four men to a police station in Akcakale, near the border. A video from Dogan News Agency showed Edouard Elias, Didier François, Pierre Torres, and Nicolas Hénin arriving at Mehmet Akif Inan Training & Research Hospital in Şanlıurfa, near the Syrian border, after their release from 10 months of captivity. After medical checks in Akcakale, the journalists were reported to be in good health, according to the office of the French president. The Turkish broadcaster DHA shared images of their arrival before the four men were transported to other destinations. "I'm very happy to be free," said 53-year-old Didier François. "We thank the Turkish authorities; they really helped us. It's wonderful to see the sky, to walk, and speak freely." French President François Hollande expressed great relief upon news of their release and was present to welcome Didier François and the others at Villacoublay air base outside Paris. Photographer Edouard Elias and reporter Didier François had been working for French radio station Europe 1 when they were taken hostage on June 6 on their way to Aleppo. Sixteen days later, journalists Nicolas Hénin and Pierre Torres were kidnapped—Hénin was working for Le Point magazine and Arte, while Torres was reporting on municipal elections. Family members greeted the journalists after their transfer from Evreux by helicopter to Villacoublay military airbase. The Committee to Protect Journalists reported that Syria was the most dangerous country for journalists in 2013, with 29 killed that year.

article_content: Google has partnered with museums worldwide to launch a major update to its online Cultural Institute, giving users the opportunity to explore significant figures and events from the past century. The new additions to the Google Cultural Institute archives, accessible from today, aim to serve as a globally available educational resource preserving history for anyone, anywhere. New interactive online exhibits recount major world events like D-Day, the Holocaust, and the struggle against Apartheid, using a mix of photographs, historical accounts, and quotes. A total of 42 exhibitions were launched, each featuring a well-crafted narrative that interlinks archival materials to highlight various perspectives and stories behind these events. Seventeen institutions—including museums and foundations—contributed to the project, drawing from their collections of letters, manuscripts, video testimonies, and more. Some of this material is presented online for the first time and is described as highly moving. These exhibitions build upon previous Google Cultural Institute projects, such as showcasing the Dead Sea Scrolls, the Yad Vashem Holocaust Museum, and the Nelson Mandela archives. Users can zoom into high-resolution images and search the vast archives by country, person, event, or date. Among the new highlights is the Coronation of Queen Elizabeth II, featuring vibrant color photos provided by Historvius. Mike Lewis, CEO of Historvius.com, stated that their collection of commentary and images brings the event back to life and sheds new light on this pivotal moment in British history, comparing its uplifting effect to that of the 2011 Royal Wedding. Other notable additions include an exhibit on South African activist Steve Biko and the many books sent to Nelson Mandela during his imprisonment. The D-Day exhibition, created in partnership with the Imperial War Museum, features detailed accounts of the Normandy landings, including photographs, personal letters, and archival orders. Amanda Mason, curator for the exhibition, highlighted the potential for global audiences to engage with these iconic materials in high resolution, at any time. Some of the most affecting exhibits focus on the fight against Apartheid, produced with the collaboration of South African institutions such as the Steve Biko Foundation and the Nelson Mandela Centre of Memory. Obenewa Amponsah and Sello Hatang, representing these institutions, emphasized the importance of making this historical legacy accessible to both local and international audiences. The Google Cultural Institute can be accessed online, offering a wide range of resources for personal and professional use.

article_content: Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a well-known advocate for the Khalistan movement, has released a new video calling for demonstrations against Air India flights departing from Toronto and Vancouver airports on December 1. According to reports from the Financial Times, U.S. authorities recently disrupted an assassination plot aimed at a Sikh separatist in the United States. The plot has allegedly been linked to Indian government involvement, and the U.S. reportedly warned India about these concerns following Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s June visit to Washington. Pannun, who is a citizen of both the United States and Canada and is the general counsel for Sikhs for Justice, was the reported target. After he posted a video threatening Air India passengers and advocating a worldwide blockade of the airline starting November 19, India’s National Investigation Agency opened a case against him. These incidents come amid increasing friction between India and Canada. Canada has claimed that Indian agents were involved in the June murder of Sikh leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar near Vancouver, though India has denied any role in the killing. This dispute led India to require Canada to reduce its diplomatic staff in New Delhi and pause visa services for Canadian nationals. Meanwhile, Indian tax authorities have reportedly uncovered around ₹10,000 crore in tax evasion over three years among online retailers selling via platforms like Instagram and Facebook, issuing notices to 45 brands so far. Additionally, a surge in GST-related notices—over 20,000 since 2022—has caused Indian businesses to reassess their tax strategies when planning mergers or other major deals. Separately, Nawaz Modi has accused her estranged husband Gautam Singhania, CEO of Raymond, of physically assaulting her and one of their daughters two months ago.

Financial Times omombe’u avei, Estados Unidos mburuvicha-kuéra ojoko hague peteĩ plan ojuka peteĩ separatista sij rehe Estados Unidos-pe, ha ojavyhague ikatuha Indian gobierno oĩ hague involucrado. article_content: This year's harvest of virgin olive oil has been severely affected by drought in southern Europe, leading to concerns about an international shortage of extra virgin olive oil. Popular chefs like Nigella Lawson and Jamie Oliver may need to adjust their recipes as this key ingredient becomes more scarce. Weather extremes are to blame, with Spain's farmers struggling through a drought while the UK experienced its wettest summer in a century in 2012. As a result, Spain's olive oil harvest is expected to be down by as much as 60%, likely causing shortages and pushing up prices. Meanwhile, British retailers are currently selling olive oil at reduced prices to attract middle-class customers, but experts warn that these discounts will not last in light of supply problems. For example, Tesco is offering several extra virgin olive oils at half price, with prices ranging from £1.74 to £2.84 for 500ml. Jeff Bayley, UK representative of the Hojiblanca Group—a cooperative of over 50,000 farmers in Andalusia and the world’s largest olive oil producer—explained that the Spanish harvest is much smaller than in previous years. The forecast for 2013 is 700,000 tonnes compared to 1.6 million tonnes last year, mainly due to the continued drought. He predicted that this would cause shortages and drive prices higher, calling current supermarket price cuts unsustainable. Other major producers such as Greece, Italy, Turkey, and Tunisia have faced similar droughts and cannot make up for Spain’s reduced supply. Experts warn that the shortage could encourage a black market in stolen olive oil and increased adulteration with cheaper substitutes. Recently, a British company, Stark Naked Foods, was fined over £20,000 for falsely advertising pesto made with extra virgin olive oil and Grana Padano cheese, when it actually contained sunflower oil and a less expensive Latvian cheese. In the US, the North American Olive Oil Association is suing Gourmet Factory, alleging that its Capatriti brand of '100% pure olive oil' is actually olive pomace oil, which is made from solid waste using solvents, not olives. Authorities have also cracked down on olive oil theft and fraud. Last July, Spanish police arrested a gang leader who stole more than a million litres of olive oil shipped to Italy. In 2011, two Spanish businessmen received prison sentences for marketing extra virgin olive oil that was mostly sunflower oil. Jeff Bayley advises consumers to check labels carefully, noting that true extra virgin olive oil should be clearly marked. He points out that refined oils, which are more processed, are often sold at similar prices to extra virgin oils in the UK, even though extra virgin is less processed and more natural. Hojiblanca Extra Virgin Olive Oil leads the Spanish market, producing around 215,000 tonnes annually—about four times the entire UK market.

article_content: Airbnb's CEO revealed that the company is using artificial intelligence (AI) to identify guests who are likely to throw house parties before they book a rental, according to a report from Bloomberg on Monday. Brian Chesky, CEO of Airbnb, discussed in a Bloomberg interview how the company is leveraging AI to address long-standing issues, including guests hosting disruptive parties despite Airbnb's strict anti-party policies. Chesky explained, 'We've used machine learning techniques to analyze the last 1.5 billion guest arrivals to determine which bookings resulted in parties and which did not. AI can analyze vast amounts of data to identify patterns and create a set of rules, which is difficult to accomplish manually.' He added that if a booking attempt raises concerns, 'we either block the booking or request more information from the guest until we feel confident.' Chesky also stated that AI is being used to verify whether photos submitted by hosts match satellite images, helping to remove fake listings from the platform. Airbnb made its ban on house parties permanent in June 2022, following a temporary ban introduced during the pandemic in 2020, after noting that some guests were behaving as if homes were bars or clubs. In December 2022, Airbnb introduced reservation screening technology to prevent certain guests from booking entire homes for one night unless they have received positive reviews from other hosts. While Chesky did not provide specific details about Airbnb’s AI technology, the use of AI to predict potential rule-breaking behavior has raised concerns, as similar technology has been shown to perpetuate bias, including racism, in some cases. Chesky remains optimistic about AI’s future at Airbnb, saying at Bloomberg’s Technology Summit in June that the platform will soon become the 'ultimate AI concierge,' helping users find the best rentals and experiences.

Efforts by OpenAI executives and investors to reinstate Sam Altman as chief executive officer have stalled over disagreements about the structure and authority of the company's board, according to sources familiar with the negotiations. Although the situation remains fluid and talks continue, a resolution could arrive soon. Altman, who was dismissed on Friday, is reportedly open to returning, but only if there are changes in governance that include removing some current board members and a public statement clearing him of any wrongdoing, these sources said.

The board faced strong internal backlash following Altman’s ouster, initially agreeing in principle to step down, but so far has not done so officially, focusing instead on evaluating candidates for board positions. Several key OpenAI leaders, including Interim CEO Mira Murati, Chief Strategy Officer Jason Kwon, and Chief Operating Officer Brad Lightcap, are urging the board to resign and to bring Altman back, according to a person close to the matter.

The campaign to reinstate Altman began shortly after his removal by board members led by Chief Scientist Ilya Sutskever, who cited concerns that Altman was not always forthcoming in his communications. In protest, President Greg Brockman, who had also been removed from the board, resigned just hours later.

A core issue dividing OpenAI has been Altman’s desire to transform the company from its nonprofit origins into a successful business and to accelerate product launches, which clashed with some board members’ concerns over the safety implications of advanced AI. As of Friday, the board included Altman, Brockman, Sutskever, Quora CEO Adam D’Angelo, entrepreneur Tasha McCauley, and Helen Toner, director of strategy at Georgetown’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology.

By midday Sunday, there were indications that negotiations may be concluding: Altman and Brockman appeared at OpenAI’s San Francisco headquarters, according to a source. Later, Altman shared a photo of himself at the office wearing a guest badge on social media with the caption, “first and last time I ever wear one of these.” Reports indicate that a 5 p.m. San Francisco deadline has been set for the board to meet the demands of Altman and his supporters. If Altman is to be reinstated, the board may need to issue a statement clearing him of wrongdoing, but this could expose them to legal risks, according to a negotiator.

Altman is said to have strong support among key employees, especially top research scientists who are central to OpenAI’s development of large language models powering products like the ChatGPT chatbot. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has played a significant role in mediation, as Microsoft is OpenAI’s largest investor with a $13 billion stake. Former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor is reportedly set to join the new board, and another Microsoft executive could as well, though regulatory issues may affect this decision.

Meanwhile, Altman is exploring other ventures, such as raising capital for a chip manufacturing startup and developing an AI-focused hardware device. In an internal memo on Saturday, Lightcap clarified that Altman’s dismissal was not due to misconduct or financial or safety violations, stating the decision “took us all by surprise” and that discussions with the board have been ongoing to understand the rationale behind it.

article_content: The internet has revolutionized our lives, from music streaming to video calling—and now, by making it much easier to access your computer remotely. There is a wide range of remote access programs available that allow one computer to connect to another over the internet, many of which are free. While Windows and macOS come with their own built-in remote access tools, they are neither especially user-friendly nor cross-platform. That’s why this article focuses on free third-party alternatives. With the right remote access program installed on both ends, you can log into a laptop or desktop from anywhere, ensuring you never have to worry about leaving important files or software behind. Chrome Remote Desktop, developed by Google, works through the Chrome browser and enables full access to any computer it's set up on. As long as Google Chrome is installed, you can use this tool. To set up Chrome Remote Desktop, open the Chrome Remote Desktop page in your browser on the computer you wish to access, sign in with your Google account, and click the download icon next to 'Set up remote access.' Download and install the provided utility, then follow the on-screen instructions. You’ll name your computer so you can identify it later and set up a six-digit PIN for security. Once set, your computer appears in the Chrome Remote Desktop list, where you can change its name or remove it using the pen and trash can icons. When connecting from another device, visit the Chrome Remote Desktop page, select your target computer, and after a short wait, you’ll have remote access via your browser. You can also adjust program options, such as resizing the remote window. TeamViewer is another popular remote access option. It's straightforward to configure and free for personal use. Business and team features require a subscription, but for individual access to your own computers, there’s no cost.

article_content: A baby girl named Faith Martin, born with part of her brain outside her skull due to a rare condition called encephalocele, is now thriving despite doctors saying her chances of survival were low. Doctors told her parents, Jessica Williams (20) and Aaron Martin (21), that Faith might not be able to breathe on her own after birth and that medical intervention would not be provided in that case. Faith’s condition was discovered during a 17-week pregnancy scan at James Cook University Hospital in Middlesbrough. Her parents were warned that survival after birth was unlikely. Encephalocele is a rare defect where part of the brain and its membranes protrude through an opening in the skull, caused by incomplete closure of the neural tube during early pregnancy. The outlook for children with encephalocele is often poor, with many not surviving and others facing neurological difficulties. Despite this, Faith’s parents decided to continue the pregnancy. When Faith was born, she cried straight away, showing she could breathe on her own. She later had surgery to remove the protrusion, which contained excess fluid and non-functioning brain tissue. Jessica said looking after Faith before surgery was difficult as the protrusion was sensitive and painful. The surgery took place at Newcastle's Royal Victoria Infirmary when Faith was three months old; a shunt was inserted to help drain any future fluid build-up. After surgery, Faith has met developmental milestones expected for her age, and her parents consider her a ‘little miracle’. Faith will need regular MRI scans and check-ups to ensure she continues to develop as expected. Jessica and Aaron are thankful for the support they have received and hope Faith will continue to thrive. A spokeswoman for South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust said they provide parents with as much information and support as possible to help with decision-making in rare cases like this.

article_content: As a ground invasion of Gaza appears imminent, Israel has outlined several reasons for pursuing such an offensive, though the operation has instilled panic and confusion among civilians. The Israeli military has ordered more than one million residents of northern Gaza to evacuate southward within the besieged enclave, as clashes with Hamas escalate. Hamas has urged Palestinians to ignore the evacuation order, labeling it as psychological warfare and insisting they remain. Israeli airstrikes have pounded Gaza since Saturday, following a surprise attack by Hamas’s Qassam Brigades. By Wednesday, Israeli ground forces, accompanied by significant military equipment, began to mass at Gaza’s border in preparation for a potential ground assault.  Israeli Defence Minister Yoav Gallant told troops near Gaza, “We started the offensive from the air. Later on, we will also come from the ground.” To support the operation, Israel has mobilized 350,000 reservists, tripling the size of its active military force.  A key question is what Israel hopes to achieve with a ground invasion. The multipronged attack by Hamas's Qassam Brigades caught Israel by surprise—a level of shock not seen since the 1973 October War. Yossi Mekelberg, a Chatham House expert, told Al Jazeera that Israel’s main goal is to destroy Hamas’s infrastructure and eliminate its military ability to mount similar attacks. However, Nimrod Goren of the Middle East Institute argues Israel may also seek to dismantle Hamas’s ability to govern Gaza, hoping to change the political landscape so that Hamas cannot return to power.  Some experts doubt that fully eradicating Hamas is possible. Zoran Kusovac, a strategic analyst, noted that distinguishing fighters from civilians is highly challenging, making the goal virtually unachievable despite Israeli intelligence efforts.  Israel previously attempted to defeat Hamas with a ground incursion during the 2014 Gaza conflict but withdrew before accomplishing its objectives. According to Sami Hamdi, managing director of International Interest, this suggests the current operation may focus more on demonstrating Israeli military strength domestically, particularly as public criticism of Prime Minister Netanyahu grows. Hamdi added that Israel seeks to restore its deterrence by inflicting significant costs in response to Hamas’s resistance.  Despite ongoing Israeli bombardment, Palestinian resistance and rocket attacks continue. Hamdi highlighted gaps in Israeli intelligence, as Israeli forces struggle to locate rocket launch sites, indicating that even a ground invasion may not resolve these challenges.  Kusovac raised another, more extreme theory: that Israel may aim to depopulate Gaza, similar to previous mass displacements in other conflicts, though he stressed the logistical and humanitarian difficulties—especially since Palestinians’ homeland is Gaza itself. Israel does not want to absorb large numbers of displaced Palestinians, and Egypt has ruled out accepting refugees, although its border remains open for humanitarian aid.  Experts like Goren assert that Israel has little appetite to reoccupy Gaza. Instead, there is speculation that replacing Hamas could allow the Palestinian Authority, based in the West Bank, to expand governance to Gaza. Goren stated, “Times of war eventually should lead to times of peace. Even if it seems far-fetched now, that is the goal of all sides.”  Still, Hamdi cautioned that the situation remains highly unpredictable, noting ongoing shock in Israel over the effectiveness of the recent Hamas attack.

Israel mburuvicha militar ordena millón peteĩ tapicha nortepeguágui osẽ hag̃ua sur gotyo ha’eñoite, Hamas katu ndoheja oiko péicha he’ívo ha’eha avañe’ẽ py’amokõi ikatu hag̃uáicha ojekyhyje. Mba’e omongu’e Israel oheka hag̃ua ataque yvygui rehe: Qassam Brigadas ojapopyre aniha’arãi Israel rehe, 1973 guive noikoi haguéicha. Yossi Mekelberg (Chatham House) he’i Israel rembiapota ha’e ombogue Hamas infraestructura militar ha ombopoi chuguive omboñe’ẽve. Nimrod Goren (Middle East Institute) he’i Israel oipota avei Hamas ndaikatúi gobernái Gaza ári.  Oĩ oporandúva ikatúpa ndojapói Hamas rehe upe omoheñóiva. Sami Hamdi (International Interest) he’i ko’ágã aimete inunekohátakua ohechauka og̃uahẽse pu’aka ojokupyty hag̃ua kritika Netanyahu rehe. Kusovac omombe’u posible mba’e ivaivéva: Israel oiporavo osẽ hag̃ua tapichakuéra Gazagui, ojoguávo umi desplazamiento ojehúva Karabájpe. Ha katu, ndaikatúi ojejapo ipe’indépe, ha Egipto ndohoryi recibívo refugiado nuevo, ha katu pytyvõ humanitario og̃uahẽ hína frontera-pe.  Goren he’i Israel ndorekói tembiporã oike jeývo Gaza gobernárõ. Ojejervéta pe autoridad Palestina (West Bank) oike hag̃ua Gaza-pe gobierno rehe. “Guerra omboguepa rire, ikatu og̃uahẽ py’aguapy. Ha ramo jepe ndaipóri esperanza, upe hína objetivo opavavépe,” he’i Goren.  Hamdi oavisa og̃uahẽ magiculaite ndajaikuaái mba’éichapa tenonderã oikotava, Israel gueteri oñemondýi ohechávo ataque ipu’akave Hamas ojapóva.

article_content: Bitcoin’s value has climbed sharply over the past year, marking a return to bullish territory. This upswing happens even as concerns linger about potential negative moves from U.S. regulators. The upcoming bitcoin halving is another major event expected to add price volatility. Dan Morehead, CEO of Pantera Capital, recently emphasized how the anticipated debut of spot bitcoin ETFs might dramatically reshape the crypto market. Ark Investment Management, headed by Cathie Wood, has submitted a proposal for a spot bitcoin ETF along with 21Shares, suggesting a management fee of 0.80%. This proposed fee is below Grayscale’s 2% charge for its primary bitcoin trust and is also lower than certain fees levied by current bitcoin futures ETFs. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is reviewing several spot bitcoin ETF bids—including Ark’s—with decisions anticipated by January 2024. Analysts speculate the SEC may approve multiple funds simultaneously, which could heighten competition in what’s perceived as a winner-takes-all market. Earlier in the year, BlackRock—the largest asset manager globally—generated additional buzz by filing for its own spot bitcoin ETF, granting potential access to the expansive U.S. wealth management sector. BlackRock’s move encouraged other major financial institutions to file similar applications, leaving the SEC to weigh roughly a dozen proposals. Bitcoin’s resurgence has paralleled gold’s gains, as the Federal Reserve keeps interest rates steady to combat inflation. According to Morehead, if BlackRock receives approval for its ETF, it will greatly increase mainstream investor access to bitcoin and likely push the market higher. Morehead is optimistic that spot bitcoin ETF approvals will happen in a few months, rather than years. Optimism is running high: Bloomberg Intelligence analysts put the chances of SEC approval of a bitcoin spot ETF by January 2024 at 90%. Morehead argues that ETF approval represents an unusual case of ‘buy the rumor, buy the news’, possibly fueling additional buying momentum for bitcoin—unlike past events such as Coinbase’s stock listing or the first bitcoin futures ETFs, which coincided with peaks in bitcoin’s price.

article_content: Roberto Di Matteo has been officially introduced as Schalke's new manager after being presented at a press conference in Veltins Arena. The Bundesliga club appointed the former Chelsea boss on Tuesday, following the dismissal of Jens Keller due to a disappointing start to the season. Di Matteo, who led Chelsea to Champions League victory in 2012, has not managed a club since leaving Chelsea in November of that year. Speaking at his unveiling, Di Matteo confirmed that his coaching staff would include his former Italy teammate Attilio Lombardo as assistant coach and Massimo Battara as goalkeeping coach. Both previously worked with Roberto Mancini at Manchester City. Di Matteo stated: 'Attilio Lombardo brings a wealth of international experience as both a player and a coach. Massimo Battara, responsible for goalkeeping training, also has significant experience in various leagues. Neither speaks German yet but will learn quickly, and for now, we will communicate in English.' The new manager set his sights on qualifying for the Champions League, aligning with the club’s targets. He also expressed excitement about the challenge ahead and mentioned Ruud Gullit as one of his managerial influences. Di Matteo emphasized the potential within the squad, acknowledging defensive issues partly due to injuries. He explained his preference for tactical flexibility, using both the 4-2-3-1 and 4-3-3 systems depending on player availability. He stressed the importance of balancing offense and defense, and his focus on strong team communication and the development of young talent. He refrained from commenting on Schalke’s upcoming Champions League group stage match against Chelsea, saying he preferred to approach each game individually. Di Matteo has signed a three-year contract with Schalke. Keller, who was appointed in December 2012, was dismissed following a series of poor results, including a 2-1 loss to Hoffenheim and an exit from the German Cup at the hands of Dynamo Dresden. Schalke will face Chelsea in the Champions League group stage in Gelsenkirchen on November 25.

article_content: Peacock might be highlighting horror films this October, but sci-fi lovers have plenty to enjoy too. Three iconic science fiction movies, all tied to Steven Spielberg’s creative touch, are back in the streaming lineup. Spielberg’s influence—whether as director or executive producer—has shaped countless major productions, especially during his landmark 1980s collaborations with Universal Pictures. Here are three recommended sci-fi films now streaming on Peacock that reflect his legacy. First, 'E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial' offers a heartwarming take on alien encounters. The story follows E.T., who is accidentally left behind on Earth and forms a powerful friendship with young Elliott, his siblings Gertie and Michael, all while being chased by government authorities. As E.T. becomes ill, Elliott’s health also declines, creating an emotional urgency to help their new friend return home. Next, 'Back to the Future'—although directed by Robert Zemeckis, Spielberg’s hand as executive producer is evident throughout. The film centers on teen Marty McFly, who is sent thirty years into the past in a time-traveling DeLorean built by Doc Brown. Marty must work to ensure his parents’ romance blossoms—or risk vanishing from existence altogether. Finally, 'Cowboys & Aliens' fuses Western action with alien invasion. With Jon Favreau directing and Spielberg producing, Daniel Craig stars as Jake Lonergan, waking up with amnesia and a mysterious alien device on his wrist. He reluctantly teams with Colonel Dolarhyde (Harrison Ford) and Ella Swenson (Olivia Wilde) to rally locals and Native tribes against the extraterrestrial threat. All three films are now available on Peacock, making them perfect picks for your next movie night.

article_content: Saracens improved their chances of reaching the European Champions Cup quarter-finals by defeating Munster 33-10 at Allianz Park. The win moved Saracens to the top of Pool One and reflected one of their most cohesive displays this season. Both Chris Wyles and Chris Ashton scored tries in the opening half, with Ashton adding a second after the break. Owen Farrell was key, delivering four penalty goals and three conversions for a personal tally of 18 points, reinforcing his credentials ahead of England's Six Nations squad announcement. While Clermont Auvergne remain favorites in the group, Saracens are well placed for a quarter-final spot, potentially as a top runner-up. Munster, however, face tough odds and need an extraordinary result in their next home match against Sale Sharks to keep hopes alive. Throughout the match, Munster struggled against Saracens' forward power and midfield dominance. Munster's late try by Denis Hurley and points from Ian Keatley provided some consolation but didn't threaten Saracens’ control. Saracens welcomed Brad Barritt back from injury, and captain Alistair Hargreaves also returned, though winger David Strettle was absent due to back trouble. Munster, meanwhile, missed scrum-half Conor Murray owing to a neck injury. Saracens set the pace early, opening with a Farrell penalty and a well-worked try by Wyles. Munster fell further behind after losing CJ Stander to injury before halftime. Munster put up more resistance in the second half, but Saracens’ early advantage endured. A yellow card against James Cronin and a brief scuffle highlighted the tension, but Saracens finished strongly as Ashton crossed for a late try, solidifying their bid for the next round.

article_content: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has urged world leaders to work together as a global community to shape a future where climate action is seen as an opportunity for innovation and growth, rather than a burden. Speaking at the APEC Informal Leaders' Dialogue in San Francisco on November 16, Goyal highlighted India's achievement in reaching its renewable energy goal of 175 gigawatts nine years ahead of schedule. "He urged world leaders to unite as a global community to create a future where sustainability becomes a way of life, and climate action leads to innovation and growth," stated the Commerce Ministry. Goyal also attended the Investor Forum of the Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII), co-hosted by US Secretary of Commerce Gina Raimondo and Senior Advisor Amos Hochstein. Discussions focused on collaboration and priorities to boost private investment in the Indo-Pacific region. Raimondo highlighted the continuing partnership between India and the US, specifically mentioning the Green Transition Fund. The minister also participated in the IPEF Leaders' Meeting, which was attended by several world leaders, including the US President. During the meeting, several IPEF initiatives such as the Critical Minerals Dialogue, Investment Accelerator, Catalytic Fund, Investor Forum, and IPEF Networks were announced. Separately, the government is examining the legality of transferring unclaimed funds from the Sahara-Sebi Refund Account to the Consolidated Fund of India, with a provision to refund investors who file claims later. In other news, Apple aims to achieve ₹1 lakh crore in iPhone production in India by the end of the current fiscal year in March 2024, having already surpassed ₹60,000 crore in the first seven months. Nawaz Modi, the estranged wife of Gautam Singhania, is seeking three-quarters of the industrialist’s reported $1.4 billion net worth for herself and their two daughters, as part of a family settlement following their separation.

article_content: A crew member from the long-running reality TV show 'Cops' has died after being shot during filming in Omaha, Nebraska last night. The unidentified crew member, who was reportedly holding a microphone, was killed during the filming of a gunfight involving police and a robbery suspect at a Wendy's restaurant at 43rd and Dodge Street. The robbery suspect, identified as a parolee from Kansas, also died in the incident, during which officers fired approximately 30 shots. Afterward, it was revealed that the suspect had been carrying an Airsoft rifle—a replica that resembles a firearm but is non-lethal. Police plan to provide more information about the fatal incident at a press conference scheduled for 2:30 p.m. According to audio from police radio posted by @MeanStreetsOMA on Soundcloud, officers described the suspect as wearing a black hoodie and a white bandana. Additional patrol cars were called to the scene after officers reported that a member of the 'Cops' crew had been shot and was unresponsive. Deputy Police Chief David Baker stated that more details about the cameraman’s condition and further information would be released the following day. He added, 'We have a lot of ground to cover here tonight and officers will continue the investigation throughout the night.' 'Cops,' created by U.S. film and TV director John Langley, has been airing since 1989 and documents police officers during patrols and special operations. The show, which began filming in Omaha in July, was broadcast on Fox for 25 years before moving to Spike TV last year. Previously, Omaha Police Chief Todd Schmaderer expressed that he wanted ‘Cops’ to film his department to showcase the professionalism of Omaha's officers. Langley Productions has not yet commented on the incident. The article also notes previous controversies around reality TV crews with Spike TV. In June, Carlos Enrique Barron, 43, was sentenced to 90 days in jail for firing shots into the air outside his Las Vegas home while a crew from the reality show 'Repo Games'—also produced by Spike TV—was filming in the area. 'Repo Games' is a program in which vehicle owners can avoid repossession by answering five general knowledge questions correctly, with the show paying off their debts if they succeed.

article_content: Individuals under 18 have been prohibited from visiting this year's World Press Photo exhibition in Budapest after Hungary's government determined that some images violate a law restricting LGBTQ+ content. The renowned exhibition, held at Hungary's National Museum in Budapest, attracts more than 4 million visitors from over 80 cities worldwide each year. Its purpose is to showcase exceptional photojournalism and bring coverage of significant events to international audiences. The restriction stems from five photographs by Filipino photojournalist Hannah Reyes Morales, which depict a community of elderly LGBTQ+ individuals in the Philippines. The photos show community members who have lived together for decades, some dressed in drag and wearing make-up. Hungarian lawmaker Dora Duro filed a complaint, leading the country's cultural ministry to determine the photos violate a national law prohibiting LGBTQ+ content for minors. As a result, no one under 18 may enter the exhibition, even with parental consent. Joumana El Zein Khoury, executive director of World Press Photo, expressed concern over the targeted censorship, stating this is the first occurrence of such audience restrictions in Europe for the exhibition. She called the situation 'worrisome and sad.' The ban is the latest in a series of moves by Hungary's government, led by Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, to limit access to LGBTQ+ content for minors across multiple forms of media, including television, film, advertisements, and literature. The government asserts that the 2021 'child protection' law is meant to shield minors from what it describes as sexual propaganda. However, the legislation has prompted legal challenges from 15 European Union countries. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the law as 'a disgrace.' Dora Duro, who initiated the complaint, claims the restriction does not infringe on press freedom or expression. She argues that what is depicted as valuable for children can influence them, and considers the exhibition harmful to minors and adults. Photographer Reyes Morales stated that the subjects of her photos are icons and role models for the LGBTQ+ community in the Philippines and are 'not dangerous or harmful.' She stated that limiting the visibility of LGBTQIA+ individuals is harmful, and she is saddened their story may not reach those who need it most. Hungary's cultural ministry did not respond to interview requests. Tamas Revesz, a former World Press Photo jury member and longtime organizer of Hungary's exhibition, remarked that some photos in the show, including images of war, are more serious and shocking than Morales' series. He noted that about half of Hungary's 50,000 exhibition visitors each year are students, meaning many youths will now miss the chance to see the collection—even images without LGBTQ+ content. Revesz called the ban a 'misguided and unprecedented move,' emphasizing the World Press Photo Foundation's value of freedom of thought and encouraging visitors to view photos without prejudice.

Ko veto hína peteĩ mba’e ojejapóva gobierno húngaro-re, ome’ẽva Táva ruvichápe Viktor Orbán-pe ha ojokóva LGBTQ+ rehegua umi mitãme heta medio rupi, televisión, cine, publicidad ha aranduka avei. He’i avei umi mba’e ojehechauka mitãme ikatu ombohape chupekuéra, ha he’i ko jehechauka iñaña mitã ha kakuaápe g̃uarã. Reyes Morales, fotógrafo, he’i umi ikatupyrýva ha modelo porãha LGBTQ+ comunidad Filipinas rehegua ha ndaha’éi mba’e ivaíva térã iñaña. He’i avei oñemomichĩ hag̃ua LGBTQIA+ rehegua ojesareko, ha oñeñandu vai haimete nomoañetéirõ umi oikotevẽva. Ministerio Cultural de Hungría ndojovakei comunicación rehe. Tamas Revesz, ypyguare World Press Photo jurado ha ojapo guasu 30 ary rupi pe jehechauka Hungría-pe, he’i oĩ animéta ta’ãnga guasu, por ejemplo, poguaha the guerra Ucrania-pe, ndaha’éi Morales rehegua. article_content: On Thursday morning, a 3.8-magnitude earthquake shook north-central Indiana, startling residents in Kokomo as they began their day. Debra Sholty, owner of Hobson Cleaners, described the experience as 'like a huge explosion under your feet.' According to the U.S. Geological Survey, the earthquake struck just before 8 a.m. ET at a depth of three miles. The initial magnitude was reported as 4.2 but was later revised to 3.8. The epicenter was about 15 miles east-southeast of Kokomo and 50 miles north of Indianapolis. No damage was immediately reported in Indianapolis, but individuals closer to the epicenter were surprised by the intensity. 'There was a very loud boom,' Sholty recalled. 'It felt like something hit the building from underneath. I actually felt an upward lift.' Laura Smith, an employee at Windmill Grill nearby, initially thought a truck had crashed into the building. 'The whole building just shook,' she said. 'You could feel your body shaking.' She added, 'Personally, I thought it was exciting.' Jerry Fiscus, owner of Hair Care East salon in Kokomo, said the quake shook his building 'pretty well,' although nothing fell off the shelves. Missy Dulmes, who was making breakfast at home, compared the experience to a 'really big thunder strike.' She said, 'You could hear the silverware shake in the drawer and the table moved.' At first, Dulmes suspected a burst water pipe. Few people contacted by CNN expressed fear, which is notable considering earthquakes are more commonly associated with the West Coast. Sholty, reflecting on the event, remarked with a laugh, 'I'm over 50. Nothing really frightens me anymore.'

article_content: As a trained chef, cooking is my greatest passion. Despite my love for creating meals, I sometimes don’t have the time to make everything from scratch, so convenience items like store-bought pesto and mayonnaise are always in my cart. Some dishes, like pavlovas, remain a challenge for me, often ending up flat or cracked. Like many busy mothers, I often wish for extra help in the kitchen. My husband is occupied with work meetings, and our daughters, aged nine and ten, are a bit too young for most kitchen tasks beyond baking cupcakes. Recently, a new appliance has entered my life: the Thermomix. At £925, it’s a significant investment, but if it works as well as promised, it could be invaluable. Far from a simple food processor, the Thermomix is more like a compact kitchen robot. Developed by German company Vorwerk in 1971, it’s praised by top chefs like Heston Blumenthal and Raymond Blanc. This machine does more than blend—it can heat, chop, stir, weigh ingredients, and guide you step-by-step through recipes via a touchscreen. With 200 recipes pre-loaded, it assists with a range of dishes, from bread and cake to salads and mousses. The built-in scales allow for precise measuring, easily resetting between ingredients. Capable of heating up to 120°C, it handles temperature-sensitive recipes, and its sharp blades can process everything from herbs to dried beans in seconds. Following the on-screen cookery book, you select a recipe, add ingredients as prompted, and let the machine take care of mixing, timing, and heat. More complicated dishes prompt you to add ingredients at various stages, pausing until you’re ready, and then tell you when the dish is complete. I wanted to see if the Thermomix lived up to the hype, so I put it through its paces with eight recipes, including typically time-consuming ones. Mayonnaise: Usually, homemade mayo splits on me, but with the Thermomix, I cracked an egg, added lemon juice, mustard powder, salt, and pepper, then drizzled in sunflower oil as it mixed. In under two minutes, I had perfect, glossy mayonnaise, much better than store-bought. Rustic Bread: Making bread can be tricky, but the Thermomix made it easier by heating the mixture to the ideal temperature for yeast, stirring gently, and kneading the dough. The result: the most delicious and wholesome bread I’ve ever had. Yoghurt Cake: The machine guided me through each step, from preparing the tin to adding ingredients and mixing the batter at speed. The outcome was a light, fluffy cake ready in half the usual time. Strawberry and Banana Sorbet: After blitzing sugar into powder, I added frozen fruit, egg white, and lemon juice, then blended. In seconds, I had a stunning sorbet—refreshing and irresistible. Beetroot Salad: Although I’m good with a knife, the Thermomix chopped beetroots, carrots, and apples finely, dressed them, and had the salad ready in five seconds. The texture and flavor exceeded my expectations. Risotto: Stirring risotto can be tedious, but the Thermomix grated Parmesan, sautéed shallots, and managed the precise timing and temperature for rice and wine, resulting in a dish that rivaled restaurant quality. Pesto: It blended Parmesan, pine nuts, garlic, basil, salt, and olive oil in under a minute, producing fresh pesto better than anything store-bought. Profiteroles: Usually, making choux pastry requires a lot of effort, but the Thermomix heated, stirred, and mixed the dough seamlessly. After baking, the result impressed even the toughest critics. Conclusion: If you’re overwhelmed by kitchen clutter, consider selling off your old appliances and investing in a Thermomix. It truly streamlines cooking and lives up to its reputation.

article_content: A CIA official has died following what sources describe as a suicide, after sustaining fatal injuries from a building fall earlier this week. CIA spokesperson Christopher White confirmed the individual’s death to The Washington Free Beacon, clarifying that the event did not take place at the agency’s Langley headquarters. The official, whose identity remains undisclosed, was reportedly a mid-level manager and the incident occurred at a facility in Fairfax County, Virginia. After the fall, the employee was transported to a local hospital where he later died. White stated, “We can confirm that there was an individual fatally injured at a facility where agency work is done. Due to privacy reasons and in respect for the family, we are not releasing further details at this time.” The CIA is known to operate at several semi-secret locations in Virginia—including Tysons Corner and safe houses—apart from its main Langley campus. According to agency sources, employees often work under intense stress, taking on roles such as intelligence analysts, support staff, technical service workers, and members of clandestine operations.

CIA moñe’ẽhára Christopher White ohechakuaa ko tembiasakue Washington Free Beacon-pe, ha he’i ndaha’eiha Langley rógape oikova’ekue. Ko mba’apohára, héra ndojekuaái, ojapova’ekue tembiapo mbytegotyhápe ha mba’éva oiko Fairfax County-pe. Upe rire oñeme’ẽ chupe pytyvõ, ha og̃uahẽ hospital-pe, upépe omano. article_content: In Washington state, a grandmother named Roxane Leilani Grove acted quickly to rescue her grandson Bryce Moser during an uncommon otter attack in the Pilchuck River, about 30 miles northeast of Seattle. After hearing Bryce cry out while swimming, Grove saw that an otter had latched onto him. She entered the water, pried the animal off, and called for help. Both Grove and Bryce sustained injuries; Grove required many stitches and treatment for an eye injury, while Bryce received staples in his head. They were both hospitalized following the incident. Authorities, including Captain Alan Myers from the Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife, are trying to capture the otter responsible. If they cannot safely relocate the animal or if doctors are concerned about rabies exposure, the otter may be euthanized, though such cases are very rare in the region. Wildlife experts have been called in to assist, especially if the otter has young. As a precaution, officials have closed Lake Conner Park and posted warnings along the Pilchuck River. Such attacks by otters are exceptionally rare, and both Bryce and his grandmother are continuing to recover with support from their community.

Bryce osapukái ha Grove ohechávo pe tapiti oipyhy hese, oike ype ojapo ñepytyvõ hatã, ohenói avei oipytyvõ hag̃ua. article_content: Two men have faced legal consequences for transforming sections of Horsham’s Great Daux roundabout and the A24 dual carriageway into makeshift stunt tracks, engaging in high-speed racing and drifting. Danny Neville, 54, drove a silver Toyota Supra, while William Smith, 22, operated a purple Nissan 200. Their actions were captured on police cameras after ongoing noise prompted resident complaints. Both were convicted of careless driving at Crawley Magistrates’ Court. Neville, from Leatherhead, was handed seven license points, a £750 fine, £100 in court costs, and a £75 victim surcharge. Smith, from Hindhead, received a 28-day driving ban, a £350 fine, £85 in costs, and a £35 surcharge. Inspector Phil Nicholas highlighted the increasing frequency of reckless driving in the area and the disruption this causes to the community. He emphasized the police force’s determination to prosecute antisocial drivers. A police spokesperson reiterated that anyone using public roads for dangerous stunts would be prosecuted, sending a strong message to deter similar behavior.

article_content: Sony’s strategy for handheld gaming has often been puzzling. While the PlayStation Vita was well-designed, it never gained the popularity of its predecessor, the PlayStation Portable. Many fans hoped for a new handheld after the Nintendo Switch brought renewed interest to the market, but instead, Sony introduced the PlayStation Portal. The PlayStation Portal aims to compete in the booming handheld scene, but its functionality is unique. Unlike typical handheld consoles, you can’t install or play games directly on the Portal. Instead, it streams games from your PlayStation 5 either through home Wi-Fi or the internet, provided you have sufficient bandwidth and the console remains powered on and online. At $200, the Portal might seem like an affordable handheld option—if not for the required PS5 console, which costs at least $400. This raises the question: who is the Portal intended for? Surprisingly, there is a market for this device. The Switch’s main draw is portable gaming anywhere, from airplanes to rooftop parties. While that convenience is appealing, many gamers primarily want to play comfortably at home, whether on the couch or in bed. For those wanting to play PS5 games away from the main TV—perhaps while someone else is watching a show—the Portal is useful. The device functions much like the Wii U’s controller, offering full streaming of the PS5 interface. If the TV connected to your PS5 is on, the same content appears on both screens. You can't use the Portal to play games while someone else uses the PS5 for streaming services like Netflix—media apps are blocked on the Portal, and it’s designed strictly for gaming. Game streaming on the Portal requires a reliable internet connection: Sony recommends at least 5 Mbps, ideally 15 Mbps, though higher speeds provide better performance. Oddly, the Portal can only stream games installed locally on your PS5; games streamed to your PS5 through PS Plus Premium can’t be accessed on the Portal. One of the Portal’s standout features is its design: essentially a DualSense controller split in half with a screen in the middle. This results in excellent compatibility with PS5 games, as they’re already designed for this layout—no need to adapt control schemes as with some other handheld systems.

Heta fan oha’arõ peteĩ pyahuitéi, Nintendo Switch oguahẽ rire omombarete jey mercado’omanoite rehe. Péro Sony ogueru PlayStation Portal. Portal ha’e peteĩ aparato handheld ojepuru hag̃ua hetaite hendápe, péro ome’ẽ mba’e rehe ambue. Ndaikatuvéi remohenda térã repojapo juego Portal-pe. Katu, ikatu remba’apo juego PS5-gui, Wi-Fi térã internet rupive, ne consola opyta va’erã oñemboheta ha online. $200 Portal rehegua, ikatu hína ha’ete peteĩ aparato barato, péro oikotevẽ peteĩ PS5 oñemomba’eguasúva $400 rupi. Upévare oje’e: mávape oipota ko dispositivo? Heta hína oipota, jahecháma. Switch iporã juego portátil haguã, repyhyi avión-pe, fiesta rupi térã mesa picnic rehe avei. Heta gamer katu oipota jejopy ógape, sofá térã tupa ári. Oipota ho’u juego PS5, opyta porã hína TV mbyte guasúgui—jepe irũnguéra oma’ẽma serie TV rehe—Portal nepytyvõ heta. Ko aparato ojogua Wii U controlador-pe, ome’ẽva PS5 interfaz. Pe TV ombojoajúva PS5 rehe, peteĩcha ojehecha Portal ha’erã TV-pe. Ndaikatúi Portal rupive remba’apo juego mombyry né irũnguéra oipuru Netflix-gui, media app ndoikói Portal-pe. Oñemboheko juego anoite. Portal rehegua streaming requiere internet potente: Sony ojerure 5 Mbps, haa 15 Mbps, ha ikatuve oñemomba’eguasu velocidad rehe. Iñañete rehe, Portal ndaikatúi omba’apo juego oma’ẽ PS5-pe; umi juegos stream PS Plus Premium-gui ndaikatúi Portal-pe. Peteĩ Portal rehegua mba’e iporãva ha’e DualSense controlador reheha pantalla peteĩ mbytépe. Upéicha, juego PS5 rehegua oguerekóva control iporãitéva, ndereikotevẽvéima remodifica botonera rehehy.

article_content: Greater Manchester Police were criticised for spending £2,500 of taxpayer money to bus approximately 700 English Defence League (EDL) supporters from train stations into Manchester city centre for a protest. The police provided this transportation to reduce the risk of disruption and to lessen the number of officers needed to escort the group through the streets. Simultaneously, about 350 Unite Against Fascism (UAF) supporters held a separate nearby protest. Both demonstrations culminated at Albert Square, which was heavily secured with more than 300 police officers, tactical units, dog teams, and helicopters. Steel fencing was installed around the square to prevent confrontations. Fifteen people were arrested during the event, which cost Greater Manchester Police over £50,000, not including VAT. Local officials, including Councillor Afzal Khan, criticised the use of public funds for such events, especially amid cuts to public services and concerns that protestors from outside the area were causing disruption. Chief Superintendent John O'Hare stated that using coaches to transport groups reduced the numbers of police needed and the chances of clashes. He emphasised that careful planning aimed to keep costs down and maintain order, arguing that poorly managed events could lead to even greater expenses.

Policía ome'ẽ ko viru ojepy’apy’ỹve hag̃ua ha avei ohechauka hag̃ua iñemomichĩha umi oficial policía ojekuaáva omoirũ hag̃ua tape rupi. Ojuehegui, 350 rupi Unite Against Fascism (UAF) rehegua ojapo avei peteĩ protesta hetãme. Mokõive aty og̃uahẽ kuri Albert Square-pe, oĩhaguépe heta policía, unidad táctica, jagua aty ha avei helikóptero. Oñemo’ã peteĩ cerca de acero omboyke hag̃ua jekakuaa. Chief Superintendent John O’Hare he’i oñembohasa hag̃ua umi aty colectivo-pe omomichĩha policía ikatu haguãicha ojeguereko pe orden ha omomichĩ avei jekakuaa. Ha’e avei omohendaha plan porã, oñeha’ãha ohechauka imichĩveha costo ha tapia omotenonde umi seguridad, ha he’i ojejapo’ỹrõ pe tembiapo porã, ikatu hetaave costo rehe.

article_content: Actor R Madhavan recently expressed gratitude on social media to the Income Tax Department for processing his company’s tax refund within three weeks of filing for the Assessment Year 2023-24. He praised the department's speed, efficiency, and transparency, calling their promptness 'unbelievable.' Madhavan also tagged Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and the Prime Minister’s Office in his post. Several users on social media echoed Madhavan's appreciation, noting marked improvements in the Income Tax system. Some commented that while further improvements could be made, the progress so far deserves recognition. However, others reported delays in receiving their refunds, with one user mentioning a five-month wait. Chartered Accountant Ankur Jain advised those facing delays to check for any pending notices or required actions in their accounts, noting that the vast majority of his clients had received refunds within three to four weeks, with delays usually due to outstanding queries. On the professional front, Madhavan will next be seen in the Netflix web series 'The Railway Men,' which tells the story of unsung heroes who saved thousands during the Bhopal tragedy. He will star alongside KK Menon. Madhavan's directorial venture, 'Rocketry: The Nambi Effect,' released in July last year, won Best Feature Film at the 69th National Film Awards and tells the story of aerospace engineer Nambi Narayanan. In other news, India’s GDP is projected to grow by 6.7% in the July-September quarter of 2023, driven by robust performance in the services sector. Meanwhile, telecom operators and device makers have voiced concerns over a proposal to beam TV content directly to mobile phones without cellular data, as the technology is considered immature. The government is also considering raising the threshold for arrests in GST evasion cases to ₹3 crore from ₹2 crore to reduce harassment and improve the business environment.

article_content: Social media often makes headlines for negative reasons, but sometimes it becomes a force for good. Recently, a campaign called 'Swab 4 Margot' spread across Twitter, Facebook, and YouTube, urging people to register as stem cell donors. The campaign centers on 17-month-old Margot Martini, who was diagnosed last October with a rare type of leukemia. She urgently needs a stem cell donor to have a chance at a cure, and since no relatives were a match, her family turned to the internet. Registering as a stem cell donor is simple. At deletebloodcancer.org.uk, people can order a free at-home mouth swab kit. Once completed and returned, their details are placed on the donor registry. Over 90,000 people in Britain have registered, but only about half of the 1,600 patients waiting for a transplant will find a suitable match. For the others, the outlook is grim. Margot's story has attracted widespread support. A YouTube video featuring her, set to a song by Ellie Goulding, has over 55,000 views and is watched more than 1,000 times daily. Celebrities like Gary Barlow, Stephen Fry, Richard Branson, and Ronnie Wood have amplified the campaign, and Margot's Facebook page has more than 8,000 likes. In the campaign's first two weeks, 12,000 people requested swab kits. Even if a match isn't found for Margot, increased registrations could save lives for many others. Such campaigns mark a significant shift in health advocacy. A decade ago, patients like Margot faced much lower chances of survival. Today, the reach of social media means more potential donors—and more hope. Two decades ago, the Sue Harris Campaign relied on speaking events and traditional media to encourage people to join the bone marrow registry; it succeeded in recruiting at least 15,000 donors. Although a match was eventually found, Sue Harris sadly died in 1997 before it could make a difference. Leukemia treatments like chemotherapy and radiotherapy attack both cancer and healthy bone marrow, so patients require stem cell transplants. Donors can give stem cells via a needle under anesthesia or by taking medication to increase cell levels for collection while awake. This pattern repeats: Jonni Berger's mother, Sharon, needed a transplant after being diagnosed with leukemia. Her children launched the #spit4mum campaign on Twitter, gaining celebrity support and driving a 1,000 percent rise in registrations. Jonni notes that real action, not just online sharing, is what saves lives. Yaser Martini, Margot’s father, describes his family’s motivation: “The first day, I felt overwhelmed, but Margot’s strength gave us strength. We needed to do everything possible for her.” He is grateful for community support but acknowledges that only a small fraction of people register. He hopes more will take that step. For now, Margot’s family anxiously waits, hoping the next registration will save their daughter. To join the registry, visit deletebloodcancer.org.uk.

article_content: Walmart is exploring a plan to have in-store customers deliver packages to online shoppers on their way home. This approach, part of the 'crowd-sourcing' or 'sharing economy', is designed to help Walmart better compete with online retail giant Amazon. Currently, the idea remains in early planning and faces legal, regulatory, and privacy challenges. Walmart is expanding efforts to ship online orders directly from stores, seeking to reduce transport costs and gain an edge over online retailers without physical stores. At present, 25 stores participate in this program, with plans to increase to 50 this year, and potentially to hundreds in the future. Walmart typically relies on carriers like FedEx for deliveries, and uses its own trucks for same-day service in select cities. According to Joel Anderson, CEO of Walmart.com (U.S.), millions of Walmart customers could sign up to deliver packages for others along their route home, in exchange for discounts on their shopping to cover their fuel costs. The plan is still in the brainstorming phase and could take a year or two to develop further, according to Jeff McAllister, Walmart U.S. senior vice president of innovations. However, Matt Nemer, a retail analyst at Wells Fargo Securities, believes widespread adoption is unlikely, suggesting it may be limited to urban markets and higher-value items. Start-ups like TaskRabbit, Fiverr, and Zipments already enable individuals to provide delivery services to businesses and customers. Zipments began as a crowdsourced delivery network, but now screens drivers and helps with insurance and licenses. CEO Garrick Pohl notes that while theft and fraud have not been issues, insurance and licensing remain important. Zipments encourages drivers to obtain personal liability and cargo insurance, and sometimes assists them in getting courier licenses where required. Pohl believes that crowdsourced delivery could work for major retailers like Walmart. While there are hurdles, similar models are used effectively in sectors such as food delivery. Zipments is pursuing partnerships with retailers, though specific companies have not been disclosed.

article_content: A Buffalo Bills fan, Robert Hopkins, was found guilty of third-degree assault and second-degree reckless endangerment on Tuesday. The verdict came after a six-member Orchard Park Town Court jury deliberated for about 20 minutes following a three-day trial. Hopkins could face up to a year in jail when sentenced on September 11. The charges are based on an incident during a Bills-New York Jets game at Ralph Wilson Stadium on November 17. Surveillance video showed Hopkins, 29, repeatedly sliding down a stadium railing before losing his balance and falling backward on his fifth attempt. He fell 20 to 25 feet from the upper deck, landing on Mark Bratcher, also 29, and causing injuries to Bratcher's head, neck, and back. Hopkins was not seriously hurt. After the incident, Hopkins lost his job in advertising and public relations and was banned from the stadium. Defense attorney Patrick Brown described the fall as an accident, arguing that while Hopkins' behavior was reckless, he did not perceive the risks at the time. Assistant District Attorney G. Michael Drmacich countered that Hopkins was aware of the danger and disregarded it. Drmacich noted that surveillance footage made the events clear. Dr. Loubert Steven Suddaby, Bratcher's neurosurgeon, testified that Bratcher sustained bulging discs in his cervical spine and a herniated disc in his mid-spine. Suddaby said that if the impact had been just two inches forward, Bratcher could have been killed or left paralyzed. Hopkins is currently awaiting sentencing.

Upe mba'e ojehu hague rire peteî seis-gua jurado rehegua Orchard Park Town Court oikuaava’ekue ojapo rire 20 aravo'i ikatu haguã. article_content: Severe flooding in India's northeastern state of Sikkim has left at least 14 people dead after intense rainfall caused the glacial Lhonak Lake to overflow. Officials report 26 injured and 102 missing, including 23 military personnel. Heavy rains — 40.9 millimeters between Tuesday and Wednesday morning, five times the average for this period — triggered the overflow, bursting the high-altitude Lhonak Lake near the base of Mount Kangchenjunga. The resulting wall of water surged downstream, swelling the Teesta River, dismantling a dam, and sweeping away houses and bridges. Sikkim authorities describe 'serious destruction'; 14 bridges and key roads were destroyed, with video footage showing collapsed homes and submerged vehicles. Rescue operations continue but are hindered by the collapse of the main highway connecting Sikkim to West Bengal and Gangtok, the capital. GT Dhungel, a local lawmaker, noted petrol and diesel shortages in Gangtok, though food is still available. Over 22,000 people are likely affected along a 120-kilometer stretch downstream. Satellite images reveal Lhonak Lake shrunk by nearly two-thirds (about 105 hectares), according to Indian Space Research Organisation. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has pledged full government support to those affected. Experts from the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development warn that as Himalayan glaciers melt faster due to climate change, such disasters may become more frequent, especially in high-altitude areas warming at double the global average. Similar extreme weather has recently caused deadly floods and landslides in other Indian mountain states, as well as in Pakistan and Nepal.

article_content: In London, the UK government introduced a legislative agenda focused on combatting crime, boosting the economy, and revising climate policies—measures that may represent Prime Minister Rishi Sunak's only King's Speech before the next general election. The plan, presented by King Charles III to lawmakers in the House of Lords, is intended to position Sunak and his Conservative Party in contrast to the opposition Labour Party, which currently leads in public opinion polls. Sunak’s administration is seeking to narrow Labour’s lead by lessening the impact of climate requirements on households and enforcing tougher sentences for serious offenders. The address by the King largely restated policies Sunak has promoted since taking office last year, after two previous Conservative leaders resigned in quick succession. During the ceremony—King Charles’s first King's Speech since his accession—he stated: 'My government will, in all respects, seek to make long-term decisions in the interests of future generations. By taking these long-term decisions, my government will change this country and build a better future.' The event, rich with British tradition, began with the King arriving by carriage and observing ceremonies dating back centuries. The speech signaled the launch of the election campaign. The government said it would proceed with introducing a Sentencing Bill to impose stricter penalties for violent crimes and reaffirmed its commitment to economic growth and maintaining low inflation. Rather than promising tax cuts, the King noted the government would focus on addressing inflation and the causes of slow growth instead of raising spending or borrowing. Given King Charles’s longstanding environmental advocacy, the practical approach to climate targets may be notable, but officials stressed the overall objectives remain. Sunak also introduced plans to legislate for annual North Sea oil and gas licensing—contrary to Labour’s position—and put forward measures to phase out tobacco sales to young people, address illegal migration, ban 'no-fault' evictions, and update property laws described as 'feudal.' Despite these policies, Sunak and the Conservatives are facing significant challenges: allegations of misconduct, ongoing questions about pandemic management, internal party divisions, and a substantial polling gap behind Labour. Nevertheless, Sunak emphasized that the government is making progress, claiming the present agenda is only the foundation for more far-reaching plans aimed at improving the country for future generations.
